mine: the right thigh
note: Shoq denotes the leg/thigh (the upper hind leg), not the shoulder; the KJV term recurs in 7:33-34, 8:25-26, 9:21, 10:14-15.

kjv: the anointing of Aaron, and of the anointing of his sons
mine: the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons
note: Mishchah here is the homonym meaning "allotted portion" (cf. Num 18:8), referring to the priestly share of the offerings, not the rite of anointing.

kjv: lifted up his (Aaron's) hand
mine: lifted his (Aaron's) hands
note: The written text (ketiv) is ydw "his hand," but the Masoretic reading (qere) is yadav "his hands"; the KJV followed the ketiv.

kjv: Uncover not your (Aaron's and his sons') heads
mine: Do not let your (Aaron's and his sons') hair hang loose
note: Para' ro'sh means to let the hair go loose/unkempt as a mourning sign (cf. 13:45, 21:10), not to remove a head covering; the KJV's "uncover" is a possible but less precise sense.

kjv: the coney
mine: the rock hyrax
note: shafan is the rock hyrax (Procavia); "coney" (rabbit) is an English approximation.

kjv: the ossifrage, and the ospray
mine: the bearded vulture, the black vulture
note: Many bird names (peres, 'ozniyyah) are uncertain; modern identifications differ from the KJV's guesses.

kjv: the owl ... the cuckow
mine: the ostrich ... the seagull
note: bat haya'anah is most likely the ostrich, and shachaf a gull; "cuckow" is a guess.

kjv: the swan, and the pelican, and the gier eagle
mine: the barn owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture
note: tinshemet, qa'at and racham are uncertain; the KJV list is guesswork, as are the modern identifications.

kjv: the lapwing
mine: the hoopoe
note: dukhifat is the hoopoe (Upupa epops), on ancient and modern evidence.

kjv: All fowls that creep, going upon all four
mine: All winged swarming creatures that walk on all fours
note: sherets ha'of means winged swarming things (insects), not birds; "fowls that creep" is misleading.

kjv: the beetle after his kind
mine: the cricket of every kind
note: chargol is a kind of locust or cricket, with leaping legs per v. 21; beetles do not fit.

kjv: the weasel ... the tortoise
mine: the mole rat ... the great lizard
note: choled is probably a mole rat, and tsav a large lizard (the dab lizard); "tortoise" is unlikely.

kjv: the ferret ... the snail, and the mole
mine: the gecko ... the skink, and the chameleon
note: These reptile names ('anaqah, koach, leta'ah, chomet, tinshamet) are uncertain, but all are lizards; "snail" and "mole" are unlikely in a list of lizards.

kjv: a young pigeon, or a turtledove, for a sin offering
mine: a young pigeon or a turtledove for a purification offering
note: chatta't here removes ritual impurity from childbirth, which is not a moral sin. "Purification offering" avoids implying that giving birth is sinful.

kjv: the plague of leprosy
mine: a case of skin disease
note: tsara'at covers various skin conditions, and even mould on fabric and walls (vv. 47-59, ch. 14). The symptoms described do not match Hansen's disease (leprosy). The term recurs through Lev 13-14.

kjv: it (the disease) is a dry scall
mine: It (the disease) is a scaly patch
note: netek is a scalp or beard condition, perhaps ringworm or favus. "Dry scall" is obsolete.

kjv: a fretting leprosy
mine: a malignant disease
note: tsara'at mam'eret is a persistent, spreading mould or decay in material. Same in v. 52 and 14:44.

kjv: it is fret inward, whether it be bare within or without
mine: whether the rot is on the back or on the front
note: pechetet beqarachto o vegabbachto uses the bald-head words of vv. 40-42 for the reverse and front of the fabric. The KJV's "bare within or without" is obscure.

kjv: the plague of leprosy in a house
mine: a case of disease in a house
note: tsara'at in a building is fungus, mould or mineral efflorescence. Calling it "leprosy" shows that the KJV's term does not fit the Hebrew category. Same through vv. 34-57.

kjv: with hollow strakes
mine: with greenish or reddish spots
note: sheqa'arurot is a hapax, perhaps depressions or eruptions. "Hollow strakes" is an obsolete guess.

kjv: [because of] his issue he [is] unclean
mine: his discharge is unclean
note: Hebrew zovo tame hu, "his discharge, it is unclean"; the KJV supplies "because of" and makes the man the subject, while the plain syntax declares the discharge itself unclean (the man's uncleanness follows in v. 3).

kjv: she shall be put apart seven days
mine: she shall be in her menstrual impurity for seven days
note: Hebrew tihyeh beniddatah, "she shall be in her niddah (menstrual impurity)"; niddah names the state of impurity, and the text does not prescribe physical seclusion as "put apart" suggests.

kjv: her flowers be upon him
mine: her menstrual impurity comes upon him
note: Hebrew niddatah, "her menstrual impurity"; "flowers" was an older English term for menstruation that modern readers will not recognise (also v. 33).

kjv: two turtles
mine: two turtledoves
note: Hebrew tor is the turtledove; "turtle" in 1611 meant the bird, but now suggests the reptile.

kjv: when they (Aaron's two sons) offered before the LORD
mine: when they (Aaron's two sons) drew near before Yahweh
note: Hebrew beqorbatam, "in their drawing near"; the verb qarav can imply offering, but the text refers to their unauthorised approach (Lev 10:1-2) rather than naming an act of sacrifice.

kjv: the other lot for the scapegoat
mine: the other lot for Azazel
note: Hebrew la'aza'zel, parallel to "for Yahweh", reads most naturally as a proper name (a wilderness being or place), not "goat that departs" (ez + azal) as the KJV, following the Vulgate caper emissarius, took it; also vv. 10, 26. Context: for Azazel (high confidence). The two lots are 'one for Yahweh and one for Azazel': the parallel requires a recipient, so Azazel is a name, as ESV, NRSV, NJPS and NET render it. What Azazel denotes (a wilderness being, a place, or 'removal') is left open by keeping the name. Other possible meanings: (1) 'for the scapegoat / the goat that departs' ('ez 'azal) — LXX to apopompaio, Vulgate caper emissarius, KJV, NIV, NASB; (2) 'for (complete) removal' — some lexicons (BDB); (3) a rugged cliff in the wilderness — Talmud (Yoma 67b), Rashi; (4) a demon or fallen angel — 1 Enoch 8-10, many modern scholars.

kjv: to let him (the goat) go for a scapegoat into the wilderness
mine: to send it (the goat) away into the wilderness to Azazel
note: Same term la'aza'zel; the goat is sent "to Azazel", the destination or recipient, rather than serving "as a scapegoat".

kjv: ye shall afflict your souls
mine: you shall humble yourselves
note: Hebrew te'annu et-naphshotekhem, "you shall humble/deny yourselves", understood as fasting and self-denial; "afflict your souls" suggests inner spiritual torment to a modern reader (also v. 31).

kjv: a sabbath of rest
mine: a sabbath of complete rest
note: Hebrew shabbat shabbaton, an intensive "sabbath of sabbath-rest", i.e. a total cessation; the KJV reduces the emphatic doubling.

kjv: unto devils
mine: to the goat-demons
note: Hebrew se'irim, literally "hairy ones / he-goats", here goat-shaped wilderness spirits worshipped in the open field; "devils" loses the specific goat imagery (cf. the goats of ch. 16).

kjv: the strangers which sojourn among you (Israel)
mine: the foreigners who reside among them (Israel)
note: The Masoretic text has betokham "among them" (also vv. 10, 13); the KJV's "among you" matches the Septuagint (en hymin) or harmonises with v. 12.

kjv: the blood [that] maketh an atonement for the soul
mine: the blood that makes atonement by means of the life
note: Hebrew bannephesh yekhapper, with the preposition be- most naturally instrumental ("by means of the life" contained in the blood) rather than "for the soul"; the KJV reading duplicates the preceding clause, while the instrumental sense explains why blood atones. Context: by means of the life (medium confidence). The verse grounds atonement in the fact that 'the life of the flesh is in the blood'; be- is most naturally instrumental, 'by means of the life' (ESV, NASB, NET), and avoids merely repeating 'for your lives'. A beth of price ('in exchange for life') is also seriously argued. Other possible meanings: (1) 'in exchange for the life' (life for life) — LXX anti psyches, several commentators; (2) 'as life' (the blood, being life, atones) — NRSV, NJPS; (3) 'for the soul/life' — Vulgate pro animae, KJV, NIV.

kjv: The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother
mine: the nakedness of your father, that is, the nakedness of your mother
note: Hebrew erwat avikha we'erwat immekha joins the two with waw; since the rest of the verse speaks only of the mother, the waw is best read as explicative (the mother's nakedness is the father's, cf. v. 8), whereas the KJV's "or" makes it two separate prohibitions including the father.

kjv: pass through [the fire] to Molech
mine: to pass them over to Molech
note: Hebrew leha'avir lammolekh, "to cause to pass over/dedicate to Molech"; the KJV supplies "the fire" (as in Deut 18:10, 2 Kgs 23:10), which is a likely meaning but not stated here.

kjv: it [is] confusion
mine: it is perversion
note: Hebrew tevel, a violation of the created order (from balal "mix"); "confusion" now suggests mere bewilderment.

kjv: ye shall offer it (the peace offering) at your own will
mine: sacrifice it (the peace offering) so that you may be accepted
note: Hebrew lirtsonkhem, "for your acceptance", i.e. in the manner that makes the offerer acceptable to God (cf. 1:3, 22:19); the KJV took ratson as the offerer's own free will.

kjv: it (the peace offering) [is] abominable
mine: it (the peace offering) is tainted
note: Hebrew piggul is a technical term for sacrificial meat that has become unfit by being kept too long; "abominable" blurs it with to'evah.

kjv: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour
mine: you shall not stand idly by when your neighbor's life is at stake
note: Hebrew lo ta'amod al dam re'ekha is idiomatic and disputed: either "do not stand (up) against your neighbour's life" (seek his death, e.g. by false testimony) or "do not stand by over his blood" (fail to help); the KJV is literal, I follow the second reading.

kjv: and not suffer sin upon him (your neighbor)
mine: so that you do not incur sin because of him (your neighbor)
note: Hebrew welo tissa alaw het, "and you shall not bear sin on his account"; the rebuke keeps the rebuker from sharing guilt, rather than (as the KJV's "suffer" = allow suggests) preventing the neighbour from continuing in sin.

kjv: a garment mingled of linen and woollen
mine: a garment of two kinds of material, of mixed fabric
note: Hebrew sha'atnez is an obscure loanword for a mixed fabric; the KJV fills in "linen and wool" from Deut 22:11, which is probably right but not what this verse says.

kjv: she shall be scourged
mine: there shall be an inquiry
note: Hebrew biqqoret, a rare word from baqar "examine", most likely means investigation or compensation/damages; "scourged" follows rabbinic and older tradition and also wrongly makes the woman alone the one punished. Context: an inquiry (low confidence). Biqqoret is a hapax from baqar 'examine, seek'; 'inquiry' (LXX episkope, NRSV) stays closest to the root, while Akkadian baqaru 'claim' supports 'compensation'. No death penalty and the guilt offering (19:21) rule out a capital sentence, but translations divide three ways; confidence lowered. Nothing in the word singles out the woman. Other possible meanings: (1) 'there shall be compensation/an indemnity' — NJPS, NET, Speiser, Milgrom; (2) 'there shall be punishment' — NIV, NASB, CSB; Vulgate vapulabunt ambo ('both shall be beaten'); (3) 'a distinction shall be made' (from adultery with a free woman) — ESV; (4) 'she shall be scourged' — Sifra, Talmud (Keritot 11a), KJV.

kjv: nor observe times
mine: or soothsaying
note: Hebrew lo te'onenu, a form of divination (perhaps by clouds or reading signs); "observe times" reflects an old guess (lucky days) that is not now favoured.

kjv: them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards
mine: the spirits of the dead or to the spiritists
note: Hebrew ha'ovot and hayyidde'onim denote ghosts of the dead consulted in necromancy and those "who know" them; "familiar spirits" and "wizards" suggest European folk magic.

kjv: in meteyard
mine: in measures of length
note: Hebrew middah, a measure of length; "meteyard" (a measuring rod) is obsolete English.

kjv: that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard
mine: who is a medium or a spiritist
note: Hebrew ki yihyeh vahem ov o yidde'oni, "in whom there is a ghost (ov) or a knowing spirit (yidde'oni)", i.e. one who practises necromancy; "familiar spirit" and "wizard" suggest European witchcraft rather than consulting the dead.

kjv: [being] a chief man among his (the priest's) people
mine: as a husband among his (the priest's) people
note: Hebrew lo yittamma ba'al be'ammaw is terse and obscure; ba'al most often means "husband/owner", suggesting the priest may not defile himself for in-laws or a wife's kin (or as a husband), whereas the KJV takes ba'al as "chief man", a sense not otherwise attested for the word. Context: as a husband (i.e. not for in-laws) (medium confidence). Ba'al most often means 'husband' or 'owner'; after 21:1-3 lists the blood relatives a priest may mourn, 21:4 most naturally excludes kin by marriage. ESV, NRSV and NET read 'as a husband'; NIV, NASB, NJPS and CSB 'for relatives by marriage'. The terse Hebrew may be damaged. Other possible meanings: (1) 'being a chief man among his people' — Vulgate (in principe), KJV, a sense of ba'al not otherwise attested; (2) not even for his own wife — some interpreters, while rabbinic tradition (Sifra) limits it to a wife unfit for him; (3) emended to refer to a married sister (cf. 21:3) — some critical scholars.

kjv: the bread of their (the priests') God
mine: the food of their (the priests') God
note: Hebrew lechem elohehem; lechem here denotes sacrificial food generally (chiefly meat and fat burned on the altar), not bread specifically (also vv. 8, 17, 21, 22).

kjv: shall not uncover his (the high priest's) head
mine: shall not let the hair of his (the high priest's) head hang loose
note: Hebrew et-rosho lo yifra', from para' "let loose/dishevel", a mourning gesture (cf. 10:6, 13:45); the issue is unbound hair, not removing a head covering.

kjv: the crown of the anointing oil
mine: the consecration of the anointing oil
note: Hebrew nezer means both "consecration/dedication" and the "crown/diadem" that marks it; here it is the anointing oil itself, so "consecration" fits the phrase better.

kjv: he that hath a flat nose, or any thing superfluous
mine: has a disfigured face or a limb too long
note: Hebrew harum and saru'a are rare; harum is probably a facial disfigurement (traditionally a split or flat nose) and saru'a "overgrown/elongated" (a deformed limb); the KJV's "any thing superfluous" is vague.

kjv: or be scurvy, or scabbed
mine: or an itching disease or scabs
note: Hebrew garav and yallefet are skin diseases (eczema, scabs); "scurvy" now names a vitamin-deficiency disease.

kjv: a leper
mine: has a skin disease
note: Hebrew tsarua', one afflicted with tsara'at, a range of skin conditions (and mould in fabrics and houses, ch. 13-14), not specifically Hansen's disease (leprosy).

kjv: [Ye shall offer] at your own will
mine: if it is to be accepted for you
note: Hebrew lirtsonkhem, "for your acceptance"; the clause states the condition for the offering to be accepted (cf. v. 20 "it will not be accepted for you"), not that it is offered of the worshipper's own free will (also v. 29).

kjv: or having a wen
mine: or having a running sore
note: Hebrew yabbelet, probably a suppurating sore or wart (from yaval "flow"); "wen" (a cyst) is an obsolete guess.

kjv: the meat offering thereof (the lamb)
mine: its (the lamb's) grain offering
note: Hebrew minchah here is an offering of flour and oil; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, but a modern reader will think of flesh (recurring term: also vv. 16, 18, 37 and throughout Leviticus).

kjv: parched corn, nor green ears
mine: roasted grain or fresh grain
note: Hebrew qali and karmel are roasted and fresh (new) grain; "corn" meant any cereal (here barley), not maize.

kjv: seven sabbaths shall be complete
mine: seven full weeks shall there be
note: Hebrew sheva shabbatot temimot; shabbat here denotes a full week (cf. "fifty days", v. 16), though the KJV's literal "sabbaths" preserves the ambiguity that fuelled ancient disputes over whether "the sabbath" in vv. 11, 15 is the weekly sabbath or the festival day.

kjv: the boughs of goodly trees
mine: the fruit of splendid trees
note: Hebrew peri ets hadar is "fruit of a splendid tree" (traditionally the citron), not "boughs"; the KJV assimilates it to the following list of branches.

kjv: the pure candlestick
mine: the lampstand of pure gold
note: Hebrew menorah is an oil-lamp stand (cf. "lamps" in the same verse and v. 2); "candlestick" suggests candles, which were not used.

kjv: shall be meat for you
mine: shall be food for you
note: Hebrew le'okhlah, "for food"; the produce is grain and fruit, and "meat" (= food in 1611) now means flesh (also v. 7).

kjv: the trumpet of the jubile
mine: the ram's horn loudly
note: Hebrew shofar teru'ah, "a horn of loud blast"; the word "jubilee" (yovel) is first introduced in v. 10, so the KJV's "trumpet of the jubile" anticipates it, and shofar is a ram's horn rather than a metal trumpet.

kjv: if a man purchase of the Levites
mine: whatever is redeemed from the Levites
note: Hebrew wa'asher yig'al min-halewiyim, "and whoever/whatever redeems from the Levites"; the verse is notoriously obscure (the Vulgate inserts "not"), and the KJV takes ga'al loosely as "purchase".

kjv: the field of the suburbs of their (the Levites') cities
mine: the pastureland belonging to their (the Levites') cities
note: Hebrew migrash is the open common land around a town used for grazing; "suburbs" now means residential districts.

kjv: [yea, though he be] a stranger, or a sojourner; that he (your brother) may live with thee
mine: as a foreigner and resident alien he (your brother) shall live with you
note: Hebrew ger wetoshav wachay immakh: the impoverished Israelite brother is to be supported and live alongside you with the status of a resident alien; the KJV's supplied words make the verse extend charity to a foreigner instead.

kjv: Take thou no usury of him (your brother)
mine: Take no interest
note: Hebrew neshekh and tarbit denote any interest or increase on a loan; "usury" now implies only excessive rates (also v. 37).

kjv: a standing image
mine: a sacred pillar
note: Hebrew matsevah is an upright standing stone used in cultic worship, not a statue or "image".

kjv: consumption, and the burning ague
mine: wasting disease and fever
note: Hebrew shachefet and qaddachat are a wasting illness and a fever; "consumption" (tuberculosis) and "ague" (malarial fever) are specific older diagnoses read into general terms.

kjv: your earth as brass
mine: your earth like bronze
note: Hebrew nechushah is copper or bronze; brass (a copper-zinc alloy) was not in use, and in 1611 "brass" covered copper alloys generally.

kjv: cut down your images
mine: cut down your incense altars
note: Hebrew hammanim, now known from inscriptions and finds to be small incense altars (possibly linked to the sun, chammah); the KJV's "images" was a guess.

kjv: they (the Israelites) then accept of the punishment of their iniquity
mine: they (the Israelites) then make amends for their iniquity
note: Hebrew yirtsu et-awonam, from ratsah "be pleased with / pay off"; the same verb is used of the land "enjoying/paying off" its sabbaths (v. 34), so the sense is paying off the debt of guilt, whether as "accepting punishment" or "making amends" (also v. 43).

kjv: When a man shall make a singular vow
mine: When anyone makes a special vow
note: yafli' neder means "makes an extraordinary or special vow". "Singular" now means "single".

kjv: None devoted, which shall be devoted of men, shall be redeemed; but shall surely be put to death
mine: No one devoted ... from among mankind, shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death
note: cherem of persons means those placed under the ban of destruction (e.g., in war or by judicial sentence). Both translations are literal. The KJV's "of men" leaves unclear whether it means a person someone has vowed or a person condemned. Context: a person under the ban of destruction (medium confidence). Cherem of persons denotes those placed under the ban of destruction, in war (1 Sam 15) or by judicial sentence (Exod 22:19). Since 27:1-8 lets vowed persons be redeemed, 27:29 is best read of persons already under the ban, not private vows. The rendering follows the Hebrew closely, as ESV and NRSV do. Other possible meanings: (1) a person devoted to God by an individual's vow must die — read by some into the Jephthah story (Judg 11:30-39), but most reject it since 27:1-8 provides redemption; (2) a person already condemned to death by a court cannot be valued or ransomed — Mishnah Arakhin, Rashi.

kjv: heads of thousands in Israel
mine: the heads of the clans of Israel
note: 'alfei yisra'el: 'elef means both "thousand" and "clan/military unit". The second sense bears on the debate over the size of the census figures.

kjv: the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death
mine: any outsider who comes near shall be put to death
note: zar here means any non-Levite, not a foreigner. "Stranger" misleads. Same in 3:10, 3:38, 18:7.

kjv: far off about the tabernacle of the congregation shall they (the Israelites) pitch
mine: They (the Israelites) shall camp facing the tent of meeting on every side
note: minneged means "opposite, facing" or "at a distance". The tribes face the tent from all sides.

kjv: the tabernacle of the congregation
mine: the tent of meeting
note: 'ohel mo'ed means the tent where God meets Israel, not a congregation's tent. The KJV uses this phrase throughout the Pentateuch.

kjv: strange fire
mine: unauthorized fire
note: Hebrew esh zarah is fire that is "foreign" to the prescribed ritual, i.e. not authorized; modern "strange" suggests merely odd.

kjv: the stranger that cometh nigh
mine: any outsider who comes near
note: Hebrew zar here means anyone not of the authorized group (a non-priest/non-Levite, even an Israelite), not a foreigner as modern "stranger" implies; same in 3:38.

kjv: the candlestick
mine: the lampstand
note: Hebrew menorah is a stand holding oil lamps; there were no candles. Recurs throughout.

kjv: the boards of the tabernacle
mine: the frames of the tabernacle
note: Hebrew qerashim are now generally understood as open wooden frames rather than solid planks.

kjv: the covering of badgers' skins
mine: a covering of fine leather
note: Hebrew tachash is uncertain (dugong/sea-cow, a dyed leather, or a fine leather from an Egyptian loanword); badgers are unlikely. Recurs in 4:8-14, 4:25. Context: a fine leather (medium confidence). As Exod 39:34: tachash is uncertain but denotes a valued material (Ezek 16:10), not a badger's pelt. 'Fine leather' (NRSV, NET; NIV 'durable leather') commits least to a species. Other possible meanings: (1) sea-cow/dugong or dolphin/porpoise skins — NJPS 'dolphin skins', NASB95 'porpoise skins', NIV 1984 'sea cows'; (2) violet/blue-dyed skins — LXX hyakinthina, Vulgate ianthina; (3) goatskins — ESV; (4) 'badgers' skins' — KJV, from a Talmudic identification of tachash as an animal.

kjv: covers to cover withal
mine: the jugs for the drink offering
note: Hebrew qesot hannesek are pitchers or jars "of the libation", vessels for pouring, not lids.

kjv: upon a bar
mine: on the carrying frame
note: Hebrew mot is a pole-frame or litter for carrying, not a single bar.

kjv: the daily meat offering
mine: the regular grain offering
note: Hebrew minchat hatamid is the continual grain offering; "meat" meant food in 1611 and now misleads.

kjv: to see when the holy things are covered
mine: to look at the holy things even for a moment
note: Hebrew kevalla' is literally "as a swallowing", most likely an idiom for "an instant" (like "a gulp"); the KJV took it as the covering ("swallowing up") of the objects. Context: even for a moment (medium confidence). 4:15-19 forbid the Kohathites to touch or see the holy things; kevalla' 'as a swallowing' is best taken as an idiom for an instant (cf. Job 7:19 'till I swallow my spit'), as ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and CSB render. The Targum and Vulgate instead relate it to the wrapping of the objects. Other possible meanings: (1) 'when the holy things are covered/wrapped' (bala' 'swallow up, envelop') — Targum Onkelos, Vulgate, Rashi, KJV; (2) 'witness the dismantling of the sanctuary' (bala' 'take down') — NJPS; (3) 'suddenly' — LXX exapina.

kjv: every leper
mine: everyone with a skin disease
note: Hebrew tsarua covers a range of scaly skin conditions (and mould on fabric/walls elsewhere), not specifically Hansen's disease (modern leprosy).

kjv: uncover the woman's head
mine: loosen the hair of the woman's head
note: Hebrew para' rosh means to let the hair hang loose or dishevelled (a sign of shame or mourning), not necessarily removing a covering.

kjv: gone aside to uncleanness [with another] instead of thy husband
mine: gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband's authority
note: Hebrew tachat ishek means "under your husband", i.e. while married to him; the KJV's "instead of" plus supplied "[with another]" shifts the sense. Same in 5:20, 5:29.

kjv: make thy thigh to rot
mine: makes your thigh waste away
note: Hebrew yarekh nofelet is literally "a falling thigh", perhaps a euphemism for miscarriage, prolapse or sterility (cf. 5:28 "shall conceive"); "rot" is an interpretation, as is "waste away". Also 5:22, 5:27.

kjv: a Nazarite
mine: a Nazirite
note: Hebrew nazir "one separated/consecrated" has nothing to do with Nazareth; the KJV spelling invites confusion with "Nazarene".

kjv: from the kernels even to the husk
mine: from the seeds to the skins
note: The rare words chartsannim and zag are uncertain (seeds/unripe grapes and skins); the KJV pair is a defensible guess, as is mine.

kjv: two turtles
mine: two turtledoves
note: Hebrew tor is the turtledove; "turtle" in 1611 meant the bird but today suggests the reptile.

kjv: One spoon of ten [shekels] of gold
mine: one gold dish of ten shekels
note: Hebrew kaf (literally "palm") is a shallow pan or dish for incense, not a spoon in the modern sense; recurs through 7:86.

kjv: from off the mercy seat
mine: from above the atonement cover
note: Hebrew kapporet (from kpr "atone/cover") is the lid of the ark where atonement blood was applied; "mercy seat" follows Tyndale/Luther and reads in a throne image.

kjv: unto the shaft thereof (the lampstand)
mine: from its (the lampstand's) base
note: Hebrew yerekh (literally "thigh") here denotes the base or stem of the lampstand; the phrase means "from base to blossoms", i.e. the whole piece.

kjv: offer the Levites before the LORD [for] an offering
mine: present the Levites before Yahweh as a wave offering
note: Hebrew henif ... tenufah is the technical "wave offering" (elevation) ritual; the KJV's generic "offering" obscures that the Levites are dedicated like a waved portion. Also 8:13, 8:15, 8:21.

kjv: whether [it was] by day or by night that the cloud was taken up
mine: or if it continued for a day and a night, when the cloud lifted
note: Hebrew o yomam valaylah "or day and night" most naturally continues the series of durations (one night; a day and a night; two days; a month); the KJV takes it as the time of lifting.

kjv: of a whole piece
mine: of hammered work
note: Hebrew miqshah denotes metal hammered or beaten into shape (as with the lampstand, 8:4, where the KJV has "beaten work").

kjv: heads of the thousands of Israel
mine: the heads of the clans of Israel
note: Hebrew elef can mean "thousand" or a clan/military unit; here it denotes the tribal subdivisions rather than a numerical count.

kjv: Raguel
mine: Reuel
note: Hebrew Re'uel is the same name the KJV spells "Reuel" in Exod 2:18; "Raguel" follows the Septuagint/Vulgate form and obscures the identity.

kjv: fell a lusting
mine: had a strong craving
note: Hebrew hitavvu ta'avah is a craving (here for food); modern "lust" suggests sexual desire. Same in 11:34 "the people that lusted".

kjv: baked [it] (the manna) in pans ... as the taste of fresh oil
mine: boiled it (the manna) in pots ... like the taste of cakes made with oil
note: Hebrew bishlu bapparur is "boiled in a pot"; leshad hashemen is uncertain (rich cream, oil cake), "fresh oil" is one guess.

kjv: they (the seventy elders) prophesied, and did not cease
mine: they (the seventy elders) prophesied, but they did not do so again
note: Hebrew welo yasafu (from yasaf "add/do again") means the prophesying was a one-time sign; the KJV follows the Targum/Vulgate sense "did not stop" (as if from suf "cease").

kjv: the servant of Moses, [one] of his young men
mine: Moses' assistant from his (Joshua's) youth
note: Hebrew mibbechurav can mean "from his youth" or "of his chosen men"; the KJV takes the latter.

kjv: two cubits [high] upon the face of the earth
mine: about two cubits above the ground
note: Hebrew ke'ammatayim al-pene ha'arets may mean the quail flew low (about a metre up) where they could be caught, rather than lay piled that high; the KJV's supplied "[high]" chooses the heap reading.

kjv: the Ethiopian woman
mine: the Cushite woman
note: Hebrew kushit is "Cushite"; Cush usually means the Nile region south of Egypt (Nubia, the Septuagint's "Ethiopia"), but some identify it with Cushan near Midian (Hab 3:7), so the bare gentilic is safer.

kjv: who [is] faithful in all mine (Yahweh's) house
mine: he (Moses) is entrusted with all My (Yahweh's) house
note: Hebrew ne'eman can mean "faithful/reliable" or "entrusted (with)"; both are defensible, the latter fits the household-steward image.

kjv: even apparently
mine: clearly
note: Hebrew mar'eh "(in) plain sight"; in 1611 "apparently" meant "manifestly, openly", while today it means "seemingly", the opposite nuance.

kjv: as men come to Hamath
mine: near Lebo-hamath
note: Hebrew levo chamat ("the entrance of Hamath") is now generally taken as a place name, Lebo(-hamath), in the Beqaa valley, rather than a description of the route.

kjv: the giants, the sons of Anak, [which come] of the giants
mine: the Nephilim (the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim)
note: Hebrew nephilim is a proper term (cf. Gen 6:4) of uncertain meaning; the KJV follows the Septuagint gigantes. The parenthesis linking Anakim to Nephilim is part of the spies' exaggeration. Context: the Nephilim, seen as giants (medium confidence). Nephilim is a proper term (Gen 6:4) of uncertain meaning; transliterating it, as ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS and CSB do, keeps it open, while the grasshopper comparison shows the spies meant men of huge size. The parenthesis linking Anakim to Nephilim is absent from the LXX and may be a gloss. Other possible meanings: (1) 'giants' — LXX and Vulgate gigantes, KJV; (2) 'fallen ones', from naphal 'fall' — some Jewish interpreters (cf. Rashi on Gen 6:4); (3) the parenthesis as a later scribal note rather than part of the spies' speech — many commentators, since the LXX lacks it.

kjv: [as] truly [as] I (Yahweh) live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD
mine: truly, as I (Yahweh) live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the glory of Yahweh
note: Hebrew chai-ani weyimmale ... is an oath formula ("as I live and as the earth is filled ..."), whose content follows in vv. 22-23; the KJV turns the second clause into an independent prophecy.

kjv: shall wander in the wilderness
mine: shall be shepherds in the wilderness
note: Hebrew ro'im means "shepherds/grazing"; the KJV's "wander" gives the effect (nomadic life) rather than the word.

kjv: ye (Israel) shall know my (Yahweh's) breach of promise
mine: you (Israel) shall know My (Yahweh's) opposition
note: Hebrew tenu'ati (from nu' "hinder, frustrate") is God's opposition or displeasure toward them; "breach of promise" implies God broke his word, which the text does not say.

kjv: a meat offering
mine: a grain offering
note: minchah here is the grain offering; "meat" meant food in 1611, but today it suggests flesh.

kjv: an heave offering
mine: a contribution
note: terumah means something lifted off and set aside, a contribution; "heave" suggests a waving or lifting rite.

kjv: the same reproacheth the LORD
mine: is blaspheming Yahweh
note: megaddef means "reviles/blasphemes"; "reproacheth" is weaker but close.

kjv: fringes in the borders of their (the Israelites') garments
mine: tassels on the corners of their (the Israelites') garments
note: tsitsit means tassels and kanfei means corners (cf. Deut 22:12, "four corners"); "borders" suggests hems.

kjv: they go down quick into the pit
mine: they go down alive into Sheol
note: chayyim she'olah: "quick" (alive) is archaic. she'ol is the realm of the dead, not a literal pit. Same in v. 33.

kjv: these men have provoked the LORD
mine: these men have despised Yahweh
note: ni'atsu means "spurned, treated with contempt". "Provoked" misses the sense.

kjv: these sinners against their own souls
mine: these men who sinned at the cost of their lives
note: (KJV 16:38) Hebrew benafshotam, "with/at the price of their lives": the point is that their sin cost them their lives, not that they wronged their own souls.

kjv: a token against the rebels
mine: a sign for the rebels
note: (KJV 17:10) Hebrew livne-meri, "for sons of rebellion"; the sign is a warning to them, which the KJV makes explicitly adversative; difference is slight.

kjv: by reason of the anointing
mine: as a portion
note: Hebrew lemoshchah is best taken from mashach II "measure off", a priestly share (cf. Lev 7:35), not "anointing"; the gifts are Aaron's allotted portion.

kjv: meat offering
mine: grain offering
note: Hebrew minchah here is the cereal offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, so a modern reader wrongly hears an animal sacrifice (recurs throughout Numbers).

kjv: the right shoulder
mine: the right thigh
note: Hebrew shoq is the leg/thigh of the animal, not the shoulder.

kjv: on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean ... then the seventh day he shall not be clean
mine: on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean ... he will not become clean
note: The Masoretic accents group "on the third day and on the seventh day" with yithchatta (purify himself), so purification is required on both days; the KJV attaches the seventh day to the result clause.

kjv: he (the unclean person) shall purify himself
mine: he (the clean person) shall purify him (the unclean person)
note: Hebrew vechitte'o is Piel with an object suffix, "he shall purify him": the clean person completes the purification of the unclean one, who then washes.

kjv: Would God that we (the people) had died
mine: If only we (the people) had perished
note: Hebrew velu is a simple wish particle ("if only"); there is no word for God, and the KJV idiom may now be read as an appeal to God.

kjv: sent an angel
mine: sent a messenger
note: Hebrew mal'akh means messenger, human or divine; addressed to Edom, the phrase may refer to Moses or to the angel of Exodus 14:19.

kjv: by the coast of the land of Edom
mine: on the border of the land of Edom
note: Hebrew gevul means border/territory; Mount Hor is inland, and "coast" in 1611 meant boundary (recurs in Num 20-22, 32).

kjv: king Arad the Canaanite
mine: the Canaanite, the king of Arad
note: Hebrew melekh-'Arad is "king of Arad"; Arad is a Negev city (cf. 33:40, Josh 12:14), not the king's personal name.

kjv: by the way of the spies
mine: by the way of Atharim
note: Hebrew ha'atarim is most likely a place or route name; the KJV, following the Targum, read it as tarim "spies" (cf. 14:6).

kjv: this light bread
mine: this worthless food
note: Hebrew haqqeloqel means contemptible, miserable (from qalal "be light, trifling"); the manna is despised, not described as light in texture.

kjv: What he (Yahweh) did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon
mine: Waheb in Suphah, and the wadis, the Arnon
note: Hebrew 'et-Vahev beSufah is an obscure poetic fragment, now usually taken as a place name Waheb in a district Suphah; the KJV follows a Jewish tradition reading it as "what he gave at the Sea of Reeds". Context: place names (medium confidence). The object marker 'et with no verb shows a quoted fragment. Waheb and Suphah are best taken as places, matching 'the wadis of the Arnon' and the itinerary of 21:10-20. ESV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS read 'Waheb in Suphah'; NIV 'Zahab in Suphah'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'what he did at the Red Sea' (Suphah taken as Yam Suph) — Targum, Rashi, Vulgate (sicut fecit in mari Rubro), KJV; (2) 'he set Zoob on fire', reading a verb — LXX; (3) 'Zahab' rather than 'Waheb' — NIV, following some versional evidence.

kjv: by the direction of the lawgiver
mine: with the scepter
note: Hebrew bimchoqeq means "with a ruler's staff" (instrument, parallel to "with their staffs"); the KJV takes the participle as a person, "lawgiver".

kjv: which looketh toward Jeshimon
mine: which overlooks the wasteland
note: Hebrew hayshimon "the desert/wasteland" has the article and may be a common noun; the KJV treats it as a place name.

kjv: on this side Jordan [by] Jericho
mine: across the Jordan from Jericho
note: Hebrew me'ever leYarden means "beyond the Jordan"; the KJV renders from the camp's viewpoint east of the river, but the phrase is a fixed term for the Transjordan opposite Jericho.

kjv: ever since [I was] thine (Balaam's)
mine: all your (Balaam's) life
note: Hebrew me'odekha means "from your existence on", i.e. as long as you have lived; the KJV's supplied words make it the length of ownership.

kjv: unto a city of Moab
mine: at Ir-moab
note: Hebrew 'ir Mo'av here is probably the place name Ir/Ar of Moab (cf. 21:15, 28), not an unnamed city.

kjv: into the high places of Baal, that thence he (Balaam) might see
mine: to Bamoth-baal, and from there he (Balaam) saw
note: Hebrew bamot ba'al is likely the place name Bamoth-baal (cf. 21:19-20), and wayyar' is a plain narrative "and he saw", not a purpose clause.

kjv: he (Balaam) went to an high place
mine: he (Balaam) went off to a bare height
note: Hebrew shefi denotes a bare, treeless hill; it is not the usual word for a cultic "high place" (bamah).

kjv: the number of the fourth [part] of Israel
mine: number the dust cloud of Israel
note: Hebrew rova' is usually "a fourth", but the parallel with "dust of Jacob" and Akkadian turbu'u suggest "dust cloud"; the KJV needs a supplied word to make "fourth part" work.

kjv: the strength of an unicorn
mine: the horns of a wild ox
note: Hebrew re'em is the wild ox (aurochs); the KJV followed the Septuagint monokeros. To'afot probably means horns or towering strength. Context: wild ox (high confidence). Re'em is the wild ox or aurochs (Akkadian rimu), a two-horned beast: Deut 33:17 speaks of the horns (plural) of a re'em. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS and CSB all read 'wild ox'. To'afot is less certain: 'horns' (ESV, NRSV, NJPS) or 'strength' (NIV). Other possible meanings: (1) 'unicorn', a one-horned beast — LXX monokeros, KJV; Vulgate 'rhinoceros'; (2) 'strength' or 'towering might' rather than 'horns' for to'afot — LXX doxa, Vulgate fortitudo, KJV, NIV.

kjv: the strength of an unicorn
mine: the horns of a wild ox
note: Hebrew re'em is the wild ox; the KJV followed the Septuagint monokeros (as in 23:22).

kjv: I (Balaam) will advertise thee (Balak)
mine: let me (Balaam) advise you (Balak)
note: Hebrew 'i'atsekha means "I will counsel/advise you"; "advertise" in 1611 meant inform or warn, not publicise.

kjv: smite the corners of Moab
mine: crush the brow of Moab
note: Hebrew pa'ate Mo'av, "the sides/temples of Moab", is probably the temples of the head (cf. Jer 48:45 "the forehead of Moab"), not the territorial corners.

kjv: until Asshur shall carry thee (Kain) away captive
mine: How long until Asshur takes you (Kain) captive?
note: Hebrew 'ad-mah is the interrogative "how long?", introducing a new clause, not the conjunction "until".

kjv: hang them (the chiefs) up before the LORD against the sun
mine: impale them (the chiefs) before Yahweh in the sun
note: Hebrew hoqa' (cf. 2 Sam 21:6) denotes a form of public execution and exposure, probably impaling or dismembering; "hang" suggests a noose.

kjv: Vex the Midianites
mine: Treat the Midianites as enemies
note: Hebrew tsaror means to be hostile to, attack; "vex" in 1611 meant harass or afflict, now it reads as merely "annoy".

kjv: commanded Moses and the children of Israel, which went forth out of the land of Egypt
mine: commanded Moses. The Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt were:
note: The Hebrew can be read as "Moses and the Israelites" as joint objects of the command, or (as the list that follows suggests) as a heading introducing the census of "the Israelites who came out of Egypt".

kjv: Sarah
mine: Serah
note: Hebrew Serach (with chet) is a different name from Sarah (Sarah with he); the KJV spells it Serah in Gen 46:17 and 1 Chr 7:30.

kjv: ye (Moses and Aaron) rebelled against my commandment ... to sanctify me at the water
mine: you (Moses and Aaron) rebelled against My command ... instead of treating Me as holy through the water
note: Hebrew lehaqdisheni is elliptical: the command was to treat God as holy, which they failed to do (cf. 20:12); the KJV's literal infinitive reads as though the rebellion served to sanctify him.

kjv: after your weeks [be out]
mine: at your Festival of Weeks
note: Hebrew beshavu'otekhem, "in/at your Weeks", names the festival (Shavu'ot, cf. Exod 34:22, Deut 16:10); the KJV's supplied words make it a time reference to the end of the seven-week count.

kjv: ye shall afflict your souls
mine: you shall humble yourselves
note: 'innitem et-nafshoteikhem means to humble or deny yourselves (fasting); "afflict your souls" suggests mental anguish.

kjv: ye shall do no servile work
mine: you shall do no regular work
note: melekhet 'avodah means ordinary occupational work; "servile" implies the work of slaves.

kjv: if she had at all an husband, when she vowed
mine: If she marries a husband while under her vows
note: hayo tihyeh le'ish means "if she indeed becomes a man's", which refers to a woman who marries while still under vows made in her father's house. Married women's vows are covered separately in v. 11. KJV 30:6.

kjv: chains, and bracelets, rings, earrings, and tablets
mine: armlets and bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants
note: kumaz is an ornament of uncertain kind (cf. Exod 35:22). "Tablets" is a guess.

kjv: an increase of sinful men
mine: a brood of sinful men
note: tarbut means "offspring, brood". "Increase" now reads as growth in number.

kjv: took the small towns thereof
mine: captured their tent villages
note: chawwot are tent encampments or villages (Havvoth-jair = "tent villages of Jair").

kjv: king Arad the Canaanite
mine: The Canaanite king of Arad
note: Arad (melekh 'arad) is the city the king ruled (cf. Num 21:1), not the king's personal name.

kjv: all their pictures
mine: all their carved figures
note: Hebrew maskiyyot denotes carved or figured stones (cultic images), not paintings as modern "pictures" suggests.

kjv: ye shall dispossess [the inhabitants] of the land
mine: You shall take possession of the land
note: Hiphil horashtem with "the land" as object means take possession of it; the KJV supplies "the inhabitants" to carry over the "drive out" sense of v.52.

kjv: with the coasts thereof
mine: with its borders
note: Hebrew gevulot means boundaries/territory; "coasts" in 1611 meant borders, not seashores, which misleads a modern reader in this inland boundary list (also vv.3, 11, 12).

kjv: unto the river of Egypt
mine: to the Wadi of Egypt
note: Hebrew nachal mitsrayim is a seasonal watercourse (usually identified with Wadi el-Arish), not the Nile, which "river of Egypt" suggests.

kjv: unto the entrance of Hamath
mine: to Lebo-hamath
note: Hebrew levo' hamat may be "the approach to Hamath" or the town name Lebo(-hamath); the latter is now widely preferred since it sits in a list of place names.

kjv: on this side Jordan
mine: beyond the Jordan
note: Hebrew me'ever le-yarden literally "from beyond the Jordan", here the east bank; the KJV renders from the speaker's Transjordan standpoint, which obscures the term.

kjv: suburbs for the cities
mine: pasturelands around the towns
note: Hebrew migrash is open grazing land around a town (v.3: "for their cattle"); "suburbs" now suggests residential districts (also vv.3-7).

kjv: with throwing a stone
mine: with a stone in the hand
note: Hebrew be'even yad is "a hand-stone", a stone held or wielded in the hand (parallel to the wooden "hand" object in v.18), not specifically a thrown one.

kjv: ye shall take no satisfaction
mine: You shall accept no ransom
note: Hebrew kofer is a ransom or payment in exchange for a life; "satisfaction" in this sense is obsolete outside theology (also v.32).

kjv: on this side Jordan
mine: beyond the Jordan
note: Hebrew be'ever ha-yarden literally "across the Jordan", a fixed term for the east bank where Moses speaks; the KJV renders it from the speaker's location (also v.5), which hides the narrator's west-bank standpoint.

kjv: over against the Red [sea]
mine: opposite Suph
note: Hebrew has only mol suf, "opposite Suph", probably a place name; the KJV supplies "sea" (in italics) to identify it with the yam suf.

kjv: which dwelt at Astaroth in Edrei
mine: who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei
note: Og lived in Ashtaroth and was defeated at Edrei (Num 21:33); the KJV reads Ashtaroth as located "in" Edrei.

kjv: ye were ready to go up
mine: thought it easy to go up
note: The rare verb vattahinu (hapax, from hun) is now generally taken as "you regarded it as easy / acted rashly", not simply "were ready".

kjv: Ye shall buy meat of them (the descendants of Esau)
mine: You shall buy food from them (the descendants of Esau)
note: Hebrew 'okhel is food in general; "meat" now means animal flesh only (also v.28).

kjv: Which also were accounted giants
mine: they (the Emim) too are counted as Rephaim
note: Hebrew repha'im is the name of an ancient population group (cf. Gen 14:5), here a category the Emim belong to; the KJV translates it as "giants", turning an ethnic name into a description.

kjv: Now rise up, [said I]
mine: 'Now rise up
note: Hebrew has no verb of saying; in context the command continues Yahweh's speech (cf. v.24), but the KJV supplies "said I", making Moses the speaker.

kjv: a land of giants: giants dwelt therein
mine: a land of Rephaim. Rephaim formerly lived there
note: Again repha'im, a people name (Ammonite "Zamzummim"), rendered "giants" by the KJV.

kjv: which dwelt in Hazerim
mine: who lived in villages
note: Hebrew chatserim is the common noun "unwalled settlements, villages"; the KJV treats it as a place name.

kjv: of the remnant of giants
mine: of the remnant of the Rephaim
note: Hebrew ha-repha'im is the name of an ancient people (cf. 2:11, 20); the KJV renders it "giants".

kjv: which was called the land of giants
mine: All that Bashan is called the land of Rephaim
note: Again 'erets repha'im, "land of the Rephaim"; the Hebrew also has a present "is called" (yiqqare'), a parenthetical note by the narrator.

kjv: Bashan-havoth-jair
mine: Havvoth-jair, as Bashan is called
note: The Hebrew places "the Bashan" as the object renamed (vayyiqra' otam ... et-ha-bashan chavvot ya'ir); the KJV fuses it into a compound place name.

kjv: half the valley, and the border
mine: with the middle of the wadi as a boundary
note: Hebrew tokh ha-nachal u-gevul means "the middle of the wadi and (as) border", i.e. the boundary ran down the riverbed; "half the valley" misreads tokh.

kjv: under Ashdoth-pisgah
mine: under the slopes of Pisgah
note: Hebrew 'ashdot is a common noun "slopes, mountain-sides" (cf. Josh 10:40); the KJV transliterates it as part of a place name.

kjv: what the LORD did because of Baal-peor
mine: what Yahweh did at Baal-peor
note: Hebrew be-ba'al pe'or can mean "at (the place) Baal-peor" or "in the matter of (the god) Baal of Peor"; the KJV takes the causal sense.

kjv: who [hath] God [so] nigh unto them
mine: that has a god so near to it
note: Hebrew 'elohim qerovim, with a plural adjective, refers to any nation's god(s) in comparison with Yahweh; the KJV's capitalised "God" blurs the comparison.

kjv: if thou turn to the LORD thy God
mine: you will return to Yahweh your God
note: The Hebrew perfects with waw (ve-shavta, ve-shama'ta; cf. u-viqqashtem in v.29) read most naturally as a prediction that Israel will return in the latter days; the KJV turns vv.29-30 into conditions ("if thou shalt seek ... if thou turn"). Context: you will return (prediction) (high confidence). The waw-perfects ve-shavta, ve-shama'ta continue the future of 4:29 ('you will seek ... you will find'), and 30:1-3 predicts the same return in exile. LXX reads a future. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS all render a prediction. Other possible meanings: (1) a condition, 'if you turn to Yahweh your God and obey his voice' — KJV, Geneva; a waw-perfect after a temporal clause can carry conditional force; (2) an exhortation, 'then return to Yahweh your God' — some commentators.

kjv: hath God assayed
mine: has any god ever tried
note: Hebrew ha-nissah 'elohim in this rhetorical comparison means "has any god attempted"; KJV "God" suggests the true God.

kjv: by temptations
mine: by trials
note: Hebrew massot means tests or trials (the plagues as ordeals), not enticements to sin as "temptations" now implies.

kjv: brought thee out in his (Yahweh's) sight
mine: he (Yahweh) Himself brought you out
note: Hebrew be-fanav, "with his presence/face", means Yahweh brought them out personally, not merely while watching.

kjv: prolong [thy] days upon the earth
mine: prolong your days in the land
note: Hebrew ha-'adamah here is the specific land Yahweh is giving Israel, not the earth at large.

kjv: under the springs of Pisgah
mine: under the slopes of Pisgah
note: Hebrew 'ashdot means slopes or mountain-sides, not springs (cf. 3:17, where the KJV transliterates it).

kjv: take the name of the LORD thy God in vain
mine: take up the name of Yahweh your God for falsehood
note: Hebrew nasa' ... la-shav' means to lift up/use the name for emptiness or falsehood (esp. false oaths, cf. shav' in v.20); "in vain" narrows it in modern ears to casual or profane speech.

kjv: Thou shalt not kill
mine: You shall not murder
note: Hebrew ratsach denotes unlawful, especially intentional homicide (it is the term for the "murderer" in Num 35); the law itself prescribes capital punishment and war, so "kill" is too broad.

kjv: The LORD our God [is] one LORD
mine: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one
note: The verbless Hebrew YHWH 'eloheinu YHWH 'echad can be parsed several ways: "Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one" (unity) or "Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone" (exclusive loyalty, fitting the following call to undivided love); the KJV takes the oneness reading. Context: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one (parsing left open) (medium confidence). A verbless clause. 'Echad normally means 'one' ('alone' is usually levad), and LXX kyrios heis estin and Mark 12:29-32 read 'one'. Leaving the first half verbless, as ESV, NIV and CSB do, keeps open both 'Yahweh our God is one Yahweh' and 'Yahweh is our God, Yahweh is one/alone'; 6:5 and 6:14-15 stress exclusive loyalty. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Yahweh is our God, Yahweh alone' — NRSV/NRSVue, NJPS, many commentators ('echad as 'only', cf. 1 Chr 29:1; Zech 14:9); (2) 'Yahweh our God is one Yahweh' — LXX, Mark 12:29, KJV, ESV/NIV notes; (3) 'Yahweh is our God; Yahweh is one', two clauses stressing his unity — NASB, NET.

kjv: Ye shall not tempt the LORD your God
mine: You shall not put Yahweh your God to the test
note: Hebrew nissah means to test or try someone (cf. massah, "testing"); "tempt" now suggests enticing to sin.

kjv: cut down their groves
mine: cut down their Asherah poles
note: Hebrew 'asherim are wooden cult objects (poles or stylised trees) associated with the goddess Asherah, not groves of trees.

kjv: break down their images
mine: smash their standing stones
note: Hebrew matstsevot are upright standing stones (cultic pillars), not images or statues; the carved images (pesilim) are listed separately.

kjv: a special people unto himself
mine: a people for His treasured possession
note: Hebrew 'am segullah means a people that is his personal treasure; "special" has lost the sense of private property.

kjv: thy corn
mine: your grain
note: Hebrew dagan is cereal grain generally (wheat, barley); "corn" now suggests maize to many readers.

kjv: The great temptations
mine: the great trials
note: Hebrew massot, the testing ordeals of the plagues (cf. 4:34); "temptations" now implies enticement to sin.

kjv: shall destroy them (the nations) with a mighty destruction
mine: throw them (the nations) into great confusion
note: Hebrew hamam ... mehumah gedolah means to throw into great panic or confusion (the divine terror of holy war); the destruction follows ("until they are destroyed").

kjv: lest thou be a cursed thing like it (the abomination)
mine: or you will become devoted to destruction like it (the abomination)
note: Hebrew cherem is something set apart for God by destruction (the "ban", cf. v.2 hacharem tacharim); "cursed thing" loses the link with the herem command.

kjv: by every [word] that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD
mine: by everything that comes out of the mouth of Yahweh
note: Hebrew kol motsa' pi-YHWH, "all that goes out of Yahweh's mouth", has no noun "word"; in context it includes the manna God decreed. The KJV supplies "word" (as Matt 4:4 does with rhema).

kjv: thou mayest dig brass
mine: you can dig copper
note: Hebrew nechoshet here is ore mined from the hills, i.e. copper; brass is a zinc alloy that is not mined.

kjv: as I (Moses) fell down [at the first]
mine: that I (Moses) lay there
note: Hebrew 'asher hitnappalti simply resumes "the forty days and forty nights that I lay prostrate" (the period of v.18); the KJV's supplied "at the first" suggests a further, separate prostration.

kjv: the ten commandments
mine: the Ten Words
note: Hebrew 'aseret haddevarim means "the ten words/sayings"; "commandments" is an interpretive gloss.

kjv: a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward
mine: awesome God, Who shows no partiality and takes no bribe
note: nora' means awe-inspiring; shochad means a bribe; "reward" now sounds positive.

kjv: which dwell in the champaign over against Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh
mine: who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oak of Moreh
note: ha'aravah is the Jordan rift valley, and 'elonei moreh is the oak (terebinth) of Moreh (cf. Gen 12:6). The KJV's "plains" again follows the Targum.

kjv: burn their groves with fire
mine: burn their Asherim with fire
note: 'asherim are cult poles of the goddess Asherah. This is the KJV's standard "grove" rendering (cf. Judg 6:25).

kjv: whatsoever thy soul lusteth after
mine: as much as you desire
note: bekhol 'awwat nafshekha means "whenever you desire (meat)". "Lust" now has a sexual sense. Same in vv. 20-21.

kjv: the children of Belial
mine: certain worthless men
note: benei-veliyya'al means "sons of worthlessness", a Hebrew idiom for scoundrels. The KJV treats "Belial" as a proper name, which later became a name for Satan (2 Cor 6:15). KJV 13:13.

kjv: a peculiar people unto himself
mine: His treasured people
note: Hebrew 'am segullah means a people that is a prized personal possession; "peculiar" in 1611 meant "one's own", not "odd".

kjv: the fallow deer ... the pygarg, and the wild ox, and the chamois
mine: the roebuck ... the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep
note: The game animals yachmur, dishon, te'o and zemer are uncertain, but "pygarg" (white-rumped antelope, from the Greek) and "chamois" (an Alpine animal absent from Palestine) are guesses; modern identifications favour ibex/antelope/wild sheep, and te'o is an antelope or oryx rather than a wild ox.

kjv: the coney
mine: the rock badger
note: Hebrew shaphan is the rock hyrax; "coney" now suggests a rabbit.

kjv: the ossifrage, and the ospray
mine: the bearded vulture, the black vulture
note: Hebrew peres ("breaker", the bone-breaking lammergeier) and 'ozniyyah are large vultures; "osprey" is a fish hawk.

kjv: the glede, and the kite, and the vulture
mine: the red kite, the falcon, and the kite
note: The birds ra'ah, 'ayyah and dayyah are all raptors of the kite/falcon group; the KJV's "vulture" for dayyah is a guess, and "glede" is an obsolete word for the kite.

kjv: the owl ... the cuckow
mine: the ostrich ... the seagull
note: Hebrew bat haya'anah is the ostrich, and shachaf is probably a gull; "cuckoo" has no basis.

kjv: the swan
mine: the barn owl
note: Hebrew tinshemet appears among owls and is probably the barn owl; "swan" follows a guess.

kjv: the pelican, and the gier eagle
mine: the desert owl, the carrion vulture
note: Hebrew qa'at is a desert-dwelling bird (Ps 102:6), likely an owl, and rachamah is the Egyptian (carrion) vulture.

kjv: the lapwing
mine: the hoopoe
note: Hebrew dukhiphat is the hoopoe, as ancient versions and modern lexicons agree.

kjv: every creeping thing that flieth
mine: every winged swarming creature
note: Hebrew sherets ha'oph means winged insects (swarming things); "creeping" now suggests crawling animals, not flying insects.

kjv: [or] if the place be too far from thee
mine: because the place ... is too far from you
note: The second clause is introduced by ki ("because/when"), explaining why the journey is too long, not giving an alternative condition; the KJV's supplied "or" makes it a separate case.

kjv: Save when there shall be no poor among you
mine: There will, however, be no poor among you
note: Hebrew 'ephes ki here introduces a strong assertion ("but indeed / nevertheless") that there will be no poor if Israel obeys; the KJV's "save when" turns it into a restriction on the release law, which then sits awkwardly with v. 11.

kjv: a thought in thy wicked heart
mine: no base thought in your heart
note: The adjective beliyya'al ("worthless, base") goes with davar ("thing, thought"), not with "heart": the warning is against a mean-spirited calculation, not a description of the heart itself.

kjv: thy servant for ever
mine: your slave for life
note: Hebrew 'eved 'olam here means a permanent slave for the rest of his life; "for ever" is literal for 'olam but the sense is lifelong.

kjv: in all thy coast
mine: in all your territory
note: Hebrew gevul means border or territory; "coast" in 1611 meant a border region, but now suggests the seashore.

kjv: thou shalt roast and eat [it] (the Passover)
mine: You shall cook it (the Passover) and eat it
note: Hebrew bishshal normally means "boil, cook"; the KJV's "roast" harmonises with Exod 12:9, which forbids boiling the Passover lamb (cf. 2 Chr 35:13, "cooked with fire").

kjv: neither take a gift: for a gift doth blind
mine: you must not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds
note: Hebrew shochad is specifically a bribe given to sway judgment, not an ordinary gift.

kjv: a grove of any trees
mine: an Asherah, any kind of tree
note: Hebrew 'asherah is a wooden cult pole or tree representing the goddess Asherah; the KJV, following the Septuagint's alsos, renders it "grove".

kjv: [any] image
mine: a sacred pillar
note: Hebrew matstsevah is a standing stone used in worship, not a carved image.

kjv: Thou shalt in any wise set [him] king over thee
mine: you may indeed set over yourself a king
note: The emphatic infinitive som tasim follows Israel's own request (v. 14); it can be read as a command, but in context most interpreters take it as permission with conditions, which bears on the long debate over whether monarchy was divinely mandated.

kjv: The priests the Levites, [and] all the tribe of Levi
mine: The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi
note: The Hebrew has no "and": kol-shevet levi stands in apposition to hakkohanim halewiyyim, so Deuteronomy treats the whole tribe as potential priests; the KJV's supplied "and" distinguishes two groups, reflecting the later priest/Levite division.

kjv: an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch
mine: a soothsayer, an interpreter of omens, or a sorcerer
note: Hebrew me'onen is a soothsayer (practice uncertain, not specifically time-reckoning), menachesh one who reads omens, and mekhashshef a male sorcerer; the KJV terms carry later European associations.

kjv: a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer
mine: one who consults a ghost or a familiar spirit, or one who inquires of the dead
note: Hebrew sho'el 'ov weyidde'oni is one person who consults the 'ov (ghost/spirit of the dead) and the yidde'oni ("knowing one", a spirit); "wizard" takes yidde'oni as a separate practitioner.

kjv: Thou shalt be perfect
mine: You shall be blameless
note: Hebrew tamim means whole, wholehearted, with integrity; "perfect" now suggests flawlessness.

kjv: a Prophet
mine: a prophet
note: Hebrew navi' is indefinite and in context (vv. 9-22, contrasting diviners with true prophets) may refer to a succession of prophets; the KJV's capital letter signals the individual, messianic reading taken up in Acts 3:22 and 7:37.

kjv: killeth his neighbour ignorantly
mine: strikes his neighbor without intent
note: Hebrew bivli-da'at means "unintentionally, without premeditation"; "ignorantly" now suggests stupidity or lack of knowledge of the law.

kjv: shall be tributaries unto thee
mine: shall become forced laborers for you
note: Hebrew mas denotes corvée, forced labour (as under Solomon, 1 Kgs 9:21), not the payment of tribute.

kjv: (for the tree of the field [is] man's [life]) to employ [them] in the siege
mine: Is the tree of the field a human being, that it should be besieged by you?
note: Hebrew ki ha'adam 'ets hassadeh lavo' mippaneykha bammatsor is terse; most modern readers take it (with the Septuagint) as a rhetorical question, "is the tree a man, to come into siege before you?", whereas the KJV, following the Masoretic pointing as a statement, supplies "life" and "employ them" to make the trees man's sustenance.

kjv: a rough valley, which is neither eared nor sown
mine: a wadi with a perennial stream, in a place that is neither plowed nor sown
note: Hebrew nachal 'etan is a valley with an ever-flowing stream ('etan = "perennial, enduring"); "rough" is a guess, and "eared" (= ploughed) is obsolete.

kjv: thou shalt not make merchandise of her
mine: you must not treat her as a slave
note: The rare verb hit'ammer (also 24:7) means to treat someone as a chattel or deal with them violently; it is not limited to trading her.

kjv: one beloved, and another hated
mine: one loved and the other unloved
note: Hebrew senu'ah ("hated") is a legal term for the less-favoured wife (cf. Gen 29:31); "hated" overstates the emotional sense in modern English.

kjv: that which pertaineth unto a man
mine: a man's gear
note: Hebrew keli-gever means a man's article or equipment (keli is used of tools and weapons), not simply clothing; the KJV's general phrase leaves the scope open, while many read it as male gear such as weapons.

kjv: be defiled
mine: will be forfeited
note: Hebrew tiqdash means "become holy", i.e. the mixed crop is forfeited to the sanctuary; the problem is that it becomes consecrated, not that it becomes impure.

kjv: they (the elders) shall amerce him (the husband) in an hundred [shekels]
mine: they (the elders) shall fine him (the husband) a hundred shekels
note: Hebrew 'anash means to impose a fine; "amerce" is obsolete.

kjv: she hath wrought folly in Israel
mine: she has done an outrageous thing in Israel
note: Hebrew nevalah is a disgraceful, scandalous act (often sexual) that violates the community; "folly" now suggests mere foolishness.

kjv: A bastard
mine: No one born of a forbidden union
note: Hebrew mamzer (only here and Zech 9:6) is of uncertain meaning; Jewish tradition takes it as the offspring of incest or adultery, not simply a child born out of wedlock as "bastard" implies. (Hebrew 23:3 = KJV 23:2.) Context: one born of a forbidden union (medium confidence). Mamzer occurs only here and Zech 9:6. Rabbinic law (m. Yevamot 4:13) takes it as the child of incest or adultery; the LXX has 'son of a harlot'. 'Forbidden union' (ESV; NIV, NRSV similar) covers these without the English sense of any child born out of wedlock. The precise reference stays uncertain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'child of a prostitute' — LXX ek pornes, Vulgate de scorto natus; (2) 'bastard', a child born outside marriage — KJV, NASB 'of illegitimate birth'; (3) a person of mixed or foreign descent — some commentators from Zech 9:6 and the following ban on Ammonites and Moabites; NJPS 'misbegotten' leaves it open.

kjv: a paddle upon thy weapon
mine: a digging tool among your equipment
note: Hebrew 'azen is a hapax usually taken as "equipment, gear" (related to zayin "weapon" only by guess); yated is a peg or digging stick. (Hebrew 23:14 = KJV 23:13.)

kjv: no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite
mine: None of the daughters of Israel shall be a cult prostitute ... a cult prostitute
note: Hebrew qedeshah and qadesh ("consecrated one") denote persons attached to a shrine for sexual rites; the KJV's "whore" and "sodomite" lose the cultic sense, and v. 19 then uses the ordinary word zonah for a prostitute. (Hebrew 23:18 = KJV 23:17.)

kjv: lend upon usury
mine: charge interest
note: Hebrew neshekh means any interest on a loan; "usury" in modern English means excessive interest, which wrongly narrows the prohibition. (Hebrew 23:20-21 = KJV 23:19-20.)

kjv: then let him write her a bill of divorcement
mine: and he writes her a certificate of divorce
note: Verses 1-3 are a single chain of "if" clauses (ki ... wekhatav ... weshillechah) describing the case, and the only command is in v. 4 (no remarriage to the first husband); the KJV makes v. 1 an instruction to divorce, the reading the Pharisees press in Matt 19:7 ("Moses commanded").

kjv: some uncleanness in her
mine: something indecent in her
note: Hebrew 'erwat davar ("nakedness of a thing") is vague and was famously debated (Hillel vs. Shammai); it suggests something shameful or improper, not ritual uncleanness.

kjv: she may go and be another man's [wife]
mine: and goes and becomes another man's wife
note: The verbs continue the protasis; the KJV's "may" turns a description into a permission.

kjv: maketh merchandise of him
mine: treats him as a slave
note: Hebrew hit'ammer (as in 21:14) means to treat as a chattel, exploit; selling is mentioned separately.

kjv: the plague of leprosy
mine: a case of a skin disease
note: Hebrew tsara'at covers a range of skin conditions (and mould on fabric and walls), not Hansen's disease specifically.

kjv: and have no child
mine: and has no son
note: Hebrew uven 'eyn-lo is literally "and he has no son"; the KJV (with the Septuagint sperma) widens it to any child, a reading later reflected in Matt 22:24 and rabbinic law.

kjv: A Syrian ready to perish [was] my father
mine: My father was a wandering Aramean
note: Hebrew 'arammi 'oved 'avi: 'oved can mean "perishing" or "straying, wandering" (of lost sheep), and the context (going down to Egypt as a sojourner) favours a homeless wanderer, i.e. Jacob; "Syrian" is an anachronistic label for Aram. Context: wandering (medium confidence). 'Oved means 'perishing, lost, straying' (of strayed animals, Deut 22:3; Jer 50:6). With 'he went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner' it describes Jacob as a homeless, endangered migrant. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and CSB read 'wandering', NJPS 'fugitive'; 'wandering' loses some of the sense of danger. Other possible meanings: (1) 'ready to perish' or 'starving' — KJV, several lexicons and medieval commentators (Ibn Ezra); (2) 'an Aramean (Laban) sought to destroy my father', reading 'oved as causative — Targum Onqelos, the Passover Haggadah, Rashi, Vulgate (persequebatur); (3) 'fugitive' — NJPS.

kjv: neither have I taken away [ought] thereof (the holy portion) for [any] unclean [use]
mine: nor removed any of it (the holy portion) while unclean
note: Hebrew bitame' most naturally means "in a state of uncleanness" (parallel to be'oni, "in my mourning"); the KJV's supplied "use" shifts the uncleanness from the offerer to the purpose.

kjv: Thou (Israel) hast avouched the LORD this day
mine: You (Israel) have declared today that Yahweh is your God
note: Hebrew he'emarta (a rare hiphil of 'amar) means "you have caused to say / declared, affirmed" in a covenant exchange; "avouched" is obsolete.

kjv: he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person
mine: anyone who takes a bribe to strike down an innocent person
note: Hebrew shochad is a bribe; "reward" obscures the corrupt payment.

kjv: confirmeth not [all] the words of this law
mine: does not uphold the words of this law
note: The Masoretic text has no "all"; the KJV supplies it in italics, matching the Septuagint (en pasin tois logois) and Paul's quotation in Gal 3:10.

kjv: thy basket and thy store
mine: your basket and your kneading bowl
note: mish'eret is the kneading trough (Exod 12:34), not a store. Same in v. 17.

kjv: and with the sword
mine: and drought
note: The MT vowels read bacherev "sword". In a list of crop and body afflictions, I repointed it as choreb "drought" (same consonants). The KJV follows the MT here.

kjv: shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth
mine: you (Israel) will be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth
note: za'avah (qere) means terror or horror (cf. Jer 15:4). The KJV took it from zua' "to move".

kjv: the botch of Egypt, and with the emerods
mine: the boils of Egypt, with tumors
note: 'ofalim (qere techorim) are tumours or haemorrhoids. "Emerods" and "botch" are obsolete English.

kjv: toward her (the tender and refined woman's) young one that cometh out from between her feet
mine: her (the tender and refined woman's) afterbirth that comes out from between her feet
note: shilyatah is the afterbirth (placenta). The children are mentioned separately in the same verse, so "young one" misreads the horror of the siege.

kjv: to add drunkenness to thirst
mine: This will lead to the sweeping away of moist and dry alike
note: lema'an sefot harawah 'et-hatsme'ah ("to sweep away the watered with the thirsty") is an obscure merism, probably meaning total destruction. The KJV takes it as a proverb about indulgence. KJV 29:19.

kjv: the LORD thy God will turn thy captivity
mine: Yahweh your God will restore your fortunes
note: shav 'et-shevutekha is an idiom for "restore the fortunes". The KJV derived shevut from shavah "take captive". The idiom is also used where there is no captivity (Job 42:10).

kjv: it (this commandment) is not hidden from thee
mine: is not too hard for you
note: lo'-nifle'th hi' mimmekha means "it is not too wonderful/difficult for you", not "hidden".

kjv: for I (Yahweh) know their (Israel's) imagination which they go about
mine: For I (Yahweh) know what they (Israel) are inclined to do
note: yitsro is their inclination or disposition (cf. Gen 6:5; 8:21). "Imagination" is a literal but now misleading gloss.

kjv: their (Israel's) spot is not the spot of his (Yahweh's) children
mine: they (Israel) are no longer His (Yahweh's) children because of their blemish
note: shichet lo lo' banav mumam is one of the most corrupt lines in the Hebrew Bible. Every rendering reconstructs it; the KJV supplies words in italics.

kjv: he (Yahweh) led him (Jacob) about, he instructed him
mine: he (Yahweh) encircled him (Jacob), He cared for him
note: yesovevenhu means "surrounded/shielded him" and yevonenehu means "watched over him". "Instructed" over-reads binah.

kjv: with the fat of kidneys of wheat
mine: with the very finest of the wheat
note: chelev kilyot chittah is an idiom ("kidney-fat of wheat") for the choicest grain. The KJV renders it literally.

kjv: They (Israel) sacrificed unto devils, not to God
mine: They (Israel) sacrificed to demons that were no gods
note: shedim are demons or spirits. lo' 'eloah means "not-god", not a contrast with the true God.

kjv: devoured with burning heat, and with bitter destruction
mine: devoured by plague and poisonous pestilence
note: reshef and qetev may be pestilence demons (cf. the Canaanite god Resheph), not "burning heat".

kjv: lest their (Israel's) adversaries should behave themselves strangely
mine: lest their (Israel's) adversaries should misunderstand
note: yenakkeru means "misconstrue, misread" what happened, not "act strangely".

kjv: the LORD shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants
mine: Yahweh will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants
note: yadin here means "vindicate" (parallel to having compassion), not condemn. yitnecham means "relent / have compassion".

kjv: from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy
mine: from the long-haired heads of the enemy
note: mero'sh par'ot 'oyev: par'ot is probably "long locks" (of warriors; cf. Judg 5:2), not "revenges".

kjv: Rejoice, O ye nations, with his (Yahweh's) people
mine: Rejoice, O nations, with His (Yahweh's) people
note: Both follow the short Masoretic text. The Dead Sea Scrolls (4QDeut-q) and the Septuagint have a longer verse that includes "let all the sons of God worship him", which is quoted in Hebrews 1:6. Similarly, at v. 8 the scrolls read "sons of God" where the MT has "sons of Israel".

kjv: he (Yahweh) came with ten thousands of saints
mine: came from the myriads of holy ones
note: Hebrew ve'atah merivevot qodesh has the preposition min "from"; KJV renders it "with", making the holy ones his escort rather than his point of departure (some emend to a place name, Meribath-kadesh).

kjv: they (the holy ones) sat down at thy feet
mine: they (the holy ones) bow down at Your feet
note: The verb tukku (from takah?) is a hapax of uncertain meaning; "sat down" and "bow/follow" are both guesses.

kjv: and let [not] his (Reuben's) men be few
mine: though his (Reuben's) men be few
note: Hebrew vihi metav mispar says only "and let his men be a number" (i.e. countable, few); the KJV supplies "not" in italics, reversing the clause into a wish for many.

kjv: let his (Judah's) hands be sufficient for him
mine: with his (Judah's) hands he contends for himself
note: Yadav rav lo: rav may be from riv "contend" or rabab "be much/enough"; both readings are defensible.

kjv: the horns of unicorns
mine: the horns of a wild ox
note: Re'em is the aurochs/wild ox; "unicorn" came from the Septuagint monokeros.

kjv: [Let] Asher [be] blessed with children
mine: Most blessed of sons is Asher
note: Barukh mibbanim most naturally means "blessed above (other) sons"; KJV takes min as "with/by" children.

kjv: Thy (Asher's) shoes [shall be] iron and brass
mine: Your (Asher's) bolts will be iron and bronze
note: Min'al is a bar or bolt of a gate (cf. na'al "lock"), not a shoe (na'al); nechoshet is bronze/copper.

kjv: none like unto the God of Jeshurun
mine: none like God, O Jeshurun
note: MT ka'el yeshurun is vocalized as an absolute noun followed by a vocative; KJV reads it as a construct "God of Jeshurun".

kjv: thine (Israel's) enemies shall be found liars unto thee
mine: Your (Israel's) enemies will cringe before you
note: Niphal of kachash here means to feign submission, come cringing; "found liars" is an over-literal sense of the root "deceive".

kjv: very far from the city Adam
mine: very far away, at Adam, the city
note: The ketiv reads be'adam "at Adam", the qere me'adam "from Adam"; KJV follows the qere, which places the heap at an unspecified distance from Adam, while the ketiv locates it at Adam itself.

kjv: until we (the Israelites) were passed over
mine: until they (the Israelites) had crossed over
note: The ketiv is 'ovrenu "we crossed", the qere 'ovram "they crossed"; KJV follows the ketiv (as if the narrator were an eyewitness), I follow the qere.

kjv: sharp knives
mine: flint knives
note: Charvot tsurim are knives of flint (tsur "rock, flint"), a detail of the archaic rite that "sharp" obscures.

kjv: the hill of the foreskins
mine: Gibeath-haaraloth
note: Giv'at ha-'aralot is treated as a place name; KJV translates it, which is accurate in sense.

kjv: the old corn of the land
mine: the produce of the land
note: 'Avur (only here and v.12) means produce or yield of the land; "old corn" is a guess from the context of eating before the new harvest, and "corn" now suggests maize.

kjv: the city shall be accursed ... to the LORD
mine: shall be devoted to Yahweh for destruction
note: Cherem is the ban: something irrevocably given over to God, usually by destruction; "accursed" suggests a curse or magical taint rather than a dedication to Yahweh (same issue with "accursed thing" in 6:18 and ch. 7).

kjv: lest ye (Israel) make [yourselves] accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing
mine: lest you (Israel) devote them to destruction and then take some of the devoted things
note: Pen-tacharimu "lest you put under the ban" has no reflexive object; KJV supplies "yourselves", whereas the sense is devoting the city and then taking from it (the Septuagint reads "lest you covet", tachmedu).

kjv: he (the man who rebuilds Jericho) shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn
mine: At the cost of his firstborn he (the man who rebuilds Jericho) shall lay its foundation
note: The preposition be- here is the beth of price: the builder will lose his eldest and youngest sons (fulfilled in 1 Kgs 16:34); KJV's literal "in" obscures this.

kjv: he (the one taken with the devoted things) hath wrought folly in Israel
mine: has done an outrageous thing in Israel
note: Nevalah denotes a disgraceful, sacrilegious outrage against the community, not mere foolishness as "folly" now suggests.

kjv: burned them (Achan and all he had) with fire, after they (all Israel) had stoned them with stones
mine: they (all Israel) burned them (Achan and all he had) with fire and stoned them with stones
note: The Hebrew simply has two coordinate clauses (vayyisrefu ... vayyisqelu); KJV turns the second into a prior action ("after"), imposing a sequence the text does not state.

kjv: at a time appointed
mine: at the appointed place
note: Lammo'ed can mean an appointed time or an appointed place; the following "facing the Arabah" suggests a location (some emend to lammorad "to the descent").

kjv: Stretch out the spear
mine: Stretch out the javelin
note: Kidon is a short throwing spear or javelin (or possibly a curved sword), distinct from the long spear chanit.

kjv: the strangers that were conversant among them (Israel)
mine: the sojourners who lived among them (Israel)
note: Hahalekh beqirbam is "who walked/lived among them"; "conversant" in 1611 meant dwelling or associating, not knowledgeable.

kjv: wine bottles, old, and rent, and bound up
mine: wineskins that were worn out, split, and patched up
note: No'dot are leather skins, which split and are patched; "bottles" now suggests glass.

kjv: dry [and] mouldy
mine: dry and crumbled
note: Niqqudim (also v.12) means crumbs or crumbly bits (possibly "spotted"); "mouldy" is one guess, "crumbled" fits dry bread better.

kjv: Let them (the Gibeonites) live; but let them be hewers of wood
mine: Let them (the Gibeonites) live. So they became woodcutters
note: Vayyihyu is a narrative "and they became", reporting the outcome; KJV folds it into the leaders' speech as a command.

kjv: the book of Jasher
mine: the Book of Jashar
