note: Sefer hayyashar means "the Book of the Upright (One)"; KJV's "Jasher" transliterates it as if a personal name.

kjv: and of the springs
mine: and the slopes
note: Ha'ashedot are the slopes or foothills (from 'eshed "slope, foot of a mountain", cf. Ashdoth-pisgah), a geographic zone, not springs.

kjv: the kings that [were] on the north of the mountains
mine: the kings who were in the north, in the hill country
note: Mitsafon bahar lists regions: "from the north, in the hill country", not a location north of the mountains.

kjv: thou (Joshua) shalt hough their (the enemy kings') horses
mine: You (Joshua) shall hamstring their (the enemy kings') horses
note: 'Iqqer is to cut the hamstring tendons, crippling the horses; "hough" is an obsolete word for this that few readers now know.

kjv: the cities that stood still in their strength
mine: the cities that stood on their mounds
note: 'Al-tillam means "on their tell", the mound of earlier occupation layers on which a city stood; KJV takes tel as "strength", missing the archaeological sense.

kjv: of the remnant of the giants
mine: one of the remnant of the Rephaim
note: Refa'im is the name of an ancient population (also used of the shades of the dead); "giants" follows the Septuagint/Vulgate gloss and loses the proper name.

kjv: and in the springs
mine: in the slopes
note: Ha'ashedot are the slopes or foothills, a geographic zone (as in 10:40), not springs.

kjv: the king of the nations of Gilgal
mine: the king of Goiim in Gilgal
note: Goyim is here a place name (cf. Gen 14:1 "Tidal king of Goiim"); KJV translates it "nations". The Septuagint reads "Galilee" for Gilgal.

kjv: unto the entering into Hamath
mine: to Lebo-hamath
note: Levo' chamat is best taken as the town name Lebo (modern Lebweh) "of Hamath"; KJV renders it "the entrance of Hamath".

kjv: With whom the Reubenites and the Gadites have received
mine: With the other half of Manasseh the Reubenites and the Gadites received
note: 'Immo "with it/him" must refer to the eastern half of Manasseh (the text appears to have lost words by haplography); KJV's "with whom" links it grammatically to the western half-tribe just named, which received no land east of the Jordan.

kjv: with their suburbs for their (the Levites') cattle
mine: with their pasturelands for their (the Levites') livestock
note: migrash means the open pasture land around a town; "suburbs" now suggests residential outskirts.

kjv: a great man among the Anakims
mine: the greatest man among the Anakim
note: ha'adam haggadol ba'anaqim is superlative by context (the eponymous founder of the Anakim).

kjv: unto the river of Egypt
mine: to the Brook of Egypt
note: nachal mitsrayim is the seasonal Wadi el-Arish, not the Nile (cf. v. 4; 2 Kgs 24:7).

kjv: thou (Caleb) hast given me (Achsah) a south land
mine: you (Caleb) have given me (Achsah) the land of the Negev
note: 'erets hannegev is the named dry region south of Judah. "South land" obscures that Achsah is complaining it has no water.

kjv: serve under tribute
mine: have been made to do forced labor
note: lemas-'oved means conscripted labour (corvée), not paying taxes.

kjv: even three countries
mine: the third is Naphath
note: sheloshet hannafet is obscure. It may be "the three heights", or refer to Naphath(-dor), the third-listed town (cf. 11:2; 12:23).

kjv: the land of the Perizzites and of the giants
mine: the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim
note: repha'im are a named ancient people (cf. Deut 2:11, 20), also associated with the dead. The KJV's "giants" follows the Septuagint and Vulgate tradition.

kjv: How long are ye (the people of Israel) slack to go to possess the land
mine: How long will you (the people of Israel) put off going in to take possession of the land
note: mitrappim means "slackening, delaying". "Slack" is archaic but close.

kjv: Beer-sheba, or Sheba
mine: Beersheba, Sheba
note: Hebrew has simply wesheba "and Sheba"; the KJV reads it as an alternative name for Beersheba to fit the total of thirteen cities in v.6 (LXX reads Shema, cf. 15:26).

kjv: Remmon-methoar to Neah
mine: Rimmon, curving toward Neah
note: Hammeto'ar is a participle "that bends/is marked out" describing the boundary's course to Neah; the KJV makes it part of a compound place name.

kjv: Hebron
mine: Ebron
note: The Hebrew is Ebron ('Evron, with ayin), a town in Asher, not the Judean Hebron (Chevron); the KJV spelling confuses the two (many MSS read Abdon, cf. 21:30).

kjv: from Allon to Zaanannim, and Adami, Nekeb
mine: from the oak at Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb
note: Me'elon betsa'anannim is "from the oak (terebinth) in Zaanannim" (cf. Judg 4:11); Adami-hanneqeb is likely a single place name.

kjv: went out [too little] for them (the people of Dan)
mine: slipped from them (the people of Dan)
note: Wayyetse gebul ... mehem "the territory went out from them" means it was lost to them (cf. Judg 1:34); the KJV supplies "too little" to make it mean their territory was too small.

kjv: the suburbs thereof for our (the Levites') cattle
mine: their pasturelands for our (the Levites') livestock
note: Migrash is the open common land around a town used for grazing (from garash "drive out" cattle); "suburbs" now suggests residential outskirts. Applies to every "suburbs" in the chapter.

kjv: Kishon
mine: Kishion
note: The Hebrew is Qishyon, the town of 19:20, not the river Kishon (Qishon); the KJV spelling conflates them.

kjv: the borders of Jordan
mine: the region of Geliloth near the Jordan
note: Geliloth hayyarden may be a common noun "circuits, districts" (KJV) or the place name Geliloth (cf. 18:17); either is defensible.

kjv: at the passage of the children of Israel
mine: on the side belonging to the people of Israel
note: 'El-'ever bene yisra'el is "toward the side (region across) of the Israelites", locating the altar on the western, Israelite bank, which is why it caused offence; "passage" suggests a ford.

kjv: The LORD God of gods
mine: The Mighty One, God, Yahweh
note: 'El 'Elohim YHWH is a triple divine name; the KJV reads it as a construct "God of gods", which the grammar (no construct form) does not require.

kjv: meat offering
mine: grain offering
note: Minchah here is the grain (cereal) offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, but modern readers will think of flesh.

kjv: called the altar [Ed:] for it [shall be] a witness
mine: gave the altar a name: "It is a witness
note: The MT gives no name after "called the altar"; the KJV supplies "Ed" ("witness") in italics, following a few Hebrew MSS and the Syriac. I translate the MT, taking the following clause as the name.

kjv: on the other side of the flood
mine: beyond the River
note: Hannahar is "the River", i.e. the Euphrates (Mesopotamia); "flood" (1611 for a large river) now suggests Noah's flood. Same in vv.3, 14, 15.

kjv: under an oak, that [was] by the sanctuary
mine: under the oak that was in the sanctuary
note: Bemiqdash YHWH is "in the sanctuary"; the KJV softens to "by", perhaps to avoid a tree inside a holy place (cf. Deut 16:21). The article (ha'allah) marks a known oak (cf. Gen 35:4).

kjv: an hundred pieces of silver
mine: a hundred qesitahs
note: Qesitah is an old unit of value of unknown weight (also Gen 33:19, Job 42:11); silver is not named in the Hebrew.

kjv: in a hill [that pertained to] Phinehas his (Eleazar's) son
mine: at Gibeah, the town of his (Eleazar's) son Phinehas
note: Giv'at pinechas is most naturally the place name Gibeah ("hill") of Phinehas, a town given to him; the KJV takes it as a common noun.

kjv: Now the children of Judah had fought against Jerusalem, and had taken it
mine: The people of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it
note: The Hebrew uses ordinary sequential narrative verbs (wayyillachamu ... wayyilkedu); the KJV's pluperfect seems meant to harmonise with 1:21 and Josh 15:63, where Jerusalem is not held.

kjv: in the valley
mine: the lowland
note: Hashshephelah is the low hill country (foothills) between the Judean highlands and the coastal plain, not a valley.

kjv: put the Canaanites to tribute
mine: put the Canaanites to forced labor
note: Mas is corvee, compulsory labour gangs (cf. 1 Kgs 5:13; 9:21), not payment of tribute. Same for "tributaries" in vv. 30, 33, 35.

kjv: from the rock, and upward
mine: from Sela and upward
note: Hasela' may be the place name Sela (in Edom) or a common noun "the rock"; with the article either is possible.

kjv: Wherefore I (Yahweh) also said
mine: So now I (Yahweh) say
note: Wegam 'amarti (perfect) can refer back to an earlier warning (KJV, cf. Num 33:55; Josh 23:13) or be a performative "I hereby declare"; the context of judgment favours the latter.

kjv: it repented the LORD
mine: Yahweh was moved to pity
note: Yinnachem (niphal of nacham) here means to be moved with compassion; "repent" now implies remorse for wrongdoing.

kjv: Baalim and the groves
mine: the Baals and the Asherahs
note: Ha'asherot are the goddess Asherah (plural, local forms) or her wooden cult poles; the KJV, following the LXX/Vulgate "groves", turns a deity into trees.

kjv: a man lefthanded
mine: a man restricted in his right hand
note: 'Itter yad-yemino is literally "bound/impeded as to his right hand"; it may mean a disability or a trained left-hander (cf. 20:16), and the narrative turns on his hiding the sword on the unexpected side.

kjv: of a cubit length
mine: a gomed in length
note: Gomed occurs only here; it is an unknown, probably shorter measure (LXX "a span"), not the usual 'ammah "cubit".

kjv: the quarries that [were] by Gilgal
mine: the carved images near Gilgal
note: Pesilim everywhere else means carved idols or images; "quarries" is a guess from the root "to hew". Same in v.26.

kjv: so that he (Ehud) could not draw the dagger out
mine: for he (Ehud) did not draw the sword out
note: Ki lo' shalaf states that Ehud did not pull it out (deliberately leaving it), not that he was unable to.

kjv: the dirt came out
mine: the dung came out
note: Happarshedonah is a hapax; it may mean faeces (the bowel contents) or an exit, "he went out to the vestibule"; the KJV and I take the first sense.

kjv: he (Eglon) covereth his feet
mine: he (Eglon) must be relieving himself
note: Mesik 'et-raglaw "covering his feet" is a euphemism for defecating (cf. 1 Sam 24:3); the literal KJV hides the point of the servants' delay.

kjv: all lusty
mine: all strong
note: Shamen "fat, robust" means stout, vigorous men; "lusty" now suggests sexual desire.

kjv: the plain of Zaanaim
mine: the oak at Zaanannim
note: 'Elon is a large tree (oak or terebinth), not a plain (KJV follows the Targum); the qere reads Zaanannim as in Josh 19:33.

kjv: a bottle of milk
mine: a skin of milk
note: No'd is a leather skin container; "bottle" now suggests glass.

kjv: prospered, and prevailed against
mine: pressed harder and harder on
note: Wattelek ... halokh weqashah is an idiom of continuing increase: the Israelites' hand "went on becoming hard (heavy)" on Jabin.

kjv: Praise ye the LORD for the avenging of Israel
mine: When the leaders took the lead in Israel
note: Bifroa' pera'ot is obscure: the root para' means "let loose (hair)", and pera'ot likely means "leaders" (cf. Deut 32:42) or "when locks hung loose" (warriors' vow); "avenging" follows a guess with no firm basis in the Hebrew. Context: when the leaders took the lead (medium confidence). Para' means 'let loose (hair)'; pera'ot is either 'leaders' (cf. Arabic far' 'top, chief'; LXX(A) 'when leaders led'; 5:9 'the commanders of Israel') or 'loose locks' of warriors under a vow (cf. Deut 32:42). The parallel 'people offered themselves' suits either. ESV, NIV, NASB and CSB read 'leaders'; NRSV and NJPS 'locks'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'when locks hang loose/long in Israel', a war vow — NRSV, NJPS, many commentators (cf. Num 6:5); (2) 'for the avenging of Israel', from Aramaic pur'anuta 'retribution' — Targum, Rashi, KJV; (3) 'when a revelation was revealed' — LXX(B).

kjv: The mountains melted ... [even] that Sinai
mine: The mountains quaked before Yahweh, the One of Sinai
note: Nazelu may be from nazal "flow" (KJV) or zalal "quake" (LXX, cf. Isa 64:1); zeh sinay is an old divine title "the One of Sinai" (cf. Ps 68:8), not a demonstrative pointing at the mountain. Context: quaked (medium confidence). MT points nazelu 'flowed' (nazal), but the same consonants read nazollu 'quaked' (zalal), as LXX esaleuthesan and Isa 63:19 [64:1]; 5:4 describes earthquake and storm. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS all read 'quaked'. 'Flowed/melted' with MT's vowels (cf. Mic 1:4; Ps 97:5) stays possible. Zeh sinay is a divine title (cf. Ps 68:9). Other possible meanings: (1) 'the mountains flowed/melted' — MT vocalization, Targum, KJV; (2) 'even this Sinai' or 'that Sinai', a demonstrative pointing to the mountain — KJV, ESV, NASB, rather than the title 'the One of Sinai' (NIV, NRSV, NJPS).

kjv: ye that sit in judgment
mine: you who sit on rich carpets
note: Middin is plural of mad "cloth, carpet" (the KJV took it from din "judge"); the line contrasts riders, the seated wealthy, and walkers.

kjv: [They that are delivered] from the noise of archers
mine: To the sound of the musicians
note: Mechatsetsim is uncertain (archers, those dividing flocks, or singers); the KJV supplies a subject not in the Hebrew.

kjv: Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles
mine: Then the survivors came down to the nobles
note: The MT points yerad as from radah "rule", which the KJV follows; the parallel yerad-li and the context of descending to battle favour "came down" (yarad), as in LXX.

kjv: a root of them against Amalek ... the pen of the writer
mine: those whose root is in Amalek ... the marshal's staff
note: Shoresham ba'amaleq means their roots are in (the hill country of) Amalek (cf. 12:15); shevet sofer is the staff of the muster officer, not a writing pen.

kjv: abode in his (Asher's) breaches
mine: stayed by his (Asher's) landing places
note: Miftsarim (only here) are inlets or harbours on the coast; "breaches" is an etymological guess from parats "break".

kjv: O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength
mine: March on, my soul, with strength
note: Tidreki is imperfect/jussive, a self-exhortation; 'oz is adverbial "with might", not the object trodden.

kjv: Then were the horsehoofs broken by the means of the pransings
mine: Then the horses' hooves hammered with the galloping
note: Halemu means "struck, pounded" (the drumming of hooves); nothing is broken. Dahar is galloping.

kjv: she (Jael) brought forth butter
mine: she (Jael) brought him (Sisera) curds
note: Chem'ah is curdled milk or yogurt, a refreshing drink, not butter in the modern sense.

kjv: she (Jael) smote off his (Sisera's) head
mine: she (Jael) crushed his (Sisera's) head
note: Machaqah (hapax) means crush or shatter; the parallel with the tent peg through the temple (4:21) shows no beheading.

kjv: cut down the grove that is by it (the altar of Baal)
mine: cut down the Asherah that is beside it (the altar of Baal)
note: 'asherah is a cult pole or image of the goddess Asherah, not a grove; the KJV follows the Septuagint/Vulgate "grove". Also in vv. 26, 28, 30.

kjv: Take thy (Gideon's) father's young bullock, even the second bullock
mine: Take your (Gideon's) father's young bull, and the second bull
note: The Hebrew is difficult; it is unclear whether one or two bulls are meant.

kjv: called it (the altar) Jehovah-shalom
mine: called it (the altar) "Yahweh is Peace"
note: One of the few places where the KJV transliterates the divine name.

kjv: the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon
mine: the spirit of Yahweh clothed Gideon
note: labshah means "clothed (itself with)"; Gideon becomes the garment the spirit wears. "Came upon" loses the image.

kjv: upon the top of this rock, in the ordered place
mine: on top of this stronghold, with the stones laid in proper order
note: ma'oz means stronghold and bamma'arakhah means "in proper arrangement"; the KJV's "ordered place" is vague.

kjv: let him return and depart early from mount Gilead
mine: let him return home and hurry away from Mount Gilead
note: weyitspor is a hapax of uncertain meaning, perhaps "depart" or "turn back". "Mount Gilead" is also odd here, since the camp is west of the Jordan. Some scholars emend it to Gilboa.

kjv: took away the ornaments that were on their (Zebah and Zalmunna's) camels' necks
mine: took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their (Zebah and Zalmunna's) camels
note: saharonim are crescent-moon shaped pendants (cf. Isa 3:18), likely amulets.

kjv: by the plain of the pillar
mine: by the oak of the pillar
note: 'elon mutsav is the oak (terebinth) of the standing stone (cf. Josh 24:26). The KJV's "plain" again follows the Targum.

kjv: wherewith by me (the olive tree) they honour God and man
mine: by which gods and men are honored
note: 'elohim in a fable spoken among Canaanite Shechemites, set alongside "men", is more naturally "gods". Same in v. 13 ("cheers gods and men").

kjv: he (Zebul) sent messengers unto Abimelech privily
mine: he (Zebul) sent messengers to Abimelech secretly
note: betormah may mean "deceitfully/secretly" (from mirmah) or be a place name "in Tormah", possibly the Arumah of v. 41.

kjv: by the plain of Meonenim
mine: from the direction of the Diviners' Oak
note: 'elon me'onenim is "the oak of the soothsayers", a sacred tree. It is not a plain.

kjv: and all to brake his (Abimelech's) skull
mine: and crushed his (Abimelech's) skull
note: All to brake (all-to = completely) is obsolete and is often misread as "all to break".

kjv: his (Yahweh's) soul was grieved for the misery of Israel
mine: he (Yahweh) became impatient over the misery of Israel
note: wattiqtsar nafsho means "his soul grew short": he could no longer bear it. This can be read as compassion or as exasperation, and the Hebrew does not decide between them.

kjv: shall I (Jephthah) be your head?
mine: I (Jephthah) will be your head
note: Hebrew anokhi ehyeh lakhem lerosh has no interrogative particle; it reads naturally as Jephthah's stated condition, though a question by tone alone is possible.

kjv: whomsoever the LORD our God shall drive out
mine: all that Yahweh our God has dispossessed
note: The verb horish is perfect, referring to the conquest already accomplished (v. 23), not a future driving out.

kjv: unto the plain of the vineyards
mine: as far as Abel-keramim
note: Abel keramim is a place name (Meadow of Vineyards); the KJV translates it as a common noun phrase.

kjv: and she (Jephthah's daughter) knew no man
mine: She (Jephthah's daughter) had never known a man
note: The circumstantial clause vehi lo yadah ish states her condition when the vow was carried out; the KJV wording lets it be read as her lifelong state after the vow, supporting the view that she was dedicated to celibacy rather than sacrificed.

kjv: to lament the daughter
mine: to commemorate the daughter
note: Letannot is from tanah 'recount, retell' (cf. Judg 5:11), so the women went to tell or commemorate her story; 'lament' is a guess from context.

kjv: went northward
mine: crossed over to Zaphon
note: Tsaphonah can mean 'northward' or 'to Zaphon', a town in the Jordan valley in Gad (Josh 13:27); crossing the Jordan from Ephraim to Gilead is eastward, which favours the place name.

kjv: thirty nephews
mine: thirty grandsons
note: Hebrew bene banim is 'sons of sons'; in 1611 'nephew' could mean grandson (Latin nepos), but a modern reader takes it as a sibling's son. Context: grandsons (high confidence). Bene banim is literally 'sons of sons', the normal expression for grandchildren (Gen 45:10; Exod 34:7). The Hebrew is not ambiguous; only the English word 'nephew' has shifted meaning. All major modern translations read 'grandsons'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'nephews' — KJV, using 'nephew' in its older sense 'grandson' (Latin nepos), so no real difference of meaning; (2) 'descendants' more broadly — bene banim can extend to later offspring, though nothing here suggests it.

kjv: very terrible
mine: very awe-inspiring
note: Nora means 'fearsome, awe-inspiring'; modern 'terrible' suggests 'very bad'.

kjv: seeing it (the angel's name) is secret
mine: It (the angel's name) is wonderful
note: Peli (pil'i) is from pl' 'be wonderful, beyond comprehension', the same root as 'Wonderful' in Isa 9:6 and 'did wondrously' in v. 19; it denotes a name beyond human grasp rather than a hidden one.

kjv: a meat offering
mine: the grain offering
note: Minchah here is the grain offering; 'meat' in 1611 meant food in general, not flesh.

kjv: in the camp of Dan
mine: in Mahaneh-dan
note: Mahaneh-dan ('camp of Dan') is a place name (cf. Judg 18:12).

kjv: thirty sheets
mine: thirty linen garments
note: Sadin is a linen wrap or undergarment (cf. Prov 31:24, Isa 3:23), worn as clothing, not bed linen.

kjv: came forth meat
mine: came something to eat
note: Maakal is food in general (the honey); 'meat' in 1611 meant food, not flesh.

kjv: Now shall I (Samson) be more blameless than the Philistines
mine: This time I (Samson) will be blameless toward the Philistines
note: Niqqeti min-pelishtim most naturally means 'I am clear (of guilt) with respect to the Philistines'; the min is not comparative here.

kjv: in the top of the rock Etam
mine: in the cleft of the rock of Etam
note: Seif means a cleft or fissure in rock (Isa 2:21, 57:5), a hiding place, not a summit; so also v. 11.

kjv: an hollow place that was in the jaw
mine: the hollow place that is at Lehi
note: Ballechi (with article) is the place Lehi named in vv. 9 and 14; the KJV takes it as the jawbone itself, so that water flows from the bone. Maktesh is a 'hollow, basin' in the terrain.

kjv: seven green withs
mine: seven fresh bowstrings
note: Yeter is a cord or bowstring (often of animal gut or sinew); 'withs' are willow twigs, a different material.

kjv: that I (Samson) may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes
mine: one act of vengeance for my (Samson's) two eyes
note: Neqam-achat mishtei einai is literally 'vengeance of one from my two eyes'; it can mean one single revenge for both eyes or revenge for (at least) one of his two eyes. The KJV's 'at once' smooths the phrase.

kjv: Micah
mine: Micaiah
note: The Hebrew has the full form Mikhayehu ('Who is like Yahweh?') in vv. 1 and 4, shortened to Mikhah from v. 5 on; the KJV uses Micah throughout, hiding the Yahwistic name of an idol-maker.

kjv: I (Micah's mother) had wholly dedicated the silver
mine: I (Micah's mother) solemnly consecrate the silver
note: Haqdesh hiqdashti is a perfect that can be performative ('I hereby consecrate') or past; the KJV's pluperfect implies an earlier vow, whereas the context reads like a new dedication made on the silver's return.

kjv: an house of gods
mine: a shrine
note: Beit elohim can be 'house of God' or 'house of gods'; Micah intends it for Yahweh (v. 13), so 'shrine' or 'house of God' fits better than an explicitly polytheistic phrase.

kjv: no magistrate in the land, that might put them (the people of Laish) to shame
mine: no one in the land humiliating them (the people of Laish) in anything or holding power over them
note: The phrase yoresh etser ('possessor of restraint/dominion') is obscure; it describes the absence of any oppressor or ruling power rather than of a local magistrate specifically.

kjv: behind Kirjath-jearim
mine: west of Kiriath-jearim
note: Achare ('behind') is a compass term in Hebrew, where one faces east, so 'behind' means west.

kjv: the carriage before them (the Danites)
mine: the goods in front of them (the Danites)
note: Kevuddah means valuables or baggage; 1611 'carriage' meant what is carried, but a modern reader thinks of a vehicle.

kjv: they (the Danites) built a city
mine: They (the Danites) rebuilt the city
note: Ha'ir has the article and refers to Laish, which they had just burned (v. 27); they rebuilt it rather than founding another city.

kjv: for the damsel's father had said unto the man
mine: Then the young woman's father said to the man
note: Wayyomer is a narrative sequential ('then he said'); the KJV's pluperfect makes the invitation precede the meal.

kjv: And they (the Levite and the young woman's father) tarried until afternoon
mine: and linger until the day declines
note: Hitmahmehu is an imperative, part of the father's speech ('linger until the day turns'), not a narrative statement that they stayed.

kjv: certain sons of Belial
mine: worthless men
note: Beliyyaal is a common noun meaning 'worthlessness, wickedness'; the KJV's capitalised 'Belial' reads like a proper name of a demon, a sense it gains only in later Jewish and Christian usage (2 Cor 6:15).

kjv: do not this folly
mine: do not do this outrageous thing
note: Nevalah denotes a vile, shameful outrage (esp. sexual crime); modern 'folly' suggests mere foolishness.

kjv: divided her (the Levite's concubine), together with her bones, into twelve pieces
mine: cut her (the Levite's concubine) up limb by limb into twelve pieces
note: Lafatseha means 'according to her bones', i.e. joint by joint, not 'along with her bones'.

kjv: went up to the house of God
mine: went up to Bethel
note: Beit-el is the town Bethel, where the ark then stood (vv. 26-27); the KJV translates the name as 'house of God' here and in vv. 26 and 31 (and 21:2), obscuring that the sanctuary was at Bethel, not Shiloh.

kjv: out of the meadows of Gibeah
mine: from the open ground near Geba
note: MT has maareh-geva 'the bare place of Geba'; the KJV reads Gibeah (as some versions do) and takes maareh as 'meadows'.

kjv: make a great flame with smoke rise up
mine: send up a great cloud of smoke
note: Masat he'ashan is a 'rising (signal) of smoke', a smoke signal; there is no separate flame (also v. 40).

kjv: the flame of the city ascended up to heaven
mine: the whole city going up in smoke to the sky
note: Kelil ha'ir means 'the whole of the city', with overtones of a whole burnt offering (kalil); the KJV renders it as 'flame'.

kjv: them which came out of the cities they destroyed in the midst of them
mine: those who came out of the cities destroyed them (the Benjaminites) in the midst of them
note: Va'asher me-he'arim mashchitim oto: 'those from the cities were destroying him'; the men from the towns are the subject, catching Benjamin between them, not the victims.

kjv: trode them (the Benjaminites) down with ease
mine: trampled them (the Benjaminites) down at their resting place
note: Menuchah may mean 'rest, resting place' (or be a place name, Menuhah); 'with ease' is one interpretive option.

kjv: as well the men of every city
mine: the whole city
note: MT ir metom is obscure ('city of soundness', i.e. the entire city); the KJV and many moderns read metim 'men' instead.

kjv: came to the house of God
mine: came to Bethel
note: Beit-el is the town Bethel, where the ark was then kept (20:26-27); the KJV again translates the name as 'house of God'.

kjv: repented them for Benjamin
mine: felt sorry for Benjamin
note: Wayyinnachamu means 'they felt sorrow, compassion' for Benjamin (also v. 15); modern 'repent' implies turning from one's own sin.

kjv: it grieveth me (Naomi) much for your (Orpah and Ruth's) sakes
mine: it is far more bitter for me (Naomi) than for you (Orpah and Ruth)
note: Mar-li meod mikkem: the min can be comparative ('more bitter for me than for you', since Naomi has no prospects) or causal ('bitter on your account'); the KJV takes the latter.

kjv: Blessed be he (Boaz) of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness
mine: May he (Boaz) be blessed by Yahweh, Whose steadfast love has not forsaken the living or the dead
note: 'asher lo'-'azav chasdo could refer to Boaz or to Yahweh as the one whose loyalty endures. Readers have long debated which is meant.

kjv: one of our next kinsmen
mine: one of our redeemers
note: go'el is a technical term for a kinsman-redeemer with legal duties (land redemption, levirate). "Next kinsman" loses the institution that chs. 3-4 depend on.

kjv: spread therefore thy (Boaz's) skirt over thine handmaid
mine: Spread the corner of your (Boaz's) garment over your servant
note: kenafekha means "your wing / the corner of your garment", a marriage gesture (cf. Ezek 16:8). It deliberately echoes 2:12, "under whose wings you have come to take refuge".

kjv: and she (Ruth) went into the city
mine: Then he (Boaz) went into the city
note: The MT has the masculine wayyavo' (Boaz went). The KJV's "she" follows some Hebrew manuscripts and the Vulgate and Syriac versions.

kjv: Who art thou (Ruth), my daughter?
mine: How did it go, my daughter?
note: mi-'at bitti, literally "who are you?", is probably idiomatic here: "how do you stand?", that is, are you now betrothed? The KJV's literal rendering is puzzling, since Naomi knows who she is.

kjv: thou (the redeemer) must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess
mine: you (the redeemer) also acquire Ruth the Moabite
note: The MT reads ume'et rut ("and from Ruth"), with ketiv qaniti ("I acquire") and qere qanitah ("you acquire"). I read we'et rut ("and Ruth") with the Vulgate and most modern versions, since the point is that whoever redeems the land must also marry Ruth (v. 10). The KJV follows the MT's "of Ruth", which blurs the marriage obligation.

kjv: Ho, such a one!
mine: Turn aside, friend
note: peloni 'almoni is a deliberate "so-and-so": the narrator withholds the man's name. "Such a one" is literal but sounds odd. Neither version conveys the narrator's snub.

kjv: he (Elkanah) gave a worthy portion
mine: he (Elkanah) gave a double portion
note: manah 'achat 'appayim ("one portion of two faces/nostrils") is obscure. It is read as "a double portion", "a special portion", or (by emendation) "only one portion although he loved her".

kjv: with three bullocks
mine: along with a three-year-old bull
note: The MT has befarim sheloshah ("with three bulls"). I follow the Septuagint and 4QSam-a, which read befar meshullash ("with a three-year-old bull"), as v. 25 mentions "the bull" in the singular.

kjv: a daughter of Belial
mine: a worthless woman
note: bat-beliyya'al is an idiom for "worthless person". As in Deut 13:14, the KJV treats it as a name.

kjv: the judge shall judge him
mine: God will mediate for him
note: ufillelo 'elohim: 'elohim may be "God" or "judges", and pillel may mean "arbitrate" or "intercede". The contrast with "against Yahweh, who can intercede?" suggests God or a divine arbiter.

kjv: thou (Eli) shalt see an enemy in my habitation
mine: in distress you (Eli) will look with envious eye
note: wehibbatta tsar ma'on is obscure ("you will look on distress of dwelling"). The KJV supplies "in my". Every rendering is conjectural.

kjv: shall die in the flower of their (Eli's descendants') age
mine: shall die by the sword of men
note: The MT reads yamutu 'anashim ("shall die as men", that is, in their prime). I followed the Septuagint and 4QSam-a's "by the sword of men"; the KJV interprets the MT.

kjv: the word of the LORD was precious in those days
mine: the word of Yahweh was rare in those days
note: yaqar means both "precious" and "rare/scarce". The parallel "no frequent vision" shows that rarity is meant.

kjv: because his (Eli's) sons made themselves vile
mine: because his (Eli's) sons were blaspheming God
note: The MT has meqallelim lahem ("cursing themselves/for themselves"), which Jewish tradition lists as a scribal alteration (tiqqun sopherim) of meqallelim 'elohim ("cursing God"). The Septuagint reads "God". I follow the reconstructed reading; the KJV renders the MT.

kjv: God is come into the camp
mine: A god has come into the camp
note: The Philistines speak as polytheists, saying ba' 'elohim, and in v. 8 they refer to "these mighty gods" in the plural. "A god" or "gods" fits their speech better than "God".

kjv: he (Yahweh) destroyed them (the people of Ashdod), and smote them with emerods
mine: he (Yahweh) terrified and afflicted them (the people of Ashdod) with tumors
note: wayshimmem means "devastated" or "terrified" them. The ketiv 'ofalim and qere techorim mean tumours or swellings, possibly bubonic, which fits the mice in 6:4. "Emerods" (haemorrhoids) is obsolete. Same through chs. 5-6.

kjv: they (the men of Gath) had emerods in their secret parts
mine: tumors broke out on them (the men of Gath)
note: wayyissateru lahem is a hapax, probably "broke out". "In their secret parts" is a guess drawn from the Vulgate's interpretation.

kjv: even unto the great stone of Abel
mine: The great stone ... is a witness to this day
note: The MT has 'avel haggedolah ("great meadow" or "Abel"). I read 'even ("stone"), with some manuscripts and the Septuagint, to match v. 14. The KJV mixes the two readings, supplying "stone of" in italics.

kjv: because they (the men of Beth-shemesh) had looked into the ark of the LORD
mine: because they (the men of Beth-shemesh) looked upon the ark of Yahweh
note: ra'u ba'aron can mean "looked at" or "looked into". The MT's numbers ("seventy men, fifty thousand men") are awkward, and the "fifty thousand" is probably a later addition.

kjv: called the name of it (the stone) Eben-ezer
mine: called its (the stone's) name Ebenezer
note: 'even ha'ezer means "Stone of Help", and Samuel's words ("Till now Yahweh has helped us") explain the name. Both versions transliterate without translating it.

kjv: to ear his (the king's) ground
mine: to plow his (the king's) ground
note: Hebrew lacharosh charisho means "to plow his plowing"; "ear" is obsolete English for plow and now suggests nothing to a reader.

kjv: confectionaries
mine: perfumers
note: Hebrew raqqachot are women who compound spices and ointments (from raqach, "mix perfumes"); "confectionaries" (makers of sweets or preserves) narrows this to food.

kjv: a mighty man of power
mine: a man of substance
note: Hebrew gibbor chayil can mean a warrior or a man of wealth and standing; with no military context here it most likely describes Kish as a prominent, well-to-do man.

kjv: on whom is all the desire of Israel?
mine: for whom is all that is desirable in Israel?
note: Hebrew ul-mi kol-chemdat yisra'el, "to whom (belongs) all the desirable things of Israel"; the KJV makes Saul the object of Israel's longing, whereas the phrase more naturally refers to the wealth and honour of the nation passing to Saul's house.

kjv: the shoulder
mine: the thigh
note: Hebrew shoq is the leg or thigh (the priestly portion of Lev 7:32), not the shoulder (zeroa').

kjv: the plain of Tabor
mine: the oak of Tabor
note: Hebrew 'elon is a large tree (oak or terebinth); the KJV regularly rendered it "plain" following some Jewish interpreters.

kjv: if the man should yet come thither
mine: Has the man come here yet?
note: The MT ha-ba 'od halom 'ish is awkward; read as a question "has the man come here?" (as the Septuagint understood it) it fits Yahweh's answer that Saul is already present and hiding, whereas the KJV's "should yet come" implies he had not arrived.

kjv: God save the king
mine: Long live the king
note: Hebrew yechi ha-melekh is literally "may the king live"; God is not named, and the KJV substitutes the English royal acclamation.

kjv: unto all the coasts of Israel
mine: throughout all the territory of Israel
note: Hebrew gevul means border or territory; "coasts" in 1611 meant borders or regions, but a modern reader thinks of seashores, which Israel's inland tribes did not have.

kjv: the LORD that advanced Moses and Aaron
mine: Yahweh Who appointed Moses and Aaron
note: Hebrew 'asah ("made, appointed") here means Yahweh installed them in office; "advanced" (raised to a position) now suggests promotion or progress.

kjv: then shall both ye (Israel) and also the king ... continue following the LORD
mine: and if both you (Israel) and the king ... follow Yahweh your God, well and good
note: The Hebrew conditional sentence lacks a clear apodosis; the final clause (vihyitem ... 'achar YHWH) can be read as the result (KJV) or as part of the condition with the consequence ("it will be well") left unstated.

kjv: against you (Israel), as it was against your fathers
mine: against you (Israel) and against your fathers
note: MT reads bakhem uva'avotekhem, "against you and against your fathers"; the KJV smooths it to a comparison, while the Septuagint reads "and against your king".

kjv: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
mine: Saul was [number missing] years old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel.
note: Hebrew ben-shanah Sha'ul be-malkho is the standard regnal formula "Saul was X years old when he became king" (cf. 2 Sam 2:10), with the number lost in transmission; the KJV reinterprets "son of a year" as length of reign and runs the verse into v. 2.

kjv: in high places, and in pits
mine: in tombs, and in cisterns
note: Hebrew tseriach is a cellar, crypt or tomb-chamber (some suggest a stronghold), not an elevated cult site; bor is a cistern.

kjv: Gibeah of Benjamin
mine: Geba of Benjamin
note: MT reads Geva', a town distinct from Gibeah (Giv'ah) though close by; the KJV conforms it to Gibeah of v. 15.

kjv: Yet they (the Israelites) had a file for the mattocks
mine: The charge was a pim for the plowshares and the mattocks
note: Hebrew pim was unknown in 1611; inscribed weights found in excavations show it is a weight of about two-thirds of a shekel, so the verse states the Philistines' fee for sharpening tools, not that Israel had files.

kjv: over against Gibeah
mine: in front of Geba
note: MT reads Geva' (Geba), the town facing Michmash across the gorge; the KJV again substitutes Gibeah.

kjv: so it was a very great trembling
mine: it became a panic from God
note: Hebrew cherdat 'elohim can be a superlative idiom ("a mighty trembling") or literally "a trembling of God"; with the earthquake the narrator likely means a God-sent panic.

kjv: they (the Philistines) went on beating down [one another]
mine: surging this way and that
note: Hebrew vayyelekh va-halom is obscure; the KJV derives halom from halam "strike", but it is more likely the adverb "hither", describing the crowd dispersing in all directions.

kjv: the people rescued Jonathan
mine: the people ransomed Jonathan
note: Hebrew padah normally means "redeem, ransom", implying a payment or substitute for the one under the death oath, not simply a rescue.

kjv: he (Saul) gathered an host
mine: He (Saul) acted valiantly
note: Hebrew vayya'as chayil, "he did valour", is an idiom for performing mighty deeds (cf. Num 24:18; Ps 60:12); the KJV takes chayil as "army".

kjv: I (Yahweh) remember that which Amalek did
mine: I (Yahweh) have taken note of what Amalek did
note: Hebrew paqadti means "I have attended to / I am calling to account", the language of reckoning and punishment, which is stronger than mere remembering.

kjv: And it grieved Samuel
mine: Samuel was angry
note: Hebrew vayyichar le-Shemu'el is the idiom for burning anger (charah), though it may be anger mixed with distress; "grieved" softens it.

kjv: It repenteth me (Yahweh)
mine: I (Yahweh) regret
note: Hebrew nichamti, "I regret / I am sorry"; to a modern reader "repent" implies turning from sin, which the text does not ascribe to God (the same verb recurs in vv. 29 and 35).

kjv: he (Saul) set him up a place
mine: he (Saul) set up a monument for himself
note: Hebrew yad ("hand") here means a memorial stela, as in 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's monument); "a place" obscures Saul's self-glorification.

kjv: the sin of witchcraft
mine: the sin of divination
note: Hebrew qesem is divination (seeking omens, cf. 1 Sam 6:2; 28:8), not witchcraft in the sense of casting spells.

kjv: the Strength of Israel
mine: the Glory of Israel
note: Hebrew netsach yisra'el is a unique title; netsach means "eminence, glory, perpetuity" and is rendered variously as Glory, Eternal One, or Strength.

kjv: Agag came unto him (Samuel) delicately
mine: Agag came to him (Samuel) confidently
note: Hebrew ma'adannot is obscure: from 'adan "delight" it suggests cheerfully or confidently (matching his words), while others read it as "in fetters" (cf. Job 38:31); "delicately" now suggests fragility.

kjv: of a beautiful countenance
mine: with beautiful eyes
note: Hebrew yefeh 'einayim is literally "fair of eyes"; the KJV generalises it to the face.

kjv: a cunning player on an harp
mine: a man who knows how to play the lyre
note: Hebrew yodea' menaggen means "skilled at playing"; "cunning" in 1611 meant skilful, but now suggests craftiness (also v. 18).

kjv: an harp
mine: the lyre
note: Hebrew kinnor is a hand-held lyre with a yoke and crossbar, distinct from the nevel; the KJV renders it "harp" throughout.

kjv: a target of brass between his (Goliath's) shoulders
mine: a bronze javelin slung between his (Goliath's) shoulders
note: Hebrew kidon is a javelin or curved sword (the War Scroll uses it of a sword); "target" (a small shield) is a guess, and the KJV itself renders kidon "spear" in v. 45 margin and "shield" in v. 45 text.

kjv: he (David) came to the trench
mine: He (David) came to the encampment
note: Hebrew ma'gal (from 'agol, "round") means the circular camp or wagon ring, not a dug trench.

kjv: left his (David's) carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage
mine: left his (David's) baggage in the care of the keeper of the baggage
note: Hebrew kelim means equipment or baggage; "carriage" in 1611 meant what is carried, but now suggests a vehicle.

kjv: the naughtiness of thine (David's) heart
mine: the evil of your (David's) heart
note: Hebrew roa' levavekha is "wickedness of heart"; "naughtiness" now sounds like childish misbehaviour.

kjv: Is there not a cause?
mine: Was it not just a word?
note: Hebrew halo' davar hu' most naturally means "it was only a word / I was only talking"; the KJV takes davar as "reason, cause", making David justify his intervention.

kjv: with a shield
mine: with ... javelin
note: Hebrew kidon, the same weapon as in v. 6, is an offensive weapon (javelin or sword) listed with sword and spear; the KJV's "shield" breaks the series of offensive arms.

kjv: the wounded of the Philistines
mine: the Philistine dead
note: Hebrew chalele pelishtim are the slain (chalal, "pierced, fatally wounded"); also MT "until you come to Gai" is read by the KJV as "the valley" (gay'), while the Septuagint reads Gath.

kjv: behaved himself (David) wisely
mine: had success
note: Hebrew yaskil (Hiphil of sakal) can mean "act prudently" or "prosper, succeed"; in a military context, and given Yahweh "with him" (v. 14), success is the likelier sense (same verb in vv. 14, 15, 30).

kjv: he (Saul) prophesied in the midst of the house
mine: he (Saul) raved within his house
note: Hebrew vayyitnabbe' (Hithpael of naba') covers ecstatic, uncontrolled behaviour; under an evil spirit it describes frenzy rather than prophecy in the usual sense.

kjv: Thou (David) shalt this day be my son in law in [the one of] the twain
mine: You (David) shall now be my son-in-law a second time
note: Hebrew bishtayim titchatten bi ha-yom is obscure; it is most likely "a second time" (after the failed Merab offer), while the KJV supplies words to make it "by one of the two daughters".

kjv: any dowry
mine: no bride-price
note: Hebrew mohar is the payment the groom makes to the bride's father; a "dowry" in modern usage is property the bride's family gives, the reverse direction.

kjv: take heed to thyself (David) until the morning
mine: be on your (David's) guard in the morning
note: Hebrew babboqer means "in the morning". The danger comes at morning (cf. v. 11), not up to it.

kjv: took an image ... a pillow of goats' hair for his bolster
mine: took the household idol ... a net of goats' hair at its head
note: hatterafim are household gods, man-sized here. kevir ha'izzim (a hapax) is probably a goat-hair net or quilt placed at the head to look like hair.

kjv: shalt remain by the stone Ezel
mine: remain beside the stone heap
note: The MT has ha'even ha'azel ("the stone Ezel", otherwise unknown). The Septuagint reads "that mound" (Hebrew ha'argav hallaz). I follow the Septuagint here and in v. 41.

kjv: David arose out of a place toward the south
mine: David rose from beside the stone heap
note: The MT reads me'etsel hannegev ("from beside the south/Negev"), which makes little sense. The Septuagint has "from beside the mound" (ha'argav), matching v. 19.

kjv: the vessels of the young men are holy, and the bread is in a manner common
mine: The vessels of the young men are holy even when it is an ordinary journey
note: wehu' derekh chol means "and it (the mission) is an ordinary journey". The KJV supplies "the bread". The Hebrew is difficult. KJV 21:5.

kjv: scrabbled on the doors of the gate
mine: made marks on the doors of the gate
note: wayetav (qere) means "made marks" (from taw, a mark). "Scrabbled" is obsolete. KJV 21:13.

kjv: and goeth at thy (Saul's) bidding
mine: and captain over your (Saul's) bodyguard
note: wesar 'el-mishma'tekha: sar may be read as "turns aside" (KJV) or "commander". mishma'at means "obedience" or "bodyguard" (cf. 2 Sam 23:23). David commanded Saul's guard (cf. 1 Sam 18:13).

kjv: they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth
mine: that place was called the Rock of Escape
note: sela' hammachleqot means "Rock of Divisions/Slipping-away", a pun on Saul and David being separated. The KJV transliterates and does not explain the pun.

kjv: Saul went in to cover his feet
mine: Saul went in to relieve himself
note: lehasekh 'et-raglav, "to cover his feet", is a euphemism for defecating. The KJV's literal rendering hides the irony of the scene. KJV 24:3.

kjv: any that pisseth against the wall
mine: so much as one male
note: mashtin beqir ("one who urinates against a wall") is a crude idiom for "male". The KJV keeps the vulgarity, which is accurate to the Hebrew. I used the plain meaning. Same in v. 34.

kjv: the man was churlish
mine: the man was harsh
note: qasheh means "harsh, hard". "Churlish" is archaic but close.

kjv: Saul lay in the trench
mine: Saul was lying inside the camp barricade
note: Hebrew ma`gal (also 26:7) is the circular camp enclosure, probably a ring of wagons or baggage, not a dug trench.

kjv: Whither have ye (David) made a road to day?
mine: Where did you (David) raid today?
note: Hebrew pashat means to make a raid; "road" in 1611 meant an inroad or raid, which a modern reader takes as a highway.

kjv: and so [will be] his (David's) manner all the while he dwelleth
mine: Such was his (David's) practice all the time he lived
note: The clause wekoh mishpato (no verb) can continue the feared report or be the narrator's comment on David's habitual practice; the past-tense "all the days he lived" favours the narrator.

kjv: I (the medium) saw gods ascending out of the earth
mine: I (the medium) see a divine being coming up out of the earth
note: Hebrew elohim with a plural participle (olim) can mean "gods" or a single supernatural being; Saul's follow-up "What does he look like?" shows one figure is meant, so "gods" misleads. Context: a divine being (medium confidence). Saul's follow-up 'What is his appearance?' (singular) and the answer 'an old man is coming up' point to one figure, and elohim can denote a single spirit-being. But the participle 'olim is plural, so she may describe more than one figure, as LXX and Vulgate read. NASB, NRSV and NJPS read 'a divine being'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'gods' or 'divine beings coming up', more than one figure — LXX theous, Vulgate deos, KJV, some commentators from the plural participle; (2) 'a god' — ESV; (3) 'a ghostly figure' or 'spirit form', the dead as elohim (cf. Isa 8:19) — NIV, CSB.

kjv: they (the Amalekites) slew not any, either great or small
mine: taken captive the women who were in it, young and old. They (the Amalekites) killed no one
note: The Masoretic accents attach miqqaton we`ad-gadol ("from small to great") to the captives, not to the killing; the KJV joins it to "they slew not any".

kjv: Chor-ashan
mine: Bor-ashan
note: The Leningrad Codex reads Bor-`ashan ("well of Ashan"); the KJV follows printed editions reading Kor-`ashan. Same place, a one-letter variant.

kjv: under a tree
mine: under the tamarisk tree
note: Hebrew ha'eshel is specifically the tamarisk (as at Gen 21:33 and 1Sa 22:6, where the KJV renders "grove"/"tree"); the article marks a known landmark.

kjv: because my (Saul's) life [is] yet whole in me
mine: though my (Saul's) life is still wholly in me
note: Hebrew ki kol-`od napshi bi: ki here is best taken concessively (agony grips him yet life lingers), which is why he asks to be finished off; "because" obscures the logic.

kjv: he (David) bade them teach the children of Judah [the use of] the bow
mine: he (David) said it should be taught to the people of Judah; it is called "The Bow"
note: Hebrew lelammed bene-yehudah qashet: "bow" with no verb is most likely the title of the lament (as in the Book of Jashar), not an order for archery training; the KJV supplies "the use of". Context: a song title (medium confidence). Qeshet stands with no verb or article right after 'to teach the sons of Judah', and the lament follows at once; nothing concerns archery, though 1:22 mentions Jonathan's bow, which may explain the title. NIV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS take it as the song's name. Other possible meanings: (1) 'teach the sons of Judah [the use of] the bow', archery training — Targum, Rashi, KJV; (2) 'bow' as a scribal intrusion or obscure musical term — the LXX (B) lacks the word and some commentators delete or emend it.

kjv: the shield of Saul, [as though he had] not [been] anointed with oil
mine: the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil
note: Hebrew beli mashiach bashshamen refers to the shield (leather shields were oiled); the KJV supplies words that make Saul himself "not anointed", a sense the Hebrew does not require.

kjv: smote him (Asahel) under the fifth [rib]
mine: struck him (Asahel) in the belly
note: Hebrew el-hachomesh was once derived from chamesh "five", hence "fifth rib"; it is now understood as the belly or abdomen (also 3:27, 4:6, 20:10).

kjv: unless thou (Abner) hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother
mine: if you (Abner) had not spoken, the troops would not have given up pursuing their brothers until morning
note: The Hebrew (mehabboqer na`alah ha`am) is terse: either Abner's appeal now ends a pursuit that would have lasted till morning, or Abner's earlier challenge (2:14) caused the fight; the KJV's literal rendering leaves the sense unclear.

kjv: Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul
mine: Abner was strengthening his own position in the house of Saul
note: Hebrew hayah mitchazzeq bebeyt sha'ul (reflexive, with "in") suggests Abner was building his own power within Saul's house, which sets up the concubine charge in 3:7; the KJV makes it simple loyal support.

kjv: [Am] I (Abner) a dog's head, which against Judah do shew kindness
mine: Am I (Abner) a dog's head belonging to Judah? Today I keep showing loyalty
note: Hebrew ha-rosh kelev anokhi asher lihudah: "that is Judah's" most naturally qualifies "dog's head" (am I a Judahite cur?); the KJV turns it into "against Judah" and joins it to the next clause.

kjv: smote him (Abner) there under the fifth [rib]
mine: struck him (Abner) in the belly
note: Hebrew hachomesh means the belly or abdomen; "fifth rib" came from a false link with chamesh "five".

kjv: one that leaneth on a staff
mine: one who holds a spindle
note: Hebrew machaziq bappelekh: pelekh is a spindle, a woman's tool, so the curse wishes effeminate or unwarlike men on Joab's house; "staff" turns it into a curse of lameness or old age.

kjv: to cause David to eat meat
mine: to urge David to eat food
note: Hebrew lehavrot lechem means to give him food (lechem "bread, food"); "meat" in 1611 meant food in general.

kjv: smote him (Ish-bosheth) under the fifth [rib:]
mine: struck him (Ish-bosheth) in the belly
note: Hebrew el-hachomesh means "in the belly"; "fifth rib" rests on a mistaken link with chamesh "five".

kjv: who [thought] that I (David) would have given him (the man who reported Saul's death) a reward for his tidings
mine: that was the reward I (David) gave him (the man who reported Saul's death) for his news
note: Hebrew asher letitti-lo besorah is elliptical; it is best read ironically (execution was the "reward" for his news), whereas the KJV supplies "thought" to make it the messenger's expectation.

kjv: Except thou (David) take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither
mine: You (David) will not get in here; even the blind and the lame will drive you off
note: Hebrew ki im-hesirkha ha`ivrim wehappischim has "the blind and the lame" as subject of hesir ("turn away, repel"): the Jebusites boast that even their disabled could repel David; the KJV makes David the one who must remove them.

kjv: getteth up to the gutter
mine: must get up through the water shaft
note: Hebrew tsinnor is a water channel or shaft (probably the city's water tunnel used to get inside); "gutter" suggests a roof drain.

kjv: [he shall be chief and captain]
mine: (absent)
note: The Hebrew sentence breaks off without a reward clause; the KJV supplies one in italics from the parallel 1 Chr 11:6.

kjv: David and his men burned them (the idols)
mine: David and his men carried them (the idols) away
note: The Hebrew has wayyissa'em "and carried them off"; the KJV follows the parallel 1 Chr 14:12, which says David ordered them burned.

kjv: fetch a compass behind them (the Philistines)
mine: circle around behind them (the Philistines)
note: Hebrew hasev means "go around"; "fetch a compass" is obsolete English for making a circuit.

kjv: over against the mulberry trees
mine: opposite the baka trees
note: Hebrew bekha'im is an unidentified tree or shrub (perhaps balsam or poplar); mulberry is a guess with no support.

kjv: [instruments made of] fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets
mine: instruments of cypress wood, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles
note: Hebrew beroshim is probably cypress or juniper, and mena`an`im (from nua` "shake") are sistrums or rattles, not horns; the parallel 1 Chr 13:8 reads "with all their might and with songs" instead of "cypress".

kjv: a flagon [of wine]
mine: a raisin cake
note: Hebrew ashishah is a pressed cake of raisins (cf. Song 2:5, Hos 3:1); the KJV took it as a wine vessel and supplied "of wine". Eshpar, rendered "a good piece of flesh"/"portion of meat", is itself uncertain.

kjv: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child
mine: And Michal daughter of Saul had no child
note: The Hebrew simply joins the note with "and" (ulemikhal); the KJV's "Therefore" makes her childlessness an explicit punishment, which the text implies at most.

kjv: and have made thee (David) a great name
mine: And I will make for you (David) a great name
note: Hebrew we`asiti is a waw-consecutive perfect, which shifts to the future: the great name is part of the dynastic promise, not a past achievement; the KJV puts it in the past.

kjv: and have caused thee (David) to rest from all thine enemies
mine: And I will give you (David) rest from all your enemies
note: Hebrew wahanichoti is likewise a waw-consecutive perfect continuing the promises of 7:10, so future; the KJV renders it as past.

kjv: And [is] this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
mine: And this is instruction for mankind, Lord Yahweh!
note: Hebrew wezot torat ha'adam is obscure; it can be an exclamation ("this is a charter/instruction for humanity") or a question; the KJV's "manner of man" reads torah as custom.

kjv: a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen
mine: 1,700 horsemen
note: The MT reads 'elef ushva'-me'ot parashim ("1,700 horsemen"). The KJV supplies "chariots" (in italics) to harmonise with 1 Chr 18:4 and the Septuagint, which read "1,000 chariots and 7,000 horsemen".

kjv: and David's sons were chief rulers
mine: and David's sons were priests
note: The Hebrew says kohanim hayu ("were priests"). The KJV, like 1 Chr 18:17 ("chief about the king"), avoids the plain sense that non-Levites held a priestly office.

kjv: As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table
mine: So Mephibosheth ate at my table
note: The MT reads 'okhel 'al-shulchani ("eats at my table") in the narrator's voice, which is awkward. The KJV adds "said the king", and the Septuagint reads "David's table". I kept the MT's wording.

kjv: hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob ... and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men
mine: hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob ... and the men of Tob, 12,000 men
note: 'ish tov means "the men of Tob" (a region; cf. Judg 11:3). It is not a place called Ish-tob. The KJV also uses "Syrians" for 'aram throughout, an anachronism for the Arameans.

kjv: after the year was expired
mine: In the spring of the year
note: litshuvat hashanah means "at the return of the year", the spring campaign season. "After the year was expired" is a literal but vague rendering.

kjv: for she (Bathsheba) was purified from her uncleanness
mine: (Now she (Bathsheba) had been purifying herself from her uncleanness.)
note: wehi' mitqaddeshet mittum'atah is a circumstantial clause. It notes that she had just completed purification after menstruation, which shows the child cannot be Uriah's. The KJV's "for" wrongly makes it the reason he lay with her.

kjv: thou (David) hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme
mine: you (David) have utterly scorned Yahweh
note: The MT reads ni'ets ni'atsta 'et-'oyevei YHWH ("you have utterly scorned the enemies of Yahweh"). "Enemies" is widely regarded as a pious scribal buffer, as in 1 Sam 25:22, to avoid saying David scorned God. The KJV keeps "enemies" and expands the verb to "given occasion to blaspheme". I removed the buffer.

kjv: put them (the people of Rabbah) under saws, and under harrows of iron ... and made them pass through the brickkiln
mine: set them (the people of Rabbah) to labor with saws and iron picks and iron axes and made them toil at the brick kilns
note: wayyasem bammegerah means "put them to (work with) the saw". he'evir bammalben (qere) means "made them work at the brick-mould". The KJV reads it as torture (being sawn and burned), which would be atrocity. The Hebrew more naturally describes forced labour.

kjv: a garment of divers colours
mine: a long robe with sleeves
note: ketonet passim (also Joseph's robe, Gen 37:3) is probably a robe reaching to the palms and soles, a long-sleeved robe. "Divers colours" follows the Septuagint's guess in Genesis.

kjv: And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom
mine: And the spirit of the king longed to go out to Absalom
note: wattekhal dawid is grammatically awkward (feminine verb with "David"). It may mean "longed for" or "ceased (from going out against)". Both versions supply a subject. The sense, longing or hostility, is debated.

kjv: neither doth God respect any person
mine: But God will not take away life
note: welo'-yissa' 'elohim nefesh means "God does not take away a life". It is not about God showing partiality (nasa' panim). The woman's argument is that God seeks to restore, not destroy.

kjv: when he (Absalom) polled his head
mine: when he (Absalom) cut the hair of his head
note: Poll (to cut hair) is obsolete. The Hebrew is gallach, "shave/cut".

kjv: tarried in a place that was far off
mine: they (the king and the people) halted at the last house
note: beit hammerchaq means "the house of the distance", probably the last house of the city before the Kidron, a landmark rather than a vague "far place".

kjv: I (David) will tarry in the plain of the wilderness
mine: I (David) will wait at the fords of the wilderness
note: The ketiv be'avrot ("at the fords") fits David's crossing of the Jordan (17:16). The qere be'arvot ("in the plains") is what the KJV follows. I chose the ketiv.

kjv: Come out, come out
mine: Get out, get out
note: Hebrew tse tse means 'go out, be gone'; Shimei is driving David away, not summoning him, which 'come out' can suggest to a modern reader.

kjv: man of Belial
mine: worthless man
note: beliyya'al is a common noun meaning 'worthlessness, baseness'; the KJV's transliteration reads like a proper name or demon.

kjv: so let him (Shimei) curse, because
mine: If he (Shimei) is cursing because
note: The qere ko yeqallel ki gives 'so let him curse, for'; the ketiv ki yeqallel vekhi gives 'if he curses and if/because'. KJV follows the qere, mine the ketiv; the sense is close.

kjv: God save the king
mine: Long live the king
note: Hebrew yechi hammelek is simply 'may the king live'; God is not named.

kjv: the man whom thou (Absalom) seekest is as if all returned
mine: The return of everyone depends on the man you (Absalom) are seeking
note: MT kesuv hakkol ha'ish asher attah mevaqqesh is elliptical ('like the return of all is the man you seek'); both renderings guess at it. The LXX reads differently ('as a bride returns to her husband; you seek the life of one man').

kjv: draw it (the city) into the river
mine: drag it (the city) down into the valley
note: nachal is a wadi or ravine (often dry); a hilltop city would be dragged into the valley below, not a river.

kjv: a wench
mine: A servant girl
note: shiphchah is a maidservant; 'wench' now sounds coarse or derogatory.

kjv: Absalom's place
mine: Absalom's Monument
note: yad (literally 'hand') here means a memorial or monument, as the context of the pillar (matstsevet) makes clear.

kjv: Cushi
mine: the Cushite
note: Hebrew hakkushi has the article: 'the Cushite' (an Ethiopian/Nubian), an ethnic designation, not a personal name.

kjv: thou (Ahimaaz) hast no tidings ready
mine: you (Ahimaaz) will have no reward for the news
note: besorah motset is terse ('news that finds/obtains'); it most likely means news that will earn a reward, as besorah means 'reward for news' in 4:10. KJV takes it as 'no news to deliver'.

kjv: were but dead men
mine: were nothing but men doomed to death
note: anshei mawet means 'men of death', i.e. men deserving or condemned to death (as rebels' kin), not men already dead. (KJV 19:28.)

kjv: a man of Belial
mine: a worthless man
note: ish beliyya'al means 'a worthless/base man'; not a proper name.

kjv: in the fifth [rib]
mine: in the belly
note: chomesh means the abdomen/belly; the KJV linked it to chamesh 'five' and supplied 'rib'.

kjv: it (the siege ramp) stood in the trench
mine: it (the siege ramp) stood against the outer rampart
note: chel is the outer fortification or rampart of a city, not a trench.

kjv: over the tribute
mine: over the forced labor
note: mas denotes the corvée, conscripted labor gangs, not a monetary tribute.

kjv: a chief ruler about David
mine: a priest to David
note: The Hebrew is kohen, the ordinary word for 'priest'. The KJV, uneasy with a non-Levite priest, took it in a broader sense of 'chief official' (cf. 8:18).

kjv: whom she (Michal) brought up for Adriel
mine: whom she (Michal) bore to Adriel
note: yaldah means 'she bore'. The KJV softened it to 'brought up' because Michal was childless (6:23) and Adriel married her sister Merab (1 Sam 18:19); some Hebrew MSS and LXX read 'Merab' here. MT says Michal.

kjv: girded with a new [sword]
mine: armed with new gear
note: chadashah ('new', feminine) has no noun; what was new (sword, armor, belt) is not stated.

kjv: slew [the brother of] Goliath the Gittite
mine: struck down Goliath the Gittite
note: MT says Elhanan killed Goliath the Gittite; the KJV inserts 'the brother of' (italics) from the parallel 1 Chr 20:5 ('Lahmi the brother of Goliath') to harmonize with 1 Sam 17. Context: Goliath (as the Hebrew says) (high confidence). MT and LXX both read 'Goliath'. The text is visibly disturbed ('oregim, 'weavers', seems copied from the line's end), and 1 Chr 20:5 may preserve an original 'Lahmi the brother of Goliath'; but no witness to Samuel reads that, so the translation keeps the source and leaves the tension with 1 Sam 17 (ESV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, CSB do the same). Other possible meanings: (1) '[the brother of] Goliath', supplied from 1 Chr 20:5 — KJV, NIV, NET; many think Chronicles reflects the better text; (2) Elhanan as another name for David — Targum and some rabbinic and later commentators; (3) a second Philistine named Goliath, or 'Goliath' as a title — some conservative commentators.

kjv: born to the giant
mine: descended from the giants
note: harapha (with article) may be an eponymous ancestor or a term for the Rephaim giant clan; the KJV takes it as one individual father of all four.

kjv: the floods of ungodly men
mine: the torrents of destruction
note: nachalei veliyya'al parallels 'breakers of death'; beliyya'al here denotes destruction/ruin (the underworld) rather than wicked people.

kjv: The sorrows of hell
mine: the cords of Sheol
note: chevlei she'ol: chevel can mean 'pangs' or 'cords', and the parallel 'snares of death' favours 'cords'. Sheol is the realm of the dead, not hell as a place of punishment.

kjv: the snares of death prevented me (David)
mine: the snares of death confronted me (David)
note: qiddemuni means 'came to meet me, confronted me'; 'prevented' in 1611 meant 'came before', not 'stopped'. Same in 22:19.

kjv: thou (Yahweh) wilt shew thyself unsavoury
mine: You (Yahweh) show Yourself shrewd
note: tittappal (from patal 'twist') means God outmanoeuvres the crooked; 'unsavoury' now suggests something distasteful or disreputable.

kjv: a bow of steel is broken by mine (David's) arms
mine: my (David's) arms can bend a bow of bronze
note: qeshet nechushah is a bow of bronze (steel was unknown), and nichat means 'press down, bend (to string)', not 'break'.

kjv: thy (Yahweh's) gentleness hath made me (David) great
mine: Your (Yahweh's) answering has made me (David) great
note: 2 Sam reads 'anotekha ('your answering/help'); the KJV gives the sense of 'anwatkha 'your humility/gentleness' from the parallel Ps 18:35.

kjv: given me (David) the necks of mine enemies
mine: made my (David's) enemies turn their backs to me
note: natattah li oref means 'you gave me (their) back of the neck', i.e. made them turn and flee; 'necks' is too literal for a modern reader.

kjv: they (the foreigners) shall be afraid out of their close places
mine: came limping out of their (the foreigners') strongholds
note: yachgeru (cf. Ps 18 yachregu) is rare, probably 'limp/come out haltingly'; misgerot are fortified places.

kjv: the sweet psalmist of Israel
mine: the delight of Israel's songs
note: ne'im zemirot yisra'el is ambiguous: 'pleasant one of Israel's songs' (the hero they sing of) or 'sweet singer'; some read zemirot as 'strength/protection' ('the favourite of the Mighty One of Israel').

kjv: He that ruleth over men [must be] just
mine: One who rules over people justly
note: The Hebrew is a verbless description (moshel ba'adam tsaddiq) which v. 4 completes with 'is like the morning light'; the KJV supplies 'must be', turning it into a requirement.

kjv: Although my (David's) house be not so with God ... although he make it not to grow
mine: Is not my (David's) house like this with God? ... Will He not cause all my salvation ... to spring up?
note: The ki-lo clauses are best read as rhetorical questions expecting 'yes', affirming the dynasty. The KJV reads them as concessive negatives, which reverses the tone of David's confidence.

kjv: [the sons] of Belial
mine: the worthless
note: beliyya'al is an abstract noun 'worthlessness'; the KJV supplies 'sons' and keeps it as a name.

kjv: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat
mine: Josheb-basshebeth, a Tahchemonite
note: yoshev bashshevet is most likely a (corrupted) personal name (cf. Jashobeam in 1 Chr 11:11), which the KJV translates literally as 'he who sat in the seat'.

kjv: two lionlike men of Moab
mine: the two Ariels of Moab
note: ari'el is obscure: possibly a personal name ('two sons of Ariel', LXX), heroes, or altar-hearths; 'lionlike men' is a guess from ari 'lion'.

kjv: on the right side of the city that lieth in the midst of the river of Gad
mine: south of the city that is in the middle of the valley, toward Gad
note: yamin ('right hand') is the standard Hebrew term for 'south'; hannachal haggad is best read as 'the wadi, toward Gad' (Arnon valley) rather than a 'river of Gad'.

kjv: did Araunah, [as] a king, give unto the king
mine: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king
note: MT ha-kol natan aravnah hammelek lammelek; hammelek is most naturally a vocative ('O king') in Araunah's speech; the KJV makes it a description of Araunah as royal, implying he was a (Jebusite) king.

kjv: let her (the young virgin) cherish him (the king)
mine: let her (the young virgin) be his (the king's) nurse
note: sokhenet means attendant or nurse. In modern English "cherish" means to love or treasure. Same word in v. 4.

kjv: his (Adonijah's) father had not displeased him at any time
mine: His (Adonijah's) father had never once rebuked him
note: 'atsavo means "pained, crossed" him, so David never reproved him. "Displeased" now sounds like the reverse.

kjv: God save king Adonijah
mine: Long live King Adonijah
note: yechi hammelekh means "may the king live". The KJV uses the English royal acclamation, which adds "God". Same in vv. 34, 39.

kjv: his (Shimei's) hoar head bring thou (Solomon) down to the grave with blood
mine: you (Solomon) shall bring his (Shimei's) gray head down with blood to Sheol
note: she'ol is the realm of the dead. The KJV alternates between "grave", "hell" and "pit" for this one word, which hides that it is a single named place.

kjv: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart
mine: Give Your servant therefore a listening heart
note: lev shomea' means "a hearing/listening heart", attentive to God and to cases brought before the king. "Understanding" loses the image that 3:11 picks up ("to hear judgment").

kjv: for her (the true mother's) bowels yearned upon her son
mine: because her (the true mother's) heart yearned for her son
note: nikhmeru rachameiha means "her compassion (womb/inner parts) grew warm". "Bowels" was the seat of emotion in 1611 English. Today it reads oddly.

kjv: Zabud the son of Nathan was principal officer
mine: Zabud the son of Nathan was priest
note: The Hebrew is kohen ("priest"). As in 2 Sam 8:18, the KJV avoids giving a non-Levite courtier a priestly title.

kjv: Adoniram ... was over the tribute
mine: Adoniram ... was in charge of the forced labor
note: mas is conscripted labour (corvée; cf. 5:27-28 and 12:18). "Tribute" suggests taxes.

kjv: for the horses and dromedaries
mine: for the horses and swift steeds
note: rekhesh are swift horses (chargers), not camels. KJV 4:28.

kjv: concerning timber of fir
mine: in the matter of cedar and juniper timber
note: berosh is probably the juniper or the Phoenician cypress. KJV 5:8.

kjv: windows of narrow lights
mine: windows with recessed frames
note: challonei shequfim 'atumim is an architectural term of uncertain meaning, perhaps framed, latticed or closed (clerestory) windows.

kjv: the oracle
mine: the inner sanctuary
note: devir is the innermost room (the Holy of Holies). "Oracle" follows the Vulgate's oraculum ("place of speaking") and now suggests a prophetess. It recurs through chs. 6-8.

kjv: the lintel and side posts were a fifth part of the wall
mine: the lintel and the doorposts formed a pentagon
note: ha'ayil mezuzot chamishit is obscure. It may describe a five-sided doorframe, or a frame that was a fifth of the wall's width. The KJV supplies "of the wall".

kjv: that lay on forty five pillars, fifteen in a row
mine: above the beams that rested on the pillars, forty-five of them, fifteen to a row
note: The number forty-five follows hatsela'ot (beams/side rooms) "that were on the pillars"; the KJV attaches it to the pillars, which conflicts with the four rows of pillars in v. 2.

kjv: the thick beam
mine: a canopy
note: Hebrew 'av is obscure here; it is usually taken as an overhang or canopy rather than a single thick beam.

kjv: had another court within the porch
mine: in the other court set back from the hall
note: Hebrew hatser ha'aheret mibbeit la'ulam locates the king's residence in a separate court behind the hall, not a court inside the porch.

kjv: a worker in brass
mine: a worker in bronze
note: Hebrew nehoshet is copper or bronze (copper-tin); brass (copper-zinc) was not used in Solomon's day. The same applies throughout the chapter and book.

kjv: did compass either of them (the two pillars) about
mine: went around the second pillar
note: The Hebrew says the line went around "the second pillar" (ha'ammud hasheni), an elliptical way of giving the same measure for each; the KJV smooths it.

kjv: to cover the chapiters that were upon the top, with pomegranates
mine: two rows of pomegranates ... to cover the capitals that were on top of the pillars
note: The MT appears to have exchanged "pillars" and "pomegranates" (it reads "the capitals on top of the pomegranates"); I follow the widely accepted transposition, while the KJV rearranges the words to make sense of the MT.

kjv: knops
mine: gourds
note: Hebrew peqa'im are gourd-shaped ornaments; "knops" (knobs) is archaic and vague.

kjv: upon the ledges there was a base above
mine: on the frames as well, above
note: Hebrew ken here is the adverb "likewise," not the noun ken "base"; the KJV read it as the noun.

kjv: certain additions made of thin work
mine: wreaths of hanging work
note: Hebrew loyot ma'aseh morad are wreaths or garlands in hanging (pendant) work.

kjv: plates of brass: and the four corners thereof (each stand's)
mine: bronze axles, and its (each stand's) four feet
note: Hebrew sarne are axles (cf. v. 32 in sense) and pa'amotav its feet, not plates and corners.

kjv: according to the proportion of every one
mine: wherever there was space
note: Hebrew kema'ar ish means "according to the clear space of each," i.e. wherever there was room.

kjv: the oracle
mine: the inner sanctuary
note: Hebrew devir is the innermost room of the temple; "oracle" now suggests a prophetic utterance.

kjv: they (the priests) drew out the staves
mine: the poles were so long
note: Hebrew wayya'arikhu habbaddim means the poles "were long" (or "they lengthened"), explaining why their ends were visible; nothing says they were pulled out.

kjv: an house to dwell in
mine: an exalted house
note: Hebrew beit zevul uses zevul "lofty abode, princely dwelling" (cf. Ugaritic zbl "prince"), not a plain dwelling.

kjv: so that thy (David's) children take heed
mine: if only your (David's) sons watch
note: Hebrew raq im "only if" makes the promise conditional; KJV "so that" meant "provided that" in 1611 but now reads as purpose.

kjv: caterpiller
mine: grasshopper
note: Hebrew hasil is a type of locust (the "consumer"), not a caterpillar.

kjv: Let your (Israel's) heart therefore be perfect
mine: Let your (Israel's) hearts be wholly devoted
note: Hebrew shalem means whole, undivided in loyalty; "perfect" now suggests sinlessness.

kjv: meat offerings
mine: the grain offering
note: Hebrew minhah here is the grain offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, and now suggests flesh.

kjv: the entering in of Hamath
mine: Lebo-hamath
note: Hebrew levo hamat is best taken as a place name, Lebo of Hamath, the northern boundary town, rather than "the entrance to Hamath."

kjv: fir trees
mine: cypress
note: Hebrew berosh is a cypress or juniper of Lebanon, not a fir.

kjv: the reason of the levy
mine: the account of the forced labor
note: Hebrew devar hammas is "the matter/account of the corvée"; mas is conscripted labor, whereas "levy" now suggests a tax.

kjv: a navy of ships
mine: a fleet of ships
note: Hebrew 'oni is a fleet of trading ships; "navy" now implies warships.

kjv: his (Solomon's) ascent by which he went up unto the house of the LORD
mine: the burnt offerings he (Solomon) offered at the house of Yahweh
note: Hebrew 'olato asher ya'aleh is most naturally "his burnt offering(s) that he offered up" ('olah + causative of 'alah); the KJV reads 'olah as "ascent," following the parallel 2 Chr 9:4 ('aliyyato). Context: burnt offerings (medium confidence). 'Olah elsewhere always means burnt offering, and 'olah with the causative of 'alah is the standard idiom 'offer a burnt offering'. LXX and Vulgate read offerings here, the LXX also at 2 Chr 9:4. ESV, NIV, NRSV, NJPS and CSB read offerings. MT 2 Chr 9:4 'aliyyato 'his ascent' supports the alternative. Other possible meanings: (1) 'his ascent (stairway) by which he went up to the house of Yahweh' — MT 2 Chr 9:4, KJV, NASB (1995); (2) 'his upper chamber' at the temple — some commentators reading 'aliyyah literally in Chronicles.

kjv: pillars
mine: supports
note: Hebrew mis'ad occurs only here; it means a support, railing or stepped structure, not pillars.

kjv: the spice merchants
mine: the merchants
note: Hebrew rokhelim are traveling traders in general; spices are not mentioned.

kjv: targets
mine: large shields
note: Hebrew tsinnah is a large body shield; "target" (a shield in 1611) now suggests something shot at.

kjv: peacocks
mine: baboons
note: Hebrew tukkiyim is uncertain; comparison with Egyptian ky "monkey" suggests baboons or another primate, though "peacocks" remains a traditional guess.

kjv: and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price
mine: and from Kue; the king's traders acquired them (the horses) from Kue at the current price
note: Hebrew miqweh (miqqeweh) is now recognized as the place name Kue (Cilicia), a known horse-trading region; the KJV took it as a noun "collection, yarn."

kjv: strange women
mine: foreign women
note: Hebrew nashim nokhriyyot are women of foreign nations; "strange" now suggests odd behavior.

kjv: in the hill that is before Jerusalem
mine: on the mountain east of Jerusalem
note: Hebrew 'al penei here has its geographical sense "facing, east of" (the Mount of Olives), not merely "in front of."

kjv: an Ephrathite
mine: an Ephraimite
note: Hebrew 'efrati here means a man of the tribe of Ephraim (as in Judg 12:5); "Ephrathite" suggests Ephrathah/Bethlehem in Judah.

kjv: ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph
mine: in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph
note: Hebrew sevel is the burden of compulsory labor; Jeroboam supervised the corvée, which explains his later grievance, not a general "charge."

kjv: who was over the tribute
mine: who was in charge of the forced labor
note: Hebrew 'al hammas denotes the overseer of the corvée (conscripted labor), the very grievance of v. 4, not a collector of tribute money.

kjv: It is too much for you (Israel) to go up to Jerusalem
mine: You (Israel) have gone up to Jerusalem long enough
note: Hebrew rav lakhem usually means "enough for you" (cf. Deut 1:6); the KJV takes it as "too much, too burdensome," which is possible but less idiomatic.

kjv: made priests of the lowest of the people
mine: appointed priests from among all the people
note: Hebrew miqtsot ha'am means "from the whole extent of the people" (cf. Gen 47:2), i.e. from any tribe rather than Levi; it says nothing about low social standing.

kjv: made again of the lowest of the people priests
mine: again appointed priests ... from among all the people
note: As in 12:31, Hebrew miqtsot ha'am means "from the whole range of the people" (non-Levites), not "the lowest" socially.

kjv: cracknels
mine: cakes
note: Hebrew niqqudim are small cakes or biscuits (perhaps crumbly or speckled); "cracknels" is an obscure English term.

kjv: their (Israel's) groves
mine: their (Israel's) Asherah poles
note: Hebrew 'asherim are wooden cult objects of the goddess Asherah, not groves of trees; the KJV followed the Septuagint/Vulgate "grove." Same at 14:23, 15:13, 16:33.

kjv: images
mine: sacred pillars
note: Hebrew matsevot are standing stones erected as cult markers, not carved images.

kjv: sodomites
