mine: male cult prostitutes
note: Hebrew qadesh means "consecrated one," a male functionary attached to a shrine (traditionally a cult prostitute); "sodomites" imports a reference to Sodom that the Hebrew lacks. Same at 15:12.

kjv: his (Abijam's) heart was not perfect with the LORD
mine: his (Abijam's) heart was not wholly true to Yahweh
note: shalem means whole or undivided in loyalty. "Perfect" suggests sinlessness. Also in v. 14.

kjv: he (Asa) took away the sodomites out of the land
mine: He (Asa) banished the male cult prostitutes from the land
note: qedeshim ("consecrated ones") are male personnel of the fertility cult. "Sodomites" imports a later, different idea.

kjv: she (Maacah) had made an idol in a grove
mine: she (Maacah) had made an abhorrent image for Asherah
note: mifletset la'asherah is a horrid object for the goddess Asherah. The KJV's "grove" follows the Septuagint and Vulgate.

kjv: There is a league between me (Asa) and thee (Ben-hadad)
mine: Let there be a treaty between me (Asa) and you (Ben-hadad)
note: The Hebrew is a verbless clause, either a statement or a wish. The proposal to buy Ben-hadad's alliance favours the wish.

kjv: provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their (Baasha and Elah's) vanities
mine: provoking Yahweh the God of Israel to anger with their (Baasha and Elah's) idols
note: hevel ("breath, vapor") is used here as a contemptuous term for idols. "Vanities" is literal but obscures the reference. Same in v. 26.

kjv: he (Hiel) laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn
mine: He (Hiel) laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn
note: be'aviram means "with/at the cost of Abiram", fulfilling Josh 6:26. It may imply foundation sacrifice or simply the sons' deaths. The KJV's literal "in" leaves this unclear.

kjv: who was of the inhabitants of Gilead
mine: of Tishbe in Gilead
note: The MT reads mittoshavei gil'ad ("of the settlers of Gilead"). The Septuagint reads "from Tishbe of Gilead" (mittishbe). I follow the Septuagint, which explains the name "Tishbite".

kjv: let this child's soul come into him again
mine: let this child's life come into him again
note: nefesh here means "life, vital breath", the life force returning. "Soul" suggests a separable immortal soul.

kjv: they (the prophets of Baal) leaped upon the altar which was made
mine: they (the prophets of Baal) limped around the altar that they had made
note: wayefasschu repeats the verb of v. 21 (pos'chim, "limping/hobbling between two opinions"), describing a lurching ritual dance around the altar. The KJV's "leaped upon" loses the pun.

kjv: either he (Baal) is talking, or he is pursuing
mine: Either he (Baal) is musing, or he has wandered away
note: siach means "musing/preoccupied". sig is obscure, perhaps "withdrawn" or a euphemism for relieving oneself. "Pursuing" is a guess.

kjv: they (the prophets of Baal) prophesied until the time of the offering
mine: they (the prophets of Baal) raved on until the time of the offering
note: wayyitnabbe'u (hithpael) here means ecstatic frenzy, not prophetic speech.

kjv: sat down under a juniper tree
mine: sat down under a broom tree
note: rotem is the white broom (Retama raetam), a desert shrub. It is not juniper. Same in v. 5.

kjv: a still small voice
mine: the sound of a thin silence
note: qol demamah daqqah is an oxymoron: "a voice/sound of thin/fine silence". The KJV's famous phrase makes it a quiet voice. The Hebrew points rather to an eerie silence, though the phrase is open.

kjv: Yet I (Yahweh) have left me seven thousand in Israel
mine: Yet I (Yahweh) will leave seven thousand in Israel
note: wehish'arti is a waw-consecutive perfect, which normally refers to the future: "I will leave" survivors after the purge of v. 17. The KJV's past tense (followed in Rom 11:4) makes it a present remnant.

kjv: thou (Ahab) shalt make streets for thee in Damascus
mine: you (Ahab) may establish bazaars for yourself in Damascus
note: chutsot here means trading quarters or market streets granted to a foreign power, a commercial concession. "Streets" misses the economic point.

kjv: disguised himself (the prophet) with ashes upon his face
mine: disguising himself (the prophet) with a bandage over his eyes
note: ba'afer is pointed by the Masoretes as "with ashes", but 'afer (a homograph) means "bandage/headband". The latter fits v. 41, where he removes it to be recognised.

kjv: Hast thou (Ahab) killed
mine: Have you (Ahab) murdered
note: The verb ratsach is the specific term for unlawful killing (the Decalogue verb), so the charge is murder, not just killing.

kjv: will take away thy (Ahab's) posterity
mine: I (Yahweh) will sweep you (Ahab) away
note: Hebrew u-vi'arti acharekha is literally "I will burn/sweep away after you"; the KJV interprets it as removing descendants, a reasonable gloss but not what the words say.

kjv: him that is shut up and left
mine: both bond and free
note: The pair 'atsur ve-'azuv is a merism of uncertain sense ("restrained and released", i.e. slave and free, or minor and adult); the KJV's literal rendering is opaque to a modern reader.

kjv: in a void place
mine: at the threshing floor
note: Hebrew goren is the ordinary word for a threshing floor, an open flat area by the gate used for public assemblies; the KJV's "void place" guesses from the sense of open space.

kjv: persuade
mine: entice
note: The verb pittah means to entice or deceive (to lure someone into folly), which fits the lying spirit; "persuade" is too neutral.

kjv: a spirit
mine: the spirit
note: Hebrew has the article, ha-ruach, "the spirit", which some take as a particular spirit (or the spirit of prophecy); the KJV makes it indefinite.

kjv: at a venture ... the joints of the harness
mine: at random ... between the joints of his (Ahab's) armor and the breastplate
note: Hebrew le-tummo means "in his innocence", i.e. without aiming, and "harness" in 1611 meant body armour; the text names two pieces, ha-devaqim (the scale joints) and ha-shiryan (the breastplate).

kjv: they washed his (Ahab's) armour
mine: the prostitutes bathed there
note: Hebrew ve-ha-zonot rachatsu means "and the prostitutes washed"; the KJV follows a rabbinic interpretation that took zonot as "armour" (via zayin, "weapon"), which the grammar does not support.

kjv: the sodomites
mine: the male cult prostitutes
note: Hebrew ha-qadesh denotes a male cult functionary/prostitute attached to a shrine (from qadosh, "consecrated"); "sodomites" names an ethnic origin and shifts the sense from cultic prostitution to sexual orientation.

kjv: the water is naught, and the ground barren
mine: the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage
note: Hebrew meshakkelet (from shakal, "be bereaved") means the land causes loss of offspring, i.e. miscarriage or death of young; also "naught" (= bad, worthless) is archaic.

kjv: death or barren land
mine: death or miscarriage
note: Same participle meshakkelet as 2:19: the problem is the water causing miscarriage or bereavement, not merely infertile soil.

kjv: little children
mine: young lads
note: Hebrew ne'arim qetannim: na'ar covers boys and young men (servants, soldiers), so "small lads" need not mean toddlers; the KJV's "little children" (and "children" for yeladim in 2:24) makes the scene sound like infants.

kjv: the image of Baal
mine: the pillar of Baal
note: Hebrew matstsevah is a standing stone or cult pillar, not a carved image or statue.

kjv: an hundred thousand rams, with the wool
mine: the wool of a hundred thousand rams
note: Hebrew me'ah elef eilim tsamer, "a hundred thousand rams, wool", is most naturally read as the wool of the rams (the fleece was the tribute), not rams plus their wool.

kjv: the meat offering
mine: the grain offering
note: Hebrew minchah here is the regular morning grain offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, and today suggests flesh.

kjv: great indignation against Israel
mine: great wrath upon Israel
note: Hebrew qetsef gadol al-Yisra'el is wrath (normally divine) coming upon Israel; whose wrath is unstated, and the KJV's "indignation against" can suggest merely human outrage at Israel.

kjv: a little chamber ... on the wall
mine: a small walled upper room
note: Hebrew aliyyat-qir is "a roof chamber of wall", most likely a permanent walled room on the roof (as opposed to a booth); the KJV places the room "on the wall".

kjv: full ears of corn in the husk thereof
mine: fresh ears of grain in his (the man from Baal-shalishah's) sack
note: Hebrew karmel be-tsiqlono: karmel is fresh new grain and the hapax tsiqlon is now understood as a bag or sack, not a husk; "corn" in 1611 meant any grain.

kjv: a leper
mine: he (Naaman) had a skin disease
note: Hebrew metsora' (tsara'at) covers a range of visible skin conditions (here one that turns the skin "white as snow", 5:27); it is not demonstrably Hansen's disease, which "leprosy" now denotes. Same throughout the chapter.

kjv: to worship there ... I (Naaman) bow myself
mine: to bow down there ... I (Naaman) bow down
note: Hebrew uses the same verb hishtachavah for the master's act and for Naaman's; the KJV's "worship" vs "bow myself" draws a distinction between them that the text does not make.

kjv: the tower
mine: the hill
note: Hebrew ha-'ophel denotes a hill or mound (often a fortified rise in a city); "tower" is a guess from the related sense of a citadel.

kjv: four leprous men
mine: four men with a skin disease
note: Hebrew metsora'im (tsara'at) is a broad term for disfiguring skin disease requiring isolation outside the city, not specifically Hansen's disease.

kjv: some mischief will come upon us (the four men with a skin disease)
mine: punishment will overtake us (the four men with a skin disease)
note: Hebrew u-metsa'anu 'avon, "guilt/punishment will find us": the lepers fear being held culpable; "mischief" in 1611 meant harm or misfortune, today mere naughtiness.

kjv: two chariot horses
mine: two chariots with horses
note: Hebrew shenei rekhev susim, "two chariot(s) of horses", is most naturally two chariots with their teams (cf. the five horses proposed in 7:13); the KJV reads it as two horses.

kjv: Athaliah, the daughter of Omri
mine: Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri
note: bat can mean female descendant. Athaliah was Ahab's daughter (v. 18), so Omri was her grandfather.

kjv: Thou (Ben-hadad) mayest certainly recover
mine: You (Ben-hadad) will certainly recover
note: The ketiv reads lo "not" ("Say: You will surely not recover"). The qere reads lo "to him". Both the KJV and I follow the qere, but the ketiv changes the sense of Elisha's message.

kjv: him that is shut up and left in Israel
mine: every male, bond or free, in Israel
note: 'atsur we'azuv is an idiomatic merism, probably "bond and free" or "minor and adult". The KJV's literal "shut up and left" is opaque.

kjv: for he (Jehu) driveth furiously
mine: for he (Jehu) drives like a madman
note: beshigga'on means "in madness". It picks up "this madman" (hammeshugga') from v. 11, a wordplay the KJV's "furiously" misses.

kjv: she (Jezebel) painted her face, and tired her head
mine: she (Jezebel) painted her eyes and adorned her head
note: watasem bappukh 'eineiha means "she put kohl on her eyes". "Tired" (attired) her head is obsolete.

kjv: unto the rulers of Jezreel
mine: to the rulers of the city
note: The MT reads sarei yizre'e'l ("rulers of Jezreel"), which is odd since the letters go to Samaria. I follow the Septuagint's "rulers of the city"; the KJV keeps the MT.

kjv: and went to the city of the house of Baal
mine: and went into the inner room of the house of Baal
note: The MT has 'ir ("city"), which makes little sense inside a temple. Many scholars read devir ("inner sanctuary"). I follow that reconstruction.

kjv: made it (the house of Baal) a draught house unto this day
mine: made it (the house of Baal) a latrine to this day
note: lemotsa'ot (qere) means "latrines". "Draught house" (privy) is obsolete.

kjv: the rulers over hundreds, with the captains and the guard
mine: the captains of hundreds, of the Carites and of the guards
note: lakkari means "the Carites", probably Carian mercenaries from Asia Minor serving as a royal bodyguard, like the Cherethites. "Captains" obscures the foreign guard. Same in v. 19.

kjv: so shall ye (the guards) keep the watch of the house, that it be not broken down
mine: shall guard the palace
note: massach is obscure, perhaps "in rotation" or "as a barrier". The KJV's "that it be not broken down" is a guess.

kjv: God save the king
mine: Long live the king!
note: yechi hammelekh means "may the king live". The KJV uses the English acclamation (cf. 1 Kgs 1:25).

kjv: every man of his (the priest's) acquaintance
mine: each from his (the priest's) donor
note: makkaro is uncertain: perhaps "his assessor/treasurer" or "his acquaintance". It likely means the person or official through whom the money came. KJV 12:5.

kjv: the children of Israel dwelt in their tents, as beforetime
mine: the people of Israel lived in their homes as formerly
note: be'oholeihem ("in their tents") is idiomatic for "at home" long after Israel's nomadic period. The KJV's literal rendering suggests they still lived in tents.

kjv: from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain
mine: from Lebo-hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah
note: levo' chamat is probably a place name (Lebo of Hamath), and yam ha'aravah is the Dead Sea. The KJV's literal "entering" and "plain" obscure the geography.

kjv: how he (Jeroboam) recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel
mine: how he (Jeroboam) restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel
note: lihudah beyisra'el is a notoriously difficult phrase. Every rendering, including the KJV's supplied words, is a conjecture.

kjv: he (Azariah) was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house
mine: he (Azariah) had a skin disease to the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house
note: metsora' refers to tsara'at, a general skin disease, not necessarily leprosy (see Lev 13). beit hachofshit means "a house of freedom/separation", either quarantine or release from duties. "Several" (separate) is archaic.

kjv: and the Syrians came to Elath
mine: and the Edomites came to Elath
note: The ketiv is 'arammim ("Arameans") and the qere is 'adomim ("Edomites"). The two words differ in one letter. Edomites fits Elath on the Red Sea (cf. 14:22). The KJV follows the ketiv.

kjv: gave him (Shalmaneser) presents
mine: paid him (Shalmaneser) tribute
note: Hebrew minchah here is the regular tribute owed by a vassal (cf. v.4 "year by year"), not a voluntary gift as "presents" now suggests.

kjv: images and groves
mine: standing stones and Asherah poles
note: Hebrew matsevot are standing stone pillars and asherim are wooden cult objects of the goddess Asherah; the KJV's "groves" follows the Septuagint/Vulgate and misleads.

kjv: made a grove
mine: made an Asherah
note: Hebrew asherah is a cult pole or image of the goddess Asherah, something "made," not a grove of trees.

kjv: the Samaritans
mine: the Samarians
note: Hebrew hashomronim are the (Israelite) inhabitants of Samaria who built the shrines; "Samaritans" evokes the later religious community, which this verse is not describing.

kjv: of the lowest of them
mine: from all ranks of people
note: Hebrew miqqetsotam means "from the whole extent of them," i.e. from people at large rather than from Levites (as 1 Kgs 12:31); it does not mean "the lowest."

kjv: he (Hezekiah) called it (the bronze serpent) Nehushtan
mine: it (the bronze serpent) was called Nehushtan
note: Hebrew vayyiqra lo can be impersonal ("one called it"), describing the object's popular name; the KJV makes Hezekiah the one who named it.

kjv: brake the images, and cut down the groves
mine: smashed the standing stones, and cut down the Asherah
note: Hebrew matsevot are standing stone pillars and asherah (singular) is the wooden cult pole of the goddess Asherah, not a grove.

kjv: the pillars
mine: the doorposts
note: Hebrew omnot occurs only here; it denotes the supports or doorposts of the temple doors, not free-standing pillars.

kjv: Tartan and Rabsaris and Rab-shakeh
mine: the Tartan, the Rab-saris, and the Rabshakeh
note: These are Assyrian official titles (commander-in-chief, chief eunuch/officer, chief cupbearer), not personal names, as the Hebrew article on tartan shows.

kjv: the Syrian language
mine: Aramaic
note: Hebrew aramit is the Aramaic language, the diplomatic lingua franca; "Syrian" now suggests a different, modern language.

kjv: Make [an agreement] with me (the king of Assyria) by a present
mine: Make peace with me (the king of Assyria)
note: Hebrew asu itti berakhah, "make a blessing with me," is an idiom for coming to terms or surrender; the KJV takes berakhah as a gift and supplies "an agreement."

kjv: and blasphemy
mine: and of disgrace
note: Hebrew neatsah means contempt or disgrace suffered by the people, not blasphemy uttered by them; the KJV word now suggests a different sin.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will send a blast upon him (Sennacherib)
mine: I (Yahweh) am about to put a spirit in him (Sennacherib)
note: Hebrew noten bo ruach means "put a spirit in him," i.e. an impulse or disposition that makes him withdraw on hearing a report; "blast" implies a destroying wind.

kjv: Ethiopia
mine: Cush
note: Hebrew kush is the Nubian kingdom on the upper Nile (modern Sudan) whose 25th-dynasty pharaoh Tirhakah ruled Egypt, not modern Ethiopia.

kjv: dwellest [between] the cherubims
mine: enthroned above the cherubim
note: Hebrew yoshev hakkeruvim means "sitting (enthroned) on the cherubim," picturing the ark's cherubim as God's throne; "between" is supplied.

kjv: the forest of his (Lebanon's) Carmel
mine: its (Lebanon's) densest forest
note: Hebrew yaar karmillo uses karmel as a common noun, "garden land, orchard," i.e. Lebanon's richest woodland, not Mount Carmel.

kjv: all the rivers of besieged places
mine: all the streams of Egypt
note: Hebrew yeore matsor: yeor is the Nile word for streams/channels and matsor is a poetic name for Egypt (Mizraim), which the KJV read as matsor "siege."

kjv: thy (Sennacherib's) tumult
mine: your (Sennacherib's) arrogance
note: Hebrew shaananekha means your complacency or arrogant ease; "tumult" follows an older guess from the parallel "rage."

kjv: the land of Armenia
mine: the land of Ararat
note: Hebrew erets ararat names Urartu; the KJV follows the Septuagint/Vulgate's Armenia, a later name for the region.

kjv: with a perfect heart
mine: with a whole heart
note: Hebrew levav shalem means an undivided, wholehearted loyalty; modern "perfect" suggests sinlessness, which Hezekiah is not claiming.

kjv: ten degrees backward ... in the dial of Ahaz
mine: back ten steps ... on the steps of Ahaz
note: Hebrew maalot means steps (of a stairway), apparently a stair on which the shadow moved; "degrees" and "dial" interpret it as a sundial, which the Hebrew does not state.

kjv: made a grove
mine: made an Asherah
note: Hebrew asherah is a manufactured cult object (pole or image) of the goddess Asherah, not a grove of trees.

kjv: observed times
mine: practiced soothsaying
note: Hebrew onen (polel of anan) denotes some form of soothsaying or divination; the KJV's "observed times" (astrological day-reckoning) is one old guess at its sense.

kjv: a graven image of the grove
mine: the carved image of Asherah
note: Hebrew pesel haasherah is a carved image of the goddess Asherah set in the temple; "image of the grove" obscures that a goddess is meant.

kjv: seduced them (the people)
mine: led them (the people) astray
note: Hebrew vayyatem means "caused them to wander, misled them"; "seduced" now carries a sexual sense absent here.

kjv: there was no reckoning made with them (the workmen)
mine: no accounting shall be asked of them (the workmen)
note: Hebrew lo yechashev is an imperfect within the king's instructions (vv.4-7), a directive that the workmen not be audited; the KJV turns it into a narrative statement of past fact.

kjv: have gathered the money
mine: have poured out the silver
note: Hebrew hittikhu (hiphil of natakh) means "poured out," i.e. emptied the chest or melted down the silver into ingots, not "gathered."

kjv: in the college
mine: in the Second Quarter
note: Hebrew mishneh ("second") names a newer district of Jerusalem (Zeph 1:10); the KJV follows the Targum's "house of instruction," implying a school.

kjv: the planets
mine: the constellations
note: Hebrew mazzalot (cf. Akkadian manzaltu, "station") denotes the constellations or signs of the zodiac rather than the planets.

kjv: he (Josiah) brought out the grove from the house of the LORD
mine: He (Josiah) brought the Asherah out from the house of Yahweh
note: Hebrew haasherah here is a portable cult object of the goddess Asherah that stood inside the temple and was burned and ground to dust; a "grove" cannot be carried out of a building.

kjv: the houses of the sodomites
mine: the houses of the male cult prostitutes
note: Hebrew qedeshim ("consecrated ones") are male personnel of a fertility cult; "sodomites" imports a later moral category and obscures the cultic setting.

kjv: in the suburbs
mine: in the precincts
note: Hebrew parvarim (cf. parbar, 1 Chr 26:18) is an architectural term for a colonnade or annex of the temple, not the outskirts of the city.

kjv: brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves
mine: smashed the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles
note: Hebrew matsevot are standing stone pillars and asherim wooden cult poles of the goddess Asherah.

kjv: What title [is] that
mine: What is that grave marker
note: Hebrew tsiyyun means a monument or sign-post marking a grave; "title" (an inscription) is a narrow sense now unfamiliar.

kjv: the images
mine: the household gods
note: Hebrew terafim are household idols or figurines used in divination (cf. Gen 31:19), not images in general.

kjv: went up against the king of Assyria
mine: went up to the king of Assyria
note: Hebrew al can mean "against" or "to/toward"; external sources (Babylonian Chronicle) show Neco marched to support Assyria against Babylon in 609 BC, so "to" is the better reading. Context: went up to the king of Assyria (high confidence). 'Alah 'al often means 'go up against', but 'al can mean 'to/toward' (as 'el), and the Babylonian Chronicle shows Neco marched in 609 BC to support Assyria at Harran against Babylon. ESV, NASB, NRSV and CSB read 'to'; NIV 'to help'. 2 Chr 35:20 gives Carchemish as his goal. Other possible meanings: (1) 'went up against the king of Assyria' — KJV, the commoner sense of 'alah 'al; Josephus (Ant. 10.74) has Neco marching against the Medes and Babylonians, and some take 'king of Assyria' as whoever then ruled Assyria (Babylon); (2) 'went up on behalf of' ('al = for) — some commentators.

kjv: from the river of Egypt
mine: from the Wadi of Egypt
note: nachal mitsrayim is a seasonal wadi (the Wadi el-Arish) on Egypt's border, not the Nile, which is ye'or or nahar.

kjv: until he (Yahweh) had cast them (Jerusalem and Judah) out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled
mine: until He (Yahweh) cast them (Jerusalem and Judah) out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled
note: The KJV makes Zedekiah's rebellion the result of God's anger, but the Hebrew wayyimrod begins a new clause.

kjv: did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison
mine: graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison
note: nasa' 'et-ro'sh is an idiom for pardon or rehabilitation (cf. Gen 40:13, 20). The KJV's literal rendering is accurate but opaque.

kjv: on the ninth day of the fourth month
mine: On the ninth day of the fourth month
note: The Hebrew here lacks "fourth" ("on the ninth of the month"). Both versions supply it from Jer 52:6; the KJV marks it in italics.

kjv: the dukes of Edom were; duke Timnah, duke Aliah
mine: The chiefs of Edom were: chiefs Timna, Alvah
note: 'alluf means clan chief. "Duke" imports European nobility. The ketiv 'alyah ("Aliah") versus the qere 'alvah ("Alvah") is a minor spelling variant.

kjv: who transgressed in the thing accursed
mine: who broke faith in the matter of the devoted thing
note: cherem means something devoted to God, here banned plunder that was to be destroyed (Josh 7). "Accursed" captures the danger but not the idea of dedication.

kjv: These were the sons of Caleb the son of Hur
mine: These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur
note: The Masoretic accents divide the verse after "Caleb" and begin a new list with "the sons of Hur", since Caleb is Hur's father (v. 19), not his son. The KJV joins the phrases.

kjv: the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son
mine: the sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son
note: 'assir can be a name, "Assir", or the word "captive", describing Jeconiah in exile. The lack of "and" before Shealtiel favours the descriptive reading.

kjv: and she bare Miriam ... (v. 18) And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took
mine: These are the sons of Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered married; and she conceived and bore Miriam
note: In the MT, "these are the sons of Bithiah..." stands at the end of v. 18, which leaves "she" in v. 17 without a referent. I moved the clause to v. 17, following a common reconstruction. The KJV keeps the MT order.

kjv: his (Mered's) wife Jehudijah
mine: his (Mered's) Judahite wife
note: hayhudiyyah, with the definite article, is a gentilic ("the Judahite woman"), not a proper name. It contrasts her with the Egyptian Bithiah.

kjv: and Jashubi-lehem. And these are ancient things
mine: and returned to Lehem (now the records are ancient)
note: weyashuvi lachem may be a name or "and they returned to Lehem/Bethlehem". The phrase "the records are ancient" acknowledges that the source is old.

kjv: he (Tiglath-pileser) carried them (Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh) away
mine: he (Tiglath-pileser) took them (Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh) into exile
note: The singular verb wayyaglem after two names ("Pul ... and Tiglath-pileser") suggests the Chronicler took Pul as another name for Tiglath-pileser III, which is historically correct. Both versions preserve the singular.

kjv: the firstborn Vashni, and Abiah
mine: Joel his (Samuel's) firstborn, the second Abijah
note: The MT reads habbekhor washni wa'aviyyah ("the firstborn, and the second, Abijah"), so the firstborn's name has dropped out. 1 Sam 8:2 and the Syriac supply "Joel". The KJV takes washni ("and the second") as a name, "Vashni". KJV 6:28.

kjv: Hebron in the land of Judah, and the suburbs thereof
mine: Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands
note: migrash means the common pasture around a town. "Suburbs" now means residential outskirts. This recurs throughout vv. 40-66. KJV 6:55.

kjv: he (Ephraim) called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house
mine: he (Ephraim) called his name Beriah, because disaster had befallen his house
note: The name is a pun on bera'ah ("in disaster"). Neither version can show the wordplay in English, but both render the sense.

kjv: at Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon
mine: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon
note: The MT omits the name. I supplied "Jeiel" from the parallel list in 9:35, as several manuscripts and versions do. The KJV follows the MT.

kjv: Merib-baal
mine: Merib-baal
note: Both keep the form with "Baal". 2 Samuel calls him "Mephibosheth", with bosheth ("shame") substituted for Baal. Chronicles preserves the original names Merib-baal and Esh-baal (v. 33). There is no difference here; this is noted for the summary.

kjv: the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were carried away to Babylon
mine: the Book of the Kings of Israel. And Judah was taken into exile in Babylon
note: The Masoretic accents allow either "the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah" or a new sentence beginning "And Judah was exiled". The verbs and the logic favour the new sentence.

kjv: and the Nethinims
mine: and the temple servants
note: netinim means "the given ones", temple servants. The KJV transliterates and adds an English plural -s to a Hebrew plural.

kjv: asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit
mine: consulted a medium
note: 'ov is a necromancer or the ghost they consult (cf. 1 Sam 28). "Familiar spirit" is an obsolete term.

kjv: the chief of the captains
mine: was chief of the three
note: The ketiv reads hashsheloshim ("the thirty") and the qere hashshalishim ("the officers"). I read "the three", following the parallel 2 Sam 23:8 and the logic of vv. 12-19. The KJV follows the qere.

kjv: he (Abishai) was chief of the three ... and had a name among the three
mine: was chief of the thirty ... and won a name beside the three
note: The MT says "chief of the three", which contradicts v. 21 ("he did not attain to the three"). I read "the thirty" with the Syriac and many modern versions. The KJV keeps the MT and smooths over the contradiction in v. 21 by supplying "[first]".

kjv: Then the spirit came upon Amasai, who was chief of the captains
mine: Then the Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the thirty
note: ruach laveshah means "the spirit clothed (itself with)" Amasai (cf. Judg 6:34). The ketiv hashsheloshim means "the thirty", while the qere, followed by the KJV, reads "the officers". KJV 12:18.

kjv: the LORD, that dwelleth between the cherubims
mine: Yahweh Who sits enthroned above the cherubim
note: yoshev hakkeruvim means "who sits (enthroned on) the cherubim", which pictures the ark as God's throne. "Cherubims" double-plurals a Hebrew plural.

kjv: over against the mulberry trees
mine: opposite the balsam trees
note: bekha'im are probably balsam or baca shrubs (cf. the Valley of Baca, Ps 84:6). Mulberries are not native to the region.

kjv: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was for song: he instructed about the song
mine: Chenaniah, leader of the Levites in music, should direct the music
note: massa' means either "carrying (of the ark)" or "lifting up (of the voice) / music". Both are possible, since the chapter covers both the procession and the music.

kjv: a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine
mine: a portion of dates, and a cake of raisins
note: 'eshpar is a rare word for a portion, perhaps of dates or meat. 'ashishah is a raisin cake, not a flagon of wine.

kjv: all the gods of the people are idols
mine: all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols
note: 'elilim means "worthless things/nonentities", a pun on 'elohim. "Idols" loses the contempt and the wordplay.

kjv: worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness
mine: Worship Yahweh in the splendor of holiness
note: behadrat-qodesh may mean "in holy attire" or "in holy splendour", referring to God's appearance or to worshippers' vestments. The KJV's phrase is close but famous for its vagueness.

kjv: and Abimelech the son of Abiathar
mine: and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar
note: The MT reads "Abimelech". I follow the parallel 2 Sam 8:17 and many manuscripts in reading "Ahimelech", since ד/ר and ב/ח confusions are common. The KJV keeps the MT.

kjv: out of Mesopotamia, and out of Syria-maachah
mine: from Aram-naharaim, from Aram-maacah
note: 'aram naharayim ("Aram of the two rivers") is the upper Euphrates region. The KJV uses the Greek "Mesopotamia" and "Syria" for Aram.

kjv: and cut them (the people of Rabbah) with saws, and with harrows of iron, and with axes
mine: and set them (the people of Rabbah) to labor with saws and iron picks and axes
note: The MT reads wayyasar bammegerah ("he sawed (them) with the saw"). The parallel 2 Sam 12:31 has wayyasem ("he set them to work"), a one-letter difference. I follow the Samuel reading of forced labour. The KJV follows the MT's sense of atrocity.

kjv: of the children of the giant
mine: one of the descendants of the Rephaim
note: haRefa'im/haRafa' is a named people, or their ancestor, not a generic "giant". Same in vv. 6, 8.

kjv: he (Yahweh) repented him of the evil
mine: he (Yahweh) relented from the calamity
note: wayyinnachem 'al-hara'ah means "he relented concerning the disaster". "Repented of the evil" now suggests God had done moral wrong.

kjv: in my trouble I (David) have prepared
mine: With great pains I (David) have provided
note: be'onyi means "in my affliction" or "by my hard effort/despite my poverty". The figures that follow (100,000 talents of gold) are hyperbolic either way.

kjv: to burn incense before the LORD
mine: make offerings before Yahweh
note: lehaqtir means to make (offerings) go up in smoke; it covers burnt offerings as well as incense, so "burn incense" is narrower than the verb.

kjv: one principal household being taken for Eleazar, and [one] taken for Ithamar
mine: one father's house being chosen for Eleazar and one chosen for Ithamar
note: MT has 'ahuz 'ahuz "taken, taken" for Eleazar and 'ahuz for Ithamar: the lots alternate (two for Eleazar to one for Ithamar per the 16:8 ratio). Both renderings smooth the doubled word.

kjv: the house of Asuppim
mine: the storehouse
note: 'asuppim means "gatherings, stores"; the KJV transliterates it as if a proper name.

kjv: At Parbar westward
mine: for the parbar on the west
note: parbar (cf. parwarim 2Ki 23:11) is an architectural term, probably a colonnade or court, not a place name; still uncertain.

kjv: but he (Joab) finished not, because there fell wrath for it (the census) against Israel
mine: but did not finish; and wrath came upon Israel because of this
note: MT links the clauses with simple wayehi "and there was"; the KJV makes the wrath the reason Joab stopped, whereas the Hebrew more naturally says the census brought wrath (cf. 21:7).

kjv: all that he (David) had by the spirit
mine: all that he (David) had in mind
note: barruah 'immo "in the spirit/mind with him": ruah can be David's own mind or the divine Spirit; v.19 claims divine revelation, so the KJV's "by the spirit" is defensible but the phrase is ambiguous.

kjv: glistering stones
mine: antimony
note: 'avne puk are stones of puk, the black antimony used as eye-paint (2Ki 9:30), here perhaps a dark mortar or inlay; not "glistering".

kjv: ten thousand drams
mine: 10,000 darics
note: 'adarkonim are Persian gold darics (an anachronism showing the Chronicler's date), not Greek drachmas.

kjv: [there is] none abiding
mine: there is no hope
note: miqweh is "hope, expectation" (Ezr 10:2); the KJV's "abiding" follows the sense of permanence, close but different.

kjv: worshipped the LORD, and the king
mine: paid homage to Yahweh and to the king
note: hishtahawu is prostration; 1611 "worship" covered honor to a king, but a modern reader hears divine worship of David.

kjv: he put before the tabernacle
mine: was there before the tabernacle
note: WLC points sam "he put"; many Hebrew mss, LXX and Vulgate read sham "there", which I followed; the KJV follows the Masoretic pointing.

kjv: came [from his (Solomon's) journey] to the high place
mine: came from the high place
note: MT has labbamah "to the high place", which makes no sense of the route; I follow LXX/Vulgate "from"; the KJV keeps "to" and patches it with an italic insertion.

kjv: horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price
mine: horses were imported from Egypt and Kue ... buy them from Kue
note: miqweh/miqwe' is Kue (Cilicia), known from Assyrian texts as a horse market; the KJV took it as a common noun ("collection", hence linen yarn).

kjv: of Huram my father's
mine: Huram-abi
note: lehuram 'abi is best read as the craftsman's name Huram-abi ("Huram my father" as an honorific title); the KJV's "of Huram my father's" makes him a servant of the king's father.

kjv: these [are the things wherein] Solomon was instructed
mine: These are Solomon's measurements (foundations)
note: hussad is the hophal of yasad "to found": "this is what Solomon laid as foundation", i.e. the ground-plan; the KJV took it from an Aramaic sense "be instructed".

kjv: he (Solomon) made chains, [as] in the oracle
mine: He (Solomon) made chains like a necklace
note: MT baddebir "in the inner sanctuary" is out of place for pillar chains; I follow the common emendation karrabid "like a necklace"; the KJV keeps MT with an italic "as".

kjv: did Huram his father make
mine: Huram-abi made
note: huram 'abiw: as at 2:12, 'abi is part of the craftsman's name or an honorific ("master"), not his literal father.

kjv: the weight of the brass could not be found out
mine: the weight of the bronze was not sought
note: lo' nehqar "was not searched out": nobody bothered to weigh it, not that it was impossible.

kjv: they (the priests) drew out the staves
mine: The poles were so long
note: wayya'arikhu habbaddim "the poles were long": the hiphil of 'arak here means "be long", not "draw out" (so also 1Ki 8:8).

kjv: an house of habitation
mine: an exalted house
note: zebul is now known from Ugaritic (zbl "prince, exalted") to mean "elevated/lofty dwelling", not simply habitation.

kjv: remember the mercies of David
mine: Remember Your (Yahweh's) steadfast love for David
note: hasde dawid may be God's loyal love promised to David (Isa 55:3) or David's own loyal deeds; the KJV's "mercies of David" keeps the ambiguity, I take it as God's covenant love.

kjv: the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon
mine: the cities that Huram had given to him (Solomon)
note: natan is simply "gave"; the KJV's "restored" harmonises with 1Ki 9:11-13, where Solomon gave Hiram cities.

kjv: them (the remaining non-Israelite peoples) did Solomon make to pay tribute
mine: these Solomon drafted as forced labor
note: mas is corvée, conscripted labour gangs (cf. v.9 "made no slaves for his work"), not monetary tribute.

kjv: his (Solomon's) ascent by which he went up into the house of the LORD
mine: his (Solomon's) burnt offerings that he offered at the house of Yahweh
note: MT 'aliyyato "his ascent/upper room"; the parallel 1Ki 10:5 and the versions read 'olotaw "his burnt offerings", which I followed; the KJV keeps the Chronicles form.

kjv: Hadoram that [was] over the tribute
mine: Hadoram, who was taskmaster over the forced labor
note: 'al hammas: mas is conscripted labour, the very grievance of v.4, not taxation.

kjv: for the devils
mine: for the goat-demons
note: se'irim are "hairy ones, goats", here goat-shaped desert spirits (Lev 17:7); "devils" imports a later Christian category.

kjv: Mahalath ... to wife, [and] Abihail the daughter of Eliab
mine: Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth ... and of Abihail
note: MT lists Abihail without a conjunction; she is most naturally Mahalath's mother (v.19 "she bore" has one wife), whereas the KJV's italic "and" makes her a second wife.

kjv: And he (Rehoboam) desired many wives
mine: and sought many wives for them (Rehoboam's sons)
note: wayyish'al hamon nashim "he asked for a multitude of wives": in context (provisions for the sons) the wives are for the sons, though it can be read of Rehoboam himself.

kjv: young and tenderhearted
mine: young and irresolute
note: rak-levav is "soft of heart", i.e. timid, lacking resolve; "tenderhearted" now means compassionate.

kjv: the high places and the images (KJV 14:5)
mine: the high places and the incense altars
note: hammanim are small incense altars (inscriptions from Palmyra and Nabataea), not images.

kjv: [it is] nothing with thee (Yahweh) to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power (KJV 14:11)
mine: there is none like You (Yahweh) to help, between the mighty and the weak
note: 'en 'immekha la'zor ben rav le'en koah: either "there is no one beside you to help the weak against the strong" or "it is nothing for you to help"; both are defensible.

kjv: the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves (KJV 14:13)
mine: the Cushites fell until none remained alive
note: le'en lahem mihyah "so that there was no preserving of life to them": a total slaughter rather than merely an inability to regroup, though mihyah can mean recovery.

kjv: Israel [hath been] without the true God
mine: For a long time Israel was without the true God
note: the Hebrew is verbless ("many days to Israel without..."), so the time is open: past (the judges era), present, or a prophetic future; the KJV's present perfect is one option.

kjv: his (Jehoshaphat's) heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD
mine: His (Jehoshaphat's) heart was courageous in the ways of Yahweh
note: wayyigbah libbo usually means pride (26:16, 32:25), but here it is qualified by "in the ways of Yahweh" and is positive; the KJV's literal rendering leaves a reader suspecting arrogance.

kjv: between the joints of the harness
mine: between the scale armor and the breastplate
note: bein haddevaqim uvein hashshiryon "between the attachments and the coat of mail"; "harness" meant body armour in 1611.

kjv: when they returned to Jerusalem
mine: They (the appointed judges) had their seat at Jerusalem
note: MT wayyashuvu "and they returned" fits poorly; I follow the revocalisation wayyeshevu "and they dwelt/sat" (cf. LXX); the KJV keeps MT.

kjv: [other] beside the Ammonites
mine: some of the Meunites
note: MT mehaʿammonim "some of the Ammonites" repeats Ammon; LXX reads "Meunites" (cf. 26:7), which I followed; the KJV keeps MT and adds an italic "other".

kjv: from beyond the sea on this side Syria
mine: from Edom, from beyond the sea
note: MT me'aram "from Aram"; one Hebrew ms and most scholars read me'edom (r/d confusion), geographically required for an army at En-gedi; the KJV follows MT.

kjv: that should praise the beauty of holiness
mine: praise Him (Yahweh) in holy attire
note: lehadrat-qodesh "in holy splendour": probably the singers' sacred vestments or "the splendour of holiness" as the object of praise; both readings are defended.

kjv: riches with the dead bodies
mine: goods, clothing
note: MT ufegarim "and corpses"; several Hebrew mss and the Vulgate read uvegadim "and garments", which fits the list of spoil; the KJV follows MT.

kjv: the LORD hath broken thy (Jehoshaphat's) works
mine: Yahweh will destroy what you (Jehoshaphat) have made
note: parats is perfect; the KJV reads it as past, I read it as a prophetic perfect fulfilled in the next clause.

kjv: Forty and two years old [was] Ahaziah
mine: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old
note: MT reads 42, which would make Ahaziah two years older than his father (21:20: Jehoram died at 40); I follow 2Ki 8:26 and some LXX/Syriac witnesses (22); the KJV keeps the impossible MT figure.

kjv: And Azariah the son of Jehoram
mine: And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram
note: MT here has 'azaryahu, a scribal slip for 'ahazyahu (so many Hebrew mss, LXX, Syriac, 2Ki 8:29); the KJV reproduces the MT name, making it look like a different king.

kjv: God save the king
mine: Long live the king
note: yehi hammelekh is "may the king live"; the KJV substitutes the English royal formula and introduces "God", absent from the Hebrew.

kjv: for they (the Arameans) left him (Joash) in great diseases
mine: leaving him (Joash) severely wounded
note: mahaluyim here refers to the wounds of battle with the Arameans (cf. 22:6 makkim), not illnesses in general.

kjv: for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada
mine: because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada
note: MT bney "sons", but only Zechariah was killed (vv.20-22); I follow LXX/Vulgate singular, the KJV keeps the MT plural.

kjv: the greatness of the burdens [laid] upon him (Joash)
mine: the many oracles against him (Joash)
note: massa' is both "burden" and "prophetic oracle"; given v.19 (prophets testified), "oracles" is likely, though "burdens" (tribute, v.23) is possible.

kjv: who had understanding in the visions of God
mine: who instructed him (Uzziah) in the fear of God
note: MT bir'ot "in seeing"; many Hebrew mss, LXX, Targum and Syriac read beyir'at "in the fear (of God)", which I followed; the KJV follows MT.

kjv: dwelt in a several house
mine: lived in a separate house
note: several meant "separate" in 1611; bet hahofshit is a house of release/quarantine.

kjv: he (Ahaz) made Judah naked
mine: he (Ahaz) had let Judah run wild
note: hifria' from para' "let loose, let go unrestrained" (Ex 32:25, Prov 29:18); the KJV took it as "uncover, strip".

kjv: to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing
mine: an object of terror, of horror, and of hissing
note: shammah is "horror, appalled desolation"; 1611 "astonishment" meant stunned dismay, but now suggests mere surprise (recurs throughout Jeremiah).

kjv: [singing] with loud instruments unto the LORD
mine: singing with all their might to Yahweh
note: MT bikhle-'oz "with instruments of strength"; I follow the reading bekhol-'oz "with all might" of the parallel 1Ch 13:8; the KJV keeps MT and supplies "singing".

kjv: the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the LORD
mine: the Levites who showed good skill in the service of Yahweh
note: hammaskilim sekhel-tov layhwh "who had good insight/skill for Yahweh": probably skill in the liturgy, not teaching.

kjv: making confession to the LORD
mine: giving thanks to Yahweh
note: mitwaddim (hithpael of yadah) can be "confess" or "give praise"; with peace offerings at a joyful feast, thanksgiving is likelier.

kjv: After these things, and the establishment thereof
mine: After these things and these acts of faithfulness
note: ha'emet ha'elleh "these (acts of) faithfulness" refers to Hezekiah's faithful reforms (31:20 "faithful before Yahweh"); "establishment" misses the moral point that invasion came despite his faithfulness.

kjv: in the chiefest of the sepulchres
mine: in the upper part of the tombs
note: bema'aleh "on the ascent/upper part": a location (higher section) rather than necessarily the most honoured tomb, though it may imply honour.

kjv: he (Manasseh) caused his children to pass through the fire
mine: he (Manasseh) burned his sons as an offering
note: he'evir ba'esh "made pass through fire": the KJV is literal; I take it, with 28:3 (wayyab'er "burned") and Jer 7:31, as child sacrifice rather than a fire ordeal.

kjv: which took Manasseh among the thorns
mine: who captured Manasseh with hooks
note: bahohim: hoah is "thorn", but here the hooks put through captives' noses or lips, as shown in Assyrian reliefs (cf. 2Ki 19:28 "my hook in your nose"); "among the thorns" pictures him hiding in a thicket.

kjv: written among the sayings of the seers
mine: written in the Chronicles of Hozai
note: MT divre hozay: either a source named after a seer Hozai or a slip for hahozim "the seers" (LXX); the KJV takes it as a plural common noun.

kjv: with their mattocks round about
mine: in their ruins all around
note: the qere beharvotehem is "in their ruins" (horvah) or "with their swords"; "mattocks" reflects a guess at a tool sense.

kjv: and they returned to Jerusalem
mine: and from the inhabitants of Jerusalem
note: I follow the ketiv weyoshve "and the inhabitants of", which completes the list of contributors; the KJV follows the qere wayyashuvu "and they returned".

kjv: she (Huldah) dwelt in Jerusalem in the college
mine: she (Huldah) lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter
note: bammishneh "in the second (district)" is a newer quarter of the city (Zeph 1:10); the KJV's "college" (following Targum's "house of instruction") makes Huldah a resident of a school.

kjv: until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths
mine: until the land had made up for its Sabbaths
note: ratsetah is from ratsah II "pay off, make restitution" (Lev 26:34,43): the land repays the Sabbath years it was denied; "enjoyed" takes the more common ratsah "be pleased with".

kjv: The Nethinims
mine: The temple servants
note: hannetinim "the given ones", temple servants (Num 31:47 sense); the KJV transliterates and adds an English plural to a Hebrew plural (recurs in Ezra-Nehemiah).

kjv: the Tirshatha
mine: The governor
note: tirshata' is a Persian title (cf. Old Persian *tarsta "the one to be feared"), i.e. the governor (Neh 8:9 of Nehemiah); the KJV leaves it untranslated.

kjv: drams of gold ... five thousand pound of silver
mine: darics of gold ... 5,000 minas of silver
note: darkemonim are Persian darics (or Greek drachmas); maneh is a mina (c. 0.5 kg), not an English pound.

kjv: written in the Syrian tongue
mine: written in Aramaic
note: 'aramit is Aramaic, the Persian chancery language (the text itself switches to Aramaic at 4:8); "Syrian tongue" suggests later Syriac.

kjv: the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites ... the Dehavites
mine: the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech ... that is, the Elamites
note: several of these Aramaic words are now known to be Persian official titles (dinaye "judges", 'afarsatkaye "envoys", tarpelaye "officials"), and dehaye is the relative "that is"; the KJV turns all of them into ethnic groups.

kjv: on this side the river, and at such a time
mine: Beyond the River, and now
note: 'avar nahara is the Persian province "Beyond the River" (west of the Euphrates, seen from Persia); ukhe'enet is the letter formula "and now", not "at such a time".

kjv: at Achmetha
mine: in Ecbatana
note: 'ahmeta' is the Aramaic form of Ecbatana (Hamadan), the Median summer capital; the KJV transliterates it as an unknown place.

kjv: your (Tattenai's) companions the Apharsachites
mine: your (Tattenai's) associates the governors
note: 'afarsekhaye is a Persian official title (cf. 4:9, 5:6), not an ethnic group.

kjv: being set up, let him be hanged thereon
mine: he shall be impaled on it
note: zeqif yitmehe 'alohi "raised up, he shall be struck/fixed on it" describes Persian impalement; "hanged" suggests a noose.

kjv: a ready scribe in the law of Moses
mine: a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses
note: sofer mahir "a skilled/expert scribe" (Ps 45:1); 1611 "ready" meant adept, a modern reader hears "prepared".

kjv: perfect [peace], and at such a time
mine: Peace. And now
note: gemir "complete" stands for the greeting (KJV supplies "peace"), and ukhe'enet is the epistolary "and now", not a time reference (cf. 4:10).

kjv: unto the king's lieutenants
mine: to the king's satraps
note: 'ahashdarpenim is the Persian title khshathrapavan "satrap", governor of a major province; "lieutenants" understates the office.

kjv: according to the counsel of my lord
mine: according to the counsel of the Lord
note: MT points 'adonay (the divine title); the KJV reads 'adoni "my lord", i.e. Ezra, which fits Shecaniah addressing him; the consonants allow both.

kjv: were employed about this [matter:] and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them (Jonathan and Jahzeiah)
mine: opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them (Jonathan and Jahzeiah)
note: 'amdu 'al-zot "stood over/against this": most now take it as opposition to the procedure (cf. 1Ch 21:1, Dan 8:25 'amad 'al "stand against"); the KJV makes them the officials in charge of it.

kjv: And Bani, and Binnui, Shimei
mine: Of the sons of Binnui: Shimei
note: MT ubani ubinnui reads as two more names; I follow LXX and 1 Esdras 9:34 mibbene binnui "of the sons of Binnui", a new family heading matching the list's pattern.

kjv: the gates of the palace which [appertained] to the house
mine: the gates of the fortress of the temple
note: habbirah 'asher-labbayit is the temple citadel (later the Hasmonean Baris / Antonia), a fortification, not a palace.

kjv: the work of their (the Tekoite nobles') Lord
mine: the work of their (the Tekoite nobles') lord
note: 'adonehem "their lords/master" may be God (KJV capital L) or their human overseer (Nehemiah or the governor); the plural of majesty fits either.

kjv: From all places whence ye shall return unto us [they will be upon you] (KJV 4:12)
mine: You must return to us.
note: the Hebrew mikkol-hammeqomot 'asher tashuvu 'alenu is elliptical: either the outlying Jews urging the workers to come home, or warning that the enemy would attack "from every place"; the KJV supplies a whole clause in italics.

kjv: [saving that] every one put them (their clothes) off for washing (KJV 4:23)
mine: each kept his weapon at his right hand
note: MT 'ish shilho hammayim "each his weapon the water" is unintelligible; I follow the common emendation bimino "in his right hand"; the KJV guesses "for washing".

kjv: would go into the temple to save his life
mine: could go into the temple and live
note: wahay "and live": either a layman entering the sanctuary would die for it (Num 18:7), or he would go in to save his life; the KJV chooses the second.

kjv: all the heathen ... saw [these things], they were much cast down
mine: all the nations around us were afraid and fell greatly in their own esteem
note: wayyir'u can be read "they saw" (from ra'ah) or "they feared" (from yare'); the following "fell in their own eyes" favours fear, the KJV takes "saw".

kjv: Their (the returned exiles') horses, seven hundred thirty and six: their mules, two hundred forty and five (KJV 7:68)
mine: (absent)
note: the Leningrad Codex lacks this verse; it is found in many Hebrew mss and matches Ezr 2:66, and the KJV (from printed Hebrew Bibles) includes it, which shifts its numbering from here to the end of the chapter.

kjv: The Tirshatha gave to the treasure a thousand drams of gold
mine: The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 darics of gold
note: as at Ezr 2:63,69: tirshata' is the Persian title "governor", and darkemonim are darics.

kjv: pine branches
mine: wild olive
note: 'ets shemen "oil tree" is probably the wild olive or oleaster (1Ki 6:23 olivewood), not pine.

kjv: Zabdiel, the son of [one of] the great men
mine: Zabdiel the son of Haggedolim
note: ben-haggedolim may be a family name or "son of the great ones"; the KJV paraphrases with italics.

kjv: of the Levites [were] divisions [in] Judah, [and] in Benjamin
mine: certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were joined to Benjamin
note: mahleqot yehudah levinyamin "divisions of Judah (belonged) to Benjamin": some Judahite Levite groups were settled with Benjamin; the KJV's two italic insertions make it a simple list.

kjv: keeping the ward at the thresholds of the gates
mine: standing guard at the storehouses of the gates
note: ba'asuppe hashe'arim: 'asuppim are storehouses (1Ch 26:15,17), not thresholds.

kjv: the other [company] went over against [them] (the first choir)
mine: The other choir ... went to the north
note: MT lemo'l "in front of" is odd for a procession going the opposite way; I follow the common emendation lismol "to the left", i.e. north, matching v.31 "to the right"; the KJV keeps MT.

kjv: white, green, and blue, [hangings]
mine: white cotton curtains and violet hangings
note: karpas is the Persian/Sanskrit word for fine cotton (karpasa), not the colour green; the paving stones (bahat, dar, soharet) are also kinds of stone rather than colours.

kjv: that [it] should be published according to the language of every people
mine: and speak according to the language of his people
note: umedabber kilshon 'ammo "and speaking in the language of his people" is part of the decree (the husband's language rules the home); the KJV makes it a note about publication.

kjv: it [is] not for the king's profit to suffer them (the Jews)
mine: it is not to the king's profit to tolerate them (the Jews)
note: lehanniham "to leave them alone"; "suffer" in 1611 meant "allow, tolerate".

kjv: [then] shall there enlargement and deliverance arise
mine: relief and deliverance will rise
note: rewah is "relief, respite" (lit. breathing space); "enlargement" in this sense (release from confinement) is now obsolete.

kjv: the crown royal which is set upon his head
mine: and on whose (the horse's) head a royal crown is set
note: wa'asher nittan keter malkhut berosho "and on whose head a royal crown has been placed": grammatically it refers to the horse (Assyrian and Persian reliefs show crested royal horses); the KJV makes it the king's crown worn by the honoree.

kjv: although the enemy could not countervail the king's damage
mine: for our affliction would not be worth troubling the king
note: ki 'en hatsar showeh benezeq hammelekh: tsar can be "enemy" or "distress", nezeq "damage/annoyance"; most now read "the trouble would not be worth bothering the king", the KJV reads "the enemy could not make up the king's loss".

kjv: riders on mules, camels, [and] young dromedaries
mine: riding on swift horses that were used in the king's service, bred from the royal stud
note: rekhesh is a swift steed, 'ahashteranim a Persian loanword "royal", bene haramakhim "offspring of the (royal) mares"; the KJV guessed three different animals.

kjv: the posts that rode upon mules [and] camels
mine: the couriers, mounted on their swift horses that were used in the king's service
note: as in v.10: rokhve harekhesh ha'ahashteranim are riders of royal horses, not mules and camels.

kjv: laid a tribute upon the land
mine: imposed forced labor on the land
note: mas is usually corvée labour (cf. 1Ki 5:13); in a Persian setting it may mean tribute in general, so the KJV's choice is defensible.

kjv: and Satan came also among them
mine: and the Satan also came among them
note: hassatan has the article throughout Job 1-2: "the adversary/accuser", a role in the heavenly court rather than a personal name; the KJV's "Satan" reads in the later developed figure of the devil.

kjv: darkness and the shadow of death
mine: gloom and deep darkness
note: tsalmawet is now usually vocalised tsalmut "deep darkness" (from tslm "be dark"); the traditional "shadow of death" (tsel + mawet) is a folk etymology, though it may be an intended wordplay (recurs Ps 23:4).

kjv: who are ready to raise up their mourning
mine: who are ready to rouse up Leviathan
note: liwyatan is the chaos sea-monster (41:1); the KJV took it as liwyatam "their mourning/companion", losing the mythological image of sorcerers who can wake the dragon.

kjv: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
mine: Can mortal man be in the right before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?
note: ha'enosh me'eloah yitsdaq: min can be comparative ("than God") or "before, in relation to God"; the question is whether any human can be justified before God, not whether a human outranks him in justice.

kjv: Doth not their (mortals') excellency [which is] in them go away?
mine: Is not their (mortals') tent-cord plucked up within them?
note: yitram here is the tent-cord (Judg 16:7 yeter "cord"), with nissa' "pulled up" a tent image for death; the KJV took yeter as "excellence, superiority".

kjv: envy slayeth the silly one
mine: jealousy slays the simple
note: poteh is the naive, easily-led person; in 1611 "silly" meant "simple, defenceless", now it means "foolish, frivolous".

kjv: and the robber swalloweth up their substance
mine: and the thirsty pant after his (the fool's) wealth
note: MT tsammim is obscure (perhaps "snare"); I follow the reading tseme'im "thirsty ones" (Syriac, Vulgate), the KJV follows a guess "robber".

kjv: thou (Job) shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin
mine: you (Job) shall inspect your fold and miss nothing
note: hata' here has its basic sense "miss (the mark)": counting the flock he finds none missing; the KJV gives the moral sense "sin".

kjv: therefore my (Job's) words are swallowed up
mine: therefore my (Job's) words have been rash
note: la'u is from la'a' "speak wildly" (Prov 20:25), not bala' "swallow".

kjv: the white of an egg
mine: the juice of the mallow
note: rir hallamut is the slimy juice of a plant, probably mallow or purslane (Talmudic hallamit); "white of an egg" is a rabbinic guess.

kjv: To him that is afflicted pity [should be shewed] from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty
mine: He who withholds kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty
note: MT lammas is obscure: "to the despairing (belongs) kindness from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty" (close to KJV) or, reading lammoneah "he who withholds", a saying about the friend; both are defended.

kjv: For now ye (Job's friends) are nothing
mine: For you (Job's friends) have now become such to me (Job)
note: the ketiv lo' "not" yields the KJV's "you are nothing"; I follow the qere lo "(such) to it/him", i.e. like the dry wadi just described.

kjv: [Is there] not an appointed time to man upon earth?
mine: Has not man hard service on earth?
note: tsava' is military service or forced labour (Isa 40:2 "her warfare"), parallel to the hired labourer; "appointed time" softens the image.

kjv: Am I (Job) a sea, or a whale
mine: Am I (Job) the sea, or a sea monster
note: tannin is the mythical sea dragon paired with Yam (the Sea), forces God must guard; "whale" turns a cosmic monster into a mammal.

kjv: I (Job) have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men?
mine: If I (Job) sin, what do I do to You, You watcher of mankind?
note: hata'ti is best taken conditionally (Job denies guilt elsewhere), and notser ha'adam is the God who watches over humans, here bitterly "keeps watch on"; "preserver" reads it as kindness.

kjv: the hypocrite's hope shall perish
mine: the hope of the godless shall perish
note: hanef means "godless, profane"; "hypocrite" (from the LXX/Vulgate hypokrites) narrows it to pretence (recurs throughout Job).

kjv: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades
mine: Who made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades
note: 'ash is probably the Great Bear (Ursa Major) or the Lion, not the single star Arcturus; kesil and kimah are Orion and the Pleiades (as in KJV).

kjv: the proud helpers do stoop under him (God)
mine: beneath Him (God) bowed the helpers of Rahab
note: rahav here is the name of the primeval sea monster (26:12, Isa 51:9), whose allies were subdued at creation; the KJV renders it as the common noun "pride".

kjv: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us (Job and God)
mine: There is no arbiter between us (Job and God)
note: mokhiah is an arbiter or umpire; "daysman" (one who fixes a day for hearing) is obsolete.

kjv: For it increaseth. Thou (God) huntest me (Job) as a fierce lion
mine: And were my head lifted up, You (God) would hunt me (Job) like a lion
note: weyig'eh "and should it rise up": the subject is most naturally Job's head from v.15; the KJV supplies an indefinite "it increaseth".

kjv: For vain man would be wise, though man be born [like] a wild ass's colt
mine: But a stupid man will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a man!
note: the line is a sarcastic proverb of impossibility: 'ish navuv yillavev we'ayir pere' 'adam yiwwaled "an empty man will get a heart when a wild ass is born human"; the KJV turns it into a statement about human pretension.

kjv: [is as] a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease
mine: In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune
note: lappid is better read lefid "for misfortune" (pid "disaster", 30:24, 31:29) than as lappid "torch"; the comfortable despise the unfortunate.

kjv: into whose hand God bringeth [abundantly]
mine: who bring their god in their hand
note: la'asher hevi' eloah beyado: either "who carry (their) god in their hand", i.e. their own might is their god (Hab 1:11), or the KJV's "whom God has put in their power"; the KJV supplies "abundantly".

kjv: Your (Job's friends') remembrances [are] like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay
mine: Your (Job's friends') maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay
note: zikhronekhem are their memorable sayings, and gabbekhem their "bosses/defences" (shield bosses, breastworks), not bodies.

kjv: For now thou (God) numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?
mine: For then You (God) would number my steps; You would not keep watch over my sin
note: vv.15-17 continue Job's wish for a future reconciliation ("then you would..."); the KJV reads v.16 as present complaint and the second line as a question.

kjv: Hast thou (Job) heard the secret of God?
mine: Have you (Job) listened in the council of God?
note: besod 'eloah: sod is first the intimate council or assembly (Jer 23:18,22, the heavenly council), and only by extension its secret deliberations.

kjv: is there any secret thing with thee (Job)?
mine: or the word that deals gently with you (Job)?
note: wedavar la'at 'immakh: la'at means "gently" (2Sa 18:5), referring to the friends' mild words; the KJV derived it from la'at "secretly".

kjv: and aforetime I (Job) was as a tabret
mine: and I (Job) am one before whom men spit
note: tofet lefanim is "spitting in the face" (from tuf "spit", cf. 30:10); the KJV derived it from tof "drum, tambourine" and lefanim "formerly".

kjv: They that come after [him] (the wicked man) shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted
mine: They of the west are appalled at his (the wicked man's) day, and horror seizes them of the east
note: 'aharonim and qadmonim can mean "later/earlier" generations or "western/eastern" peoples (directions face east: behind = west); the spatial reading gives a universal horror, the KJV's temporal one a historical sequence.

kjv: though I (Job) intreated for the children's [sake] of mine own body
mine: and I (Job) am a stench to the children of my own mother
note: hannoti is from hnn II "be loathsome" (parallel "my breath is strange"), and bene bitni are "the sons of my womb", i.e. of the womb that bore me, his brothers; the KJV takes hnn I "plead" and makes them Job's own children (who are dead, 1:19).

kjv: he (Job's Redeemer) shall stand at the latter [day] upon the earth
mine: at the last He (Job's Redeemer) will stand upon the dust
note: we'aharon is adverbial "at the last" or a title "as the Last/Afterward one"; the KJV's italic "day" makes it the eschatological Last Day, and 'afar "dust" may also be the grave.

kjv: And [though] after my (Job's) skin [worms] destroy this [body], yet in my flesh shall I see God
mine: And after my (Job's) skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall see God
note: the Hebrew has no "worms" or "body" (both KJV italics), and mibbesari can mean "from (within) my flesh", i.e. still embodied, or "apart from my flesh"; the KJV commits the verse to a bodily-resurrection reading that the Hebrew allows but does not state. Context: 'from my flesh' (ambiguity kept; most read embodied sight) (medium confidence). 'From my flesh' keeps the Hebrew min open: 'from within' (embodied sight, supported by 19:27 'my eyes shall behold, and not another') or 'apart from'. ESV, NIV, NRSV, NJPS and CSB render 'in my flesh'; NASB 'from my flesh'. Whether Job means after death, resurrection, or vindication before death stays open. Other possible meanings: (1) 'without/apart from my flesh', seeing God after death — RSV, ESV/NIV/NRSV footnotes, many critical commentators; (2) 'in my flesh', bodily resurrection — Vulgate (in carne mea), KJV, traditional Christian reading; (3) 'while still in my flesh', before death — NJPS.

kjv: and shall rain [it] upon him (the wicked man) while he is eating
mine: and rain it upon him (the wicked man) into his body
note: bilhumo is "into his flesh/body" (lahum, cf. Zeph 1:17) rather than "in his eating" (lehem); the KJV reads it from "bread".

kjv: and in a moment go down to the grave
mine: and in peace they (the wicked) go down to Sheol
note: uverega' can be "in a moment" (a quick, painless death) or "in tranquillity" (raga' "be at rest"); either way the point is an untroubled end, not sudden punishment.

kjv: His breasts are full of milk
mine: his pails full of milk
note: 'atinaw is a hapax; "his pails/vats" or "his haunches (full of fat)" are proposed; "breasts" of a man is unlikely.

kjv: the Almighty shall be thy (Job's) defence
mine: the Almighty will be your (Job's) gold
note: betsarekha here continues the wordplay with betser "gold ore" in v.24, not "defence/fortress".

kjv: thou (Job) shalt say, [There is] lifting up
mine: you (Job) say, 'It is because of pride'
note: gewah means "pride" (33:17) or "lifting up"; the line is obscure, and either reading is defended.

kjv: He (God) shall deliver the island of the innocent
mine: He (God) delivers even the one who is not innocent
note: 'i-naqi: 'i is the rare negative "not" (1Sa 4:21 'i-khavod), so "the not-innocent"; the KJV took 'i as "island", producing nonsense.

kjv: No; but he (God) would put [strength] in me
mine: No; He (God) would pay attention to me
note: lo' 'akh-hu' yasim bi "surely he would set (his mind) on me", i.e. give me a hearing (cf. 4:20 sim "regard"); the KJV supplies "strength".

kjv: Because I (Job) was not cut off before the darkness, [neither] hath he (God) covered the darkness from my face
mine: yet I (Job) am not silenced because of the darkness, nor because thick darkness covers my face
note: nitsmatti can mean "silenced/annihilated" and mippene "because of/before"; the line is obscure, and the KJV's italic "neither" reverses the second clause.

kjv: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?
mine: Why are not times of judgment kept by the Almighty, and why do those who know Him never see His days?
note: lo'-nitspenu means "are not stored up / reserved" (cf. 15:20, 21:19 tsafan "store up"): God does not set days of reckoning; the KJV's "not hidden" turns it into a statement of God's knowledge.

kjv: yet God layeth not folly [to them]
mine: yet God charges no one with wrong
note: lo'-yasim tiflah: God does not regard (it as) wrong/unseemly; the subject is God's inaction toward the oppressors, and "folly" is an over-literal rendering of tiflah "unseemliness, wrongdoing" (cf. 1:22).

kjv: Dead [things] are formed from under the waters
mine: The dead tremble under the waters
note: harefa'im are the shades of the dead (Isa 14:9), and yeholalu is "writhe, tremble" (hul); the KJV's "dead things are formed" takes hul in the sense "be brought forth".

kjv: Hell [is] naked before him (God), and destruction hath no covering
mine: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering
note: she'ol and 'avaddon are names of the underworld (Abaddon "place of destruction", cf. Rev 9:11); "Hell" imports later ideas of punishment and "destruction" hides the proper name.

kjv: by his (God's) understanding he smiteth through the proud
mine: by His (God's) understanding He shattered Rahab
note: as at 9:13, rahav is the primeval sea monster, parallel to "the sea" in the first line.

kjv: his (God's) hand hath formed the crooked serpent
mine: His (God's) hand pierced the fleeing serpent
note: holelah is "pierced" (Isa 51:9 mehollelet tannin), and nahash bariah "the fleeing/gliding serpent" is the sea dragon of Isa 27:1; the KJV makes God the creator, not the slayer, of the monster.

kjv: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; [even the waters] forgotten of the foot: they are dried up
mine: He (man) opens shafts in a valley away from where anyone lives; they are forgotten by travelers; they hang in the air
note: the context is mining: nahal is a shaft or gully, and dallu "they dangle" describes miners suspended on ropes; the KJV pictures floods and drying waters.

kjv: the price of wisdom [is] above rubies
mine: the price of wisdom is above pearls
note: peninim are probably pearls or red coral; "rubies" is a traditional guess (also Prov 3:15, 31:10).

kjv: juniper roots [for] their (Job's mockers') meat
mine: the roots of the broom tree for their (Job's mockers') food
note: rotem is the white broom (Retama raetam), as in 1Ki 19:4; "juniper" is a traditional misidentification.

kjv: I (Job) am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls
mine: I (Job) am a brother of jackals and a companion of ostriches
note: tannim (plural of tan) are jackals, whose howling suits lament (Mic 1:8), and benot ya'anah are ostriches; the KJV's "dragons" and "owls" recur throughout the prophets.

kjv: behold, my desire [is, that] the Almighty would answer me (Job)
mine: Here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me (Job)!
note: hen-tawi "here is my taw", the mark or signature (taw was the cross-shaped last letter) put to a legal deposition; the KJV's "my desire" is a guess.

kjv: Behold, I (Elihu) [am] according to thy (Job's) wish in God's stead
mine: Behold, I (Elihu) am toward God as you (Job) are
note: hen-'ani khefikha la'el "I am like your mouth (= like you) toward God": Elihu says he is a fellow creature, not God's spokesman; the KJV's "according to thy wish in God's stead" makes him claim to stand in for God.

kjv: and sealeth their instruction
mine: and terrifies them with warnings
note: MT yahtom "he seals"; I follow LXX and the common revocalisation yehittem "he terrifies", which matches the night-vision context (cf. 7:14).

kjv: He (God) looketh upon men, and [if any] say, I have sinned ... and it profited me not
mine: He (the restored man) sings before men and says: 'I sinned ... and it was not repaid to me'
note: yashor is from shir "sing" (or shur "look"); with the restored man's testimony following, he sings to others; lo' shawah li means "it was not requited to me", not "it profited me not".

kjv: He (God) will deliver his soul from going into the pit
mine: He (God) has redeemed my (the restored man's) soul from going down into the pit
note: the ketiv napshi ... wehayyati "my soul ... my life" continues the man's first-person song; the KJV follows the qere "his soul ... his life".

kjv: [yet] judgment [is] before him (God); therefore trust thou (Job) in him
mine: that the case is before Him (God), and you (Job) are waiting for Him
note: din lefanaw ut(e)holel lo continues Job's complaint (the case is lodged, and he waits); the KJV turns it into Elihu's exhortation "trust thou in him".

kjv: yet he (God) knoweth [it] not in great extremity
mine: and He (God) does not take much note of transgression
note: bappash is a hapax, probably "arrogance/transgression" (cf. pesha'); "in great extremity" is a guess.

kjv: and their (the godless') life [is] among the unclean
mine: and their (the godless') life ends among the cult prostitutes
note: qedeshim are male cult prostitutes (Deut 23:17, 1Ki 14:24), who apparently died young; "the unclean" blurs the reference.

kjv: Fair weather cometh out of the north
mine: Out of the north comes golden splendor
note: zahav is "gold", here the golden radiance of the theophany (or, as some think, the gold guarded in the north); "fair weather" is an interpretive guess.

kjv: the sweet influences of Pleiades
mine: the chains of the Pleiades
note: ma'adannot is probably "bonds, fetters" (from 'nd "bind", metathesis of 'dn), matching "cords of Orion"; "sweet influences" derives it from 'eden "delight" with an astrological gloss.

kjv: guide Arcturus with his sons
mine: guide the Bear with its children
note: 'ayish is the Great Bear constellation, whose "children" are the stars of its tail; Arcturus is a single star.

kjv: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?
mine: Who has put wisdom in the ibis or given understanding to the rooster?
note: tuhot and sekhwi are rare words; in a list of creatures they are most likely birds that forecast weather (ibis for the Nile flood, rooster for dawn), though "inward parts" (Ps 51:6) is possible.

kjv: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee (Job)
mine: Is the wild ox willing to serve you (Job)?
note: re'em is the aurochs or wild ox (Akkadian rimu), a real two-horned animal; "unicorn" comes from the LXX monokeros.

kjv: [Gavest thou] the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
mine: The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the pinions and plumage of love?
note: renanim "the shrill-voiced ones" are ostriches (the subject of vv.13-18), and hasidah is the stork, whose name means "the loyal/kind one", contrasted with the ostrich's neglect; the KJV supplies a question and two wrong birds.

kjv: hast thou (Job) clothed his (the horse's) neck with thunder?
mine: Do you (Job) clothe his (the horse's) neck with a mane?
note: ra'mah is the "quivering" mane (from r'm "tremble"); the KJV linked it to ra'am "thunder".

kjv: Behold, I (Job) am vile
mine: Behold, I (Job) am of small account
note: qalloti "I am light, insignificant" (opposite of kavod "weighty"); "vile" suggests moral baseness, which Job does not confess.

kjv: Behold, he (Behemoth) drinketh up a river, [and] hasteth not
mine: Behold, if the river is turbulent he (Behemoth) is not frightened
note: ya'ashoq nahar lo' yahpoz: the river "oppresses/surges" and he is not alarmed (hafaz "be in haste, alarmed"); the KJV makes the beast drink the river dry.

kjv: by reason of breakings they (the mighty) purify themselves (KJV 41:25)
mine: at the crashing they (the mighty) are beside themselves
note: yithatta'u here is "they lose themselves, are bewildered" (from hata' "miss"), not the ritual "purify themselves".

kjv: Wherefore I (Job) abhor [myself], and repent in dust and ashes
mine: I (Job) reject my words and repent
note: 'em'as has no object in Hebrew (KJV supplies "myself"), and nihamti 'al can mean "repent of" or "be comforted concerning"; whether Job confesses guilt or retracts his lawsuit and accepts consolation is the central interpretive crux of the book. Context: I reject my words and repent (low confidence). 'Em'as has no object: 42:3 ('I spoke what I did not understand') favours rejecting his words, though 'despise myself' (LXX, Vulgate) is equally defensible. Nicham 'al most naturally means 'repent/relent' here (ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, CSB, NET); 'be consoled' (Targum) is a minority reading. Whether he repents of sin or of his lawsuit stays open; 42:7 affirms Job. Other possible meanings: (1) 'I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes' — LXX, Vulgate, KJV, ESV, NIV, NRSV, NET; (2) 'I recant and relent, being but dust and ashes' (creaturely humility, cf. Gen 18:27) — NJPS, CSB; (3) 'I am consoled concerning dust and ashes' or 'I repent of dust and ashes' (cease mourning) — Targum, some modern commentators; (4) 'I melt away' — LXX etaken, some scholars.

kjv: the LORD turned the captivity of Job
mine: Yahweh restored the fortunes of Job
note: shav 'et-shevut is an idiom "restore the fortunes" (Deut 30:3, Ps 126:4); Job was never a captive.

kjv: when his wrath is kindled but a little
mine: for His wrath is quickly kindled
note: ki-yiv'ar kim'at 'appo: kim'at can be "soon, quickly" or "a little"; the warning is that his anger flares quickly, not that a small amount suffices.

kjv: will ye (men) love vanity, [and] seek after leasing? (KJV 4:2)
mine: How long will you (men) love vain words and seek after lies?
note: kazav is "lie, falsehood"; "leasing" (Old English leasung "lying") is obsolete and now suggests rental (also Ps 5:6).

kjv: Stand in awe, and sin not (KJV 4:4)
mine: Be angry, and do not sin
note: rigzu means "tremble, be agitated", whether with fear or anger; the LXX "be angry" is quoted in Eph 4:26, while the KJV chooses awe.

kjv: thou (Yahweh) shalt destroy them that speak leasing (KJV 5:6)
mine: You (Yahweh) destroy those who speak lies
note: as at 4:3, kazav is "lies"; "leasing" is obsolete.

kjv: (yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy:) (KJV 7:4)
mine: or plundered my enemy without cause
note: wa'ahalletsah can be "rescue" or "despoil" (hlts II, cf. Aramaic); in a list of oaths of innocence "plundered" fits, while the KJV makes it a parenthesis about sparing his enemy.

kjv: he (God) ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors (KJV 7:13)
mine: making His (God's) arrows fiery shafts
note: hitsaw ledoleqim yif'al "he makes his arrows into burning ones" (dalaq "burn"); the KJV took doleqim as "pursuers" (Aramaic sense).

kjv: a little lower than the angels (KJV 8:5)
mine: a little lower than God
note: me'elohim is "than God" or "than divine beings"; the KJV follows the LXX "angels", which Heb 2:7 quotes, but the Hebrew sets humanity just below God himself.

kjv: The wicked shall be turned into hell (KJV 9:17)
