mine: The wicked shall return to Sheol
note: she'olah "to Sheol", the realm of all the dead (6:6); "hell" makes it a place of eternal punishment, a later concept. The KJV renders Sheol "hell" 31 times, "grave" 31 times and "pit" 3 times.

kjv: and blesseth the covetous, [whom] the LORD abhorreth
mine: and the one greedy for gain curses and renounces Yahweh
note: uvotsea' berekh ni'ets yhwh: botsea' is most naturally the subject ("the greedy man"), and berekh "bless" is the scribal euphemism for "curse" (as in Job 1:5) paired with ni'ets "spurns"; the KJV makes the wicked bless the greedy and God abhor them. Context: the greedy man curses and renounces Yahweh (low confidence). Ni'ets with God as object recurs in 10:13 ('why does the wicked renounce God?'), so 'renounces Yahweh' is secure. Barakh is unsettled: 'curses' (scribal euphemism, as Job 1:5; 1 Kgs 21:10) with the greedy man as subject (ESV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS), or the wicked 'blesses the greedy' (NIV, CSB, NET). Other possible meanings: (1) 'he blesses the greedy and spurns Yahweh' — NIV, CSB, NET; (2) 'the greedy man blesses himself', i.e. boasts — some commentators; (3) 'blesses the covetous, whom Yahweh abhors', Yahweh as subject — KJV (less likely given 10:13); (4) 'the unjust man is blessed' — LXX, Vulgate.

kjv: His (the wicked man's) ways are always grievous
mine: His (the wicked man's) ways prosper at all times
note: yahilu derakhaw: hyl/hwl here means "be firm, prosper" (cf. Job 20:21), not "be grievous".

kjv: Upon the wicked he (Yahweh) shall rain snares
mine: Let Him (Yahweh) rain coals on the wicked
note: MT pahim "snares" sits oddly with rain and fire; I follow Symmachus and the common revocalisation pahame "coals of"; the KJV keeps MT.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will set [him] (the needy) in safety [from him that] puffeth at him (KJV 12:5)
mine: I (Yahweh) will place him (the needy) in the safety for which he longs
note: 'ashit beyesha' yafiah lo: yafiah can be "pant/long for" (Hab 2:3) or "snort at" (10:5); the KJV supplies "from him that" to make it the enemy's contempt.

kjv: when the LORD bringeth back the captivity of his people
mine: When Yahweh restores the fortunes of His people
note: shuv shevut is the idiom "restore the fortunes" (cf. Job 42:10); "bring back the captivity" assumes an exile the psalm may not refer to (recurs Ps 53:6, 85:1, 126:1,4).

kjv: [O my soul], thou hast said unto the LORD
mine: I say to Yahweh
note: MT 'amart is a feminine "you said"; I read 'amarti "I said" (many Hebrew mss, LXX, Syriac); the KJV keeps the form and supplies "O my soul" in italics.

kjv: my goodness [extendeth] not to thee (Yahweh)
mine: I have no good apart from You (Yahweh)
note: tovati bal-'aleykha "my good is not beyond/apart from you": God is the psalmist's only good; the KJV makes it a statement that his goodness cannot benefit God.

kjv: thou (Yahweh) wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption
mine: You (Yahweh) will not abandon My soul to Sheol, nor let Your faithful one see the pit
note: hasidekha is "your faithful/devoted one" (not the title "Holy One"), she'ol is the realm of the dead, and shahat is "the pit"; the KJV follows the LXX diaphthora "corruption" as quoted in Acts 2:27 and 13:35, where the verse is applied to Jesus' resurrection.

kjv: whose belly thou (Yahweh) fillest with thy hid [treasure]
mine: You (Yahweh) fill their womb with treasure
note: utsefunkha "your stored-up things" may be God's provisions for the wicked or his stored-up punishment for them (cf. Job 21:19); the line is obscure and the KJV and I read it similarly, but the KJV's "men [which are] thy hand" reverses "from men by your hand".

kjv: The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid (KJV 18:4)
mine: The cords of death encompassed me; the torrents of destruction assailed me
note: hevle mawet are "cords of death" (parallel "cords of Sheol", "snares of death"), though hevel can also mean "pangs"; nahale veliya'al are "torrents of destruction/Belial", the chaos waters, not "ungodly men".

kjv: with the froward thou (Yahweh) wilt shew thyself froward (KJV 18:26)
mine: with the crooked You (Yahweh) make Yourself seem tortuous
note: 'iqqesh "crooked, perverse" and titpattal "you show yourself twisted/shrewd"; "froward" is obsolete (cf. 2Sa 22:27).

kjv: [There is] no speech nor language, [where] their (the heavens') voice is not heard (KJV 19:3)
mine: There is no speech, nor are there words; their (the heavens') voice is not heard
note: 'en-'omer we'en devarim beli nishma' qolam: the heavens' testimony is wordless, "without their voice being heard"; the KJV's italic "where" reverses it into a claim that their voice is heard in every language.

kjv: Save, LORD: let the king hear us when we call (KJV 20:9)
mine: O Yahweh, save the king! May he answer us when we call
note: MT yhwh hoshi'ah hammelekh ya'anenu can be divided "save, O Yahweh; may the King (God) answer us" (KJV) or "save the king; may he answer us" (LXX); the KJV's "hear" for ya'aneh is close enough.

kjv: my darling from the power of the dog (KJV 22:20)
mine: My precious life from the power of the dog
note: yehidati "my only one" = my unique life (parallel "my soul"); "darling" now means a loved person.

kjv: from the horns of the unicorns (KJV 22:21)
mine: From the horns of the wild oxen
note: re'emim are wild oxen (cf. Job 39:9); and 'anitani is "you have answered me", a sudden turn from lament to thanks that the KJV's "thou hast heard me" partly preserves.

kjv: the valley of the shadow of death
mine: the valley of deep darkness
note: ge' tsalmawet: tsalmawet is "deep darkness" (see Job 3:5); "shadow of death" is the traditional etymology, which narrows a dark valley of any danger to the moment of dying.

kjv: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever
mine: and I shall return to the house of Yahweh for length of days
note: MT weshavti "and I shall return" (shuv); the LXX/Syriac read weyashavti "I shall dwell", which the KJV follows; le'orekh yamim is "for length of days", i.e. all my life, not "for ever".

kjv: that seek thy face, O Jacob
mine: who seek Your face, O God of Jacob
note: MT has only ya'aqov "Jacob"; I follow two Hebrew mss, LXX and Syriac in reading "God of Jacob"; the KJV's literal "thy face, O Jacob" is awkward but is the MT.

kjv: The secret of the LORD [is] with them that fear him
mine: The friendship of Yahweh is for those who fear Him
note: sod is intimate counsel or friendship (Job 29:4), the circle of confidants, rather than a "secret".

kjv: try my reins and my heart
mine: test my heart and my mind
note: kilyotay "my kidneys" stand for the innermost emotions and conscience; "reins" (= kidneys) is obsolete and now unintelligible (recurs Ps 7:9, 16:7, 73:21, 139:13, Jer 11:20 etc.).

kjv: [I had fainted], unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD
mine: If I had not believed that I would see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living—!
note: lule' "if not" begins a sentence that the psalmist leaves unfinished (the Masoretes mark the word as doubtful); the KJV completes it in italics with "I had fainted".

kjv: The LORD [is] their strength
mine: Yahweh is the strength of His people
note: MT lamo "to them" has no clear antecedent; I follow several Hebrew mss, LXX and Syriac reading le'ammo "to his people" (cf. 29:11); the KJV keeps "their".

kjv: Give unto the LORD, O ye mighty
mine: Ascribe to Yahweh, O heavenly beings
note: bene 'elim "sons of gods" are members of the divine council (89:6, cf. Job 1:6), summoned to praise; the KJV's "ye mighty" makes them earthly potentates.

kjv: and discovereth the forests
mine: and strips the forests bare
note: wayyehesof "strips bare"; "discover" in 1611 meant "uncover", not "find".

kjv: in his (Yahweh's) favour [is] life (KJV 30:5)
mine: and His (Yahweh's) favor is for a lifetime
note: hayyim birtsono stands in parallel to rega' be'appo "a moment in his anger": "a lifetime in his favour"; the KJV's "in his favour is life" loses the moment/lifetime contrast.

kjv: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee
mine: which must be curbed with bit and bridle, or it will not stay near you
note: bal qerov 'eleykha "(else) there is no coming near you": without bridle the animal will not come to its master; the KJV reverses it into a danger of the animal approaching.

kjv: none of them that trust in him (Yahweh) shall be desolate (KJV 34:22)
mine: none of those who take refuge in Him (Yahweh) will be condemned
note: lo' ye'shemu "will not be held guilty" ('asham), contrasting with v.22 "those who hate the righteous will be condemned"; the KJV's "desolate" confuses 'asham with shamem.

kjv: [yea], the abjects gathered themselves together against me
mine: wretches whom I did not know
note: nekim is obscure ("smiters" or "cripples, outcasts"); "abjects" (outcasts) is now obsolete as a noun.

kjv: The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart (KJV 36:1)
mine: Transgression speaks to the wicked deep in his heart
note: MT libbi "my heart"; I follow some Hebrew mss, LXX, Syriac and Jerome in reading libbo "his heart", since the rest of the verse describes the wicked man's inner life; the KJV keeps "my heart".

kjv: [so] shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed
mine: dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness
note: shekhan-'erets ur'eh 'emunah are both imperatives: "dwell ... and tend/pursue faithfulness" (or "feed on faithfulness"); the KJV turns them into promises.

kjv: as the fat of lambs: they (the enemies of Yahweh) shall consume
mine: like the glory of the pastures; they (the enemies of Yahweh) vanish
note: kiqar karim: karim can be "lambs" or "pastures", and yeqar "precious part/glory"; either the burnt fat of sacrifices or the brief splendour of meadow flowers, both vanishing like smoke.

kjv: spreading himself (the wicked man) like a green bay tree
mine: spreading himself (the wicked man) like a luxuriant native tree
note: 'ezrah ra'anan is "a luxuriant native (tree)", i.e. one growing in its own soil; "green bay tree" (laurel) is a guess (LXX "cedars of Lebanon").

kjv: for the end of [that] man [is] peace
mine: for there is a future for the man of peace
note: ki-'aharit le'ish shalom: 'aharit is "posterity, future" (v.38 "the future of the wicked shall be cut off"); the KJV reads "the end of the man (is) peace".

kjv: verily every man at his best state [is] altogether vanity (KJV 39:5)
mine: Surely all mankind stands as a mere breath
note: 'akh kol-hevel kol-'adam nitsav: hevel is "breath, vapour" (transience rather than moral vanity), and nitsav "standing (firm)" means even the person who seems secure; the KJV's "at his best state" paraphrases nitsav well, but "vanity" now suggests conceit.

kjv: O spare me, that I may recover strength (KJV 39:13)
mine: Look away from me, that I may smile again
note: hasha' mimmenni "look away from me" (cf. Job 7:19, 14:6) is a plea that God stop scrutinising him; we'avligah "that I may brighten up".

kjv: thou (Yahweh) wilt make all his bed in his sickness (KJV 41:3)
mine: in his illness You (Yahweh) restore him to full health
note: kol-mishkavo hafakhta vehol(y)o "you overturn his whole bed in his sickness" is an idiom for transforming the sickbed, i.e. healing; the KJV pictures God making the bed.

kjv: [how] thou (God) didst afflict the people, and cast them out (KJV 44:2)
mine: You (God) afflicted the peoples, but them (Israel's fathers) You set free
note: watteshallehem "and you sent them out": the pronoun most naturally refers, like "you planted them", to Israel spreading out like a vine (80:11), not to the expelled nations.

kjv: in the place of dragons (KJV 44:19)
mine: in the place of jackals
note: tannim are jackals, inhabitants of ruins (cf. Job 30:29), not dragons; the KJV may have read tannin "sea monster".

kjv: The king's daughter [is] all glorious within (KJV 45:13)
mine: All glorious is the princess in her chamber
note: penimah "inside" refers to her location in the inner palace before she is led out (v.15); the KJV's "within" is often read of inner, spiritual beauty.

kjv: [on] the sides of the north (KJV 48:2)
mine: in the far north
note: yarkete tsafon "the recesses of Zaphon" echoes Mount Zaphon, the Canaanite mountain of the gods (Isa 14:13); Zion is given the title of the divine mountain, not a northern location.

kjv: [when] the iniquity of my heels shall compass me about (KJV 49:5)
mine: when the iniquity of those who cheat me surrounds me
note: 'aqevay is best read 'oqevay "my supplanters/deceivers" ('aqav "cheat", cf. Jacob), matching v.7 "those who trust in their wealth"; "my heels" is the literal vocalisation.

kjv: Their (the fools') inward thought [is, that] their houses [shall continue] for ever (KJV 49:11)
mine: Their (the fools') graves are their homes forever
note: MT qirbam "their inward part"; I follow LXX, Syriac and Targum reading qivram "their grave" (transposed letters); the KJV keeps MT and supplies four italic words.

kjv: death shall feed on them (the fools) (KJV 49:14)
mine: death shall be their (the fools') shepherd
note: mawet yir'em "death shepherds them" continues the sheep image; ra'ah is "to shepherd, pasture", not "to feed on".

kjv: to him that ordereth [his] conversation [aright]
mine: to one who orders his way rightly
note: wesam derekh "he who sets/prepares a way"; 1611 "conversation" meant manner of life, which a modern reader takes as talk.

kjv: uphold me [with thy] free spirit (KJV 51:12)
mine: uphold me with a willing spirit
note: weruah nedivah tismekheni "may a willing/generous spirit sustain me": the spirit is the psalmist's own renewed disposition; the KJV's italic "thy" makes it God's Spirit.

kjv: for there were many with me (KJV 55:18)
mine: for many are arrayed against me
note: ki-verabbim hayu 'immadi: 'im can mean "with" or "against" (in battle contexts), and the context is enemies in combat; the KJV's "many with me" suggests allies.

kjv: Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? (KJV 58:1)
mine: Do you indeed decree what is right, you gods?
note: MT 'elem "silence" makes little sense; most read 'elim "gods" (the divine rulers condemned as in Ps 82), while the KJV takes it as "congregation" (perhaps from 'alam "bind together"); the psalm then rebukes heavenly, not human, judges. Context: you gods ('elim: rulers or divine beings) (medium confidence). MT 'elem 'silence' scarcely works as an address; nearly all modern versions read the same consonants as 'elim 'gods, mighty ones'. 'Your hands deal out violence on earth' (v. 3) and Ps 82 point to powers who judge; whether they are human rulers or heavenly beings is left open by 'you gods'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'O congregation' — KJV, taking 'elem as 'band, assembly'; (2) 'you silent ones' / 'in silence' — MT vowels, Rashi, NKJV; (3) 'you rulers / mighty ones' (human leaders) — NIV, NET, CSB, NJPS; (4) heavenly beings judged as in Ps 82:1, 6 — some commentators.

kjv: [Because of] his strength will I wait upon thee (KJV 59:9)
mine: O my Strength, I will watch for You
note: MT 'uzzo "his strength"; I follow many Hebrew mss, LXX and Targum in reading 'uzzi "my strength", matching the refrain in v.18; the KJV keeps "his" and supplies "because of".

kjv: The God of my mercy shall prevent me (KJV 59:10)
mine: My God in His steadfast love will meet me
note: yeqaddemeni "will come to meet me"; 1611 "prevent" meant "go before, anticipate", the reverse of its modern sense "hinder".

kjv: that it (the banner) may be displayed because of the truth (KJV 60:4)
mine: that they (those who fear God) may flee to it (the banner) from the bow
note: mippene qoshet: qoshet is either Aramaic "truth" or a byform of qeshet "bow" (LXX "from the bow"); with lehitnoses (rally/flee to the banner) the military image fits the bow.

kjv: Judah [is] my (God's) lawgiver (KJV 60:7)
mine: Judah is My (God's) scepter
note: mehoqeqi is the ruler's staff or scepter (Gen 49:10, Num 21:18), matching "Ephraim is my helmet".

kjv: ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall [shall ye be] (KJV 62:3)
mine: How long will all of you attack a man to batter him, like a leaning wall
note: MT points terats(e)hu as passive ("you will be murdered"); I follow the Ben Naphtali/active reading "you will batter (him)", so that the leaning wall is the victim, not the attackers.

kjv: they (David's enemies) shall be a portion for foxes (KJV 63:10)
mine: they (David's enemies) shall be a portion for jackals
note: shu'alim covers both foxes and jackals; scavengers of corpses on a battlefield are jackals (also Judg 15:4, Lam 5:18).

kjv: How terrible [art thou in] thy works!
mine: How awesome are Your deeds!
note: nora' "to be feared, awe-inspiring"; 1611 "terrible" meant "causing terror/awe", now "very bad" (recurs throughout Psalms: 47:2, 68:35, 99:3 etc.).

kjv: extol him (God) that rideth upon the heavens (KJV 68:4)
mine: lift up a song to Him (God) Who rides through the deserts
note: larokhev ba'aravot: 'aravot is "steppes, deserts" (cf. v.8 "through the wilderness"); many compare Ugaritic rkb 'rpt "rider of the clouds", but "heavens" is not the word's meaning (contrast v.34 "rides in the heavens").

kjv: great [was] the company of those that published [it] (KJV 68:11)
mine: the women who announce the news are a great host
note: hamevasserot is feminine plural: women heralds of victory (cf. Miriam, 1Sa 18:6); the KJV's neutral "those" loses this.

kjv: Though ye have lien among the pots (KJV 68:13)
mine: though you men lie among the sheepfolds
note: shefattayim are probably sheepfolds or saddlebags (Judg 5:16 mishpetayim, of those who stayed home); "pots" is a rabbinic guess.

kjv: thou (God) hast received gifts for men (KJV 68:18)
mine: receiving gifts among men
note: laqahta mattanot ba'adam "you took gifts among/from men" (tribute from the defeated); Eph 4:8 quotes a tradition (also in the Targum) "he gave gifts to men", which the KJV's "for men" harmonises toward.

kjv: Rebuke the company of spearmen (KJV 68:30)
mine: Rebuke the beasts that dwell among the reeds
note: hayyat qaneh is "the beast of the reed", the hippopotamus or crocodile as a figure for Egypt; the KJV takes qaneh as "spear".

kjv: They gave me also gall for my meat (KJV 69:21)
mine: They gave me poison for food
note: ro'sh is a poisonous bitter plant (Deut 29:18, often paired with wormwood), not bile; "meat" here is archaic for food. The verse is echoed in the crucifixion accounts (Mt 27:34,48).

kjv: He (the king) shall have dominion also from sea to sea
mine: May he (the king) have dominion from sea to sea
note: the verbs of vv.2-17 are mostly jussives (yadin, yishpot, weyerd "may he rule"), a prayer for the king; the KJV renders them as future predictions ("he shall"), which supports a messianic reading.

kjv: There shall be an handful of corn in the earth
mine: May there be abundance of grain in the land
note: pissat bar: pissah is a hapax, probably "abundance" (from pss "spread"); the rabbinic "handful" suggests scarcity, the opposite of the context.

kjv: [there are] no bands in their (the wicked's) death: but their strength [is] firm
mine: they (the wicked) have no pangs until death; their bodies are fat and sleek
note: hartsubbot are "bonds, pangs", and lemotam "to their death" is often redivided lamo tam "for them; sound (is their body)"; either way the point is that the wicked suffer no pains, not that their death is free of bonds.

kjv: and waters of a full [cup] are wrung out to them
mine: and find no fault in them (the wicked)
note: umey male' yimmatsu lamo "and waters of fullness are drained by them" is obscure; I take it as the people eagerly drinking in the wicked's words, while the KJV renders it literally with an italic "cup".

kjv: they (God's foes) have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land
mine: they (God's foes) burned all the meeting places of God in the land
note: mo'ade-'el are "meeting places/appointed places of God"; "synagogues" names a later institution and is an anachronism for the period of the temple's destruction.

kjv: thou (God) brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters
mine: you (God) broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters
note: tanninim are the sea monsters of creation myth (paired with Leviathan in v.14); "dragons" conveys a land-based fire-breather.

kjv: [A man] was famous according as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees
mine: They (God's foes) were like those who swing axes in a forest of trees
note: yiwwada' "it was known/seemed" is obscure: the enemies looked like woodcutters; the KJV reads it as "a man was famous".

kjv: When I (God) shall receive the congregation I will judge uprightly (KJV 75:2)
mine: At the set time that I (God) appoint I will judge with equity
note: ki 'eqqah mo'ed: mo'ed is "an appointed time" (God speaking), not "congregation"; God chooses his moment for judgment.

kjv: For promotion [cometh] neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south (KJV 75:6)
mine: For not from the east or from the west and not from the wilderness comes lifting up
note: midbar harim can be "the wilderness of the mountains" (the south) or "the wilderness (does not bring) lifting up" (harim "to raise"); the KJV supplies "promotion" and "south".

kjv: the remainder of wrath shalt thou (God) restrain (KJV 76:10)
mine: the remnant of wrath You (God) will put on like a belt
note: tahgor is "you gird on": God wears the residue of human fury as an ornament or weapon; "restrain" is a contextual guess.

kjv: my sore ran in the night, and ceased not (KJV 77:2)
mine: in the night my hand is stretched out without wearying
note: yadi laylah niggerah "my hand was poured out/stretched out by night" in prayer; the KJV reads yad as a running "sore".

kjv: This [is] my infirmity: [but I will remember] the years of the right hand of the most High (KJV 77:10)
mine: This is my grief: that the right hand of the Most High has changed
note: shenot can be "years" or the infinitive "changing" (shanah II): the psalmist's anguish is that God's right hand has changed; the KJV, with italic insertions, turns it into a resolve to remember better years.

kjv: Man did eat angels' food
mine: Man ate of the bread of the mighty ones
note: lehem 'abbirim "bread of the mighty": the LXX and KJV take the mighty ones as angels (cf. 103:20); the Hebrew may simply mean noble or heavenly food.

kjv: and limited the Holy One of Israel
mine: and provoked the Holy One of Israel
note: hitwu is a rare verb, probably "pained, provoked" (Syriac tewa "regret"); "limited" derives it from taw "mark, boundary".

kjv: by sending evil angels [among them] (the Egyptians)
mine: a company of destroying angels
note: mishlahat mal'akhe ra'im "a deputation of angels of harm": they bring evil on Egypt (cf. the destroyer of Ex 12:23), not angels who are themselves wicked.

kjv: And he (the Lord) smote his enemies in the hinder parts
mine: And He (the Lord) put His adversaries to rout
note: wayyakh-tsarayw 'ahor "he struck his foes backward", i.e. drove them back; the KJV's "hinder parts" (followed by the Vulgate's in posteriora) is an over-literal reading.

kjv: and the branch [that] thou (God) madest strong for thyself (KJV 80:15)
mine: and for the son whom You (God) made strong for Yourself
note: we'al-ben is "and for the son", anticipating v.18 "the son of man whom you made strong"; ben can denote a shoot of a plant (Gen 49:22), which the KJV chooses to keep the vine image.

kjv: in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day (KJV 81:3)
mine: at the full moon, on our feast day
note: bakkeseh is "at the full moon" (Akkadian kuse'u, Prov 7:20), paired with "at the new moon"; "time appointed" is a guess.

kjv: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty
mine: God has taken His place in the divine council
note: ba'adat-'el "in the assembly of El", the heavenly council of the gods (cf. 89:6-8), over whom God pronounces judgment (vv.6-7); "congregation of the mighty" lets the reader take them as human rulers, the reading Jesus' argument in Jn 10:34 also allows.

kjv: thou, whose name alone [is] JEHOVAH (KJV 83:18)
mine: You alone, Whose name is Yahweh
note: one of the few places where the KJV prints the divine name (as JEHOVAH) instead of LORD; "alone" also belongs with "you", not with the name.

kjv: make them (God's enemies) like a wheel
mine: make them (God's enemies) like whirling dust
note: galgal here is the whirling tumbleweed or dust driven by the wind (Isa 17:13), parallel to chaff.

kjv: Preserve my soul; for I [am] holy
mine: Preserve my life, for I am faithful
note: hasid is "loyal, devoted" (one who shows hesed), not qadosh "holy"; the psalmist claims faithfulness, not sinlessness.

kjv: thou (the Lord) hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell
mine: You (the Lord) have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol
note: she'ol tahtiyyah "the lowest Sheol" is the grave/underworld from which the psalmist was rescued alive; "hell" implies damnation.

kjv: As well the singers as the players on instruments [shall be there]
mine: Singers and dancers alike say
note: holelim are dancers (from hwl/hll "whirl, dance"; cf. mehol "dance"); the KJV's "players on instruments" derives it from halil "flute".

kjv: The enemy shall not exact upon him (David) (KJV 89:22)
mine: The enemy shall not outwit him (David)
note: lo'-yashshi' 'oyev bo: nasha' II "deceive, outwit" (cf. Gen 3:13), or nasha' I "exact a debt"; the parallel "shall not humble him" and the hiphil favour deceit.

kjv: we spend our years as a tale [that is told]
mine: we bring our years to an end like a sigh
note: kemo-hegeh: hegeh is a murmur, moan or sigh (Job 37:2 "rumbling"), something brief and fading; the KJV's "tale" with its italic supplement follows the Vulgate.

kjv: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet
mine: the young lion and the serpent you will trample underfoot
note: tannin here, paired with "adder", is a serpent (as Ex 7:9-12), not a dragon.

kjv: like [the horn of] an unicorn (KJV 92:10)
mine: like that of the wild ox
note: re'em is the wild ox (see 22:22, Job 39:9); "unicorn" comes from the LXX monokeros.

kjv: as in the provocation, [and] as [in] the day of temptation in the wilderness
mine: as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness
note: Meribah ("quarrel") and Massah ("testing") are the place names of Ex 17:7; the KJV translates them (following the LXX, quoted in Heb 3:8), so the historical allusion is hidden.

kjv: [it is] he (Yahweh) [that] hath made us, and not we ourselves
mine: It is He (Yahweh) Who made us, and we are His
note: the ketiv wl' "and not (we)" and the qere wlw "and his (we are)" sound alike; the KJV follows the ketiv, while the qere (supported by many Hebrew mss and the Targum) gives "we are his", matching "his people" in the next clause.

kjv: I am like a pelican of the wilderness (KJV 102:6)
mine: I am like a desert owl of the wilderness
note: qa'at is an unclean bird living in ruins and desert (Isa 34:11, Zeph 2:14), probably an owl; a pelican does not live in the wilderness.

kjv: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good [things]
mine: Who satisfies you with good as long as you live
note: 'edyekh is obscure: "your ornament", "your years/duration" (LXX "your desire"); "mouth" is a guess, and the KJV adds three italic words.

kjv: Who maketh his (Yahweh's) angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire
mine: he (Yahweh) makes the winds His messengers, flaming fire His ministers
note: in a hymn about weather (vv.3-4 clouds, wind) the natural sense is that God uses winds as his messengers and fire as his servants; the KJV reverses subject and object ("makes angels into spirits"), as Heb 1:7 reads the LXX.

kjv: [and] the rocks for the conies
mine: the rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers
note: shefannim are rock hyraxes (Procavia), small mammals of rocky slopes; "conies" (rabbits) is an English approximation (also Lev 11:5, Prov 30:26).

kjv: he (Joseph) was laid in iron
mine: his (Joseph's) neck was put in a collar of iron
note: barzel ba'ah nafsho "his nefesh came into iron": nefesh here is the throat/neck (cf. Jonah 2:5), so an iron collar; the Prayer Book's "the iron entered into his soul" and the KJV's "he was laid in iron" both miss this.

kjv: but sent leanness into their (the Israelites') soul
mine: but sent a wasting disease among them (the Israelites)
note: razon benafsham "wasting in their nefesh": the event is the plague of Num 11:33; nefesh here means their bodies/persons, though the KJV's "soul" invites a spiritual reading.

kjv: they (the Israelites) sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils
mine: They (the Israelites) sacrificed their sons and their daughters to the demons
note: shedim are foreign deities/spirits (Akkadian shedu, Deut 32:17), "demons"; "devils" imports later Christian demonology.

kjv: and let Satan stand at his right hand
mine: let an accuser stand at his right hand
note: satan without the article is a legal adversary, the prosecutor standing at the defendant's right (Zech 3:1); in a courtroom curse the KJV's capitalised "Satan" introduces the devil.

kjv: The LORD said unto my (David's) Lord
mine: Yahweh says to my (David's) lord
note: ne'um yhwh la'doni: the Masoretic 'adoni ("my lord") is the address to a human superior such as the king (distinct from 'adonay, God); the KJV's capital L reflects the Christian reading of the verse as God addressing the Messiah (Mt 22:44, Acts 2:34).

kjv: I believed, therefore have I spoken
mine: I believed, even when I spoke
note: he'emanti ki 'adabber: ki can be "that/when/even though"; the KJV's "therefore" follows the LXX (episteusa, dio elalesa), which Paul quotes in 2Cor 4:13.

kjv: I am become like a bottle in the smoke
mine: I have become like a wineskin in the smoke
note: no'd is a leather skin bottle, which shrivels and blackens in smoke; "bottle" now means glass.

kjv: I hate [vain] thoughts
mine: I hate the double-minded
note: se'afim are "divided ones", those who waver (cf. 1Ki 18:21 se'ippim "two opinions"); the KJV takes it as "thoughts" and adds "vain".

kjv: Thy word [is] true [from] the beginning
mine: The sum of Your word is truth
note: ro'sh-devarkha 'emet: ro'sh is "head, sum total" (as in counting); the KJV's "from the beginning" supplies a preposition.

kjv: with coals of juniper
mine: with glowing coals of the broom tree
note: rotem is the broom bush, whose charcoal burns long and hot (cf. Job 30:4).

kjv: we found it in the fields of the wood
mine: we found it in the fields of Jaar
note: sede-ya'ar is probably the place name Jaar, short for Kiriath-jearim where the ark stayed (1Sa 7:1-2); the KJV translates ya'ar as "wood".

kjv: that went down to the skirts of his (Aaron's) garments
mine: running down on the collar of his (Aaron's) robes
note: 'al-pi middotaw "upon the mouth of his robes" is the neck opening (Ex 28:32 pi), i.e. the collar; "skirts" (hem) makes the oil run the full length of the robe.

kjv: for thou (Yahweh) hast magnified thy word above all thy name
mine: for You (Yahweh) have exalted above all things Your name and Your word
note: MT higdalta 'al-kol-shimkha 'imratekha "you have made your word great above all your name" is awkward; I follow the common emendation 'al-kol shimkha we'imratekha "above everything, your name and your word"; the KJV keeps MT literally.

kjv: in thy book all [my members] were written, [which] in continuance were fashioned
mine: in Your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me
note: kullam "all of them" is explained by the next words yamim yutsaru "days (that) were formed": God's book records the psalmist's days before they began; the KJV supplies "my members", making it a list of body parts.

kjv: my prayer also [shall be] in their (the evildoers') calamities
mine: my prayer is continually against their (the evildoers') evil deeds
note: Hebrew bera'oteyhem can mean "their evils" (deeds) or "their calamities"; the verse is notoriously obscure.

kjv: overthrown in stony places
mine: thrown over the cliff
note: Hebrew bide-sela' "by the hands of the rock" = over the crag, describing execution by being thrown down.

kjv: I looked on [my] right hand, and beheld
mine: Look to the right and see
note: Hebrew habbet ... re'eh are imperatives/infinitives addressed to God ("look and see"), not past narrative.

kjv: our oxen [may be] strong to labour
mine: our cattle be heavy with young
note: Hebrew 'allupenu mesubbalim "laden/bearing": either loaded for work or pregnant; context (flocks multiplying) favours fertility.

kjv: ye dragons
mine: you sea monsters
note: Hebrew tanninim are sea creatures (cf. Gen 1:21), not dragons in the modern sense.

kjv: organs
mine: pipe
note: Hebrew 'ugab is a wind instrument (flute or pipe); "organ" now means the keyboard instrument.

kjv: the prosperity of fools
mine: the complacency of fools
note: Hebrew shalwah is ease or carefree security; here the false security of complacency rather than wealth.

kjv: the strange woman
mine: the forbidden woman
note: Hebrew 'ishshah zarah is a woman outside one's marriage, an adulteress; "strange" now suggests odd. Recurs throughout Prov 5–7 (flagged here once).

kjv: the guide of her (the forbidden woman's) youth
mine: the companion of her (the forbidden woman's) youth
note: Hebrew 'alluph means close friend or companion (here her husband), not a guide.

kjv: more precious than rubies
mine: more precious than corals
note: Hebrew peninim is probably coral or pearls; the precise gem is uncertain but "rubies" is a guess.

kjv: Wisdom [is] the principal thing; [therefore] get wisdom
mine: The beginning of wisdom is this: Get wisdom
note: Hebrew re'shit chokmah qeneh chokmah: "the beginning of wisdom (is): acquire wisdom"; the KJV reads re'shit as "chief thing" and supplies "therefore".

kjv: Ponder the path of thy feet
mine: Make level the path of your feet
note: Hebrew palles means to make level or smooth (a path); the sense "weigh" is secondary.

kjv: Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life ... thou canst not know
mine: she (the forbidden woman) does not keep to the path of life ... she does not know it
note: Hebrew tephalles and teda' can be 2nd masc. ("you") or 3rd fem. ("she"); context about her ways favours "she".

kjv: Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad
mine: Should your springs be scattered abroad?
note: Hebrew yaphutsu is best read as a rhetorical question (answered by v. 17 "let them be yours alone"); the KJV's wish says the opposite of the passage's point.

kjv: by means of a whorish woman [a man is brought] to a piece of bread
mine: the price of a prostitute is only a loaf of bread
note: Hebrew be'ad-'ishshah zonah 'ad-kikkar lechem is elliptical: either she reduces a man to poverty (KJV) or her price is small compared to the adulteress who costs a life.

kjv: at the day appointed
mine: at full moon
note: Hebrew keseh (cf. Ps 81:3) is the full moon, a specific date some two weeks off.

kjv: [as] one brought up [with him] (Yahweh)
mine: like a master workman
note: Hebrew 'amon is disputed: "craftsman, artisan" ('omman) or "nursling, ward" ('amun); the KJV takes the second.

kjv: he that sinneth against me (Wisdom)
mine: he who fails to find me (Wisdom)
note: Hebrew chot'i is literally "the one missing me", the antithesis of "whoever finds me" in v. 35; "sin" is a secondary sense.

kjv: the knowledge of the holy
mine: the knowledge of the Holy One
note: Hebrew qedoshim is plural but parallels Yahweh, so likely a plural of majesty for God (cf. 30:3), not "holy things/ones".

kjv: he (Yahweh) casteth away the substance of the wicked
mine: he (Yahweh) thwarts the craving of the wicked
note: Hebrew hawwat here means desire or craving (parallel to the righteous not going hungry), not property.

kjv: he that refuseth reproof erreth
mine: he who rejects reproof leads others astray
note: Hebrew mat'eh is causative (hiphil): he misleads others, not merely errs himself.

kjv: the hope of unjust [men] perisheth
mine: the expectation of wealth perishes too
note: Hebrew 'onim can be "strength, wealth" (from 'on) or "iniquity" (from 'awen); the parallel with death favours the hope placed in wealth.

kjv: he that winneth souls [is] wise
mine: whoever captures souls is wise
note: Hebrew loqeach nephashot means "takes lives/persons"; often used of killing, here likely "wins people over"; the KJV phrase is not about evangelism in the original setting.

kjv: A fool's wrath is presently known
mine: The vexation of a fool is known at once
note: Presently in 1611 meant immediately (Hebrew bayyom, "on the same day"); today it suggests "eventually/currently".

kjv: The righteous [is] more excellent than his neighbour
mine: The righteous guides his neighbor
note: Hebrew yater is obscure: "is more excellent than" (KJV) or, with slight emendation (yatur), "searches out / guides"; the parallel "leads astray" favours guidance.

kjv: the way of transgressors [is] hard
mine: the way of the treacherous is their ruin
note: MT 'eytan means "enduring, perennial", which hardly fits; I follow the common emendation 'eydam "their calamity" (cf. LXX "in destruction"). The KJV's "hard" stretches 'eytan.

kjv: there is [that is] destroyed for want of judgment
mine: it (the fallow ground of the poor) is swept away through injustice
note: Hebrew belo' mishpat means "without justice": the poor lose their produce through injustice, not through their own lack of good judgment.

kjv: a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself
mine: a good man with the fruit of his deeds
note: Hebrew ume'alayw is obscure ("from upon him"); usually read as ma'alalayw "his deeds" to parallel "his ways".

kjv: [that which is] in the midst of fools is made known
mine: it (wisdom) makes itself known even in the midst of fools
note: The clause is elliptical; the KJV supplies a different subject (the fools' folly). The LXX reads a negative ("is not known").

kjv: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, [is] from the LORD
mine: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from Yahweh
note: Hebrew le'adam ... umeYHWH contrasts "to man belong" with "from Yahweh"; the KJV merges both halves so that both come from God, losing the antithesis.

kjv: The LORD hath made all [things] for himself
mine: Yahweh has made everything for its purpose
note: Hebrew lamma'anehu is "for its answer/purpose" (ma'aneh) rather than "for his own sake"; a verse often cited in predestination debates.

kjv: A gift [is as] a precious stone
mine: A bribe is like a magic stone
note: Hebrew shochad is specifically a bribe (cf. v. 23), and 'eben-chen a "stone of favour", a charm; the proverb observes how bribers see bribery.

kjv: seeketh [and] intermeddleth with all wisdom
mine: he breaks out against all sound judgment
note: Hebrew bekol-tushiyyah yitgalla' means "he bursts out (quarrels) against all sound wisdom" (cf. 17:14, 20:3); the KJV turns a censure of the loner into a commendation of study.

kjv: as wounds
mine: like delicious morsels
note: Hebrew mitlahamim (also 26:22) means "things swallowed greedily, tidbits"; the KJV guessed "wounds".

kjv: A man [that hath] friends must shew himself friendly
mine: A man of many companions may come to ruin
note: Hebrew lehitro'ea is from ra'a' "be broken", i.e. many shallow friends lead to ruin, contrasted with one true friend; the KJV derived it from rea' "friend".

kjv: he that hasteth with [his] feet sinneth
mine: whoever makes haste with his feet misses the way
note: Hebrew chote' has the basic sense "miss the mark" (cf. Judg 20:16); in this practical proverb it means to stumble or go astray, not moral sin.

kjv: let not thy soul spare for his (your son's) crying
mine: do not set your heart on putting him (your son) to death
note: Hebrew hamito is "his death" (hiphil of mut): discipline must not go as far as killing; the KJV read it as from hamah "moan", reversing the caution into "ignore his cries".

kjv: the man [who] devoureth [that which is] holy
mine: to say rashly, "It is holy"
note: Hebrew yala' means to speak rashly or blurt out (cf. Job 6:3), i.e. dedicating something to God without thought; not "devour".

kjv: the plowing of the wicked
mine: the lamp of the wicked
note: Hebrew nir can be vocalised as "tillage, newly broken ground" (KJV) or as ner "lamp" (LXX, Targum); the "lamp of the wicked" is a stock image (13:9, 24:20).

kjv: of them that seek death
mine: a snare of death
note: MT mebaqshe-mawet "seekers of death"; some Hebrew manuscripts and the LXX read moqshe-mawet "snares of death", which I follow.

kjv: The righteous [man] wisely considereth ... [but God] overthroweth
mine: The Righteous One observes ... He throws the wicked down
note: Hebrew tsaddiq without article is likely God (one subject for both verbs); the KJV makes it a human and supplies "God" for the second verb.

kjv: excellent things
mine: thirty sayings
note: Ketiv shilshom "formerly", qere shalishim "officers/excellent things"; most scholars read sheloshim "thirty", matching the thirty chapters of the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope that 22:17–24:22 parallels.

kjv: For as he (the stingy man) thinketh in his heart, so [is] he
mine: for he (the stingy man) is like one who is inwardly calculating
note: Hebrew kemo-sha'ar benaphsho ken-hu describes the stingy host who reckons the cost of every bite; the KJV wording, often quoted as a general maxim about thought shaping character, is not the sense in context. sha'ar is rare ("reckon, calculate").

kjv: as [for] a prey
mine: like a robber
note: Hebrew chetheph (hapax) is best taken as "robber, bandit" (Aramaic/Arabic cognates); the KJV supplies "for" and makes it the prey.

kjv: the prince whom thine eyes have seen
mine: What your eyes have seen / do not hastily bring into court
note: The clause 'asher ra'u 'eneykha can close v. 7 (KJV) or open v. 8 as the object of "bring to court"; the latter gives v. 8 its missing object.

kjv: in pictures of silver
mine: in a setting of silver
note: Hebrew maskiyyot means carved work or settings (filigree); "pictures" in 1611 meant images, which now misleads.

kjv: The north wind driveth away rain
mine: The north wind brings forth rain
note: Hebrew techolel means "brings forth, produces" (as in birth); the KJV reverses it to "drives away" and inverts the second line so the angry face drives off the backbiter, when the Hebrew says the backbiting tongue produces angry looks.

kjv: The great [God] that formed all [things] both rewardeth the fool
mine: Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool
note: The verse is among the most obscure in Proverbs; rab can be "archer" (Jer 50:29) and mecholel "wounding"; the KJV supplies "God" and reads a theological statement into it. Context: archer image; hires a fool or hires passers-by (MT) (low confidence). Among the most obscure lines in Proverbs. Rab as 'archer' (Jer 50:29) and meholel 'wounding' fits the fool-similes of 26:1-12, as most modern versions take it. The CT now follows the Masoretic text ('hires ... hires') instead of repointing the second soker as shikkor 'drunkard', which no ancient witness requires. Other possible meanings: (1) 'The great God who formed all things rewards the fool and rewards transgressors' — KJV, some medieval Jewish readings (rab = God); (2) 'A master produces everything, but one who hires a fool ...' — NJPS (rab = master craftsman); (3) 'a passing fool or drunkard' — ESV, NRSV, repointing shikkor; (4) the LXX has an entirely different line about the flesh of fools suffering.

kjv: a potsherd covered with silver dross
mine: a glaze covering an earthen vessel
note: Hebrew kesef sigim is now usually redivided kesapsagim "like glaze" (Ugaritic spsg), a shiny coat over cheap pottery; the KJV's sense is similar but less precise.

kjv: the kisses of an enemy [are] deceitful
mine: profuse are the kisses of an enemy
note: Hebrew na'tarot is from 'atar "be abundant"; the enemy's kisses are lavish (and so suspect), the contrast being with the friend's few, faithful wounds. The KJV's "deceitful" gets the implication rather than the word.

kjv: He that is of a proud heart
mine: A greedy man
note: Hebrew rechav-nephesh is "wide of appetite", i.e. greedy (cf. Isa 5:14 Sheol "widens its appetite"), not specifically proud.

kjv: Where [there is] no vision, the people perish
mine: Where there is no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint
note: Hebrew chazon is prophetic revelation (cf. 1 Sam 3:1) and yippara' means "let loose, run wild" (Exod 32:25), not "perish"; the verse is widely quoted about leadership vision, which is not its sense.

kjv: shall have him (the servant) become [his] son at the length
mine: will in the end find him (the servant) his heir
note: Hebrew manon is a hapax of uncertain meaning (guesses: "son, heir", "grief", "insolent"); both renderings are conjectures.

kjv: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal
mine: The man declares: I (Agur) am weary, O God; I am weary, O God, and worn out
note: The consonants l'yty'l l'yty'l w'kl can be read as names (MT vocalisation) or as la'iti 'el ... wa'ekel "I am weary, O God ... and worn out", which fits the confession of ignorance in vv. 2–3. Context: I am weary, O God ... and worn out (revocalised) (low confidence). The consonants allow names (MT vowels: 'to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal') or a confession, la'iti 'el ... wa'ekel 'I am weary, O God ... and worn out'. The confession fits vv. 2-3 and explains the doubled phrase but needs new vowels; major versions divide almost evenly, so the CT keeps it with low confidence. Other possible meanings: (1) personal names 'to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal' — MT vowels, KJV, NASB, NJPS, CSB, NET; (2) 'I am weary, O God ... how can I prevail?' / 'but I can prevail' (we'ukal 'I am able') — NRSV, NIV; (3) 'There is no God ... and I am helpless' — some commentators; (4) Vulgate interprets the names: 'the man with whom God is, who was strengthened'.

kjv: The conies
mine: the rock badgers
note: Hebrew shephannim are rock hyraxes, native to Palestine; "coney" meant a rabbit, which does not live in cliffs.

kjv: The spider taketh hold with her hands
mine: the lizard you can take in your hands
note: Hebrew semamit is a gecko or lizard; the verb can mean "you can catch it in your hands".

kjv: A greyhound ... a king, against whom [there is] no rising up
mine: the strutting rooster ... a king with his army around him
note: Hebrew zarzir motnayim ("girded of loins") is uncertain, often a rooster; 'alqum is obscure, often taken as "army, troop" (Arabic al-qawm).

kjv: king Lemuel, the prophecy
mine: Lemuel, king of Massa
note: Hebrew massa' can be "oracle" or the Arabian tribe/place Massa (Gen 25:14); the word order melek massa' favours "king of Massa".

kjv: a virtuous woman
mine: An excellent wife
note: Hebrew 'eshet chayil is a woman of strength, capability and worth; "virtuous" in 1611 still carried the sense of valour (Latin virtus) but now suggests mainly chastity.

kjv: vanity and vexation of spirit
mine: vapor and a chasing after wind
note: Hebrew re'ut ruach (from ra'ah "shepherd, pursue") is "striving after / herding the wind", an image of futility, not inner vexation. Recurs through the book (flagged here once). Hebrew hebel "vapor, breath" is the KJV's "vanity" throughout (systematic).

kjv: [as] musical instruments, and that of all sorts
mine: many concubines
note: Hebrew shiddah weshiddot (hapax) is most likely "a woman and women", i.e. a harem, following "the delights of the sons of man"; the KJV's "musical instruments" is a guess from the Targum. Context: many concubines (a harem) (medium confidence). Shiddah weshiddot occurs only here. Placed after male and female singers and 'the delights of the sons of man', 'a woman and women', i.e. a harem, suits a king's catalogue (cf. 1 Kgs 11:3) and is followed by most modern versions; but the etymology is uncertain and the ancient versions each guess differently. Other possible meanings: (1) 'musical instruments, and that of all sorts' — KJV, following some medieval Jewish commentators; (2) 'male and female cupbearers' — LXX; (3) 'cups and pitchers for pouring wine' — Vulgate; (4) 'chests, coffers' (Mishnaic shiddah) — NJPS 'coffers and coffers of them'; (5) baths and bathhouses — Targum.

kjv: more than I (the Preacher)
mine: apart from Him (God)
note: MT chuts mimmenni "apart from me"; the LXX, Syriac and some Hebrew manuscripts read mimmennu "apart from him" (God), matching v. 24. I follow the latter.

kjv: he (God) hath set the world in their heart
mine: he (God) has put eternity into man's heart
note: Hebrew ha'olam in biblical Hebrew means "long duration, eternity"; the sense "world" is post-biblical. Some read 'elem "ignorance". The KJV's "world" reflects later usage.

kjv: God requireth that which is past
mine: God seeks what has been driven away
note: Hebrew nirdaf is "the pursued/persecuted" (or "what has passed by"); the KJV interprets it as past time being called to account.

kjv: the spirit of man that goeth upward
mine: whether the spirit of man goes upward
note: MT vocalises ha'olah and hayyoredet with the article ("that goes up / that goes down"), as the KJV does, probably to avoid doubting the afterlife; the LXX, Vulgate and syntax favour the interrogative "whether ... whether", making it a question about human destiny. Context: a question: who knows whether ... whether (medium confidence). The consonants allow the interrogative ha- 'whether', read by the LXX (ei), Vulgate (si) and most modern versions and suiting the doubt of 3:19-22. But MT points it as the article ('that goes up'), and 12:7 'the spirit returns to God' shows the book does not deny an ascent, so the question is favoured, not certain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Who knows the spirit of man that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes down?' — MT vowels, KJV, NASB, NKJV, much Jewish tradition, implying that man's spirit does rise; (2) the question read as a denial ('no one knows that it rises') rather than as honest uncertainty — some commentators.

kjv: that for this a man is envied of his neighbour
mine: come from a man's envy of his neighbor
note: Hebrew qin'at-'ish mere'ehu "man's rivalry with his neighbour": the motive of toil is competition, not merely that the worker attracts envy.

kjv: neither say thou before the angel (KJV 5:6)
mine: do not say before the messenger
note: Hebrew mal'akh here is probably the temple official or priest's messenger who collects vows (LXX "before God"); "angel" suggests a heavenly being.

kjv: [he that is] higher than the highest regardeth (KJV 5:8)
mine: the high official is watched by a higher, and there are yet higher ones over them
note: Hebrew gaboah me'al gaboah shomer describes layers of officials watching one another (explaining corruption); the KJV's phrasing invites reading it as God's oversight.

kjv: the king [himself] is served by the field (KJV 5:9)
mine: a king committed to cultivated fields
note: The verse is obscure; melekh lesadeh ne'ebad can mean "a king for a cultivated field" or "a king is subject to the field".

kjv: they (the wicked) were forgotten in the city
mine: were praised in the city
note: MT weyishtakkechu "and they were forgotten"; some Hebrew manuscripts, the LXX and Vulgate read weyishtabbechu "and they were praised", which fits the complaint (the wicked honoured). I follow the latter.

kjv: no man knoweth either love or hatred [by] all [that is] before them
mine: Whether it is love or hate, man does not know; both are before him
note: The syntax is compressed: man cannot tell whether God's love or hate awaits him, since everything lies ahead (lipnehem); the KJV makes it a statement that outward circumstances reveal nothing.

kjv: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better
mine: If the serpent bites before it is charmed, there is no advantage to the charmer
note: Hebrew ba'al hallashon "master of the tongue" is the snake-charmer (cf. Ps 58:5, Jer 8:17); bel' lachash is "before/without charming". The point is skill used too late, not babblers.

kjv: the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail
mine: the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire fails
note: Hebrew yistabbel hechagav "the locust drags itself / is laden" is part of an allegory of old age; 'abiyyonah is literally the caperberry, an appetite stimulant, so "desire" is interpretive in both.

kjv: nails fastened [by] the masters of assemblies
mine: like nails firmly fixed are the collected sayings
note: Hebrew ba'ale 'asuppot "masters of collections" most likely denotes the collected sayings (or their compilers); the KJV supplies "by" and makes them assembly leaders.

kjv: as one that turneth aside
mine: like one who veils herself
note: MT ke'otyah "like one veiling herself" (perhaps as a prostitute, cf. Gen 38:14); the KJV follows the versions' reading ketho'iyyah "like a wanderer".

kjv: a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots
mine: a mare among Pharaoh's chariots
note: Hebrew susati is "my mare"; chariot teams were stallions, so a mare among them causes a stir, a vivid compliment lost in "company of horses".

kjv: the rose of Sharon
mine: a crocus of Sharon
note: Hebrew chavatselet is a bulb flower of the plain (crocus, asphodel or narcissus), not a rose; the KJV's article also makes it a title.

kjv: Stay me (the woman) with flagons
mine: Sustain me (the woman) with raisin cakes
note: Hebrew 'ashishot are pressed raisin cakes (2 Sam 6:19, Hos 3:1), not flasks of wine.

kjv: nor awake [my] love, till he please
mine: or awaken love until it pleases
note: Hebrew ha'ahavah is "love" itself (abstract, with the article), and techpats "it pleases" (fem.). The KJV supplies "my" and "he", making it the sleeping beloved rather than a warning not to rouse passion prematurely.

kjv: the voice of the turtle
mine: the voice of the turtledove
note: Hebrew tor is the turtledove; "turtle" for the bird is obsolete and now suggests the reptile.

kjv: doves' eyes within thy (the woman's) locks
mine: Your (the woman's) eyes are doves behind your veil
note: Hebrew tsammah (also 4:3, 6:7; Isa 47:2) is a woman's veil; the KJV guessed "locks" of hair.

kjv: builded for an armoury
mine: built in courses
note: Hebrew talpiyyot is a hapax; suggestions include "in courses/layers", "for weapons" or "for an armoury"; all are conjectures.

kjv: my bowels were moved for him (her beloved)
mine: my heart was thrilled within me
note: Hebrew me'ay "my inward parts" is the seat of emotion; "bowels" in 1611 carried that sense, but now reads as merely physical.

kjv: the chariots of Amminadib
mine: the chariots of my noble people
note: Hebrew 'ammi-nadib can be a personal name (KJV) or "my noble people / a prince's"; the verse is among the most obscure in the Song.

kjv: the king [is] held in the galleries (KJV 7:5)
mine: a king is held captive in the tresses
note: Hebrew rehatim here means locks or tresses of hair (literally "troughs, runnels", of flowing hair); the KJV's "galleries" misses the image.

kjv: causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak (KJV 7:9)
mine: gliding over lips and teeth
note: MT siphte yeshenim "lips of sleepers"; the LXX, Syriac and Vulgate read sephatay weshinnay "my lips and teeth", which I follow.

kjv: [which hath a] most vehement flame
mine: the very flame of Yah
note: Hebrew shalhebetyah ends in -yah, either a superlative ("a mighty flame") or the divine name (the only possible mention of God in the Song); the KJV takes the former.

kjv: the maker of it as a spark
mine: his (the strong one's) work a spark
note: Hebrew po'alo is "his work/deed" (the idols or deeds he made), not "its maker"; the strong man and his handiwork burn together.

kjv: upon all pleasant pictures
mine: against all the beautiful craft
note: Hebrew sekiyyot hachemdah, parallel to "ships of Tarshish", is now understood as "desirable vessels/craft" (cf. Egyptian sk.t "ship"); the KJV's "pictures" guesses from sakah "look".

kjv: the LORD will discover their (the daughters of Zion's) secret parts
mine: Yahweh will lay bare their (the daughters of Zion's) foreheads
note: Hebrew pothen is obscure: "their foreheads/scalps" (cf. Akkadian pūtu) parallel to "crown of the head", or "their private parts"; the KJV takes the latter.

kjv: behold oppression
mine: behold, bloodshed
note: Hebrew mispach (a wordplay on mishpat "justice") is a hapax, probably "bloodshed" (cf. Arabic safaha "shed blood"); "oppression" is a guess from context.

kjv: whose substance [is] in them, when they cast [their leaves]
mine: whose stump remains when it is felled
note: Hebrew beshalleket matsebet is "when felled, a stump (remains)"; the KJV supplies "their leaves" and renders matsebet "substance", obscuring the image of a cut-down tree with a living stump.

kjv: a virgin shall conceive
mine: the young woman is pregnant
note: Hebrew ha'almah is "the young woman" (of marriageable age; the specific word for virgin is betulah), and harah is an adjective, "pregnant" (now or about to be). The KJV follows the LXX parthenos, the reading Matthew 1:23 quotes. Theologically the most debated verse in Isaiah. Context: the young woman is pregnant (a sign in Ahaz's time) (medium confidence). 'Almah is a young woman of marriageable age (Gen 24:43; Exod 2:8), not the specific word for virgin (betulah); Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion render neanis. Harah is an adjective, 'pregnant', and v. 16 sets the sign within a few years. But harah can look forward (Judg 13:5), and the major versions divide, so this is favoured rather than certain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'the/a virgin shall conceive' — LXX parthenos, Vulgate virgo, Matt 1:23, KJV, ESV, NIV, NASB, CSB, holding that 'almah implies an unmarried, chaste girl and that the sign looks to the Messiah; (2) 'the young woman shall conceive / is about to conceive' (future) — RSV, NET; (3) the mother identified as Ahaz's wife or Isaiah's wife (cf. 8:3) — Jewish tradition and many commentators.

kjv: that he (Immanuel) may know to refuse the evil
mine: when he (Immanuel) knows how to refuse the evil
note: Hebrew leda'to is temporal ("by the time he knows"), dating the sign by the child's age (cf. v. 16), not giving the purpose of his diet.

kjv: wizards that peep, and that mutter
mine: necromancers who chirp and mutter
note: Hebrew metsaphtsephim describes the bird-like twittering voice of spirits called up by mediums; "peep" in 1611 meant chirp, not look.

kjv: [and] not increased the joy (KJV 9:3)
mine: you (God) have increased its (the nation's) joy
note: The ketiv lo' "not" gives the KJV's self-contradictory "multiplied the nation and not increased the joy"; the qere lo "to it" gives "increased its joy", which the rest of the verse requires.

kjv: every battle of the warrior [is] with confused noise ... but [this] shall be with burning (KJV 9:5)
mine: every boot of the trampling warrior ... will be burned as fuel
note: Hebrew se'on (hapax, Akkadian shenu "shoe") is a soldier's boot; the verse says battle gear will be burned, not that this battle will be by fire.

kjv: Wonderful, Counsellor (KJV 9:6)
mine: Wonderful Counselor
note: Hebrew pele' yo'ets is a construct pair, "a wonder of a counselor", like the other three two-word titles; the KJV comma yields five names.

kjv: Without me they shall bow down
mine: Nothing remains but to crouch
note: Hebrew bilti kara' is "nothing but crouching"; the KJV reads bilti as "without (me)", supplying God as speaker.

kjv: the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing
mine: the yoke will be broken because of the fatness
note: Hebrew mippene-shamen "because of oil/fat" is obscure (perhaps the neck grown too fat for the yoke, or a corrupt text); "anointing" is an interpretation that has become a popular slogan.

kjv: shall make him (the shoot of Jesse) of quick understanding in the fear of the LORD
mine: His (the shoot of Jesse's) delight shall be in the fear of Yahweh
note: Hebrew wahariho is literally "his smelling", i.e. delighting in (as in savouring a sacrifice's scent, Amos 5:21); the KJV renders it as keen perception.

kjv: owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there
mine: there ostriches will dwell, and there wild goats will dance
note: Hebrew benot ya'anah are ostriches and se'irim "hairy ones" are male goats (possibly goat-demons, cf. Lev 17:7); "satyrs" imports Greek mythology.

kjv: the wild beasts of the islands ... and dragons
mine: Hyenas ... and jackals
note: Hebrew 'iyyim "howlers" (hyenas or jackals), not "of the islands" ('iyyim is a homonym), and tannim are jackals, not dragons.

kjv: O Lucifer, son of the morning
mine: O Shining One, son of Dawn
note: Hebrew helel ben-shachar "shining one, son of dawn" (the morning star, Venus) is a taunt against the king of Babylon (v. 4). "Lucifer" is the Vulgate's Latin for the morning star; the KJV kept it as a proper name, which fostered its later identification with Satan. Context: Shining One, son of Dawn (taunt on the king of Babylon) (high confidence). Helel ben-shachar 'shining one, son of dawn' names the morning star (Venus), and 14:4 explicitly makes the song a taunt 'against the king of Babylon'. 'Lucifer' is the Vulgate's Latin word for the morning star, not a Hebrew name. Applying the passage to Satan's fall is a later, secondary interpretation. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Lucifer' as a proper name, applied to Satan — Vulgate lucifer, KJV, Tertullian, Origen and much later Christian tradition (cf. Luke 10:18); (2) 'Day Star / morning star' — LXX heosphoros, ESV, NRSV, NIV, NASB, CSB; (3) 'Howl!' (helel from yalal, as in Zech 11:2) — Peshitta and some ancient Jewish readers.

kjv: a possession for the bittern
mine: a possession of the hedgehog
note: Hebrew qippod is probably the hedgehog or porcupine (cf. Arabic qunfudh), though some take it as a bird.

kjv: a cockatrice
mine: an adder
note: Hebrew tsepha' is a venomous snake (viper); the "cockatrice" was a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg.

kjv: for the foundations of Kir-hareseth
mine: for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth
note: Hebrew 'ashishe means raisin cakes (cf. Song 2:5, Hos 3:1), symbolising the lost vineyards (vv. 8–10); Jer 48:31 has "men of Kir-heres".

kjv: either the groves, or the images
mine: either the Asherim or the incense altars
note: Hebrew chammanim are incense altars (Palmyrene/Nabataean inscriptions); "images" is a guess. ('Asherim as "groves" is systematic.)

kjv: a nation scattered and peeled ... a nation meted out and trodden down
mine: a nation tall and smooth ... a nation mighty and conquering
note: Hebrew memushshak umorat means "drawn out (tall) and polished (smooth-skinned)", describing the Cushites (cf. Herodotus 3.20); qaw-qaw umebusah is obscure, probably "of strength and trampling". The KJV makes the conquerors into victims. Context: tall and smooth; mighty and conquering (medium confidence). Memushshak umorat most naturally means 'drawn out (tall) and polished (smooth)', fitting Cush (18:1; cf. Herodotus 3.20 on the tall Ethiopians) and the 'feared' people of the next line; the LXX's 'lofty nation' agrees. Qaw-qaw umebusah is obscure, and 'mighty and conquering' is a reasonable guess among several. Other possible meanings: (1) 'scattered and peeled ... meted out and trodden down' — KJV, making the people victims; (2) 'a nation of strange speech' / 'gibber and chatter' for qaw-qaw (cf. 28:10) — NIV, NJPS; (3) 'far and remote, thrust forth and away' — NJPS; (4) 'a lofty nation, a strange and harsh people' — LXX.

kjv: all that make sluices [and] ponds for fish
mine: all who work for pay will be grieved
note: Hebrew 'ose-sekher 'agme-naphesh is "wage-earners, grieved of soul" ('agmei from 'agem "sad"); the KJV read sekher as "dam" and 'agam as "pond".

kjv: The city of destruction
mine: the City of the Sun
note: MT 'ir haheres "city of destruction"; some Hebrew manuscripts, the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll (1QIsa-a) and the Vulgate read hacheres "of the sun", i.e. Heliopolis (On), which I follow.

kjv: Tartan
mine: the commander in chief
note: Hebrew tartan is the Assyrian title turtanu (chief army commander), not a personal name.

kjv: And he (the watchman) cried, A lion
mine: Then the seer cried out
note: MT wayyiqra' 'aryeh "and he cried, a lion"; the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll (1QIsa-a) reads hr'h "the seer", fitting the watchman of v. 6, which I follow.

kjv: will carry thee (Shebna) away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee
mine: will hurl you (Shebna) away violently, O you strong man. He (Yahweh) will seize firm hold on you
note: Hebrew metaltelkha taltelah gaber is "hurling you a hurling, O man", and 'otkha 'atoh "grasping you firmly"; the KJV's "cover" takes the wrong root.

kjv: they raised up the palaces thereof
mine: they stripped her palaces bare
note: Hebrew 'oreru (from 'arar) means "they laid bare, razed" (cf. Jer 51:58), not "raised up"; the verse describes destruction throughout.

kjv: glorify ye the LORD in the fires
mine: in the east give glory to Yahweh
note: Hebrew ba'urim "in the (regions of) light", i.e. the east, parallel to "the coastlands of the sea" (west, v. 14); the KJV renders 'urim literally as "fires".

kjv: [together with] my dead body shall they arise ... the dew of herbs
mine: their bodies shall rise ... a dew of light
note: MT nebelati "my corpse" is awkward; I read nebelotam "their corpses" (Syriac, Targum). The KJV keeps the MT but supplies "together with", turning it into the prophet rising with them. 'orot can be "herbs" (2 Kgs 4:39) or "lights"; a key OT resurrection text.

kjv: leviathan the piercing serpent
mine: Leviathan the fleeing serpent
note: Hebrew nachash bariach is "fleeing (or gliding) serpent", the same epithet as Ugaritic Lotan btn brh; "piercing" misreads bariach "bar/fugitive".

kjv: precept upon precept ... line upon line
mine: tsav la-tsav ... qav la-qav
note: Hebrew tsaw latsaw qaw laqaw is most likely mocking babble, the drunken leaders imitating the prophet's "baby-talk", answered in v. 11 by foreign speech; the KJV makes it a commendation of step-by-step teaching, as it is now often quoted. Context: transliterated sound-play (tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav) (medium confidence). Vv. 9-10 quote scoffers mocking the prophet as if he taught infants; v. 11 answers with 'stammering lips and a foreign tongue', and v. 13 turns the same syllables into judgment. Many scholars hear childish or nonsense syllables, but tsav and qav are real words and most major versions translate them; transliteration keeps both open. Other possible meanings: (1) 'precept upon precept, line upon line' — KJV, ESV, NRSV, NASB, CSB 'law after law', mocking the prophet's elementary lessons; (2) 'Do this, do that, a rule for this, a rule for that' — NIV; (3) 'mutter upon mutter' / meaningless gibberish — NJPS, NET; (4) 'affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope' — LXX; 'command, command again; wait, wait again' — Vulgate.

kjv: the fitches ... the rie
mine: dill ... emmer
note: Hebrew qetsach is black cumin or dill (Nigella sativa) and kussemet is emmer wheat; rye did not grow in ancient Israel.

kjv: let them kill sacrifices
mine: let the feasts run their round
note: Hebrew chaggim yinqophu means "let festivals go round (complete their cycle)" (naqaph "go around"); the KJV's "kill" takes naqaph "strike off".

kjv: Their (the Egyptians') strength [is] to sit still
mine: Rahab who sits still
note: Hebrew rahab hem shabet names Egypt "Rahab" (the chaos monster, cf. 51:9, Ps 87:4) who "sits idle", a mocking nickname for a useless ally. The KJV's "their strength is to sit still" is now quoted as counsel to be calm, which is not the sense.

kjv: thy teachers ... thy teachers
mine: your Teacher ... your Teacher
note: Hebrew moreykha is plural in form but takes a singular verb (yikkanef), suggesting God as "your Teacher"; the KJV takes human teachers.

kjv: The vile person shall be no more called liberal
mine: The fool will no more be called noble
note: Hebrew nadib is "noble, generous"; "liberal" in 1611 meant generous or gentlemanly, a sense now overshadowed by the political one.

kjv: the unicorns
mine: Wild oxen
note: Hebrew re'emim are wild oxen (aurochs); the KJV follows the LXX monokeros.

kjv: the screech owl also shall rest there
mine: there Lilith shall settle
note: Hebrew lilit is Lilith, a known Mesopotamian night demon (lilitu); the KJV's "screech owl" (Vulgate lamia) hides a mythological reference. The same verse has se'ir "satyr" for the goat (cf. 13:21).

kjv: in the habitation of dragons
mine: in the haunt of jackals
note: Hebrew tannim are jackals (cf. 13:22, 34:13), not dragons.

kjv: Rabshakeh
mine: the Rabshakeh
note: Hebrew rab-shaqeh is an Assyrian title (rab shaqe "chief cupbearer/officer"), not a personal name; the same applies to 2 Kgs 18.

kjv: he (Yahweh) will cut me (Hezekiah) off with pining sickness
mine: he (Yahweh) cuts me (Hezekiah) off from the loom
note: Hebrew middallah is "from the thrum (loose warp threads)", continuing the weaving image; the KJV read dallah as "weakness".

kjv: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye
mine: A voice cries: "In the wilderness prepare
note: Hebrew qol qore' bammidbar pannu: the Masoretic accents and the parallel "in the desert make straight" attach "in the wilderness" to the command; the KJV follows the LXX reading quoted in the Gospels (Matt 3:3), where the voice itself is in the wilderness.

kjv: all the goodliness thereof (all flesh)
mine: all its (all flesh's) loyalty
note: Hebrew chasdo is "its steadfastness/loyalty" (chesed); the LXX doxa "glory" (quoted in 1 Pet 1:24) and the KJV's "goodliness" soften it to beauty.

kjv: Who raised up the righteous [man] from the east
mine: Who stirred up one from the east whom victory meets at every step
note: Hebrew tsedeq yiqra'ehu leraglo is "victory/righteousness calls him to its foot", i.e. success attends him; the conqueror is Cyrus (cf. 44:28), not a "righteous man". The KJV makes tsedeq an attribute of the person.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will destroy and devour at once
mine: I (Yahweh) will gasp and pant
note: Hebrew 'eshshom we'esh'aph continues the labour image: "I will gasp (nasham, breathe hard) and pant (sha'aph)"; the KJV derived the verbs from shamem "lay waste" and sha'aph "swallow".

kjv: blind as [he that is] perfect
mine: blind as My (Yahweh's) dedicated one
note: Hebrew meshullam (pual of shalam) is "one in covenant of peace / devoted", a title for the servant Israel; "perfect" implies moral flawlessness.

kjv: the dragons and the owls
mine: the jackals and the ostriches
note: Hebrew tannim are jackals and benot ya'anah ostriches (cf. 13:21–22, 34:13).

kjv: that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself (Yahweh)
mine: Who spread out the earth by Myself (Yahweh)
note: The ketiv mi 'itti "who was with me?" makes it a rhetorical question; the qere me'itti "by myself" (followed by the KJV and me) is a statement. The sense is the same.

kjv: make the crooked places straight
mine: level the mountains
note: MT hadurim is obscure ("swellings"?); the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll (1QIsa-a) reads hararim "mountains" (LXX "mountains"), which I follow.

kjv: I (Yahweh) make peace, and create evil
mine: I (Yahweh) make well-being and create calamity
note: Hebrew ra' paired with shalom means disaster or calamity (the opposite of well-being), not moral evil; the KJV's "evil" is often read as God creating sin.

kjv: concerning the work of my hands command ye me (Yahweh)
mine: will you command Me (Yahweh) concerning My children and the work of My hands?
note: The Hebrew imperatives (she'aluni ... tetsawwuni) are best read as an indignant rhetorical question following the woes of vv. 9–10; the KJV gives a straightforward invitation to command God.

kjv: he (Yahweh) created it (the earth) not in vain
mine: he (Yahweh) did not create it (the earth) empty
note: Hebrew lo'-tohu bera'ah "he did not create it a waste (tohu)", echoing Gen 1:2; the verse is cited in "gap theory" debates.

kjv: uncover thy (Babylon's) locks
mine: put off your (Babylon's) veil
note: Hebrew tsammatekh is the veil (cf. Song 4:1); removing it is the humiliation of a lady made a slave-girl.

kjv: thou (Babylon) shalt not know from whence it riseth
mine: which you (Babylon) will not know how to charm away
note: Hebrew shachrah is best taken as "its charming/spell" (shachar II, cf. Akkadian), parallel to "atone for it"; the KJV read shachar "dawn".

kjv: Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I (the servant) be glorious
mine: that Israel might be gathered to Him (Yahweh)—for I (the servant) am honored
note: The ketiv lo' "not" gives the KJV's "though Israel be not gathered"; the qere lo "to him" (and 1QIsa-a) gives "that Israel might be gathered to him", parallel to "bring Jacob back to him".

kjv: the land of Sinim
mine: the land of Syene
note: MT sinim is unknown; the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll reads swnyym, i.e. Syene (Aswan) in southern Egypt, where there was a Jewish colony. "Sinim" was once popularly taken as China.

kjv: shall die in like manner
mine: will die like gnats
note: Hebrew kemo-ken can be "likewise" or "like gnats" (ken, cf. kinnim Exod 8:16); the image of tiny, short-lived insects fits the smoke and worn garment.

kjv: So shall he (the servant) sprinkle many nations
mine: so shall He (the servant) startle many nations
note: Hebrew yazzeh is normally the hiphil of nazah "sprinkle" (of priestly cleansing), but "sprinkle nations" is odd and the parallel (kings shut their mouths, v. 14 "appalled") suggests "startle"; the LXX has "many nations will marvel". The KJV's priestly reading is theologically significant.

kjv: he (the servant) hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows
mine: he (the servant) has borne our sicknesses and carried our pains
note: Hebrew choli and mak'ob are "sickness" and "pain" (as in v. 3 "acquainted with sickness"); Matt 8:17 applies the verse to physical healing. The KJV's "griefs/sorrows" make it emotional.

kjv: who shall declare his (the servant's) generation?
mine: as for His (the servant's) generation, who considered
note: Hebrew we'et-doro mi yesocheach is obscure: "his generation/fate, who gave it a thought?"; the KJV's "declare his generation" (LXX) has been read as his descent or posterity.

kjv: when thou shalt make his (the servant's) soul an offering for sin
mine: when His (the servant's) soul makes an offering for guilt
note: Hebrew tasim can be 2nd masc. ("you make") or 3rd fem. with naphsho as subject ("his soul makes"); 'asham is specifically the guilt (reparation) offering.

kjv: thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles
mine: your battlements of rubies, your gates of crystal
note: Hebrew shimshot is literally "suns", the shining pinnacles; kadkod and 'eqdach are uncertain gemstones. The KJV's "windows" and gem names are guesses, as are mine.

kjv: Enflaming yourselves with idols
mine: who burn with lust among the oaks
note: Hebrew ba'elim can be "among the terebinths/oaks" (cf. 1:29) or "with gods/idols"; the parallel "under every green tree" favours trees.

kjv: thou lovedst their bed where thou sawest [it]
mine: you have loved their bed; you have looked on nakedness
note: Hebrew yad chazit "you gazed on a hand" uses yad as a sexual euphemism (cf. Ugaritic); the KJV's "where thou sawest it" takes yad as "place".

kjv: [we are] in desolate places as dead [men]
mine: among those in full vigor we are like dead men
note: Hebrew ba'ashmannim (hapax) is probably "among the robust/stout" (shamen "fat"), contrasting with "dead men"; the KJV guessed "desolate places".

kjv: When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him
mine: for He will come like a rushing stream, which the wind of Yahweh drives
note: Hebrew ki-yabo' kannahar tsar ruach YHWH nosesah bo: tsar is "narrow/pent-up" (a rushing river), the subject is God coming, and nosesah is "drives on". The KJV makes tsar "enemy" and nosesah "raise a banner", producing a popular verse about spiritual defence that the Hebrew does not contain.

kjv: beauty for ashes
mine: a beautiful headdress instead of ashes
note: Hebrew pe'er is a turban or headdress (cf. v. 10), a wordplay with 'epher "ashes": the mourner's ashes on the head are replaced by a festive head-covering.

kjv: I (Yahweh) hate robbery for burnt offering
mine: I (Yahweh) hate robbery with wrong
note: The consonants b'wlh can be vocalised be'olah "for burnt offering" (MT, KJV) or be'awlah "with injustice" (LXX, Targum, many modern versions), which fits the context of justice.

kjv: neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, [what] he hath prepared for him (KJV 64:4)
mine: no eye has seen a God besides You, Who acts for those Who wait for Him
note: Hebrew 'ayin lo'-ra'atah 'elohim zulatekha ya'aseh: "no eye has seen a God except you, who acts..."; the KJV takes 'elohim as a vocative and supplies "what he hath prepared" (as Paul paraphrases in 1 Cor 2:9).

kjv: in those is continuance, and we shall be saved (KJV 64:5)
mine: in our sins we have been a long time, and shall we be saved?
note: Hebrew bahem 'olam wenivvashea' is obscure; most read it as a despairing question ("shall we be saved?"); the KJV's confident statement reverses the tone.

kjv: prepare a table for that troop, and that furnish the drink offering unto that number
mine: who set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny
note: Hebrew gad and meni are the names of the deities Fortune (Gad) and Destiny (Meni), worshipped with banquets; the KJV translates the names as "troop" and "number", hiding the idolatry, though it keeps the wordplay of v. 12 "I will number (maniti) you".

kjv: Tarshish, Pul, and Lud
mine: to Tarshish, Put, and Lud
note: MT pul is otherwise unknown as a nation; the LXX reads Put (Libya), paired with Lud as elsewhere (Jer 46:9, Ezek 27:10), which I follow.

kjv: the face thereof [is] toward the north
mine: facing away from the north
note: Hebrew upanayw mippene tsaphonah is "its face (tilted) from the north", i.e. about to spill southward from the north, matching v. 14 "out of the north disaster".

kjv: I (Israel) will not transgress
mine: I (Israel) will not serve
note: The ketiv 'e'ebod "I will not serve" (LXX, Vulgate) fits the broken yoke; the qere 'e'ebor "I will not transgress" (KJV) makes Israel promise obedience.

kjv: We (Israel) are lords
mine: We (Israel) are free
note: Hebrew radnu (from rud "roam") means "we roam free"; the KJV derived it from radah "rule".

kjv: I have not found it by secret search, but upon all these
mine: you (Israel) did not find them (the poor) breaking in. Yet in spite of all these things
note: Hebrew lo'-bammachteret metsa'tim refers to Exod 22:2: the poor were not burglars caught in the act whose killing would be excused; the KJV's "secret search" misses the legal allusion.

kjv: fed horses in the morning
mine: well-fed, lusty stallions
note: Hebrew mashkim is obscure; it is usually connected with "having large testicles" (cf. Arabic), i.e. lusty, rather than hiphil of shakam "rise early".

kjv: Go ye up upon her (Jerusalem's) walls ... take away her battlements
mine: Go up through her (Jerusalem's) vine rows ... strip away her branches
note: Hebrew sharot are vineyard terraces/rows and netishot are tendrils (cf. 48:32, Isa 18:5); the image is of a vineyard, not a city wall.

kjv: I (Yahweh) have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate [woman]
mine: The lovely and delicately bred I (Yahweh) will destroy, the daughter of Zion
note: Hebrew damiti can be from damah I "liken" or damah II "destroy, silence"; the context of attack favours the latter.

kjv: I (Yahweh) have set thee (Jeremiah) [for] a tower [and] a fortress
mine: I (Yahweh) have made you (Jeremiah) an assayer and tester
