note: Hebrew bachon is "assayer, tester" (of metals, cf. vv. 28–30); mibtsar is probably to be read mebatser "refiner" rather than "fortress".

kjv: certainly in vain made he [it (the law);] the pen of the scribes [is] in vain
mine: the lying pen of the scribes has made it (the law) into a lie
note: Hebrew lashsheqer 'asah 'et sheqer sopherim: sheqer is "falsehood", not "vanity"; the charge is that scribes have falsified the written Torah, a significant claim the KJV blunts into futility.

kjv: [When] I would comfort myself against sorrow
mine: My joy is gone; grief is upon me
note: Hebrew mabligiti is obscure (perhaps "my cheerfulness"); many redivide as mibbeli gehah "beyond healing". The KJV supplies "when I would comfort myself".

kjv: all [that are] in the utmost corners, that dwell in the wilderness (KJV 9:26)
mine: all who dwell in the desert who cut the corners of their hair
note: Hebrew qetsutse pe'ah is "clipped at the temples", the Arab practice of trimming the side hair (cf. Lev 19:27, Jer 25:23), not "in the utmost corners".

kjv: They [are] upright as the palm tree
mine: Their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber field
note: Hebrew ketomer miqshah: tomer here is "scarecrow" (cf. Letter of Jeremiah 70, "a scarecrow in a cucumber bed") and miqshah "cucumber field" (Isa 1:8); the KJV read tomer as "palm tree" and miqshah as "turned/upright", reversing the ridicule.

kjv: [seeing] she (Judah) hath wrought lewdness with many, and the holy flesh is passed from thee
mine: when she (Judah) has done many vile deeds? Can vows and sacred flesh avert your doom?
note: MT is very difficult (hamzimmatah harabbim); I follow the LXX's "vows" (nedarim for harabbim) and read ya'aviru "avert"; the KJV renders the MT literally.

kjv: like a lamb [or] an ox
mine: like a gentle lamb
note: Hebrew kekebes 'alluf is "like a tame/docile lamb" ('alluf "tame, familiar"); the KJV took 'alluf as "ox" and supplied "or".

kjv: in the swelling of Jordan
mine: in the thicket of the Jordan
note: Hebrew ge'on hayyarden "the pride of the Jordan" is its dense jungle along the banks, haunt of lions (49:19, 50:44); the KJV takes it as flood-swell.

kjv: Say unto the king and to the queen
mine: Say to the king and the queen mother
note: Hebrew gebirah is the queen mother, an official position in Judah (here Nehushta, mother of Jehoiachin; 2 Kgs 24:8, Jer 29:2), not the king's wife.

kjv: Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I (Yahweh) will cause the enemy to entreat thee (Jeremiah) [well]
mine: Have I (Yahweh) not set you (Jeremiah) free for their good? Have I not pleaded for you before the enemy
note: The verse is obscure: ketiv sherotikha / qere sheritikha ("I have released you" or "your remnant"), and hipga'ti bekha ("I interceded with you" or "made the enemy entreat you"). Both renderings are attempts.

kjv: Neither shall [men] tear [themselves] for them in mourning
mine: No one shall break bread for the mourner
note: Hebrew lo'-yiphresu lahem (read lechem with the LXX) refers to breaking the mourning meal for the bereaved, parallel to the "cup of consolation"; the KJV's self-laceration belongs to v. 6.

kjv: desperately wicked
mine: desperately sick
note: Hebrew 'anush means "incurable, mortally ill" (cf. 15:18, 17:16 "day of sickness", 30:12); the verse describes the heart as hopelessly diseased rather than "wicked", a frequently quoted text.

kjv: the partridge sitteth [on eggs], and hatcheth [them] not
mine: the partridge that gathers a brood that she did not hatch
note: Hebrew qore' dagar welo' yalad is "a partridge that broods (gathers) what it did not lay", reflecting the belief that it steals others' eggs; the KJV makes it fail to hatch its own.

kjv: Magor-missabib
mine: Terror on Every Side
note: Hebrew magor missabib is a symbolic name meaning "terror all around" (repeated in v. 10, 6:25); the KJV transliterates it here, so the wordplay is lost to English readers.

kjv: What burden? I (Yahweh) will even forsake you (this people)
mine: You (this people) are the burden, and I (Yahweh) will cast you off
note: MT 'et-mah-massa' "what burden?"; the LXX and Vulgate redivide the same consonants as 'attem hammassa' "you are the burden", making the pun (massa' = oracle / load) explicit; I follow the versions.

kjv: I (Yahweh), even I, will utterly forget you
mine: I (Yahweh) will surely lift you up and cast you away
note: MT wenashiti 'etkhem nasho' "I will utterly forget you"; some Hebrew manuscripts and the versions read wenasa'ti ... nasa' "I will lift you up" (from nasa'), continuing the massa' pun. I follow the latter.

kjv: because of the fierceness of the oppressor
mine: because of the sword of the oppressor
note: MT charon hayyonah "the fierceness of the oppressor" duplicates the following "fierce anger"; some Hebrew manuscripts and the LXX read chereb hayyonah "the sword of the oppressor" (as in 46:16, 50:16), which I follow.

kjv: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim
mine: In the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah
note: MT has "Jehoiakim" (repeated from 26:1), but the chapter concerns Zedekiah (vv. 3, 12; 28:1 "in that same year... Zedekiah"); a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac read "Zedekiah", which I follow. The KJV keeps the MT, creating a chronological contradiction.

kjv: to give you (the exiles) an expected end
mine: to give you (the exiles) a future and a hope
note: Hebrew 'acharit wetiqwah is "a future and a hope" (two nouns); the KJV combines them as "an expected end", which today sounds like an anticipated termination.

kjv: The LORD hath appeared of old unto me
mine: Yahweh appeared to him (Israel) from far away
note: Hebrew merachoq is usually spatial "from afar" (from Zion to the exiles), though it can be temporal; the MT's "to me" may be read "to him" (LXX) as I do, continuing v. 2's Israel.

kjv: the LORD the maker thereof, the LORD that formed it
mine: Yahweh Who made the earth, Yahweh Who formed it
note: MT 'osah "who made it" has no antecedent for "it"; the LXX reads "who made the earth" ('oseh 'erets), which I follow. The KJV's "thereof" leaves the referent unclear.

kjv: three or four leaves
mine: three or four columns
note: Hebrew delatot "doors" here means the columns of writing on a scroll; "leaves" suggests a bound book (codex), which did not yet exist.

kjv: to separate himself (Jeremiah) thence in the midst of the people
mine: to receive his (Jeremiah's) portion there among the people
note: Hebrew lachaloq misham is "to take a share (of property) from there", i.e. to attend to a family inheritance in Benjamin (cf. ch. 32); the KJV took chalaq as "slip away".

kjv: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag
mine: Nergal-sharezer of Samgar, Nebu-sarsekim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag
note: Rab-saris ("chief official") and Rab-mag (a high Babylonian office) are titles, not names; a Babylonian tablet names one Nabu-sharrussu-ukin as rab sha-reshi, matching "Nebu-sarsekim the Rab-saris". The KJV lists six persons.

kjv: ye (the remnant of Judah) dissembled in your hearts
mine: you (the remnant of Judah) have gone astray at the cost of your lives
note: Hebrew hit'etem benaphshotekhem "you have erred against your lives" (qere), i.e. made a fatal mistake; the KJV's "dissembled" (acted deceitfully) imputes hypocrisy the text may not intend.

kjv: hide them (the stones) in the clay in the brickkiln
mine: hide them (the stones) in the mortar in the brick pavement
note: Hebrew malben here is a brick terrace or pavement at the palace entrance (excavations at Tahpanhes found such a platform), not a kiln.

kjv: he (Nebuchadnezzar) shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment
mine: he (Nebuchadnezzar) shall clean the land of Egypt as a shepherd cleans his cloak of vermin
note: Hebrew 'atah can mean "wrap oneself" or "delouse, pick clean" (cf. Isa 22:17); the second gives a sharper image of Nebuchadnezzar picking Egypt clean.

kjv: Why are thy valiant [men] swept away? they stood not
mine: Why has Apis fled? Why does your bull not stand?
note: MT nischaph 'abbireka "your mighty one is swept away"; the LXX redivides as nas chaph "Hapi (Apis) has fled", with 'abbir "bull" referring to the Apis bull of Memphis (v. 14). I follow the LXX division.

kjv: destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north
mine: a gadfly from the north has come upon her (Egypt)
note: Hebrew qerets (hapax) is best understood as a stinging insect (gadfly) that torments the "beautiful heifer" Egypt; "destruction" loses the image.

kjv: the multitude of No
mine: Amon of Thebes
note: Hebrew 'amon minno' is "Amon of No (Thebes)", the chief Egyptian god Amun; the KJV takes 'amon as hamon "multitude", hiding the reference to Egypt's god alongside "her gods".

kjv: I will send unto him (Moab) wanderers, that shall cause him to wander
mine: I shall send to him (Moab) pourers who will pour him
note: Hebrew tso'im "tilters, decanters" (those who tip wine jars) continues the image of v. 11 (wine settled on its lees); the KJV's "wanderers" (from tsa'ah "wander") breaks the metaphor.

kjv: why [then] doth their king inherit Gad
mine: Why then has Milcom dispossessed Gad
note: Hebrew malkam can be "their king" or vocalised Milkom, the Ammonite god (1 Kgs 11:5); the LXX, Syriac and Vulgate read Milcom, and v. 3 "with his priests" confirms a god. Same in v. 3.

kjv: A sword [is] upon the liars; and they shall dote
mine: A sword against the diviners, that they may become fools
note: Hebrew baddim here (as in Isa 44:25) denotes oracle-priests or diviners (Akkadian baru), not liars in general; "dote" in 1611 meant "act foolishly", now it means "be fond of".

kjv: them that dwell in the midst of them that rise up against me (Yahweh)
mine: the inhabitants of Leb-kamai
note: Hebrew leb qamay "heart of my adversaries" is an atbash cipher for Kasdim (Chaldea), like Sheshach for Babel (v. 41); the KJV translates the code-name literally. (Ruach can also be "wind" or "spirit".)

kjv: [this] Seraiah [was] a quiet prince
mine: Seraiah was the quartermaster
note: Hebrew sar menuchah is "officer of the resting place", i.e. the official in charge of camp halts on the journey; the KJV's "quiet prince" describes temperament.

kjv: children of a span long
mine: the children they (the women) have cherished
note: Hebrew 'olale tippuchim is "children of their nursing/dandling" (tippach, v. 22 "whom I dandled"); the KJV derived it from tophach "handbreadth".

kjv: [It is of] the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed
mine: The steadfast love of Yahweh never ceases
note: MT ki lo'-tamnu "that we are not consumed"; the Targum and Syriac read tammu "they have not ceased", parallel to "his mercies never come to an end". I follow the latter.

kjv: Give them (the enemies) sorrow of heart
mine: You (Yahweh) will give them (the enemies) dullness of heart
note: Hebrew meginnat-leb (hapax) is literally "a covering of the heart", i.e. obstinacy or dullness of mind; "sorrow" is a guess.

kjv: Even the sea monsters draw out the breast
mine: Even jackals offer the breast
note: The ketiv tannin "sea monster/dragon" vs qere tannim "jackals"; mammals that nurse their young fit the qere, which I follow.

kjv: Her (Zion's) Nazarites were purer than snow
mine: Her (Zion's) princes were purer than snow
note: Hebrew nezireha can be "her Nazirites" (consecrated men) or "her princes, nobles" (nazir, cf. Gen 49:26); the description of physical splendour suggests nobles.

kjv: But thou (Yahweh) hast utterly rejected us; thou art very wroth against us
mine: unless You (Yahweh) have utterly rejected us, and You remain exceedingly angry with us
note: Hebrew ki 'im is most naturally "unless" or "even if", leaving the book's last line as an anxious qualification of the prayer in v. 21; the KJV's "but" makes it a flat statement of rejection.

kjv: as the appearance of a sapphire stone
mine: in appearance like lapis lazuli
note: Hebrew sappir in antiquity denoted lapis lazuli (opaque deep blue with golden flecks; cf. Exod 24:10); the modern sapphire was little known before Roman times. Recurs in Ezekiel (flagged once).

kjv: [saying], Blessed [be] the glory of the LORD from his place
mine: as the glory of Yahweh rose from its place
note: MT baruk kebod-YHWH "blessed be the glory" requires the KJV's supplied "saying"; a one-letter emendation to berum "when (the glory) rose" fits v. 13 (the sound of wings and wheels). I follow the emendation.

kjv: Because ye (Jerusalem) multiplied more than the nations
mine: Because you (Jerusalem) are more turbulent than the nations
note: Hebrew hamonkem is from hamah/hamon "be in uproar, turbulent", not rabah "multiply"; the charge is unruliness, not numbers.

kjv: more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblath
mine: from the wilderness to Riblah
note: MT midbar diblatah "from the wilderness to Diblah" (an unknown place); a d/r confusion gives Riblah, the known northern limit (cf. Num 34:11), which many follow. The KJV also takes min as comparative ("more than").

kjv: The morning is come unto thee (the inhabitant of the land)
mine: Your doom has come to you (the inhabitant of the land)
note: Hebrew hatsephirah (also v. 10) is obscure; "morning" (Aramaic tsapra) or, from context, "doom, the turn (of fate)"; the parallel "the time has come" favours the latter.

kjv: [It is] not near; let us build houses
mine: The time is not near to build houses
note: Hebrew lo' beqarob benot battim is elliptical: either "(the disaster) is not near; let us build" (KJV) or "it is not time to build houses" (i.e. we are secure in the city as meat in a pot). The second fits the pot image.

kjv: as a little sanctuary
mine: a sanctuary to them (the exiles) for a while
note: Hebrew miqdash me'at can be "a small sanctuary" or "a sanctuary for a little while"; later Jewish tradition applied "little sanctuary" to the synagogue.

kjv: sew pillows to all armholes
mine: sew magic bands upon all wrists
note: Hebrew kesatot (cf. Akkadian kasu "bind") are magical bands or amulets tied on the wrists ('atstsile yaday "joints of the hands"); "pillows ... armholes" are guesses. Same in v. 20.

kjv: Noah, Daniel, and Job
mine: Noah, Daniel, and Job
note: The ketiv spelling Dn'l (Dan'el, also 28:3) matches the ancient righteous king Danel of Ugaritic legend, a figure of antiquity like Noah and Job, rather than the young exile of the book of Daniel; both versions write "Daniel", but the reference may differ from what readers assume.

kjv: shod thee (Jerusalem) with badgers' skin
mine: shod you (Jerusalem) with fine leather
note: Hebrew tachash (also of the tabernacle covering, Exod 25:5) is an uncertain fine leather, perhaps dugong or dolphin skin (Arabic tuchas) or dyed leather; badgers are not native to the region.

kjv: The way of the Lord is not equal
mine: The way of the Lord is not just
note: Hebrew lo' yittaken "is not adjusted/fair"; "equal" in 1611 meant equitable, which modern readers do not hear. Recurs in vv. 29, 33:17, 20.

kjv: it (the sword) contemneth the rod of my son, [as] every tree (KJV 21:10)
mine: You have despised the rod, my son, with everything of wood
note: The Hebrew shevet beni moeset kol-ets ("rod of my son, despising every tree") is one of the most obscure lines in Ezekiel; both renderings are guesses at a probably damaged text.

kjv: he (the king of Babylon) made [his] arrows bright, he consulted with images (KJV 21:21)
mine: He (the king of Babylon) shakes the arrows; he consults the teraphim
note: qilqal bahitsim means "shook" the arrows (belomancy, drawing lots from a quiver), not polishing them; terafim are household cult figures, a specific object rather than generic "images".

kjv: Remove the diadem (KJV 21:26)
mine: Remove the turban
note: mitsnefet is the turban of the high priest (Exod 28:4), pointing to removal of both priestly and royal insignia; "diadem" loses the priestly reference.

kjv: until he come whose right it is (KJV 21:27)
mine: until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs
note: asher-lo hammishpat: mishpat is "judgment/justice", and in context it may be Nebuchadnezzar who is given the judging task; KJV's "right" (and its messianic echo of Gen 49:10) is one possible reading. Context: literal 'the one to whom judgment belongs'; referent left open (low confidence). Mishpat can mean 'judgment' or 'right, due' (Deut 21:17; Jer 32:8), and the line echoes Gen 49:10. It may mean Nebuchadnezzar, to whom God commits judgment (cf. 23:24), or the rightful Davidic king for whom the crown waits (cf. 34:23-24; 37:24). The LXX and most versions take 'right'. The literal English leaves both open. Other possible meanings: (1) 'until he comes whose right it is' — the rightful (messianic) king; LXX 'to whom it belongs', KJV, NASB, NRSV, NIV, NJPS, much Jewish and Christian exegesis; (2) 'the one to whom I have assigned the judgment' — Babylon's king as God's agent; NET, W. L. Moran and many commentators.

kjv: thou (Jerusalem) shalt take thine inheritance in thyself
mine: you (Jerusalem) shall be profaned by your own doing
note: venihalt is most naturally the Niphal of halal "be profaned" (as in 22:26 "I am profaned among them"); KJV derived it from nahal "inherit", which gives an unusual sense here. Context: you shall be profaned (Niphal of halal) (medium confidence). Venihalt is best taken as the Niphal of halal 'be profaned', as in 7:24 (venihalu) and 22:26, matching the shame of exile in 22:15; most modern versions agree. The ancient versions derive it from nahal 'inherit, possess', mostly with God as subject, so another sense remains possible. Other possible meanings: (1) 'you shall take your inheritance in yourself' — KJV (nahal); (2) 'I will take possession of you' — LXX, Vulgate (possidebo), reading a first-person verb from nahal; (3) 'I shall be profaned through you' — NRSV, first person with halal (cf. 20:9, 14).

kjv: brought Sabeans from the wilderness
mine: drunkards were brought from the wilderness
note: The ketiv sove'im means "drunkards" and the qere sava'im "Sabeans"; KJV follows the qere, I follow the ketiv, which fits the carousing scene.

kjv: the pot whose scum [is] therein
mine: the pot whose corrosion is in it
note: hel'ah is the rust or encrusted corrosion of a bronze pot (24:11-12 speak of heating the empty pot to burn it off), not froth skimmed from boiling meat.

kjv: eat not the bread of men
mine: do not eat the bread of mourners
note: lehem anashim "bread of men" is usually understood as food brought to the bereaved by neighbours (many emend to onim "mourners"); KJV's literal phrase hides the mourning custom.

kjv: they (the people of the East) shall set their palaces in thee (the Ammonites)
mine: they (the people of the East) shall set their encampments among you (the Ammonites)
note: tirot are walled nomad encampments (Gen 25:16), fitting "the people of the East" who pitch tents; "palaces" suggests permanent royal buildings.

kjv: the company of the Ashurites have made thy (Tyre's) benches [of] ivory
mine: they made your (Tyre's) deck of ivory inlaid in cypress
note: bat-ashurim is best read as one word bit'ashurim "in cypress (te'ashur) wood"; KJV split it into "daughter/company of the Ashurites", inventing an Assyrian guild of craftsmen.

kjv: emeralds ... agate
mine: turquoise ... rubies
note: nofekh and kadkod are uncertain gemstones; nofekh is probably turquoise (or garnet), and kadkod a red stone such as ruby; KJV's identifications are guesses.

kjv: they (Aram) occupied in thy (Tyre's) fairs
mine: they (Aram) exchanged for your (Tyre's) wares
note: occupy here meant "trade" and "fairs" render izbonim "wares/goods", not markets or festivals; modern readers miss the commercial sense.

kjv: Javan going to and fro
mine: Javan from Uzal
note: me'uzzal is "from Uzal" (a place in Arabia, Gen 10:27), not the participle "going to and fro".

kjv: wiser than Daniel
mine: wiser than Danel
note: The consonants dn'l (as in 14:14) point to Danel, the wise and just king of Ugaritic legend, rather than the exile Daniel, a younger contemporary of Ezekiel.

kjv: Thou (the king of Tyre) sealest up the sum
mine: You (the king of Tyre) were the seal of perfection
note: hotem toknit is a noun phrase "a seal (signet) of proportion/perfection" describing the king as a model of perfection, not a verb "you seal up the sum".

kjv: the workmanship of thy (the king of Tyre's) tabrets and of thy pipes
mine: your (the king of Tyre's) settings and your mountings were crafted in gold
note: tuppim and neqavim here are jeweller's terms (settings and sockets for the stones just listed); KJV read them as drums and pipes, introducing musical instruments into the description.

kjv: the sardius, topaz, and the diamond ... the carbuncle
mine: carnelian, chrysolite, and moonstone ... emerald
note: The nine stones (a subset of the high priest's breastplate) are uncertain; yahalom cannot be diamond, which could not be engraved in antiquity, and the MT list has nine stones while KJV ends with "carbuncle" from barekat.

kjv: the great dragon
mine: the great monster
note: tannim (for tannin) is a great water creature, here the Nile crocodile as an image of Pharaoh; "dragon" suggests a fire-breathing beast of later legend.

kjv: from the tower of Syene
mine: from Migdol to Syene
note: mimmigdol seveneh names two border towns, Migdol in the north-east delta and Syene (Aswan) in the south, giving a north-to-south merism; KJV took migdol as a common noun "tower".

kjv: Noph ... Zoan ... No ... Sin
mine: Memphis ... Zoan ... Thebes ... Pelusium
note: KJV transliterates the Hebrew city names (Noph, No, Sin, Aven); these are now identified as Memphis, Thebes, Pelusium and On/Heliopolis, so the KJV forms are opaque rather than wrong.

kjv: the chesnut trees
mine: the plane trees
note: armon is the oriental plane tree (Platanus orientalis), native to the region, not the chestnut.

kjv: thou (Pharaoh) [art] as a whale in the seas
mine: you (Pharaoh) are like a monster in the seas
note: tannim (as in 29:3) is a great water creature, in context the Nile crocodile thrashing in its streams; "whale" does not fit rivers.

kjv: The way of the Lord is not equal
mine: The way of the Lord is not right
note: lo yittakhen means "is not fair/correct (measured right)"; "not equal" now suggests inequality rather than injustice (as at 18:25).

kjv: are talking against thee (Ezekiel)
mine: who talk about you (Ezekiel)
note: nidbarim bekha can mean "speak about" or "speak against"; the following invitation to come and hear suggests curious chatter, not hostility.

kjv: a very lovely song
mine: one who sings lustful songs
note: shir agavim, as with agavim in 33:31, refers to erotic love songs; the people treat the prophet as entertainment, and KJV's "lovely" softens this.

kjv: a plant of renown
mine: a planting place of renown
note: matta is a planting or plantation (fertile land that ends famine, as the context says); KJV's singular "plant" has often been read as a messianic figure.

kjv: that dwell in the midst of the land
mine: who dwell at the navel of the earth
note: tabbur ha'arets (also Judg 9:37) is "the navel of the earth", the idea of Jerusalem/Israel as the world's centre; "midst of the land" loses the cosmic image.

kjv: leave but the sixth part of thee (Gog)
mine: drive you (Gog) forward
note: The hapax shishshe'tikha was linked by KJV to shesh "six" ("leave a sixth"); it is now generally taken as "lead/drive along" (cf. Ethiopic and the parallel verbs), so there is no sixth surviving.

kjv: it (the valley) shall stop the [noses] of the passengers
mine: It (the valley) will block the travelers
note: hosemet hi et-ha'overim means "it blocks the travellers" (the mass grave obstructs the route); KJV supplied "noses" (italicised) to make it a stench.

kjv: After that they (Israel) have borne their shame
mine: They (Israel) shall forget their shame
note: venasu can be from nasa (bear) with lost aleph or from nashah (forget); the time clause "when they dwell securely" suits forgetting rather than bearing shame afterward.

kjv: the little chambers ... the arches
mine: the guardrooms ... the vestibules
note: ta'im are gate guardrooms and elammot the gate vestibules/porches; ancient gates of this plan (Megiddo, Gezer) show no arches, so KJV's "arches" misleads the reader on the architecture.

kjv: hooks, an hand broad
mine: ledges, a handbreadth long
note: shefattayim is uncertain: either double-pronged hooks for hanging carcasses or rims/ledges; both renderings are guesses.

kjv: a winding about still upward
mine: the structure surrounding the temple went up story by story
note: musav/nasvah describe the side-chamber structure surrounding the temple and widening as it rose on wall offsets (41:6); KJV's "winding about" suggests a spiral staircase.

kjv: So the altar [shall be] four cubits; and from the altar
mine: the altar hearth, four cubits; and from the altar hearth
note: har'el/ari'el is the specific term for the top hearth of the stepped altar (cf. Moabite Mesha stele 'r'l), not the altar as a whole; with "settle" for azarah (ledge) KJV obscures the three-tier structure.

kjv: five and twenty thousand [reeds]
mine: 25,000 cubits
note: The Hebrew gives only the number; KJV's italic "reeds" makes the district six times larger than "cubits" (implied by the 50-cubit margin in 45:2), and commentators are divided.

kjv: the river to the great sea
mine: along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea
note: nahlah is "to the wadi", i.e. the Wadi of Egypt (Wadi el-Arish), the standard southern border (Num 34:5); "the river" suggests the Nile or an unnamed river.

kjv: Then said Daniel to Melzar
mine: Then Daniel said to the steward
note: hammeltsar has the article and is an Akkadian title (massaru, "guard/steward"), not a personal name.

kjv: let them give us (Daniel and his friends) pulse
mine: let us (Daniel and his friends) be given vegetables
note: zero'im are things grown from seed (vegetables generally); "pulse" (legumes) is both narrower and now unfamiliar.

kjv: The thing is gone from me (Nebuchadnezzar)
mine: The word from me (Nebuchadnezzar) is firm
note: azda is a Persian loanword meaning "certain/publicly decreed"; the king has not forgotten his dream but is testing the diviners, which KJV's rendering (implying he forgot it) obscures; also at 2:8.

kjv: they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men
mine: they will mix with one another in marriage
note: bizra anasha "by the seed of men" is usually taken of dynastic intermarriage; KJV's literal phrase has fed speculative readings.

kjv: the form of the fourth is like the Son of God
mine: the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods
note: bar-elahin (plural, no article) on a pagan king's lips means "a divine being", which he calls "his angel" in 3:28; KJV's capitalised "the Son of God" reads a christological title into it.

kjv: cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer
mine: horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe
note: qatros (Greek kitharis), sabbekha (Greek sambyke, a triangular harp), pesanterin (psalterion) and sumponyah are Greek instrument names; "sackbut" (a trombone) and "dulcimer" are anachronistic European instruments.

kjv: neither were instruments of musick brought before him (Darius) (KJV 6:18)
mine: no diversions were brought to him (Darius)
note: dahavan is a hapax of unknown meaning (suggestions: food, concubines, entertainment); "instruments of music" is one guess among several.

kjv: the thrones were cast down
mine: thrones were placed
note: remiw "were cast/set" here means thrones were set in place for the heavenly court (the Ancient of Days then sits); "cast down" reverses the image into thrones being overthrown.

kjv: [one] like the Son of man
mine: one like a son of man
note: kevar enash has no article and means "one like a human being", contrasted with the beasts; KJV's capitalised "the Son of man" reads the later messianic title (Mark 14:62) into the vision.

kjv: the saints of the most High
mine: the holy ones of the Most High
note: qaddishe elyonin may denote angels (as qaddish in 4:10, 4:14) or faithful Israel; "saints" settles the question in favour of human believers.

kjv: Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed
mine: For 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary shall be restored to its rightful state
note: erev boqer "evening morning" likely counts the twice-daily tamid offerings (1,150 days, about the Maccabean desecration); KJV's "days" doubled the span and underlies historicist date-setting; nitsdaq means "be set right/vindicated", while "cleansed" comes from the LXX.

kjv: by peace shall destroy many
mine: Without warning he (the king of bold face) shall destroy many
note: beshalvah "in (their) security/unawares" describes surprise attacks on those at ease, not destruction by means of peace.

kjv: to anoint the most Holy
mine: to anoint a most holy place
note: qodesh qodashim ("holy of holies") elsewhere always denotes a sacred place or objects, never a person; KJV's capitalised "most Holy" invites a reading as the Messiah.

kjv: unto the Messiah the Prince [shall be] seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks
mine: until an anointed one, a prince, there shall be seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it (Jerusalem) shall be built again
note: mashiah nagid lacks the article ("an anointed one, a prince"), and the Masoretic accent (atnach) ends the clause after "seven weeks"; KJV joins 7+62 = 69 weeks to the coming of "the Messiah", the basis of the classic Christian chronology. Context: seven weeks to an anointed prince; then sixty-two weeks of rebuilding (MT accents) (low confidence). The WLC's atnach divides after 'seven weeks', 'an anointed one, a prince' lacks the article, and 9:26 places an anointed one 'cut off' after the 62 weeks, suggesting two figures. But Theodotion and the Vulgate join both numbers to the anointed one, the accents are mediaeval, and major versions split. The CT follows its source's accents with low confidence. Other possible meanings: (1) 'unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks' (69 weeks to the Messiah) — Theodotion, Vulgate, KJV, NIV, NASB, CSB, NET, the classic Christian chronology ending in Jesus; (2) the anointed one after seven weeks as Cyrus (Isa 45:1), Zerubbabel or Joshua the high priest — commentators following the accents, cf. ESV, NRSV, NJPS.

kjv: shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself
mine: an anointed one shall be cut off and shall have nothing
note: ve'en lo means "and there is nothing/no one for him", not "not for himself" (a vicarious reading); the anointed one, without article, is often identified with the high priest Onias III.

kjv: for the overspreading of abominations he shall make [it] desolate
mine: on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate
note: kenaf shiqqutsim meshomem is "on the wing (pinnacle) of abominations, a desolator"; the phrase underlies "abomination of desolation" (Dan 11:31, 12:11; Mark 13:14), which KJV's wording obscures.

kjv: but the time appointed [was] long
mine: and it (the word) was a great conflict
note: tsava gadol means "a great war/conflict" (tsava = host, warfare, hard service), anticipating the wars of ch. 11, not a long appointed time.

kjv: Neither shall he (the king) regard the God of his fathers
mine: He (the king) shall pay no attention to the gods of his fathers
note: elohe avotav, said of a Seleucid king (Antiochus IV) who neglected his ancestral Greek gods for Zeus Olympios, is naturally plural; KJV's singular capitalised "God" has fed the idea of a Jewish apostate antichrist.

kjv: the God of forces
mine: the god of fortresses
note: eloah ma'uzzim is "god of strongholds/fortresses" (often linked to Zeus or Jupiter Capitolinus); "forces" now suggests military power or natural forces in general.

kjv: many [countries] shall be overthrown
mine: tens of thousands shall fall
note: rabbot can be "many (fem.)" or repointed ribbot "tens of thousands"; KJV's italic "countries" is a supply the Hebrew does not specify.

kjv: but I (Yahweh) will utterly take them (the house of Israel) away
mine: that I (Yahweh) should forgive them (the house of Israel) at all
note: ki naso essa lahem: nasa with lamed usually means "forgive/bear with" (so "no more mercy ... that I should forgive them"); KJV took it as "take away" (exile), a defensible but different sense.

kjv: thou (Israel) shalt call me (Yahweh) Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali (KJV 2:16)
mine: you (Israel) will call Me (Yahweh) 'My Husband,' and no longer ... 'My Baal.'
note: ishi "my husband" and ba'ali "my master/my Baal" are a pun on the god Baal; transliterating both leaves the English reader unable to see the point.

kjv: love flagons of wine
mine: love cakes of raisins
note: ashishe anavim are pressed raisin cakes, associated with cultic feasts (2 Sam 6:19; Song 2:5), not flagons.

kjv: without an image
mine: without pillar
note: matsevah is a standing stone/sacred pillar, not a carved image.

kjv: they (the men) sacrifice with harlots
mine: sacrifice with cult prostitutes
note: qedeshot ("consecrated women") are distinguished from zonot "prostitutes" in the same verse; the sacrificial setting points to women attached to shrines, a distinction KJV's "whores ... harlots" erases.

kjv: now the LORD will feed them (Israel) as a lamb in a large place
mine: can Yahweh now feed them (Israel) like a lamb in a broad pasture?
note: After "Israel is stubborn like a heifer", the clause is best read as an ironic question; KJV's statement turns it into a promise or threat of exposure.

kjv: he (Ephraim) willingly walked after the commandment
mine: he (Ephraim) was determined to go after worthless precepts
note: tsav is obscure (perhaps a mocking word "precept" as in Isa 28:10, or "filth/vanity"); KJV's "the commandment" sounds like obedience to God, the opposite of the context.

kjv: sent to king Jareb
mine: sent to the great king
note: melekh yarev is best read malki rav "the great king", the Assyrian royal title (sharru rabu); no king Jareb is known.

kjv: they (Ephraim and Judah) like men have transgressed the covenant
mine: like Adam they (Ephraim and Judah) transgressed the covenant
note: ke'adam can be "like Adam" (the first covenant-breaker), "like humans", or (emended be'adam) the town of Adam, which suits the following "there"; KJV's "like men" is the weakest reading.

kjv: Israel [is] an empty vine
mine: Israel is a luxuriant vine
note: boqeq usually means "lay waste/empty", but here, followed by "yields its fruit" and increasing altars, it is generally taken as "luxuriant, spreading" (cf. Arabic); KJV's "empty" contradicts the rest of the verse.

kjv: for a present to king Jareb
mine: as tribute to the great king
note: As at 5:13, melekh yarev is the Assyrian title "great king", not a name.

kjv: I (God) will not enter into the city
mine: I (God) will not come in wrath
note: be'ir can be "into a city" or (from a homonym, cf. ar "enemy") "in wrath/terror"; the parallel with "burning anger" favours the latter.

kjv: but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the saints (KJV 11:12)
mine: and Judah still wanders with God, but is faithful to the Holy One
note: rad is obscure ("roam/be restless" or "rule"); qedoshim, a plural of majesty for God parallel to el, is "the Holy One", not "saints"; the line may be praise or censure of Judah.

kjv: O death, I (Yahweh) will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction
mine: O Death, where are your plagues? O Sheol, where is your destruction?
note: ehi is the interrogative "where?" (as in 13:10), which is how Paul quotes the verse in 1 Cor 15:55; KJV read it as ehyeh "I will be", which also makes the opening lines promises rather than questions.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will be thy (Israel's) king: where [is any other]
mine: Where now is your (Israel's) king
note: ehi malkekha efo is "where then is your king?", not "I will be thy king".

kjv: Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves
mine: Those who sacrifice human beings kiss calves!
note: zovhe adam can be "sacrificers of men" (human sacrifice) or "men who sacrifice"; the ironic contrast of killing humans while kissing calf-idols is lost in KJV.

kjv: so will we (Israel) render the calves of our lips (KJV 14:2)
mine: we (Israel) will offer the bulls of our lips
note: parim sefatenu "bulls (of) our lips" is usually read (with LXX, Heb 13:15) as "fruit (peri) of our lips", i.e. praise in place of sacrifice; both versions keep the MT image, but KJV's "calves" is a misleading animal.

kjv: palmerworm ... locust ... cankerworm ... caterpiller
mine: cutting locust ... swarming locust ... hopping locust ... destroying locust
note: gazam, arbeh, yeleq and hasil are all locust terms (probably stages or kinds of locust, as 2:25 calls them "my great army"); KJV's worms and caterpillars suggest different pests.

kjv: the former rain moderately ... in the first [month]
mine: the early rain for your vindication ... as before
note: hammoreh litsdaqah is "the early rain in righteousness/for vindication" (some: "the teacher of righteousness"), not "moderately"; barishon here means "as at first/as before".

kjv: I (Yahweh) will cleanse their blood [that] I have not cleansed (KJV 3:21)
mine: I (Yahweh) will declare innocent their blood, which I had not declared innocent
note: niqqah means "acquit/hold innocent" (the shed blood is declared innocent, i.e. avenged); KJV's "cleanse" is literal-sounding but obscure, and the LXX reads "avenge".

kjv: shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done [it]?
mine: Does disaster come to a city, unless Yahweh has done it?
note: ra'ah here is calamity (parallel to the alarm-trumpet of attack); modern readers take "evil" as moral wickedness, raising a theological problem the verse does not pose.

kjv: and in Damascus [in] a couch
mine: and part of a bed
note: dmsq is probably not the city Damascus but a word for part of a couch (perhaps "damask" cover or a bed-leg), parallel to "corner of a couch"; the image is of pitiful remnants rescued, like scraps from a lion.

kjv: ye (the cows of Bashan) shall cast [them] into the palace
mine: you (the cows of Bashan) shall be cast out into Harmon
note: haharmonah is an unknown word, perhaps a place name (Harmon, or emended Hermon); KJV's "palace" (from armon) is a guess.

kjv: ye (Israel) have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images
mine: You (Israel) shall take up Sikkuth your king, and Kiyyun your star-god
note: Sikkut and Kiyyun are the Mesopotamian astral deities Sakkut and Kaiwan (Saturn), vocalised in MT like shiqquts "abomination"; KJV's "tabernacle of your Moloch" blends the LXX (quoted in Acts 7:43) with the Hebrew malkekhem "your king".

kjv: That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong
mine: Who makes destruction flash forth against the strong
note: hammavlig shod is "who makes destruction flash/smile" (balag "brighten"), part of a doxology of God's power, not the empowerment of the plundered.

kjv: Ye which rejoice in a thing of nought ... taken to us horns
mine: you who rejoice in Lo-debar ... captured Karnaim
note: Lo-debar and Karnaim are Transjordanian towns retaken by Jeroboam II; Amos puns on their names ("no-thing", "horns"); KJV translates the puns and loses the historical reference.

kjv: They that swear by the sin of Samaria
mine: Those who swear by Ashimah of Samaria
note: ashmat shomron, parallel to "your god, O Dan", is probably the goddess Ashima (2 Kgs 17:30), punned with ashmah "guilt"; KJV gives only the pun.

kjv: hath founded his (Yahweh's) troop in the earth
mine: founds His (Yahweh's) vault upon the earth
note: aguddah here is the firmament/vault (a "bound" structure) resting on the earth, parallel to "upper chambers in the heavens"; "troop" is a different sense of the word that does not fit.

kjv: have laid a wound under thee (Edom)
mine: have set a trap beneath you (Edom)
note: mazor here is usually derived from a root "net/snare" (or emended mazor = "trap"); "wound" (mazor elsewhere) makes little sense "under" someone.

kjv: thou (Edom) shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger
mine: do not gloat over the day of your (Edom's) brother in the day of his misfortune
note: al-tere with jussive forms is a prohibition (warning or retrospective rebuke); nokhro is "his misfortune/disaster", not "became a stranger".

kjv: God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do
mine: God relented of the disaster that He had said He would do
note: niham means "relent/change course" and ra'ah here is the threatened calamity; to a modern reader "repented of the evil" implies God had done moral wrong (also 4:2 "repentest thee of the evil").

kjv: the LORD God prepared a gourd
mine: Yahweh God appointed a castor-oil plant
note: qiqayon is most likely the castor-oil plant (Egyptian kiki), a fast-growing broad-leaved shrub; "gourd" follows the LXX kolokynthe.

kjv: a wailing like the dragons, and mourning as the owls
mine: lamentation like the jackals, and mourning like the ostriches
note: tannim are jackals (whose howl suits lament) and benot ya'anah ostriches; "dragons" and "owls" are mistaken identifications common in the KJV prophets.

kjv: as the sheep of Bozrah
mine: like sheep in a fold
note: botsrah here is the common noun "sheepfold/enclosure" (parallel to "flock in its pasture"), not the Edomite city Bozrah.

kjv: whose goings forth [have been] from of old, from everlasting (KJV 5:2)
mine: Whose origins are from of old, from ancient days
note: mime olam means "from days of antiquity" (as in 7:14 "as in the days of old"), pointing to the ancient Davidic line from Bethlehem; KJV's "from everlasting" suggests the eternal pre-existence of the ruler, the classic messianic reading.

kjv: in that day shall the decree be far removed
mine: In that day the boundary shall be far extended
note: hoq can be "decree" or "boundary"; in context of rebuilding walls and peoples streaming in, the frontier is extended, not a decree removed.

kjv: from the fortified cities, and from the fortress even to the river
mine: from ... the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt to the River
note: matsor is a poetic name for Egypt (as in 2 Kgs 19:24, Isa 19:6), giving the Assyria/Egypt pair; KJV takes it as "fortress".

kjv: the fir trees shall be terribly shaken (KJV 2:3)
mine: the cypress spears are brandished
note: haberoshim "the cypresses" here are spear-shafts made of cypress wood, brandished by the attacking army, not trees shaking.

kjv: And Huzzab shall be led away captive (KJV 2:7)
mine: it is decreed: she is stripped
note: hutsav is a Hophal verb "it is fixed/decreed" (or an epithet of the queen or city), not a personal name Huzzab.

kjv: Art thou (Nineveh) better than populous No
mine: Are you (Nineveh) better than Thebes
note: no amon is "No of (the god) Amon", i.e. Thebes, sacked by Assyria in 663 BC; KJV read amon as hamon "multitude" ("populous").

kjv: the just shall live by his faith
mine: the righteous shall live by his faithfulness
note: emunah is steadfastness/fidelity (the righteous person's loyal endurance while awaiting the vision); KJV's "faith" follows Paul's use (Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11), which reads it as trust or belief, a theologically pivotal shift.

kjv: to him that ladeth himself with thick clay
mine: loads himself with pledges
note: avtit is a hapax from avot "pledge" (taking goods in pawn), fitting the debtors of 2:7; KJV divided it as av tit "thick mud".

kjv: he (God) had horns [coming] out of his hand
mine: rays flashed from His (God's) hand
note: qarnayim here are rays of light (cf. Exod 34:29 Moses' face "shone"), parallel to brightness; "horns" is the literal sense that misleads.

kjv: burning coals went forth at his (God's) feet
mine: plague followed at His (God's) heels
note: resheph is plague or the plague-deity Reshep, paralleling "pestilence"; "burning coals" is a secondary sense (Song 8:6) that breaks the parallel.

kjv: O nation not desired
mine: O shameless nation
note: lo nikhsaf may mean "not longing/not ashamed" (kasaf "grow pale, long for"); "not desired" (unloved) is one guess, "shameless" another.

kjv: both the cormorant and the bittern shall lodge in the upper lintels of it (Nineveh)
mine: even the owl and the hedgehog shall lodge in her (Nineveh's) capitals
note: qa'at and qippod are probably an owl and the hedgehog (or porcupine), creatures of ruins; cormorant (a sea bird) and bittern (a marsh bird) do not fit a dry ruined city.

kjv: the desire of all nations shall come
mine: the treasures of all nations shall come in
note: hemdat kol-haggoyim takes a plural verb (uva'u) and is followed by "the silver is mine, and the gold is mine" (2:8): it is the nations' wealth flowing into the temple; KJV's singular "the desire of all nations" made it a classic title of the Messiah.

kjv: red horses, speckled, and white
mine: red, sorrel, and white horses
note: seruqqim is a horse colour (sorrel/chestnut or bay), not "speckled".

kjv: four carpenters (KJV 1:20)
mine: four craftsmen
note: harashim are craftsmen or smiths in general (here, those who "cast down" horns, likely metalworkers); "carpenters" is too narrow.

kjv: and Satan standing at his (Joshua's) right hand to resist him
mine: and the Accuser standing at his (Joshua's) right hand to accuse him
note: hassatan has the article ("the adversary/accuser"), a role in the heavenly court as in Job 1-2, with a wordplay on lesitno "to accuse him"; KJV's proper name "Satan" imports the later figure of the devil.

kjv: When they had sent unto the house of God Sherezer
mine: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer
note: bet-el is the subject ("Bethel sent"), i.e. the town's people sent a delegation to Jerusalem; KJV makes it the destination "house of God", which in Zechariah's day was the Jerusalem temple, not called Bethel.

kjv: The burden of the word
mine: An oracle: the word
note: Hebrew massa' (from nasa', "lift up") is a technical heading for a prophetic pronouncement; "burden" reflects a derivation from "load" and suggests a weight rather than an utterance.

kjv: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod
mine: A mongrel people will live in Ashdod
note: Hebrew mamzer here refers to a population of mixed or foreign descent replacing the Philistines, not an individual illegitimate child as the modern sense of "bastard" implies.

kjv: because of the army
mine: as a guard
note: The consonants mtsbh are vocalised matsavah ("guard, garrison"), so God himself stands guard; the KJV read mi-tsava ("because of the army").

kjv: he (the king) is just, and having salvation
mine: he (the king) is righteous and victorious
note: Hebrew nosha' is a Niphal participle, "saved/delivered" (hence "victorious, given victory"); the KJV follows the active sense of the versions ("saviour"), making the king the bringer of salvation.

kjv: subdue with sling stones
mine: trample down the sling stones
note: Hebrew kavshu avney-qela' has the sling stones as direct object: the enemy's missiles are trampled underfoot, not used by Israel as weapons.

kjv: lifted up as an ensign upon his (Yahweh's) land
mine: sparkling over His (Yahweh's) land
note: Hebrew mitnosesot is best taken from a root meaning "glitter, sparkle" (of crown jewels); the KJV derived it from nes ("banner, ensign").

kjv: the LORD shall make bright clouds
mine: Yahweh, Who makes the storm clouds
note: Hebrew chazizim (also Job 28:26) denotes thunderclouds or lightning flashes that bring rain, not merely bright clouds.

kjv: out of him (Judah) every oppressor together
mine: from him (Judah) every ruler together
note: Hebrew noges (elsewhere "taskmaster") here stands in a list of positive leadership images (cornerstone, tent peg, bow) and means a ruler or commander; "oppressor" gives the opposite tone.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will hiss for them (Ephraim)
mine: I (Yahweh) will whistle for them (Ephraim)
note: Hebrew sharaq is to whistle or pipe as a signal to call a flock together; "hiss" now suggests contempt.

kjv: the forest of the vintage is come down
mine: the dense forest has been cut down
note: The ketiv habbatsur means "inaccessible, impenetrable" (a dense forest); the KJV follows the qere habbatsir ("the vintage"), which makes little sense of a forest. I preferred the ketiv.

kjv: the pride of Jordan is spoiled
mine: the thickets of the Jordan are ruined
note: Hebrew ge'on hayyarden (also Jer 12:5; 49:19) is the lush jungle along the Jordan where lions lived, not an abstract "pride".

kjv: And I (Zechariah) will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock
mine: So I (Zechariah) shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, the afflicted of the flock
note: Hebrew wa'er'eh is a past narrative form: the prophet carries out the command of 11:4; "the afflicted of the flock" stands in apposition, not as a vocative address.

kjv: the idol shepherd
mine: My worthless shepherd
note: Hebrew ro'i ha'elil uses 'elil in its basic sense "worthless, good-for-nothing"; the shepherd is useless, not an idol.

kjv: The burden of the word
mine: An oracle: the word
note: Hebrew massa' is a heading for a prophetic pronouncement ("oracle"), not a "burden" in the sense of a load.

kjv: when they (the peoples) shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem
mine: and Judah too will be caught up in the siege against Jerusalem
note: The elliptical Hebrew wegam 'al-yehudah yihyeh bammatsor 'al-yerushalayim most naturally says that Judah also will be involved in (or affected by) the siege of Jerusalem; the KJV makes Judah a second target of the besiegers.

kjv: for man taught me to keep cattle from my youth
mine: for a man made me his servant from my youth
note: Hebrew 'adam hiqnani is from qanah ("acquire"): "a man acquired me", i.e. I have been a bondservant (many emend to "the land has been my possession"); the KJV linked it with miqneh ("cattle").

kjv: What are these wounds in thine hands?
mine: What are these wounds on your chest?
note: Hebrew beyn yadeykha is literally "between your hands", i.e. on the chest or torso (cf. 2 Kgs 9:24); in context these are the self-inflicted cuts of an ecstatic prophet, and "in thine hands" invites a reading as nail wounds.

kjv: the light shall not be clear, nor dark
mine: there will be no light; the glorious lights will congeal
note: An obscure line: lo'-yihyeh 'or yeqarot yiqpa'un (ketiv) / weqippa'on (qere); yeqarot "precious, glorious ones" is probably the luminaries and qp' means "congeal, freeze" (many emend to "no cold or frost"). The KJV took the words as "clear" and "dark".

kjv: there shall be no more the Canaanite
mine: there will no longer be a trader
note: Hebrew kena'ani can be the ethnic term or the common noun "trader, merchant" (as in Prov 31:24; Zeph 1:11); in a verse about Temple vessels and sacrifices the commercial sense fits well.

kjv: The burden of the word
mine: An oracle: the word
note: Hebrew massa' is a technical heading for a prophetic pronouncement ("oracle"), not a "burden" in the sense of a load.

kjv: for the dragons of the wilderness
mine: to the jackals of the wilderness
note: Hebrew tannot (from tan) denotes jackals, animals of ruined places; "dragons" comes from confusion with tannin.

kjv: We (Edom) are impoverished
mine: We (Edom) have been shattered
note: Hebrew rushashnu is from rashash, "beat down, shatter", describing Edom's devastation rather than poverty (from the similar rush, "be poor").

kjv: The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel
mine: Great is Yahweh, even beyond the borders of Israel
note: Hebrew me'al ligvul yisra'el means "above / beyond the territory of Israel": Yahweh's greatness extends past Israel's borders, as seen in his judgment of Edom.

kjv: Who is there even among you (the priests) that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought.
mine: Oh, that one of you (the priests) would shut the doors, so that you would not light fires on My altar for nothing!
note: Hebrew mi gam-bakhem weyisgor delatayim is an idiomatic wish ("who among you would shut...?" = "if only someone would shut"): God wants the Temple closed rather than receive worthless sacrifices; the KJV reads it as a complaint that priests will not work without pay.

kjv: my (Yahweh's) name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered
mine: my (Yahweh's) name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered
note: The Hebrew clauses are verbless or participial (gadol shemi, muqtar mugash), naturally present tense; the KJV makes them a future prophecy, a reading important in later Christian interpretation (e.g. of the Eucharist).

kjv: ye (the priests) brought that which was torn
mine: You (the priests) bring what was stolen
note: Hebrew gazul is the passive participle of gazal, "seize, rob": animals taken by robbery, not torn by beasts (which would be terefah).

kjv: my (Yahweh's) name is dreadful among the heathen
mine: my (Yahweh's) name is feared among the nations
note: Hebrew nora' means "feared, awe-inspiring"; modern "dreadful" suggests "very bad".

kjv: I (Yahweh) will corrupt your (the priests') seed
mine: I (Yahweh) am going to rebuke your (the priests') offspring
note: Hebrew go'er means "rebuke" (threaten, check); the LXX/Vulgate read zeroa' ("arm") and "cut off". "Corrupt" matches neither the Hebrew verb nor the versions.

kjv: the master and the scholar
mine: whoever he may be
note: Hebrew 'er we'oneh, literally "one who rouses and one who answers", is an obscure idiom generally taken as an all-inclusive pair ("anyone at all"); the KJV's "master and scholar" follows a rabbinic guess (teacher and pupil).

kjv: And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one?
mine: Did not the One make you, and is not a remnant of spirit His? And what was the One seeking?
note: One of the most obscure verses in the OT; the Hebrew welo'-'echad 'asah ushe'ar ruach lo can mean "did not one (God) make (them)" or "no one would do (this) who had a remnant of spirit". Both renderings are attempts; the KJV takes "one" as the one flesh of marriage.

kjv: he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment
mine: For the man who hates and divorces ... covers his garment with violence
note: Hebrew ki-sane' shallach has a third-person participle ("one hating"), not "I hate"; it can mean "(he) hates divorce" or describe the man who rejects and divorces his wife. The second clause is wekhissah chamas 'al-levusho, "covers his garment with violence" (violence stains him), which the KJV reverses. Context: the man who hates and divorces covers his garment with violence (medium confidence). Sane' is third person ('one hating'), not 'I hate', and the LXX, 4QXIIa, Targum and Vulgate all make the husband the subject. This continues 2:14-15 and fits the closing 'do not be faithless'. Yet a divine statement 'I hate divorce' is widely held, and the syntax is difficult. Other possible meanings: (1) 'For I hate divorce / he hates divorce, says Yahweh' — KJV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, NET, as God's own attitude; (2) 'if you hate her, divorce her' (permission, cf. Deut 24:1) — 4QXIIa, Targum, Vulgate, LXX 'if you hate and send away'; (3) 'covers violence with his garment' — KJV, reversing the image.

kjv: therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed
mine: and you, children of Jacob, have not come to an end
note: Hebrew we'attem beney-ya'aqov lo' kelitem is joined by a simple "and"; it may mean "you have not perished" (so KJV, with an added "therefore") or "you have not ceased (from your ways)", leading into 3:7.

kjv: that there may be meat in mine (Yahweh's) house
mine: so that there may be food in My (Yahweh's) house
note: Hebrew teref means food or provisions (the tithes were largely grain, wine and oil); "meat" in 1611 meant food in general.

kjv: that there shall not be room enough to receive it (the blessing)
mine: until there is no more need
note: Hebrew 'ad beli-day means "until there is no lack / without limit"; the KJV's italic supplement "room enough to receive it" gives a picture not in the Hebrew.

kjv: in that day when I (Yahweh) make up my jewels
mine: My treasured possession, on the day that I (Yahweh) act
note: Hebrew segullah is a "treasured possession" (as in Exod 19:5), describing the God-fearers themselves; 'oseh is "act, do" (as in 3:21). The KJV makes "jewels" the object of "make up".

kjv: grow up as calves of the stall
mine: leap like calves from the stall
note: Hebrew pishtem is from push, "frisk, leap, paw the ground" (cf. Jer 50:11; Hab 1:8), describing released calves frolicking rather than growing. (KJV numbers this verse 4:2.)

kjv: the great and dreadful day of the LORD
mine: the great and terrible day of Yahweh
note: Hebrew nora' means "fearsome, awe-inspiring"; modern "dreadful" suggests merely very bad. (KJV 4:5.)

kjv: lest I (Yahweh) come and smite the earth with a curse
mine: so that I (Yahweh) do not come and strike the land with a ban of destruction
note: Hebrew cherem is the "ban" of total destruction (devotion to God), stronger than a curse, and ha'arets here is most naturally the land of Israel. (KJV 4:6.)

kjv: Abia begat Asa
mine: Abijah the father of Asaph
note: SBLGNT (with the earliest manuscripts) reads Asaph, probably Matthew's own spelling or a play on the psalmist; TR "asa" corrects it to the king's name (also 1:8).

kjv: Manasses begat Amon
mine: Manasseh the father of Amos
note: Earliest manuscripts read Amos (possibly echoing the prophet); TR "amon" harmonises with 2 Kings 21.

kjv: till she (Mary) had brought forth her firstborn son
mine: until she (Mary) had given birth to a son
note: TR adds "ton prototokon" ("her firstborn") from Luke 2:7; it is absent from the earliest witnesses (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus), and the phrase was later used in debates about Mary's other children.

kjv: we (the magi) have seen his (Jesus') star in the east
mine: we (the magi) saw His (Jesus') star when it rose
note: en te anatole (singular, with article) is the technical astronomical term for a star's rising; "from the east" in 2:1 is the plural apo anatolon, so KJV's "in the east" blurs the distinction.

kjv: those which were lunatick
mine: those having seizures
note: seleniazomenoi ("moon-struck") denotes epileptic seizures (cf. 17:15); "lunatic" now means insane.

kjv: whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause
mine: everyone who is angry with his brother
note: TR adds "eike" ("without a cause"), absent from P64, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the addition softens an absolute prohibition of anger.

kjv: it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery
mine: it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.'
note: TR adds "tois archaiois" ("by/to them of old") by assimilation to 5:21 and 5:33.

kjv: bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you
mine: pray for those who persecute you
note: TR expands the saying with phrases from Luke 6:27-28 ("eulogeite tous katarōmenous ... epēreazontōn"); the shorter text is in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: do not even the publicans so
mine: Do not even the Gentiles do the same
note: TR repeats "telōnai" (tax collectors) from 5:46; the earliest manuscripts read "ethnikoi" (Gentiles).

kjv: hell fire
mine: the Gehenna of fire
note: geenna tou pyros names the valley of Hinnom as the place of final judgment; KJV's "hell" merges it with hades and the OT Sheol (systematic in KJV).

kjv: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the doxology "hoti sou estin he basileia kai he dynamis kai he doxa eis tous aionas amen", a liturgical ending (cf. Didache 8.2, 1 Chr 29:11) absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae and the early fathers' commentaries on the prayer.

kjv: deliver us from evil
mine: deliver us from the evil one
note: apo tou ponerou may be neuter ("evil") or masculine ("the evil one", as in 13:19, 38); Matthew's usage favours the personal sense.

kjv: shall reward thee openly
mine: will reward you
note: TR adds "en to phanero" ("openly") here and in 6:6, 6:18, making the public reward explicit; absent from the earliest manuscripts.

kjv: that ye do not your alms before men
mine: Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people
note: TR reads eleemosynen ("alms"); the earliest manuscripts read dikaiosynen ("righteousness"), a heading for almsgiving, prayer and fasting (6:2-18).

kjv: Give us this day our daily bread
mine: Give us today our bread for the coming day
note: epiousios is a rare word of uncertain meaning: "for the coming day", "necessary for existence" or "daily"; "daily" follows the Old Latin quotidianum.

kjv: can add one cubit unto his stature
mine: can add a single hour to his span of life
note: helikia can mean stature or age/lifespan; a cubit (c. 45 cm) added to one's height would be no small thing, so a measure of time fits the context of anxiety about life.

kjv: into the country of the Gergesenes
mine: to the country of the Gadarenes
note: TR "gergesenon" (an Origen-era correction) against "Gadarenon" in Vaticanus and others; the manuscripts also offer Gerasenes, reflecting uncertainty about the site.

kjv: What have we (the demons) to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God?
mine: What have You to do with us (the demons), O Son of God?
note: TR adds "Iesou" from Mark 5:7/Luke 8:28.

kjv: I (Jesus) am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance
mine: For I (Jesus) came not to call the righteous, but sinners
note: TR adds "eis metanoian" ("to repentance") from Luke 5:32; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus
mine: Thaddaeus
note: TR conflates two readings ("Lebbaios ho epiklētheis Thaddaios"); the earliest manuscripts have simply Thaddaeus.

kjv: Simon the Canaanite
mine: Simon the Zealot
note: Kananaios transliterates Aramaic qan'ana "zealot" (Luke 6:15 Zēlōtēs); "Canaanite" wrongly suggests an inhabitant of Canaan.

kjv: he (John) sent two of his disciples
mine: he (John) sent word by his disciples
note: TR "duo" ("two") from Luke 7:19; earliest manuscripts read "dia" ("by/through").

kjv: wisdom is justified of her children
mine: wisdom is justified by her deeds
note: TR "teknon" ("children") assimilates to Luke 7:35; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "ergon" ("works/deeds"), linking to "the deeds of the Christ" in 11:2.

kjv: which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell
mine: will you (Capernaum) be exalted to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades
note: TR "he ... hypsotheisa" (statement) vs the earliest "me ... hypsothese" (question expecting "no"); KJV also renders hades as "hell".

kjv: in this place is [one] greater than the temple
mine: something greater than the temple is here
note: TR has masculine meizon ("one greater"); the earliest manuscripts have neuter meizon ("something greater"), as also in 12:41-42 where KJV supplies "a greater".

kjv: in the whale's belly
mine: in the belly of the great fish
note: ketos is any huge sea creature (LXX for Jonah's dag gadol); "whale" is a specific modern identification.

kjv: sowed tares among the wheat
mine: sowed darnel among the wheat
note: zizania is darnel (Lolium temulentum), a weed that looks like wheat until it heads; "tares" (vetch) is a different plant.

kjv: the harvest is the end of the world
mine: The harvest is the end of the age
note: synteleia aionos is "the consummation of the age" (also 13:40, 49; 24:3; 28:20); KJV's "world" suggests the end of the physical cosmos rather than of the present era.

kjv: his (Jesus') brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas
mine: his (Jesus') brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas
note: TR "Iōsēs" (from Mark 6:3) against "Iōsēph" in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: kept secret from the foundation of the world
mine: hidden since the foundation
note: TR adds "kosmou" ("of the world"); its absence in Sinaiticus (first hand) and others makes the shorter text likely.

kjv: the ship was now in the midst of the sea
mine: the boat by this time was a long way from the land
note: TR "meson tes thalasses en" (from Mark 6:47); Vaticanus and others read "stadious pollous apo tes ges apeichen" ("many stadia from the land").

kjv: This people draweth nigh unto me (God) with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips
mine: This people honors Me (God) with their lips
note: TR adds "engizei moi ... to stomati auton" by fuller assimilation to LXX Isa 29:13; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: came into the coasts of Magdala
mine: went to the region of Magadan
note: TR "Magdala" replaces the unknown "Magadan" of the earliest manuscripts with a known place.

kjv: made the commandment of God of none effect
mine: made void the word of God
note: TR "entolen" ("commandment", from 15:3) against "logon" ("word") in Sinaiticus (corrector) and Vaticanus.

kjv: the gates of hell shall not prevail against it (the church)
mine: the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it (the church)
note: pylai hadou are the gates of the realm of the dead (Hades), i.e. death's power; KJV's "hell" suggests the place of punishment or demonic forces.

kjv: that he was Jesus the Christ
mine: that He was the Christ
note: TR adds "Iesous"; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 17:21 ("touto de to genos ouk ekporeuetai ei me en proseuche kai nesteia") is imported from Mark 9:29 (itself with "and fasting" added); it is absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Theta and early versions.

kjv: Because of your (the disciples') unbelief
mine: Because of your (the disciples') little faith
note: TR "apistian" ("unbelief") against "oligopistian" ("little faith") in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the rare word fits Matthew's usage (6:30, 8:26, 14:31, 16:8).

kjv: he (the boy) is lunatick, and sore vexed
mine: he (the boy) has seizures and he suffers terribly
note: seleniazetai describes epileptic seizures (falling into fire and water); "lunatic" now means insane.

kjv: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 18:11 ("elthen gar ho huios tou anthropou sosai to apololos") is imported from Luke 19:10; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Theta and early versions.

kjv: Until seventy times seven
mine: seventy-seven times
note: hebdomekontakis hepta echoes LXX Gen 4:24 (Lamech's "seventy-seven-fold"), so 77 is the likely meaning; 490 is a possible reading of the Greek.

kjv: forgive not every one his brother their trespasses
mine: if you do not forgive your brother from your heart
note: TR adds "ta paraptomata auton" ("their trespasses") at the end; absent from the earliest manuscripts.

kjv: Why callest thou me (Jesus) good? there is none good but one, that is, God
mine: Why do you ask Me (Jesus) about what is good? There is only one Who is good
note: TR "ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei me heis ho theos" assimilates to Mark 10:18/Luke 18:19; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have Matthew's distinctive "ti me erotas peri tou agathou; heis estin ho agathos".

kjv: Good Master, what good thing shall I do
mine: Teacher, what good deed must I do
note: TR adds "agathe" ("good") to "Teacher" from Mark/Luke; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus, matching Matthew's reworded reply in 19:17.

kjv: in the regeneration
mine: in the renewal of all things
note: palingenesia here is the cosmic renewal of the world at the end (as in Stoic and Jewish usage), not the individual spiritual "regeneration" of Titus 3:5 that the English word now suggests.

kjv: for many be called, but few chosen
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "polloi gar eisin kletoi oligoi de eklektoi" from 22:14; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others.

kjv: and to be baptized with the baptism that I (Jesus) am baptized with
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the baptism clause here and in 20:23 from Mark 10:38-39; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: ye have made it (the temple) a den of thieves
mine: you make it (the temple) a den of robbers
note: lestai are robbers or bandits (Jer 7:11), not sneak-thieves (kleptai); the image is a bandits' hideout.

kjv: went into the temple of God
mine: entered the temple
note: TR adds "tou theou"; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 23:14 is imported from Mark 12:40/Luke 20:47; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae and early versions, and placed before or after 23:13 in different manuscripts.

kjv: for one is your Master, even Christ
mine: for you have one teacher
note: TR "kathegetes ho christos" from 23:10; earliest manuscripts read simply "ho didaskalos".

kjv: which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel
mine: straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel
note: diylizontes is filtering liquid to strain out an impurity; "strain at" (perhaps a printing slip for "strain out") suggests exertion or difficulty swallowing.

kjv: no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only
mine: not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the Father only
note: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus (original hand), Bezae and others include "oude ho huios" ("nor the Son"); TR omits it, likely an early omission because the admission of the Son's ignorance was doctrinally awkward (it stands undisputed at Mark 13:32).

kjv: and of the end of the world
mine: and of the end of the age
note: synteleia tou aionos is the consummation of the present age (as at 13:39); "world" shifts the question to the end of the physical cosmos.

kjv: famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes
mine: famines and earthquakes
note: TR adds "kai loimoi" ("and pestilences", a wordplay with limoi) from Luke 21:11; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: there will the eagles be gathered together
mine: there the vultures will gather
note: aetoi gathering at a carcass are vultures (the Greek word covers both); eagles do not flock to corpses.

kjv: neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh
mine: neither the day nor the hour
note: TR adds "en he ho huios tou anthropou erchetai" (from 24:44); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others.

kjv: this is my blood of the new testament
mine: this is My blood of the covenant
note: TR adds "kaines" ("new") from Luke 22:20/1 Cor 11:25; absent from P37, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus. KJV's "testament" for diatheke (here the covenant of Exod 24:8) also misleads modern readers.

kjv: Friend, wherefore art thou (Judas) come?
mine: Friend, do what you (Judas) came to do
note: eph' ho parei is elliptical; most take it as a command ("[do] that for which you are here"), not a question, which would require a different construction.

kjv: a notable prisoner, called Barabbas
mine: a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas
note: SBLGNT (with Theta, family 1 and manuscripts known to Origen) reads "Iesoun Barabban" in 27:16-17, sharpening Pilate's choice between two men named Jesus; TR omits the first name, perhaps out of reverence. Context: Jesus Barabbas (SBLGNT) (medium confidence). SBLGNT reads Iesoun Barabban in 27:16-17 with Theta, family 1 and copies known to Origen, who disliked giving the name Jesus to a sinner; omission out of reverence is easier to explain than insertion, and Pilate's choice between two men called Jesus gains point. But the supporting witnesses are few, and NA28 brackets the name. Other possible meanings: (1) 'a notable prisoner, called Barabbas' — TR/Majority text, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus (whose 'ton Barabban' in 27:17 may preserve a trace of the name), most manuscripts, KJV, ESV, NASB, CSB. 'Jesus Barabbas' is read by NIV, NRSV and NET.

kjv: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the fulfilment citation of Ps 22:18 from John 19:24; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus, Bezae.

kjv: They (the soldiers) gave him (Jesus) vinegar to drink mingled with gall
mine: they (the soldiers) offered Him (Jesus) wine to drink, mixed with gall
note: TR "oxos" ("vinegar", conforming to Ps 69:21) against "oinon" ("wine") in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: Truly this was the Son of God
mine: Truly this was the Son of God
note: theou huios without articles on a Roman soldier's lips may mean "a son of God"; both versions follow the Christian confessional sense.

kjv: And as they (the women) went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them
mine: And behold, Jesus met them (the women)
note: TR adds "hos de eporeuonto apangeilai tois mathetais autou"; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations
mine: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations
note: matheteusate is "make disciples", followed by baptizing and teaching as its means; KJV's "teach" anticipates the separate verb didaskontes in 28:20.

kjv: unto the end of the world. Amen.
mine: to the end of the age
note: synteleia tou aionos is the end of the age (as at 13:39, 24:3); TR also adds a closing "amen".

kjv: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God
mine: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ
note: SBLGNT follows Sinaiticus (first hand), Theta, 28 and Origen in omitting "huiou theou"; TR includes it (with Vaticanus, Bezae). The manuscripts are divided, and the phrase may have been lost by eye-skip over the abbreviated nomina sacra or added early.

kjv: As it is written in the prophets
mine: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet
note: TR "en tois prophetais" against "en to Esaia to prophete" in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae; the composite citation (Mal 3:1 + Isa 40:3) was evidently "corrected" so as not to attribute Malachi to Isaiah.

kjv: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand
mine: Moved with anger, He stretched out His hand
note: SBLGNT adopts orgistheis ("angered", Bezae and Old Latin) as the harder reading that scribes would soften, against splanchnistheis ("moved with compassion") in TR and most manuscripts; the choice is disputed. Context: moved with anger (orgistheis) (medium confidence). SBLGNT adopts orgistheis (Bezae and several Old Latin manuscripts) as the harder reading: scribes would soften anger to compassion more readily than the reverse, and Matthew and Luke both omit the emotion here. 1:43 'sternly charged him' fits. But nearly all manuscripts read splanchnistheis, and NA28 prints it. Other possible meanings: (1) 'moved with compassion/pity' — splanchnistheis, TR/Majority, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, most manuscripts and versions, NA28, KJV, ESV, NASB, CSB; (2) anger directed at the disease and its effects rather than at the man — NIV 'indignant', NET 'indignation' and commentators who adopt orgistheis.

kjv: I (Jesus) came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance
mine: I (Jesus) came not to call the righteous, but sinners
note: TR adds "eis metanoian" from Luke 5:32 (as in Matt 9:13).

kjv: is in danger of eternal damnation
mine: is guilty of an eternal sin
note: TR "aioniou kriseos" ("eternal judgment") replaces the harder "aioniou hamartematos" ("eternal sin") of Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; KJV's "damnation" adds a further shade of meaning.

kjv: when his (Jesus') friends heard of it
mine: when His (Jesus') family heard it
note: hoi par' autou ("those from him") are his relatives, who appear in 3:31; "friends" weakens the point that his own family thought him out of his mind.

kjv: Simon the Canaanite
mine: Simon the Zealot
note: Kananaios is Aramaic qan'ana "zealot", not "of Canaan" (as at Matt 10:4).

kjv: how is it that ye (the disciples) have no faith?
mine: Have you (the disciples) still no faith?
note: TR "pos ouk echete pistin" against "oupo echete pistin" ("not yet/still not") in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: to know the mystery of the kingdom of God
mine: the secret of the kingdom of God
note: mysterion is a revealed secret (God's hidden plan now disclosed), not something mysterious or unknowable as "mystery" now suggests; TR also adds "gnonai" ("to know") from Matthew/Luke.

kjv: into the country of the Gadarenes
mine: to the country of the Gerasenes
note: TR "Gadarenon" (Matthew's form) against "Gerasenon" in Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: As soon as Jesus heard the word
mine: But overhearing what they (the men from the ruler's house) said
note: TR "eutheos akousas" against "parakousas" ("overhearing" or "ignoring") in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds this sentence from Matt 10:15; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: he (Herod) did many things, and heard him (John) gladly
mine: he (Herod) was greatly perplexed, and yet he heard him (John) gladly
note: TR "polla epoiei" against "polla eporei" ("was much perplexed") in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus, a one-letter difference that changes Herod's response.

kjv: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 7:16 is a scribal refrain (from 4:9, 4:23); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Codex Regius and others.

kjv: and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
mine: and is expelled? (Thus He (Jesus) declared all foods clean.)
note: katharizon panta ta bromata (masculine participle in the best manuscripts) agrees with the subject of "he says" in 7:18, i.e. Jesus' declaration that all foods are clean; KJV (with TR's neuter katharizon) attaches it to the digestive process, losing Mark's comment on the food laws.

kjv: as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye (the Pharisees) do
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "baptismous xeston kai poterion ..." from 7:4 and 7:13.

kjv: Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town
mine: Do not even enter the village
note: TR adds "mede eipes tini en te kome"; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: and lose his own soul
mine: and forfeit his life
note: psyche here (as in 8:35 "save his life ... lose it") is one's life or self; KJV switches between "life" in 8:35 and "soul" in 8:36-37 for the same word, obscuring the wordplay.

kjv: This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
mine: This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer.
note: TR adds "kai nesteia" ("and fasting"), absent from Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus; the addition reflects growing ascetic practice in the early church.

kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 9:44 repeats 9:48 (Isa 66:24) after each saying; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, L, W.

kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
mine: (absent)
note: As 9:44, a scribal repetition of 9:48 absent from the earliest manuscripts.

kjv: If thou (the father) canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
mine: 'If you (the father) can'! All things are possible for one who believes.
note: TR adds "pisteusai" ("to believe"), turning Jesus' echo of the father's "if you can" into a condition on the father's faith.

kjv: cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I (the father) believe
mine: cried out and said, "I (the father) believe
note: TR adds "meta dakryon" ("with tears") and "kyrie"; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds a second clause from Lev 2:13; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
mine: how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God!
