note: TR adds "tous pepoithotas epi tois chremasin" ("for those who trust in riches"), softening the saying into one about attitude rather than wealth or entry as such; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: come, take up the cross, and follow me (Jesus)
mine: come, follow Me (Jesus)
note: TR adds "aras ton stauron" (from 8:34); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: And the Pharisees came to him (Jesus), and asked him
mine: And they asked Him (Jesus)
note: SBLGNT alone among the major editions omits "proselthontes Pharisaioi" (with D and some Old Latin); WH, Tregelles, NA28 and the Byzantine text all have it, so the KJV here matches most critical editions. My first draft had wrongly supplied the words; corrected to the SBLGNT text.

kjv: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 11:26 is imported from Matt 6:15; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W, Delta.

kjv: Blessed be the kingdom of our father David, that cometh in the name of the Lord
mine: Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!
note: TR repeats "en onomati kyriou" from 11:9; absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus.

kjv: ye have made it (the temple) a den of thieves
mine: you have made it (the temple) a den of robbers
note: lestai are bandits, as at Matt 21:13.

kjv: the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing
mine: the abomination of desolation standing
note: TR adds "to rethen hypo Danieel tou prophetou" from Matt 24:15; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae.

kjv: Take ye heed, watch and pray
mine: Be on guard, keep awake
note: TR adds "kai proseuchesthe" ("and pray"); absent from Vaticanus and Bezae.

kjv: This is my blood of the new testament
mine: This is My blood of the covenant
note: TR adds "kaines" ("new") from Luke/Paul; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, L. KJV's "testament" for diatheke also obscures the covenant allusion (Exod 24:8).

kjv: Take, eat: this is my body
mine: Take; this is My body
note: TR adds "phagete" ("eat") from Matt 26:26; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, D.

kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he (Jesus) was numbered with the transgressors.
mine: (absent)
note: TR's 15:28 imports Isa 53:12 from Luke 22:37; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, C, D, and Mark rarely cites fulfilment formulae.

kjv: saw that he (Jesus) so cried out, and gave up the ghost
mine: saw that in this way He (Jesus) breathed His last
note: TR adds "kraxas" ("cried out"); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L. KJV's "gave up the ghost" for exepneusen ("breathed out") is also now an idiom rather than a description.

kjv: Now when Jesus was risen early ... (16:9-20, printed as part of Mark without comment)
mine: [[16:9-20 in double brackets]]
note: The "longer ending" is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus and unknown to Clement and Origen; Eusebius and Jerome say it was missing from most copies they knew, and its vocabulary and style differ from Mark's. SBLGNT prints it in double brackets as a later addition; KJV presents it as Mark's own text, including the snake-handling and poison promises of 16:17-18. Context: a later addition, kept in double brackets (high confidence). Sinaiticus and Vaticanus end at 16:8; Clement and Origen show no knowledge of 16:9-20; Eusebius and Jerome report it missing from most copies they knew; and its vocabulary, style and abrupt reintroduction of Mary Magdalene (named in 16:1) differ from Mark. Most scholars and SBLGNT judge it an early second-century addition. Other possible meanings: (1) the authentic conclusion of Mark — TR/Majority, A, C, D, W and the great majority of manuscripts, Irenaeus (Against Heresies 3.10.5 cites 16:19), Tatian; KJV, NKJV and defenders such as Burgon, Lunn and Snapp; (2) the Shorter Ending — L, Psi and a few others; (3) Mark's true ending was lost after 16:8 rather than meant to stop there — some scholars.

kjv: (absent)
mine: [[But they (the women) reported briefly to Peter ... eternal salvation. Amen.]]
note: The "shorter ending", found in Codex Bobiensis (k) and several Greek manuscripts (L, Psi, 099) that also have the longer ending, is printed by SBLGNT in double brackets after 16:8; TR and KJV omit it.

kjv: he that believeth not shall be damned
mine: whoever does not believe will be condemned
note: katakrithesetai is "will be condemned" (judicial verdict); "damned" has acquired a specific sense of eternal perdition and an expletive use.

kjv: the Lord is with thee (Mary): blessed art thou among women
mine: the Lord is with you (Mary)!
note: TR adds "eulogemene sy en gynaixin" from Elizabeth's words in 1:42; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W. The phrase is familiar from the Ave Maria.

kjv: that holy thing which shall be born of thee (Mary)
mine: the child to be born
note: TR adds "ek sou" ("of thee"); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, C, D.

kjv: the dayspring from on high hath visited us
mine: the sunrise from on high will visit us
note: TR aorist "epeskepsato" against future "episkepsetai" in Sinaiticus (first hand) and Vaticanus.

kjv: seeing I (Mary) know not a man
mine: since I (Mary) do not know a man
note: Both keep the Hebraic euphemism (ginosko = sexual relations); modern readers may miss that Mary states she is a virgin.

kjv: on earth peace, good will toward men
mine: on earth peace among those with whom He (God) is pleased
note: TR has nominative "eudokia" (a third clause, "good will toward men"); Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, A, D have genitive "eudokias" ("people of [God's] good pleasure"), a Semitic idiom also found at Qumran; one letter changes the angels' message.

kjv: And Joseph and his (Jesus') mother marvelled
mine: And His (Jesus') father and His mother marveled
note: TR "Ioseph" replaces "ho pater autou" of Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, W, evidently to avoid calling Joseph Jesus' father; Luke himself uses "his parents" (2:41) and Mary says "your father and I" (2:48).

kjv: Joseph and his (Jesus') mother knew not of it
mine: His (Jesus') parents did not know it
note: TR "Ioseph kai he meter autou" against "hoi goneis autou" in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, for the same reason as 2:33.

kjv: the days of her (Mary's) purification
mine: the time came for their purification
note: TR "autes" ("her") against "auton" ("their") in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, L.

kjv: wist ye not that I (Jesus) must be about my Father's business?
mine: Did you not know that I (Jesus) must be in My Father's house?
note: en tois tou patros mou ("in the things of my Father") most naturally means "in my Father's house" (contrasted with searching elsewhere); "business" is a possible but less likely sense.

kjv: there was no room for them (Joseph and Mary) in the inn
mine: there was no place for them (Joseph and Mary) in the guest room
note: katalyma is a guest room or lodging (the same word for the "guest chamber" of 22:11), not necessarily a commercial inn (pandocheion, 10:34).

kjv: Which was the son of Aminadab, which was the son of Aram
mine: the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni
note: TR assimilates to Matt 1:3-4 and Ruth 4:19 ("Aram"); the earliest manuscripts have the otherwise unknown names Admin and Arni (with many variants).

kjv: Which was the son of Jose
mine: the son of Joshua
note: TR "Iose" against "Iesou" (Joshua/Jesus) in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L; KJV elsewhere renders Iesous as "Jesus" even for Joshua (Acts 7:45, Heb 4:8).

kjv: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written
mine: It is written
note: TR adds "hypage opiso mou satana" from Matt 16:23 (cf. Matt 4:10); absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, L, W.

kjv: he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "iasasthai tous syntetrimmenous ten kardian" from LXX Isa 61:1; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, L, W.

kjv: but by every word of God
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "all' epi panti rhemati theou" from Matt 4:4; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W.

kjv: he (Jesus) preached in the synagogues of Galilee
mine: he (Jesus) was preaching in the synagogues of Judea
note: TR "Galilaias" corrects the harder "Ioudaias" (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, L), which Luke uses for the whole Jewish land.

kjv: and both are preserved
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "kai amphoteroi syntērountai" from Matt 9:17; absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W.

kjv: straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better
mine: desires new, for he says, 'The old is good.'
note: TR adds "eutheos" and has the comparative "chrestoteros" ("better"); the earliest manuscripts have the positive "chrestos" ("good").

kjv: on the second sabbath after the first
mine: On a Sabbath
note: TR "en sabbato deuteroproto" (a puzzling word found nowhere else, probably from a marginal note) against "en sabbato" in P4, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W.

kjv: for it (the house) was founded upon a rock
mine: because it (the house) had been well built
note: TR "tethemeliōto gar epi ten petran" (from Matt 7:25) against "dia to kalos oikodomesthai auten" in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W.

kjv: lend, hoping for nothing again
mine: lend, expecting nothing in return
note: meden apelpizontes may mean "expecting nothing back" or (as in later Greek) "despairing of no one"; both versions take the first sense.

kjv: there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist
mine: none is greater than John
note: TR adds "prophetes" and "tou baptistou"; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L, W.

kjv: Her (the woman's) sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much
mine: her (the woman's) sins, which are many, are forgiven—for she loved much
note: hoti can give the ground of the statement (her love shows she has been forgiven, as the parable in 7:41-43 implies) rather than the cause of forgiveness; KJV's wording, like mine, is ambiguous, but has often been read as love earning forgiveness.

kjv: the country of the Gadarenes
mine: the country of the Gerasenes
note: TR "Gadarenon" against "Gerasenon" in P75, Vaticanus, D (also 8:37).

kjv: the multitude throng thee (Jesus) and press thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
mine: the crowds surround You (Jesus) and are pressing in on You!
note: TR adds "kai legeis, tis ho hapsamenos mou;" from Mark 5:31; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L.

kjv: that he (Jesus) would not command them (the demons) to go out into the deep
mine: not to command them (the demons) to depart into the abyss
note: abyssos is the underworld prison of demons (Rev 9:1, 20:3), not the sea ("the deep"), into which the pigs later plunge.

kjv: and said, Ye (James and John) know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them.
mine: But He (Jesus) turned and rebuked them (James and John).
note: TR adds Jesus' words (9:55b-56a) with D and later manuscripts; absent from P45, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, C, L, W. The saying echoes Luke 19:10.

kjv: consume them (the Samaritans), even as Elias did?
mine: consume them (the Samaritans)?
note: TR adds "hos kai Elias epoiesen" (alluding to 2 Kgs 1:10-12); absent from P45, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L.

kjv: This is my beloved Son: hear him (Jesus)
mine: This is My Son, My Chosen One; listen to Him (Jesus)!
note: TR "agapetos" ("beloved", from Mark/Matthew) against "eklelegmenos" ("chosen") in P45, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L (cf. Isa 42:1, Luke 23:35).

kjv: spake of his (Jesus') decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem
mine: spoke of His (Jesus') departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem
note: exodos is "departure" and evokes Israel's Exodus (death, resurrection and ascension as a new exodus); KJV's "decease" narrows it to death.

kjv: the Lord appointed other seventy also
mine: the Lord appointed seventy-two others
note: TR "hebdomekonta" against "hebdomekonta duo" in P75, Vaticanus, D (also 10:17); the manuscripts are closely divided, and both numbers have symbolic resonance (the nations of Gen 10 are 70 in the MT, 72 in the LXX).

kjv: But one thing is needful
mine: but few things are needed, or only one
note: SBLGNT follows P3, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus (oligon de estin chreia e henos); TR has the shorter "henos de estin chreia" with P45, P75, A, C, W.

kjv: Jesus rejoiced in spirit
mine: He rejoiced in the Holy Spirit
note: TR "to pneumati" (Jesus' own spirit) against "to pneumati to hagio" in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, D, L.

kjv: which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell
mine: will you (Capernaum) be exalted to heaven? You shall be brought down to Hades
note: As at Matt 11:23, TR has a statement where the earliest manuscripts have a question expecting "no"; KJV again renders hades as "hell".

kjv: Our Father which art in heaven ... Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.
mine: Father, may Your name be kept holy. Your kingdom come.
note: TR expands Luke's shorter prayer to match Matthew 6:9-10, adding "hemon ho en tois ouranois" and "genetheto to thelema sou ..."; P75, Vaticanus and others (with Origen's explicit testimony) have Luke's own five-petition form.

kjv: but deliver us from evil
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds "alla rysai hemas apo tou ponerou" from Matt 6:13; absent from P75, Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, L.

kjv: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone?
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the bread/stone pair from Matt 7:9; absent from P45, P75, Vaticanus.

kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!
mine: Woe to you!
note: TR adds "grammateis kai pharisaioi hypokritai" from Matthew; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, C, L.

kjv: because of his importunity
mine: because of his shameless persistence
note: anaideia is "shamelessness" (lack of regard for propriety), which may describe the asker's boldness or, as some argue, the sleeper's concern to avoid shame.

kjv: he (the master of the house) would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through
mine: he (the master of the house) would not have left his house to be broken into
note: TR adds "egregoresen an kai" from Matt 24:43; absent from P75, Sinaiticus (first hand), D.

kjv: seek ye the kingdom of God
mine: seek His kingdom
note: TR "tou theou" against "autou" in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, L.

kjv: can add to his stature one cubit
mine: can add a single hour to his span of life
note: As at Matt 6:27, helikia is better taken as lifespan; 12:26 calls this "the smallest thing", which a cubit of height would not be.

kjv: your (Jerusalem's) house is left unto you desolate
mine: your (Jerusalem's) house is forsaken
note: TR adds "eremos" ("desolate") from Matt 23:38; absent from P45, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, L.

kjv: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit
mine: Which of you, having a son or an ox that has fallen into a well
note: TR "onos" ("ass", by assimilation to 13:15) against the harder "huios" ("son") in P45, P75, Vaticanus, A, W.

kjv: the lord commended the unjust steward
mine: The master commended the dishonest manager
note: lord (kyrios) is ambiguous in English and has often been read as Jesus; in the parable it is the rich man, the steward's master.

kjv: that, when ye fail
mine: so that when it (unrighteous wealth) fails
note: TR "eklipete" (you fail, i.e. die) against "eklipe" (it, the mammon, fails).

kjv: with the crumbs which fell
mine: with what fell
note: TR adds "crumbs" (psichion) from Mt 15:27.

kjv: in hell he (the rich man) lift up his eyes
mine: in Hades, being in torment, he (the rich man) lifted up his eyes
note: Hell for hades, the realm of the dead, conflates it with Gehenna; Luke's scene is the intermediate state.

kjv: the kingdom of God is within you (the Pharisees)
mine: the kingdom of God is in your (the Pharisees') midst
note: entos hymon is addressed to the Pharisees; "within you" makes the kingdom an inner state, while the context (here/there, the Son of Man's day) points to its presence among them in Jesus.

kjv: Two [men] shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
mine: (absent)
note: Imported from Mt 24:40; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, W. Most TR editions print it; KJV includes it.

kjv: thither will the eagles be gathered together
mine: there the vultures will gather
note: aetos here means carrion birds gathering at a body.

kjv: I (the Pharisee) give tithes of all that I possess
mine: I (the Pharisee) give tithes of all that I get
note: ktaomai (present) means acquire, i.e. income, not existing possessions.

kjv: when Jesus saw that he (the ruler) was very sorrowful
mine: Jesus, seeing him (the ruler)
note: SBLGNT (with WH, Sinaiticus, B, L) omits "perilypon genomenon" (having become very sad), which Tregelles, NA28 and the TR include, repeating 18:23.

kjv: Occupy till I (the nobleman) come
mine: Engage in business until I (the nobleman) come
note: Occupy in 1611 meant "trade, do business"; a modern reader hears "hold territory".

kjv: them that sold therein, and them that bought
mine: those who sold
note: TR adds "and them that bought" from Mk 11:15.

kjv: and said unto them (the spies), Why tempt ye me (Jesus)?
mine: and said to them (the spies),
note: TR adds "Why tempt ye me?" from Mt 22:18 / Mk 12:15.

kjv: the same shall receive greater damnation
mine: They (the scribes) will receive the greater condemnation
note: krima is judgment/condemnation; "damnation" imports a doctrine of eternal punishment.

kjv: cast in unto the offerings of God
mine: contributed
note: TR adds "of God" (tou theou) to "the gifts".

kjv: that ye may be accounted worthy to escape
mine: that you may have strength to escape
note: TR "kataxiothete" (be counted worthy) against "katischysete" (have strength) in Sinaiticus, B, L, W.

kjv: which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me (Jesus)
mine: [which is given for you … poured out for you]
note: Both print 22:19b–20; SBLGNT brackets it because Codex Bezae and some Old Latin omit it (the "Western non-interpolation"). Most scholars now accept it.

kjv: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon
mine: Simon, Simon
note: TR adds an introductory "And the Lord said".

kjv: And there appeared an angel unto him (Jesus) from heaven, strengthening him.
mine: [[And there appeared to Him (Jesus) an angel from heaven …]]
note: 22:43–44 (the angel and the bloody sweat) are absent from P75, Vaticanus, A, W and others; SBLGNT double-brackets them as a very early addition. The KJV prints them without mark.

kjv: they struck him (Jesus) on the face, and asked him
mine: blindfolded Him (Jesus) and kept asking Him
note: TR adds "they struck him on the face" from Mk 14:65.

kjv: ye (the council) will not answer me (Jesus), nor let [me] go
mine: you (the council) will not answer
note: TR adds "me, nor let me go".

kjv: for I (Pilate) sent you to him (Herod)
mine: for he (Herod) sent Him (Jesus) back to us
note: TR "anepempsa gar hymas pros auton" against "anepempsen gar auton pros hemas" (P75, Sinaiticus, B).

kjv: (For of necessity he (Pilate) must release one unto them at the feast.)
mine: (absent)
note: Absent from P75, Vaticanus, A; appears at different places in other manuscripts, a sign of insertion from Mk 15:6 / Mt 27:15.

kjv: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
mine: [[And Jesus said, "Father, forgive them …"]]
note: The prayer is absent from P75, Vaticanus, D*, W and others; SBLGNT double-brackets it. The KJV prints it without mark. Its age and authenticity are debated. Context: uncertain; printed in double brackets with SBLGNT (low confidence). Strong early witnesses omit the prayer (P75, Vaticanus, D*, W, Theta), but Sinaiticus*, A, C, L, most manuscripts and early Fathers include it; its Lukan style (prayer to 'Father', 23:46; cf. Acts 7:60) supports authenticity, and deliberate omission is conceivable. The brackets mark doubt, not rejection. Other possible meanings: (1) authentic Luke, printed without marks — TR/Majority, Sinaiticus*, A, C, L, Irenaeus (Latin), KJV, and in the text of ESV, NIV, NRSV and NET with footnotes; (2) an authentic saying of Jesus from oral tradition but not part of Luke's text — Westcott and Hort; (3) a later addition modelled on Acts 7:60 — some textual critics.

kjv: written over him (Jesus) in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew
mine: an inscription over Him (Jesus)
note: TR adds the three languages from Jn 19:20.

kjv: he (the criminal) said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me
mine: he (the criminal) said, "Jesus, remember me
note: TR turns the vocative "Jesus" into "unto Jesus" and adds "Lord".

kjv: Certainly this was a righteous man
mine: Certainly this man was innocent
note: dikaios in a verdict after Pilate's threefold "no guilt" means innocent; "righteous" is also defensible.

kjv: and saith unto them, Peace [be] unto you
mine: he (Jesus) Himself stood among them
note: SBLGNT omits "and said to them, Peace to you" with Codex Bezae and Old Latin; most other critical editions (NA28) include it.

kjv: a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb
mine: a piece of broiled fish
note: TR adds "and of a honeycomb"; absent from P75, Sinaiticus, B, A, D.

kjv: repentance and remission of sins
mine: repentance for the forgiveness of sins
note: TR "kai" (and) against "eis" (for), the reading of P75, Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: praising and blessing God. Amen.
mine: blessing God.
note: TR conflates "praising" (D) and "blessing" (P75, B) and adds a liturgical "Amen".

kjv: without him (the Word) was not any thing made that was made. In him was life
mine: without Him (the Word) not one thing came into being. What has come into being in him was life
note: SBLGNT punctuates "ho gegonen" with v.4, following the earliest manuscripts and most early Fathers; the KJV attaches it to v.3. Both are grammatical.

kjv: the darkness comprehended it (the light) not
mine: the darkness has not overcome it (the light)
note: katalambano = seize, overtake (cf. 12:35); "comprehended" (in 1611 also "grasped") now reads as "understood".

kjv: the only begotten of the Father
mine: the only Son from the Father
note: monogenes = one of a kind, unique (Heb 11:17 of Isaac); "only begotten" follows the Latin "unigenitus". Also at 1:18, 3:16, 3:18.

kjv: the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom
mine: the only God, Who is at the Father's side
note: P66, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus read "monogenes theos"; the TR "monogenes huios" is the easier, later reading. The early text calls the Son "God" a second time in the prologue.

kjv: in Bethabara beyond Jordan
mine: in Bethany across the Jordan
note: Bethabara is Origen's conjecture, adopted in later manuscripts; the early text reads "Bethany".

kjv: Simon the son of Jona
mine: Simon the son of John
note: TR "Iona" assimilates to Mt 16:17; P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B read "Ioannou".

kjv: Hereafter ye shall see heaven open
mine: you will see heaven opened
note: TR adds "ap' arti" (from now on) from Mt 26:64.

kjv: containing two or three firkins apiece
mine: each holding two or three measures
note: Firkin is an English cask (about 9 gallons); "metretes" is about 39 litres, so the jars hold far more than a reader of "firkins" would picture.

kjv: Except a man be born again
mine: unless one is born from above
note: anothen means both "again" and "from above"; Nicodemus hears "again" (3:4), but John's usage (3:31, 19:11) is "from above". English cannot keep the pun; the KJV picks Nicodemus' sense.

kjv: the Son of man which is in heaven
mine: the Son of Man
note: TR adds "ho on en to ourano"; absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: should not perish, but have eternal life
mine: may have eternal life in Him (the Son of Man)
note: TR adds "should not perish" from 3:16.

kjv: he that believeth not the Son shall not see life
mine: whoever does not obey the Son shall not see life
note: apeitheo is "disobey", not "disbelieve"; John contrasts believing with disobedience.

kjv: God [is] a Spirit
mine: God is spirit
note: The KJV supplies the article "a" (in italics); the Greek predicates the nature of God ("spirit"), not membership of a class of spirits.

kjv: this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world
mine: this is indeed the Savior of the world
note: TR adds "ho Christos".

kjv: withered, waiting for the moving of the water
mine: blind, lame, and paralyzed
note: TR adds "waiting for the moving of the water" (5:3b), absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B, the lead-in to 5:4.

kjv: For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water ...
mine: (absent)
note: The angel stirring the water is absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B, C*, D; where present it is often marked with obeli. A popular explanation of 5:7 that entered the text.

kjv: Search the scriptures
mine: You (the Jews) search the Scriptures
note: eraunate can be imperative or indicative; the following "because you think" and "yet you refuse" (5:40) favour the indicative, a rebuke rather than a command.

kjv: he (Jesus) distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down
mine: he (Jesus) distributed them to those who were seated
note: TR adds the disciples as intermediaries, from Mt 14:19.

kjv: He that believeth on me (Jesus) hath everlasting life
mine: whoever believes has eternal life
note: TR adds "eis eme" (on me); absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: thou (Jesus) art that Christ, the Son of the living God
mine: You (Jesus) are the Holy One of God
note: TR assimilates Peter's confession to Mt 16:16; P75, Sinaiticus, B, C*, D read "the Holy One of God", a rarer title (cf. Mk 1:24).

kjv: I (Jesus) go not up yet unto this feast
mine: I (Jesus) am not going up to this feast
note: TR "oupo" (not yet) against "ouk" (not) in Sinaiticus, D; scribes softened the apparent contradiction with 7:10. SBLGNT reads "ouk".

kjv: for the Holy Ghost was not yet [given]
mine: for as yet the Spirit had not been given
note: TR adds "hagion"; both supply "given" (KJV in italics).

kjv: And every man went unto his own house.
mine: [[And each went to his own house.
note: 7:53–8:11 (the woman taken in adultery) is absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A and C (lacunose), W and the early versions; no Greek Father comments on it before the 12th century; some manuscripts place it after Lk 21:38 or Jn 21:25. SBLGNT double-brackets it. The KJV prints it as John's text. Context: a later addition, kept in double brackets (high confidence). 7:53-8:11 is absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, W and the earliest versions; no Greek Father comments on it before the 12th century; its vocabulary is Lukan; and manuscripts place it variously (after John 7:36, 7:44 or 21:25, or Luke 21:38). 7:52 flows into 8:12. Most scholars see an old, possibly genuine story, not John's text. Other possible meanings: (1) part of John's original Gospel — TR/Majority (from Codex D, c. 400, onward), Vulgate (Jerome included it), Augustine, who thought some removed it for fear of moral laxity; KJV, NKJV; (2) an early, authentic story about Jesus later inserted into John — Papias (via Eusebius), the Didascalia, most scholars; printed bracketed in ESV, NIV, NASB, CSB.

kjv: Even [the same] that I (Jesus) said unto you from the beginning
mine: Why do I (Jesus) even speak to You at all?
note: ten archen ho ti kai lalo hymin is notoriously obscure; "ten archen" used adverbially means "at all", making a question or exclamation. The KJV's "from the beginning" is a possible but strained reading.

kjv: going through the midst of them, and so passed by
mine: went out of the temple
note: TR adds a phrase from Lk 4:30; absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus*, B, D, W.

kjv: I (Jesus) must work the works of him that sent me
mine: We must work the works of Him Who sent Me (Jesus)
note: TR "eme" against "hemas" (P66, P75, Sinaiticus*, B, D); the plural draws the disciples into the work.

kjv: Dost thou (the blind man) believe on the Son of God?
mine: Do you (the blind man) believe in the Son of Man?
note: TR "theou" against "anthropou" in P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B, D, W; the more familiar confessional title replaced John's.

kjv: and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd
mine: So there will be one flock, one shepherd
note: poimne is "flock", not "aule" ("fold", used earlier in the verse). The KJV (following the Vulgate's "ovile") makes Jesus promise one institutional enclosure rather than one flock under one shepherd.

kjv: My Father, which gave [them] me, is greater than all
mine: What My Father has given Me is greater than all
note: SBLGNT follows B, Sinaiticus with neuter "ho … meizon"; TR has masculine "hos … meizon". The manuscripts are divided.

kjv: he (Jesus) groaned in the spirit, and was troubled
mine: he (Jesus) was deeply indignant in His spirit and greatly troubled
note: embrimaomai denotes anger or stern indignation (Mk 1:43, 14:5); "groaned" turns it into sorrow, which the verse expresses separately with "wept" (11:35). Also 11:38.

kjv: took away the stone [from the place] where the dead was laid
mine: took away the stone
note: TR adds "hou en ho tethnekos keimenos"; absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: against the day of my burying hath she (Mary) kept this
mine: so that she (Mary) may keep it for the day of My burial
note: TR "tetereken" (she has kept) against "hina … terese" (P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B, D, W).

kjv: when he (Isaiah) saw his (Jesus') glory
mine: because he (Isaiah) saw His (Jesus') glory
note: TR "hote" (when) against "hoti" (because) in P66, P75, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: And supper being ended
mine: During supper
note: TR aorist "genomenou" (having taken place) against present "ginomenou" (Sinaiticus*, B, W); the KJV's "ended" conflicts with 13:4, 26, where the meal is still in progress.

kjv: In my Father's house are many mansions
mine: In My Father's house are many dwelling places
note: mone is a place to stay (cf. 14:23 "make our home"); "mansions" (from Latin "mansiones", then meaning lodgings) now suggests great houses.

kjv: If ye shall ask any thing in my name
mine: If you ask Me anything in My name
note: TR omits "me" (present in P66, Sinaiticus, B, W); with it, prayer is addressed to Jesus himself.

kjv: he (the Father) shall give you another Comforter
mine: he (the Father) will give you another Advocate
note: parakletos is one called alongside, a helper or advocate (1 Jn 2:1 of Jesus, KJV "advocate"); "Comforter" (Wyclif/Tyndale) narrows it. Also 14:26, 15:26, 16:7.

kjv: every [branch] that beareth fruit, he (the Father) purgeth it
mine: every branch that does bear fruit He (the Father) prunes
note: kathairo is the vinedresser's cleaning or pruning, with a play on "katharoi" (clean) in 15:3; "purgeth" keeps the play but loses the horticultural sense.

kjv: he (the Advocate) will reprove the world of sin
mine: he (the Advocate) will convict the world concerning sin
note: elencho is to expose and convict, as in a court; "reprove" weakens the forensic sense of the Advocate's work.

kjv: and ye shall see me (Jesus), because I go to the Father
mine: and you will see Me (Jesus)
note: TR adds "because I go to the Father" from 16:17; absent from P5, P66, Sinaiticus, B, D, W.

kjv: keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me (Jesus)
mine: keep them (the disciples) in Your name, which You have given Me (Jesus)
note: TR "hous" (those whom) against "ho" (dative "which", attracted to "name") in P66, P75, Sinaiticus, B; the early text speaks of the divine name given to Jesus. Also 17:12.

kjv: thou (the Father) shouldest keep them (the disciples) from the evil
mine: that You (the Father) keep them (the disciples) from the evil one
note: tou ponerou is most likely masculine, as in 1 Jn 2:13–14, 5:18–19.

kjv: And said, Hail, King of the Jews!
mine: They (the soldiers) came up to Him (Jesus), saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
note: TR lacks "kai ercheto pros auton" (and they kept coming up to him), present in P66, P90, Sinaiticus, B, W; the repeated approach sharpens the mockery.

kjv: Touch me (Jesus) not
mine: Do not cling to Me (Jesus)
note: Present imperative "me mou haptou" forbids an action in progress (stop holding on to me); "Touch me not" (Vulgate "noli me tangere") suggests he may not be touched at all, against 20:27.

kjv: that ye might believe
mine: so that you may continue to believe
note: SBLGNT reads present "pisteuete" (P66vid, Sinaiticus*, B) against aorist "pisteusete" (TR); the present suggests readers who already believe.

kjv: Simon, [son] of Jonas
mine: Simon, son of John
note: TR "Iona" against "Ioannou" (Sinaiticus, B, C*, D, W), as at 1:42. Also 21:16, 21:17.

kjv: lovest thou (Peter) me (Jesus)? … Lovest thou me?
mine: do you (Peter) love Me (Jesus)? … Do you love Me?
note: Both versions render "agapao" (21:15–16) and "phileo" (21:17) alike. Whether John intends a distinction is disputed; he uses the verbs interchangeably elsewhere (3:35/5:20), so neither translation is wrong.

kjv: the books that should be written. Amen.
mine: the books that would be written.
note: TR adds a liturgical "Amen".

kjv: by many infallible proofs
mine: by many convincing proofs
note: tekmerion is a sure sign or decisive evidence; "infallible" overstates it.

kjv: in prayer and supplication
mine: to prayer
note: TR adds "kai te deesei"; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, D.

kjv: thou (God) wilt not leave my soul in hell
mine: You (God) will not abandon My soul to Hades
note: Hell for hades (Ps 16:10 Sheol), the grave or realm of the dead; also 2:31. The KJV rendering underlies the creedal "descended into hell".

kjv: according to the flesh, he (God) would raise up Christ to sit on his (David's) throne
mine: that He (God) would set one of his (David's) descendants on his throne
note: TR adds "to kata sarka anastesein ton Christon"; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D.

kjv: the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved
mine: the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved
note: TR adds "te ekklesia" (absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C); and "such as should be saved" reads a present participle ("those being saved") as a decree of predestination.

kjv: hath glorified his Son Jesus
mine: glorified His servant Jesus
note: pais here echoes Isaiah's Servant (Isa 52:13 LXX, "my servant shall be glorified"); "Son" loses the allusion. Also 3:26 and 4:27, 4:30 ("holy child").

kjv: killed the Prince of life
mine: killed the Author of life
note: archegos is founder, originator or pioneer (Heb 2:10, 12:2), not a ruler.

kjv: when the times of refreshing shall come
mine: that times of refreshing may come
note: hopos an introduces purpose ("so that"), not time; the KJV makes the times of refreshing a dated future event rather than the goal of repentance.

kjv: Who by the mouth of thy servant David hast said
mine: Who through the mouth of our father David, Your servant, said by the Holy Spirit
note: The early text (P74, Sinaiticus, A, B) has a famously awkward phrase naming the Holy Spirit and "our father"; the TR smooths it.

kjv: against thy holy child Jesus
mine: against Your holy servant Jesus
note: pais as at 3:13; "child" (1611 sense "boy, servant") is now misleading. Also 4:30.

kjv: to teach and preach Jesus Christ
mine: teaching and preaching that the Christ is Jesus
note: euangelizomenoi ton Christon Iesoun in Jerusalem preaching means announcing that the Messiah is Jesus; the KJV reads "Jesus Christ" as a compound name.

kjv: a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews
mine: a complaint by the Hellenists against the Hebrews
note: Hellenistai are Greek-speaking Jews, not Greeks; "Grecians" blurs the distinction, which matters for 11:20.

kjv: Stephen, full of faith and power
mine: Stephen, full of grace and power
note: TR "pisteos" (from 6:5) against "charitos" (P8, P45, Sinaiticus, A, B, D).

kjv: he (Moses), that was in the church in the wilderness
mine: the one (Moses) who was in the assembly in the wilderness
note: ekklesia here is Israel's assembly at Sinai (LXX "qahal"); "church" imports a Christian institution into the exodus.

kjv: brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles
mine: brought it (the tent of witness) in with Joshua
note: Iesous is the Greek form of Joshua; the KJV's "Jesus" makes Stephen speak of Jesus leading Israel into Canaan. Same at Heb 4:8.

kjv: a tabernacle for the God of Jacob
mine: a dwelling place for the house of Jacob
note: TR "theo" against "oiko" (P74, Sinaiticus*, B, D); "house" is the harder reading, so SBLGNT adopts it.

kjv: calling upon [God], and saying, Lord Jesus
mine: he (Stephen) called out, "Lord Jesus
note: The KJV supplies "God" (in italics); the object of "calling upon" is the Lord Jesus named next. The insertion turns a prayer to Jesus into a prayer to God.

kjv: And Philip said, If thou (the eunuch) believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he (the eunuch) answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
mine: (absent)
note: Absent from P45, P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C and most minuscules; a baptismal confession added (Western text) to answer the eunuch's question. Erasmus printed it from a margin and the Latin.

kjv: it is hard for thee (Saul) to kick against the pricks. And he (Saul) trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?
mine: I am Jesus, Whom you (Saul) are persecuting. But rise
note: The words from "it is hard" to "have me to do" are found in no Greek manuscript at this point; Erasmus translated them from the Latin Vulgate, importing them from 26:14 and 22:10. A rare case where the TR follows no Greek witness. Spans 9:5–6.

kjv: he (Saul) preached Christ in the synagogues
mine: he (Saul) proclaimed Jesus in the synagogues
note: TR "ton Christon" against "ton Iesoun" (P45, P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, E).

kjv: Then had the churches rest
mine: So the church … had peace
note: TR plural "ekklesiai" against singular "ekklesia" (P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C); Luke speaks of one church across three regions.

kjv: he (Peter) shall tell thee (Cornelius) what thou oughtest to do
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds a clause from 9:6/11:14; absent from all early Greek manuscripts.

kjv: Four days ago I (Cornelius) was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed
mine: Four days ago, about this hour, I (Cornelius) was praying … at the ninth hour
note: TR adds "nesteuon kai" (fasting and); absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C. Ascetic additions of fasting recur in the TR (Mk 9:29, 1 Cor 7:5).

kjv: spake unto the Grecians
mine: spoke to the Hellenists also
note: SBLGNT and TR both read "Hellenistas" here (many editions prefer "Hellenas", Greeks), but Luke's contrast with "Jews only" (11:19) requires Gentiles. "Grecians" (cf. 6:1) leaves the point unclear.

kjv: intending after Easter to bring him (Peter) forth
mine: intending after the Passover to bring him (Peter) out
note: pascha is everywhere else in the KJV "passover" (29 times); here alone "Easter" (inherited from Tyndale), which is anachronistic, since 12:3 dates the arrest to the Jewish feast of Unleavened Bread.

kjv: returned from Jerusalem
mine: returned to Jerusalem
note: TR "ex" against "eis" (Sinaiticus, B); "to" is geographically awkward after 11:30, which is why scribes changed it, but it is the harder and better-attested reading.

kjv: after that he (God) gave [unto them] judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years
mine: for about 450 years. And after that He (God) gave them judges
note: In the early text (P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C) the 450 years cover the sojourn, wilderness and conquest; the TR applies them to the judges, which conflicts with 1 Kgs 6:1 (480 years from exodus to temple).

kjv: when the Jews were gone out of the synagogue, the Gentiles besought
mine: As they (Paul and Barnabas) went out, the people begged
note: TR adds "the Jews" and "the Gentiles", introducing an ethnic contrast that Luke reserves for 13:45–46.

kjv: they (the crowds) called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius
mine: Barnabas they (the crowds) called Zeus, and Paul, Hermes
note: The Greek names Zeus and Hermes are rendered by their Latin equivalents, a convention of 1611; the local legend of Zeus and Hermes visiting Phrygia (Ovid's Baucis and Philemon) explains the crowd's reaction.

kjv: Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.
mine: known from of old.
note: TR expands the end of the Amos citation into a separate sentence; the early text (Sinaiticus, B, C) has only "gnosta ap' aionos".

kjv: saying, [Ye must] be circumcised, and keep the law
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds a clause from 15:1, 5; absent from P33, P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, D.

kjv: Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.
mine: (absent)
note: Absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, E; added (Western text) to explain why Silas is in Antioch at 15:40 after leaving in 15:33.

kjv: but the Spirit suffered them (Paul and his companions) not
mine: but the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them (Paul and his companions)
note: TR omits "Iesou" (present in P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D, E); "the Spirit of Jesus" is unique in the NT.

kjv: I (Paul) perceive that in all things ye (the Athenians) are too superstitious
mine: I (Paul) perceive that in every way you (the Athenians) are very religious
note: deisidaimonesterous can be positive or negative, but Paul is opening a courteous speech (captatio benevolentiae) and goes on to cite their altar; "too superstitious" makes his first words an insult.

kjv: hath made of one blood all nations
mine: he (God) made from one man every nation
note: TR adds "haimatos" (blood); absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: that the Godhead is like unto gold
mine: that the divine being is like gold
note: to theion is "the divine, deity", a philosophical term suited to the Athenian audience; "Godhead" suggests the Trinitarian term (cf. Col 2:9 "theotes", Rom 1:20 "theiotes").

kjv: I (Paul) must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return
mine: I (Paul) will return to you if God wills
note: TR adds Paul's intention to keep the feast in Jerusalem; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, E.

kjv: Have ye (the disciples) received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?
mine: Did you (the disciples) receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?
note: The aorist participle "pisteusantes" is coincident with the main verb ("when you believed"); "since" implies a later, second experience and has been used to support that doctrine.

kjv: silver shrines for Diana
mine: silver shrines of Artemis
note: The KJV uses the Roman name Diana for the Ephesian Artemis, a very different deity in cult and image. Throughout 19:24–35.

kjv: which are neither robbers of churches
mine: who are neither sacrilegious
note: hierosylos is a temple robber; "churches" is anachronistic for a pagan temple.

kjv: neither count I (Paul) my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy
mine: nor as precious to myself (Paul), if only I may finish my course
note: TR adds "with joy" (meta charas) and smooths the syntax; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, D.

kjv: which he (God) hath purchased with his own blood
mine: which He (God) obtained with the blood of His own
note: dia tou haimatos tou idiou can mean "his own blood" (making "God" the one who bled) or "the blood of his own [Son]"; both texts read "church of God" here (some manuscripts "of the Lord"), and the KJV's choice settles a disputed point.

kjv: we (the elders) have written [and] concluded that they (the Gentile believers) observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves
mine: we (the elders) have sent a letter with our judgment that they (the Gentile believers) should abstain
note: TR adds "that they observe no such thing, save only"; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: four thousand men that were murderers
mine: four thousand men of the Assassins
note: sikarioi (from Latin sica, dagger) names the Jewish dagger-men known from Josephus, a specific group, not murderers in general.

kjv: saw indeed the light, and were afraid
mine: saw the light
note: TR adds "kai emphoboi egenonto"; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: consenting unto his (Stephen's) death
mine: approving
note: TR adds "te anairesei autou" from 8:1.

kjv: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him (Paul), let us not fight against God
mine: What if a spirit or an angel spoke to him (Paul)?
note: TR completes the broken-off sentence with "me theomachomen" (from 5:39); absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: and would have judged according to our law. But the chief captain Lysias came [upon us] ... Commanding his (Paul's) accusers to come unto thee (Felix)
mine: (absent)
note: 24:6b–8a is absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, H, L, P; a Western expansion. Without it, "by examining him" in 24:8 refers to Paul, not Lysias.

kjv: temperance
mine: self-control
note: enkrateia is self-mastery in general (especially sexual, apt for Felix and Drusilla); "temperance" now suggests abstinence from alcohol.

kjv: questions against him (Paul) of their own superstition
mine: points of dispute with him (Paul) about their own religion
note: deisidaimonia on the lips of a Roman governor addressing a Jewish king is neutral, "religion"; "superstition" makes Festus insult his royal guest.

kjv: Almost thou (Paul) persuadest me (Agrippa) to be a Christian
mine: In a short time would you (Paul) persuade me (Agrippa) to become a Christian?
note: en oligo means "in a short time" or "with little effort" (cf. Paul's reply, "whether short or long"), and SBLGNT reads "poiesai" (to make), not TR "genesthai"; Agrippa's words are a dry deflection. The KJV turns them into a near-conversion and the source of a famous hymn and sermon theme.

kjv: a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon
mine: a tempestuous wind, called the northeaster
note: TR "Euroklydon" (east wind + wave) against "Eurakylon" (Sinaiticus, A, B), a Greek-Latin hybrid (Eurus + Aquilo) for an east-north-east wind, the sailors' own term.

kjv: the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered
mine: Paul was allowed
note: TR adds a Western expansion about the "stratopedarches"; absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: And when he (Paul) had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
mine: (absent)
note: Absent from P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, E; a Western addition repeating 28:25.

kjv: the gospel of Christ
mine: the gospel
note: TR adds "tou Christou"; absent from P26, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D*.

kjv: who hold the truth in unrighteousness
mine: who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth
note: katecho here is to hold down, suppress; "hold" in modern English reads as "possess".

kjv: his eternal power and Godhead
mine: His eternal power and divine nature
note: theiotes is divinity, divine quality, distinct from "theotes" (deity, Col 2:9); the KJV renders both "Godhead".

kjv: unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness
mine: unrighteousness, evil
note: TR adds "porneia"; absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
mine: You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
note: hierosyleo is to rob temples (cf. Acts 19:37); "commit sacrilege" is vaguer and loses the paradox of a Jew profiting from pagan shrines.

kjv: by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe
mine: through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe
note: pistis Iesou Christou may mean faith in Christ or Christ's own faithfulness; the KJV's literal "faith of" keeps the ambiguity that modern versions resolve. TR also adds "and upon all" (kai epi pantas).

kjv: a propitiation … for the remission of sins that are past
mine: a mercy seat … because … he (God) had passed over former sins
note: paresis is passing over, a temporary leaving unpunished, not "aphesis" (remission, forgiveness); the KJV erases Paul's argument that God's earlier forbearance needed vindicating. "hilasterion" is the LXX word for the ark's mercy seat (Heb 9:5).

kjv: he (Abraham) considered not his own body now dead
mine: when he (Abraham) considered his own body, which was as good as dead
note: TR adds "ou" (not); Sinaiticus, A, B, C read that Abraham did consider his body and still believed, which makes his faith clear-eyed rather than oblivious.

kjv: by whom (Jesus Christ) we have now received the atonement
mine: through Whom (Jesus Christ) we have now received reconciliation
note: katallage is reconciliation (as in 5:10 and 2 Cor 5:18–19, where the KJV so renders it); "atonement" here (in its 1611 sense "at-one-ment") is the KJV's only NT use of the word and is now read as expiation.

kjv: he that is dead is freed from sin
mine: one who has died has been set free from sin
note: dedikaiotai is literally "has been justified" (acquitted); both versions render "freed", losing the legal term that links chapter 6 to chapters 3–5.

kjv: that (the law) being dead wherein we were held
mine: having died to that (the law) which held us captive
note: TR "apothanontos" (the law being dead) against "apothanontes" (we having died); the KJV makes the law die, contrary to 7:4.

kjv: I thank God through Jesus Christ
mine: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ
note: TR "eucharisto to theo" against "charis to theo" (Sinaiticus*, B).

kjv: who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit
mine: (absent)
note: TR imports the clause from 8:4; absent from Sinaiticus*, B, C, D*, F, G. Without it the "no condemnation" is unconditional.

kjv: The Spirit itself beareth witness
mine: The Spirit Himself bears witness
note: auto to pneuma is grammatically neuter; the KJV's "itself" (also 8:26) follows the Greek gender, but in English reads as impersonal, against the KJV's own "he" in John 14–16.

kjv: the glorious liberty of the children of God
mine: the freedom of the glory of the children of God
note: A Hebraism; the KJV turns "the freedom of the glory" into an adjective ("glorious liberty"), which shifts the emphasis from glory to liberty.

kjv: For he will finish the work, and cut [it] short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make
mine: for the Lord will carry out His sentence upon the earth fully and without delay
note: TR adds "en dikaiosyne hoti logon syntetmemenon" from Isa 10:23 LXX; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B.

kjv: as it were by the works of the law
mine: as if it were based on works
note: TR adds "nomou"; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, B, F, G.

kjv: the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things
mine: the feet of those who preach the good news
note: TR adds "ton euangelizomenon eirenen" from Isa 52:7; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C.

kjv: hearing by the word of God
mine: hearing through the word of Christ
note: TR "theou" against "Christou" (P46vid, Sinaiticus*, B, C, D*).

kjv: But if [it be] of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the converse clause; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, C, D, F, G.

kjv: blindness in part is happened to Israel
mine: a partial hardening has come upon Israel
note: porosis is hardening (Mk 3:5, Eph 4:18 KJV "hardness/blindness"); also 11:7 "were blinded" for "eporothesan".

kjv: which is your reasonable service
mine: which is your rational worship
note: logike latreia is worship (latreia is cultic service, as in 9:4 "service of God"); "reasonable service" suggests a modest demand rather than a spiritual form of sacrifice.

kjv: they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation
mine: those who resist will incur judgment
note: krima is judgment or condemnation (here probably by the civil ruler, 13:3–4); "damnation" makes resistance to the state a matter of eternal punishment.

kjv: Thou shalt not bear false witness
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the ninth commandment; absent from P46, A, B, D, F, G.

kjv: and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard [it]
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds the converse clause about not observing the day; absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, D.

kjv: the judgment seat of Christ
mine: the judgment seat of God
note: TR "Christou" (from 2 Cor 5:10) against "theou" (Sinaiticus*, A, B, C*, D, F, G).

kjv: he that doubteth is damned if he eat
mine: whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats
note: katakekritai is "stands condemned" (self-condemned by conscience); "damned" now implies eternal perdition for eating with a doubtful conscience.

kjv: Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you
mine: I hope to see you in passing as I go to Spain
note: TR adds "eleusomai pros hymas" (I will come to you); absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C.

kjv: the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ
mine: the fullness of the blessing of Christ
note: TR adds "tou euangeliou"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C, D.

kjv: Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church
mine: our sister Phoebe, a deacon of the church
note: diakonos with "of the church at Cenchreae" names an office (as in Phil 1:1, 1 Tim 3:8, where the KJV has "deacons"); "servant" here hides that a woman held it.

kjv: Andronicus and Junia … who are of note among the apostles
mine: Andronicus and Junia … They are well known among the apostles
note: Both versions read the woman's name Junia (some modern editions printed a male "Junias"). The KJV's "of note among" also allows the reading that Junia was an apostle.

kjv: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen.
mine: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
note: SBLGNT prints this benediction (with the Byzantine text) and the KJV has it too; Westcott–Hort, Tregelles and NA28 omit it, following P46, P61, Sinaiticus, A, B, C. No difference between KJV and SBLGNT here; listed because the editions disagree.

kjv: Now to him (God) that is of power to stablish you … (16:25–27, printed as the letter's close)
mine: Now to Him (God) Who is able to strengthen you … (16:25–27, from WH, Tregelles and NA28)
note: The doxology floats in the manuscripts: after 14:23 (the Byzantine majority), after 15:33 (P46), after 16:23 (P61, Sinaiticus, B, C, D), in two places (A, P), or nowhere (F, G; apparently Marcion's text). SBLGNT leaves it out of the main text altogether; WH, Tregelles and NA28 print it here, with identical wording, and this translation follows them. The KJV's placement agrees with these editions.

kjv: the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began
mine: the mystery that was kept silent through long ages
note: chronois aioniois is "for eternal/long ages" (dative of time, as in 2 Tim 1:9); "since the world began" fixes a starting point the Greek does not name, and "sesigemenou" is "kept silent", not "kept secret".

kjv: unto us which are saved it is the power of God
mine: to us who are being saved it is the power of God
note: Present participles "apollymenois / sozomenois" describe processes ("perishing / being saved"); the KJV keeps "perish" progressive but makes "saved" a completed state.

kjv: by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe
mine: through the folly of what we preach to save those who believe
note: kerygma is the content preached (the message of the cross), not the act of preaching; the KJV phrase is often quoted as a defence of preaching as such.

kjv: we speak wisdom among them that are perfect
mine: among the mature we do impart wisdom
note: teleioi are the mature, as opposed to infants (3:1); "perfect" suggests sinlessness.

kjv: envying, and strife, and divisions
mine: jealousy and strife
note: TR adds "kai dichostasiai"; absent from P11, P46vid, Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy
mine: If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy him
note: The same verb "phtheiro" appears twice; the KJV's "defile … destroy" loses Paul's measure-for-measure.

kjv: For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified
mine: For I am not aware of anything against myself, but I am not thereby acquitted
note: Know nothing by myself in 1611 meant "know nothing against myself"; a modern reader hears a confession of ignorance.

kjv: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us
mine: Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed
note: TR adds "hyper hemon"; absent from P46, P11, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C*, D.

kjv: nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind
mine: nor men who submit to homosexual acts, nor men who practice them
note: malakoi (soft) and "arsenokoitai" (a rare compound from Lev 18:22/20:13 LXX) refer to the passive and active partners in male intercourse; the KJV's euphemisms obscure the referent, and "effeminate" suggests mannerism rather than acts. The exact sense remains debated.

kjv: All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient
mine: All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful
note: Paul is quoting a Corinthian slogan and replying to it (also 6:13, 7:1, 8:1); the KJV presents the slogan as Paul's own statement.

kjv: glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's
mine: So glorify God in your body.
note: TR adds "kai en to pneumati hymon, hatina estin tou theou"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, D*, F, G. The addition softens Paul's focus on the body.

kjv: It is good for a man not to touch a woman
mine: It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.
note: Most interpreters take this as a Corinthian ascetic slogan that Paul qualifies in 7:2–5; the KJV gives it as Paul's own maxim.

kjv: that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer
mine: that you may devote yourselves to prayer
note: TR adds "te nesteia kai"; absent from P11, P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C, D, F, G. One of several ascetic additions of "fasting" in the TR.

kjv: toward his virgin … let him do what he will … let them marry
mine: toward his betrothed … let them marry
note: parthenos autou is most likely a fiancée (an engaged couple deciding whether to marry); the KJV's "his virgin" with 7:38 "giveth her in marriage" has led to readings about a father and his daughter.

kjv: to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them
mine: to those under the law I became as one under the law (though not being myself under the law)
note: TR lacks "me on autos hypo nomon", present in P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, D, F, G; the omission (by homoeoteleuton) loses Paul's own disclaimer.

kjv: lest that by any means … I myself should be a castaway
mine: lest … I myself should be disqualified
note: adokimos is the athletic term "disqualified" (continuing the race image of 9:24–26); "castaway" suggests shipwreck or reprobation.

kjv: is it not the communion of the blood of Christ?
mine: is it not a participation in the blood of Christ?
note: koinonia is sharing, participation; "communion" has become the name of the rite itself.

kjv: for the earth [is] the Lord's, and the fulness thereof
mine: (absent)
note: TR repeats 10:26; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, D, F, G.

kjv: ought the woman to have power on [her] head
mine: a wife ought to have authority on her head
note: exousia is authority; the KJV margin and later readers took it as a "sign of [her husband's] power", i.e. a veil, which the Greek does not say.

kjv: Take, eat: this is my (Jesus') body, which is broken for you
mine: This is My (Jesus') body, which is for you
note: TR adds "Take, eat" (from Mt 26:26) and "broken" (klomenon); absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C*.

kjv: he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord's body
mine: anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on himself
note: TR adds "anaxios" (unworthily) and "tou kyriou" (of the Lord); and "krima" is "judgment", which 11:30–32 explains as illness and discipline "so that we may not be condemned". "Damnation" has kept many from communion.

kjv: have been all made to drink into one Spirit
mine: all were made to drink of one Spirit
note: TR adds "eis" (into), turning the drinking metaphor into a second baptismal image; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C*, D.

kjv: and have not charity
mine: but have not love
note: agape is love; the KJV uses "charity" (Vulgate "caritas") 26 times in the NT, mostly in Paul, alongside "love" elsewhere. "Charity" now means almsgiving, which 13:3 shows Paul distinguishes from love. Systematic; flagged once.

kjv: is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil
mine: is not irritable or resentful
note: easily has no basis in the Greek ("ou paroxynetai"); "thinketh no evil" (ou logizetai to kakon) means "keeps no record of wrongs".

kjv: through a glass, darkly
mine: in a mirror dimly
note: esoptron is a (bronze) mirror; "glass" in 1611 meant a looking-glass, but now suggests a window.

kjv: he that speaketh in an [unknown] tongue
mine: one who speaks in a tongue
note: The KJV supplies "unknown" (in italics) throughout chapter 14, deciding that the tongues are unintelligible languages; Paul only says "glossa", tongue/language.

kjv: But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.
mine: If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.
note: TR imperative "agnoeito" against passive "agnoeitai" (Sinaiticus*, A*, D, F, G); the early text is a sanction (God does not recognize him), not a shrug.

kjv: the second man [is] the Lord from heaven
mine: the second man is from heaven
note: TR adds "ho kyrios"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, B, C, D*, F, G.

kjv: we shall also bear the image of the heavenly
mine: let us also bear the image of the man of heaven
note: SBLGNT follows the better-attested subjunctive "phoresomen" (P46, Sinaiticus, A, C, D, F, G) against TR future "phoresomen" (B); the difference is one vowel, so many editors prefer the future on contextual grounds.

kjv: O death, where [is] thy sting? O grave, where [is] thy victory?
mine: O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?
note: TR has "hade" (grave/Hades) in the second line, from Hos 13:14 LXX, and reverses the order; P46, Sinaiticus, B, C read "death" twice.

kjv: let him be Anathema Maranatha
mine: let him be accursed. Our Lord, come!
note: Anathema (accursed) and "Marana tha" (Aramaic, "Our Lord, come!") are separate; the KJV runs them together as a single intensified curse formula.

kjv: in Christ Jesus. Amen.
mine: in Christ Jesus.
note: TR adds a closing "Amen"; absent from B, F, G and others.

kjv: given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts
mine: given us His (God's) Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee
note: arrabon is a down payment or pledge; "earnest" (as in "earnest money") is now obscure. Also 5:5, Eph 1:14.

kjv: which (God) always causeth us to triumph in Christ
mine: Who (God) in Christ always leads us in triumphal procession
note: thriambeuo is to lead in a Roman triumph, where captives were paraded; Paul pictures himself as Christ's captive (cf. Col 2:15), not as a victor.

kjv: which corrupt the word of God
mine: peddlers of God's word
note: kapeleuo is to hawk goods for profit (a retail huckster); "corrupt" catches the dishonesty but not the money.

kjv: able ministers of the new testament
mine: ministers of a new covenant
note: diatheke here contrasts with the Sinai covenant (3:14 "old covenant"); "testament" now suggests the book. Systematic; flagged here for Paul.

kjv: their (the Israelites') minds were blinded
mine: their (the Israelites') minds were hardened
note: poroo is to harden (as at Rom 11:7, where the KJV also has "blinded").

kjv: the god of this world
mine: the god of this age
note: aion is "age"; the KJV's "world" (also "the end of the world" in the Gospels) turns a temporal contrast between this age and the age to come into a spatial one.

kjv: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord
mine: knowing the fear of the Lord
note: phobos tou kyriou is the reverent fear of the Lord (Prov 1:7), not terror of him; the KJV phrase has been used for fear-based preaching.

kjv: behold, all things are become new
mine: behold, the new has come
note: TR adds "ta panta"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, B, C, D*, F, G. The early text is about a new creation breaking in, not "all things" being renewed.

kjv: for ye are the temple of the living God
mine: for we are the temple of the living God
note: TR "hymeis este" against "hemeis esmen" (P46, Sinaiticus*, B, D*); Paul includes himself.

kjv: in your love to us
mine: in the love from us that is in you
note: TR "ex hymon en hemin" against "ex hemon en hymin" (P46, B); the early text speaks of Paul's love kindled in them. The manuscripts are divided.

kjv: Casting down imaginations
mine: We destroy arguments
note: logismous are reasonings or arguments (the sophistry of Paul's opponents), not "imaginations" (fantasies).

kjv: I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles
mine: I am not in the least inferior to these super-apostles
note: hyperlian apostoloi is sarcastic, aimed at Paul's rivals in Corinth (11:13 "false apostles"); "the very chiefest apostles" suggests the Twelve. Also 12:11.

kjv: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
mine: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus
note: TR adds "hemon" and "Christou"; absent from Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: my (the Lord's) strength is made perfect in weakness
mine: power is made perfect in weakness
note: TR adds "mou" (my); absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A*, B, D*, F, G. Without it the saying is a general principle about power.

kjv: except ye be reprobates
mine: unless indeed you fail to meet the test
note: adokimoi plays on "dokimazete" (test yourselves): failing a test, not damnation; also 13:6–7.

kjv: be with you all. Amen.
mine: be with you all.
note: TR adds "Amen". KJV numbers this verse 13:14 (it splits 13:12 into two).

kjv: deliver us from this present evil world
mine: deliver us from the present evil age
note: aion is age, in the apocalyptic contrast of this age and the age to come; "world" turns it into a place.

kjv: to see Peter
mine: to visit Cephas
note: TR "Petron" against "Kephan" (P46, P51, Sinaiticus*, A, B); Paul uses the Aramaic name.

kjv: But when Peter was come to Antioch
mine: But when Cephas came to Antioch
note: TR "Petros" against "Kephas" (P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C); also 2:14.

kjv: by the faith of Jesus Christ
mine: through faith in Jesus Christ
note: pistis Christou as at Rom 3:22: the KJV's literal "faith of" keeps the ambiguity (faith in Christ / Christ's faithfulness). Also 2:20 "faith of the Son of God".

kjv: that ye should not obey the truth … crucified among you
mine: It was before your eyes that Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified
note: TR adds "te aletheia me peithesthai" (from 5:7) and "en hymin"; absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, D*, F, G.

kjv: the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ
mine: a covenant previously ratified by God
note: TR adds "eis Christon"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: the law was our schoolmaster [to bring us] unto Christ
mine: the law was our guardian until Christ came
note: paidagogos was the slave who supervised a child, not a teacher; and "eis Christon" is temporal ("until Christ"), as 3:23, 25 show, not "to bring us to Christ" (KJV italics).

kjv: an heir of God through Christ
mine: an heir through God
note: TR "kleronomos theou dia Christou" against "kleronomos dia theou" (P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C*).

kjv: which (the Jerusalem above) is the mother of us all
mine: she (the Jerusalem above) is our mother
note: TR adds "panton"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, B, C*, D, F, G.

kjv: I would they were even cut off which trouble you
mine: I wish those who unsettle you would go all the way and emasculate themselves
note: apokopsontai (middle) means to castrate oneself, a bitter jibe at those demanding circumcision; "cut off" reads as excommunication.

kjv: Adultery, fornication, uncleanness
mine: sexual immorality, impurity
note: TR adds "moicheia"; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, B, C. Also 5:21 TR adds "murders" (phonoi), absent from P46, Sinaiticus, B.

kjv: longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith
mine: patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness
note: pistis in a list of virtues is faithfulness, not belief; "chrestotes" is kindness, and the KJV's "gentleness" here duplicates its "meekness" (prautes) in 5:23.

kjv: Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you
mine: See with what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand
note: pelikois grammasin is "with what large letters" (characters), Paul's own handwriting at the end of a dictated letter; the KJV makes it the length of the epistle, which is short.

kjv: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth
mine: For neither circumcision counts for anything
note: TR adds "en Christo Iesou" from 5:6; absent from P46, B.

kjv: to the saints which are at Ephesus
mine: to the saints who are [in Ephesus]
note: en Epheso is absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, B*, 1739 and was unknown to Origen and Marcion's text; the letter may have been a circular. SBLGNT brackets it; the KJV prints it plainly.

kjv: your faith in the Lord Jesus, and love unto all the saints
mine: your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love toward all the saints
note: SBLGNT includes "ten agapen" with the TR; P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B omit it (making "faith … toward all the saints"). Divided evidence; listed for completeness.

kjv: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened
mine: having the eyes of your hearts enlightened
note: TR "dianoias" against "kardias" (P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, D, F, G).

kjv: And you [hath he (God) quickened], who were dead
mine: And you were dead
note: The KJV supplies "hath he quickened" (in italics) from 2:5 to complete Paul's broken sentence; "quicken" (make alive) is now obscure.

kjv: what [is] the fellowship of the mystery … who created all things by Jesus Christ
mine: what is the plan of the mystery … Who created all things
note: TR "koinonia" (fellowship) against "oikonomia" (plan, administration; all early manuscripts), and adds "dia Iesou Christou".

kjv: unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
mine: before the Father
note: TR adds "tou kyriou hemon Iesou Christou"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C. Without it the wordplay "patera … patria" (Father … every family) in 3:15 stands out.

kjv: Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named
mine: from Whom every family in heaven and on earth is named
note: pasa patria without the article is "every family/clan", each deriving its name from the Father; "the whole family" makes it one family, the church.

kjv: and in you all
mine: and in all
note: TR adds "hymin"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: he (Christ) also descended first into the lower parts of the earth
mine: he (Christ) had also descended into the lower regions, the earth
note: TR adds "proton" (first); and "the lower parts of the earth" is probably appositional ("the lower regions, namely the earth", i.e. the incarnation), though the KJV wording has long been read as a descent into hell.

kjv: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying
mine: to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up
note: The three prepositions are not parallel (pros … eis … eis): leaders equip the saints, who do the work of ministry. The KJV's commas make all three the clergy's tasks; this is the famous "fatal comma".

kjv: For the fruit of the Spirit
mine: for the fruit of light
note: TR "pneumatos" (from Gal 5:22) against "photos" (P46, Sinaiticus, A, B, D*, F, G), which fits the light imagery of 5:8–14.

kjv: Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God
mine: submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ
note: TR "theou" against "Christou" (P46, Sinaiticus, A, B). In the early text 5:22 has no verb of its own and depends on this participle, so mutual submission frames the household code; the KJV supplies "submit yourselves" in 5:22.

kjv: members of his (Christ's) body, of his flesh, and of his bones
mine: members of His (Christ's) body
note: TR adds "ek tes sarkos autou kai ek ton osteon autou" from Gen 2:23; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B.

kjv: Servants, be obedient to them that are [your] masters
mine: Slaves, obey your earthly masters
note: douloi are slaves; "servants" (also Col 3:22, 1 Pet 2:18) softens the institution Paul is addressing.

kjv: against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places
mine: against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places
note: kosmokratoras are cosmic powers; "en tois epouraniois" is "in the heavenly places" (1:3, 1:20, 2:6, 3:10), not "high places" (which suggests human rulers).

kjv: in sincerity. Amen.
mine: with love incorruptible.
note: TR adds "Amen"; and "en aphtharsia" is "in incorruptibility", which the KJV renders "in sincerity".

kjv: with the bishops and deacons
mine: with the overseers and deacons
note: episkopoi (plural, in one city) are local overseers, the same as elders (Acts 20:17, 28); "bishops" suggests the later single bishop over a diocese.

kjv: my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace
mine: it has become known throughout the whole imperial guard
note: praitorion here is the praetorian guard (a body of soldiers, "and to all the rest"), not a palace building.

kjv: thought it not robbery to be equal with God
mine: did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped
note: harpagmos here (with "ouch … hegesato … alla ekenosen") means something to be seized or exploited; the KJV's "not robbery" makes Christ assert that equality with God was rightly his, the opposite emphasis to Paul's self-emptying.

kjv: But made himself (Christ) of no reputation
mine: but emptied Himself (Christ)
note: heauton ekenosen is "emptied himself" (the source of "kenosis"); "made himself of no reputation" reduces it to a loss of status.

kjv: let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing
mine: let us hold true to what we have attained
note: TR adds "kanoni, to auto phronein"; absent from P16, P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B.

kjv: For our conversation is in heaven
mine: But our citizenship is in heaven
note: politeuma is citizenship or commonwealth (pointed at Philippi, a Roman colony); "conversation" (1611: manner of life) is now meaningless here.

kjv: who (Christ) shall change our vile body
mine: Who (Christ) will transform our lowly body
note: soma tes tapeinoseos is the body of humiliation; "vile" (1611: lowly) now means disgusting.

kjv: Let your moderation be known unto all men
mine: Let your reasonableness be known to everyone
note: epieikes is gentleness, forbearance, a yielding spirit; "moderation" now suggests restraint in consumption.

kjv: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me
mine: I can do all things through Him Who strengthens me
note: TR adds "Christo"; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, B, D*. And in context (4:11–12) "all things" means enduring plenty and want, not unlimited achievement.

kjv: from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
mine: from God our Father
note: TR adds "and the Lord Jesus Christ" from the other Pauline greetings; absent from B, D, and others.

kjv: we have redemption through his (the Son's) blood
mine: we have redemption
note: TR adds "dia tou haimatos autou" from Eph 1:7; absent from all early Greek manuscripts.

kjv: the firstborn of every creature
mine: the firstborn of all creation
note: prototokos pases ktiseos is a title of rank and priority (1:16 "for by him all things were created"); "of every creature" can suggest that Christ is himself the first creature, the Arian reading.

kjv: the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ
mine: God's mystery, which is Christ
note: TR "tou theou kai patros kai tou Christou" is a conflation; P46, B read "tou theou, Christou" ("God's mystery, Christ"). One of the most varied readings in the NT.

kjv: the body of the sins of the flesh
mine: the body of the flesh
note: TR adds "ton hamartion"; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, B, C, D*, F, G.

kjv: intruding into those things which he hath not seen
mine: going on in detail about visions
note: TR adds "me" (not), reversing the sense; the early text (P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, D*) has "ha heoraken", what he has seen, i.e. visionary experiences.

kjv: inordinate affection, evil concupiscence
mine: passion, evil desire
note: pathos is (sexual) passion; "inordinate affection" and "concupiscence" are now technical or obscure.

kjv: let the peace of God rule in your hearts
mine: let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts
note: TR "theou" against "Christou" (P46, Sinaiticus*, A, B, C*, D*, F, G).

kjv: Marcus, sister's son to Barnabas
mine: Mark the cousin of Barnabas
note: anepsios is a cousin; "sister's son" (nephew) is the later sense of the word.

kjv: Nymphas, and the church which is in his house
mine: Nympha and the church in her house
note: TR reads a man "Nymphas" with "autou" (his); B reads "autes" (her), a woman hosting a house church. SBLGNT follows B.

kjv: Grace [be] with you. Amen.
mine: Grace be with you.
note: TR adds "Amen".

kjv: Grace [be] unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ
mine: Grace to you and peace
note: TR expands the greeting with the standard Pauline formula; absent from B, F, G and others.

kjv: Who (the Jews) both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets
mine: who (the Jews) killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets
note: TR adds "idious" (their own); absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, D*, F, G.

kjv: our brother, and minister of God, and our fellowlabourer in the gospel
mine: our brother and God's coworker in the gospel
note: The early text has the bold "synergon tou theou" (God's coworker, D*, 33); scribes softened it to "minister" (Sinaiticus, A) or conflated both (TR).

kjv: how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour
mine: how to control his own body in holiness and honor
note: to heautou skeuos ktasthai may mean "control his own body" or "acquire a wife" (cf. 1 Pet 3:7 "weaker vessel"); the KJV keeps the literal "vessel" and so the ambiguity.

kjv: shall not prevent them which are asleep
mine: will not precede those who have fallen asleep
note: Prevent in 1611 meant "go before"; now it means "stop".

kjv: warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded
mine: admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted
note: ataktoi are the idle or disorderly (2 Th 3:6–11); "oligopsychoi" are the discouraged, not the "feebleminded".

kjv: Abstain from all appearance of evil
mine: Abstain from every form of evil
note: eidos is form or kind; the KJV's "appearance" turns a call to avoid evil itself into a call to avoid what looks bad, a common basis for rules of conduct.

kjv: the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ
mine: the gospel of our Lord Jesus
note: TR adds "Christou"; absent from B, D, F, G.

kjv: admired in all them that believe
mine: marveled at among all who have believed
note: TR present "pisteuousin" against aorist "pisteusasin" (Sinaiticus, A, B); "admired" (1611: wondered at) is also archaic.

kjv: as that the day of Christ is at hand
mine: to the effect that the day of the Lord has come
note: enesteken is perfect, "has come / is present" (the Thessalonians thought it had already arrived); "is at hand" says the opposite of the error Paul is correcting. TR also reads "Christ" for "Lord".

kjv: that man of sin be revealed
mine: the man of lawlessness is revealed
note: TR "hamartias" against "anomias" (Sinaiticus, B), which fits "mystery of lawlessness" (2:7) and "the lawless one" (2:8).

kjv: only he who now letteth [will let]
mine: Only he who now restrains it
note: Let in 1611 meant "hinder" (as in "without let"); a modern reader takes it to mean "allow", the reverse.

kjv: God hath from the beginning chosen you
mine: God chose you as the firstfruits
