note: TR "ap' arches" against "aparchen" (B, F, G, 33); the readings differ by one letter division, and the manuscripts are divided.

kjv: into the patient waiting for Christ
mine: to the steadfastness of Christ
note: hypomone tou Christou is Christ's own endurance (or endurance like his), parallel to "the love of God"; "patient waiting for Christ" makes it an expectation of the second coming.

kjv: rather than godly edifying which is in faith
mine: rather than the stewardship from God that is by faith
note: TR "oikodomian" (edifying) against "oikonomian" (stewardship, plan), the reading of all early manuscripts.

kjv: for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers
mine: men who practice homosexuality, enslavers
note: arsenokoitai as at 1 Cor 6:9; "andrapodistai" are slave-traders or kidnappers, the KJV's "menstealers" is accurate but obscure.

kjv: the only wise God
mine: the only God
note: TR adds "sophos" (wise) from Rom 16:27; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, D*, F, G.

kjv: I speak the truth in Christ, [and] lie not
mine: I am telling the truth, I am not lying
note: TR adds "en Christo"; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, D*, F, G.

kjv: nor to usurp authority over the man
mine: or to exercise authority over a man
note: authentein (only here in the NT) is debated; the KJV's "usurp" assumes the authority is illegitimate, a sense the word may or may not carry.

kjv: no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre
mine: not violent … not a lover of money
note: TR adds "me aischrokerde" (from Titus 1:7); absent from Sinaiticus, A, D, F, G.

kjv: Even so [must their (the deacons')] wives [be] grave
mine: Women likewise must be dignified
note: gynaikas in a list of deacons' qualifications may be deacons' wives or women deacons (cf. Phoebe, Rom 16:1); the KJV supplies "their" (in italics) and decides the question.

kjv: God was manifest in the flesh
mine: He (Christ) was manifested in the flesh
note: TR "theos" (ΘΣ) against "hos" (ΟΣ, "who/he who") in Sinaiticus*, A*, C*, F, G; the two differ by a stroke in uncial script. "Hos" begins a hymn about Christ; "God" makes the verse a direct statement of the incarnation of God, long cited for that doctrine.

kjv: For bodily exercise profiteth little
mine: for while bodily training is of some value
note: pros oligon ophelimos is "of some (limited) value"; "profiteth little" sounds dismissive.

kjv: in charity, in spirit, in faith
mine: in love, in faith
note: TR adds "en pneumati"; absent from Sinaiticus, A, C, D, F, G.

kjv: Having damnation, because they (the younger widows) have cast off their first faith
mine: and so incur condemnation for having abandoned their (the younger widows') former faith
note: krima is judgment or censure (for breaking a pledge to serve as an enrolled widow); "damnation" makes remarriage a cause of eternal loss.

kjv: If any man or woman that believeth have widows
mine: If any believing woman has relatives who are widows
note: TR "pistos e piste" (man or woman) against "piste" alone (Sinaiticus, A, C, F, G).

kjv: supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself
mine: imagining that godliness is a means of gain
note: The KJV reverses subject and predicate (the error is treating religion as a way to make money, as 6:6 shows); TR also adds "aphistaso apo ton toiouton".

kjv: the love of money is the root of all evil
mine: the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils
note: rhiza has no article and "panton ton kakon" is plural; the KJV's "the root of all evil" makes it the single source of every evil, a stronger claim than Paul's.

kjv: oppositions of science falsely so called
mine: contradictions of what is falsely called "knowledge"
note: gnosis is knowledge (perhaps an early Gnostic claim); "science" in 1611 meant knowledge in general, but now invites a misreading about the natural sciences.

kjv: of power, and of love, and of a sound mind
mine: of power and love and self-control
note: sophronismos is self-discipline or self-control; "a sound mind" is often read as mental health.

kjv: a teacher of the Gentiles
mine: teacher
note: TR adds "ethnon" from 1 Tim 2:7; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, I.

kjv: Study to shew thyself approved unto God … rightly dividing the word of truth
mine: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved … rightly handling the word of truth
note: spoudazo is to make every effort, not to study; the KJV verse is widely quoted to encourage Bible study. "Orthotomeo" (cut straight) means to handle correctly, and "dividing" has been taken as a warrant for schemes that divide Scripture into eras (dispensationalism).

kjv: their word will eat as doth a canker
mine: their talk will spread like gangrene
note: gangraina is gangrene; "canker" (ulcer) is close but obscure.

kjv: reprobate concerning the faith
mine: disqualified regarding the faith
note: adokimos as at 2 Cor 13:5: failing the test, not "reprobate" in the later theological sense.

kjv: I charge [thee] therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge
mine: I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, Who is to judge
note: TR adds "oun ego" and "tou kyriou"; and reads "kata" (at his appearing) for "kai" (and by his appearing).

kjv: The Lord Jesus Christ [be] with thy spirit. Grace [be] with you. Amen.
mine: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.
note: TR adds "Jesus Christ" and "Amen"; absent from Sinaiticus*, F, G.

kjv: Grace, mercy, [and] peace
mine: Grace and peace
note: TR adds "eleos" (mercy) from 1–2 Timothy; absent from Sinaiticus, C*, D, F, G.

kjv: the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
mine: the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ
note: With one article governing "great God and Savior" (Granville Sharp's rule), the Greek most naturally calls Jesus Christ "our great God and Savior"; the KJV's "the great God and our Saviour" can be read as two persons. It also turns "the glory" into an adjective ("glorious").

kjv: a peculiar people
mine: a people for His (Christ's) own possession
note: periousios is "treasured possession" (Exod 19:5 LXX); "peculiar" in 1611 meant "belonging to oneself", now it means "odd".

kjv: A man that is an heretick
mine: a person who stirs up division
note: hairetikos (only here) is a factious, divisive person; "heretic" now means one who holds false doctrine, which the context (3:9 quarrels) does not mention.

kjv: Grace [be] with you all. Amen.
mine: Grace be with you all.
note: TR adds "Amen".

kjv: the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee
mine: the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you
note: splanchna (inward parts) was the seat of feeling; "bowels" now reads as anatomy. Also 1:12, 1:20.

kjv: thou therefore receive him (Onesimus), that is, mine own bowels
mine: sending my very heart
note: TR adds "proslabou" (receive him), supplying the missing verb; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, C.

kjv: with your spirit. Amen.
mine: with your spirit.
note: TR adds "Amen".

kjv: by whom (the Son) also he (God) made the worlds
mine: through Whom (the Son) also He (God) created the ages
note: tous aionas is literally "the ages" (the world in its temporal extent); the KJV's "worlds" is defensible (cf. 11:3) but loses the temporal sense.

kjv: when he (the Son) had by himself purged our sins
mine: After making purification for sins
note: TR adds "di' heautou" (by himself) and "hemon" (our); absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, D*.

kjv: and didst set him over the works of thy hands
mine: (absent)
note: TR completes the Ps 8:6 citation; absent from P46, B, D, and the Byzantine majority.

kjv: to make the captain of their salvation perfect
mine: should make the founder of their salvation perfect
note: archegos as at Acts 3:15 (pioneer, founder); also 12:2 "author".

kjv: For verily he (Jesus) took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham
mine: For surely it is not angels that He (Jesus) helps, but He helps the offspring of Abraham
note: epilambanetai means "takes hold of (to help)", as in 8:9; the KJV supplies "the nature of" (in italics) and turns a statement about whom Christ rescues into one about the incarnation.

kjv: the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end
mine: our boasting in our hope
note: TR adds "mechri telous bebaian" (firm to the end) from 3:14; absent from P13, P46, B.

kjv: not being mixed with faith in them that heard it
mine: because they (those who left Egypt) were not united by faith with those who listened
note: TR singular "synkekramenos" (the word was not mixed with faith) against plural "synkekerasmenous" (they were not united), the reading of P13vid, P46, A, B, C, D*.

kjv: For if Jesus had given them rest
mine: For if Joshua had given them rest
note: Iesous is Joshua, who led Israel into Canaan; the KJV's "Jesus" makes the author deny that Jesus gave rest, the opposite of his argument. As at Acts 7:45.

kjv: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God
mine: So then, there remains a Sabbath rest
note: The author switches from "katapausis" to the rare "sabbatismos" (Sabbath-keeping); the KJV renders both "rest" and loses the point.

kjv: and was heard in that he (Jesus) feared
mine: and He (Jesus) was heard because of His reverence
note: eulabeia is godly reverence or piety (12:28 "godly fear"); "in that he feared" suggests he was heard because he was afraid.

kjv: leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection
mine: let us leave the elementary doctrine of Christ and go on to maturity
note: teleiotes is maturity (5:14 "the mature"); "perfection" has fed doctrines of sinless perfection.

kjv: If they shall fall away
mine: and then have fallen away
note: parapesontas is one of a series of aorist participles describing the same people; the KJV's conditional "if" softens the warning into a hypothesis.

kjv: Thou (Jesus) [art] a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec
mine: 'You (Jesus) are a priest forever.'
note: TR completes the quotation with "kata ten taxin Melchisedek"; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, B, C.

kjv: a surety of a better testament
mine: the guarantor of a better covenant
note: diatheke in Hebrews 7–10 is the covenant of Jer 31 (8:8–10, where the KJV has "covenant"); the KJV alternates "testament" and "covenant" for the same word.

kjv: their sins and their iniquities will I (the Lord) remember no more
mine: I (the Lord) will remember their sins no more
note: TR adds "kai ton anomion auton" from 10:17; absent from P46, Sinaiticus*, B.

kjv: an high priest of good things to come
mine: a high priest of the good things that have come
note: TR "mellonton" (to come) against "genomenon" (that have come; P46, B, D*); the early text treats the blessings as already realised.

kjv: now once in the end of the world hath he (Christ) appeared
mine: he (Christ) has appeared once for all at the end of the ages
note: epi synteleia ton aionon is "at the culmination of the ages"; "end of the world" (as in Matthew) suggests the world's end, not the turning point of history.

kjv: the profession of [our] faith
mine: the confession of our hope
note: The Greek (both TR and critical text) reads "elpidos" (hope); the KJV renders it "faith", its only such mistranslation, perhaps to avoid repeating "hope".

kjv: ye had compassion of me in my bonds
mine: you had compassion on those in prison
note: TR "tois desmois mou" (my bonds, assuming Pauline authorship) against "tois desmiois" (the prisoners; A, D*, 33).

kjv: Now the just shall live by faith
mine: but My (God's) righteous one shall live by faith
note: TR omits "mou" (my); P46, Sinaiticus, A have "ho dikaios mou".

kjv: faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
mine: faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen
note: hypostasis can mean "substance/reality" (as at 1:3) or "assurance" (3:14); "elenchos" is proof or conviction. The KJV's philosophical "substance" is defensible but is usually now read as abstract.

kjv: and were persuaded of [them (the things promised)], and embraced [them]
mine: and greeted them (the things promised) from afar
note: TR adds "kai peisthentes" (and were persuaded); absent from all early manuscripts.

kjv: they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain
mine: they were sawn in two, they were killed with the sword
note: SBLGNT omits "epeirasthesan" (were tempted) with P46 and the Syriac; it sits oddly in a list of violent deaths and may be a corruption of "epristhesan" (sawn).

kjv: the author and finisher of [our] faith
mine: the founder and perfecter of our faith
note: archegos (pioneer) and "teleiotes" (perfecter); the KJV supplies "our" (in italics), which turns Jesus' own exemplary faith into the source of ours.

kjv: it (the beast) shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart
mine: it (the beast) shall be stoned
note: TR adds "e bolidi katatoxeuthesetai" from Exod 19:13; absent from all early manuscripts.

kjv: Marriage [is] honourable in all
mine: Let marriage be held in honor among all
note: The verbless clause in a series of imperatives (13:1–5) is an exhortation; the KJV makes it a statement.

kjv: Make you perfect in every good work
mine: equip you with everything good
note: TR adds "ergo" (work); absent from P46, Sinaiticus, D*.

kjv: Grace [be] with you all. Amen.
mine: Grace be with all of you.
note: TR adds "Amen".

kjv: when ye fall into divers temptations
mine: when you meet trials of various kinds
note: peirasmos in 1:2–12 is testing or trial (producing endurance); in 1:13–14 it is temptation to sin. The KJV uses "temptation" throughout, blurring James's distinction.

kjv: superfluity of naughtiness
mine: rampant wickedness
note: Naughtiness in 1611 meant wickedness; now it suggests a child's misbehaviour.

kjv: if there come unto your assembly
mine: if … comes into your synagogue
note: synagoge is the word for a Jewish meeting place; this is the only NT use for a Christian gathering, a clue to the letter's Jewish-Christian setting. The KJV's "assembly" hides it.

kjv: faith without works is dead
mine: faith apart from works is useless
note: TR "nekra" (dead, from 2:17, 26) against "arge" (idle, useless; B, C*), a pun on "erga" (works) that the TR loses.

kjv: be not many masters
mine: Not many of you should become teachers
note: didaskaloi are teachers; "masters" (1611: schoolmasters) now suggests owners.

kjv: Therewith bless we God, even the Father
mine: With it (the tongue) we bless our Lord and Father
note: TR "ton theon" against "ton kyrion" (Sinaiticus, A, B, C).

kjv: so [can] no fountain both yield salt water and fresh
mine: Neither can a salt pond yield fresh water
note: TR "houtos oudemia pege halykon kai glyky" against the shorter "oute halykon glyky" (Sinaiticus, A, B, C*).

kjv: Ye kill, and desire to have
mine: You covet and cannot obtain, so you … murder
note: The KJV punctuation joins "ye kill" with "and desire to have", obscuring James's two parallel sequences: desire → murder, covet → fight.

kjv: Ye adulterers and adulteresses
mine: You adulterous people!
note: TR adds "moichoi kai"; the early text (Sinaiticus*, A, B) has only the feminine "moichalides", Israel's prophetic image of an unfaithful wife.

kjv: The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy
mine: He (God) yearns jealously over the spirit that He has made to dwell in us
note: An obscure verse; SBLGNT reads "katoikisen" (he made to dwell), making God the subject who jealously longs for the spirit; the KJV makes the human spirit the subject of envious desire.

kjv: the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy
mine: the Lord is compassionate and merciful
note: Pitiful in 1611 meant "full of pity"; now it means "contemptible".

kjv: Confess [your] faults one to another
mine: confess your sins to one another
note: TR "paraptomata" (faults) against "hamartias" (sins; Sinaiticus, A, B); "faults" softens what is confessed.

kjv: The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much
mine: The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working
note: energoumene (working) is rendered by two words, "effectual fervent"; "fervent" has no basis in the Greek.

kjv: gird up the loins of your mind
mine: preparing your minds for action
note: A literal rendering of a Semitic idiom (tucking up a robe to work or run); vivid but now opaque.

kjv: in obeying the truth through the Spirit … with a pure heart fervently
mine: by your obedience to the truth … earnestly from a pure heart
note: TR adds "dia pneumatos"; SBLGNT omits "katharas" (pure) with A, B. Minor.

kjv: the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby
mine: the pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation
note: TR omits "eis soterian" (into salvation; P72, Sinaiticus, A, B, C). "Logikon" is "spiritual / rational", not "of the word" (a pun on logos the KJV makes explicit).

kjv: a peculiar people
mine: a people for His (God's) own possession
note: As at Titus 2:14.

kjv: to the king, as supreme
mine: to the emperor as supreme
note: basileus in a letter to the Roman provinces of Asia Minor is the emperor; also 2:17.

kjv: sanctify the Lord God in your hearts
mine: in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy
note: TR "ton theon" against "ton Christon" (P72, Sinaiticus, A, B, C); the early text applies Isa 8:13 ("the LORD") to Christ.

kjv: suffered for sins … quickened by the Spirit
mine: suffered once for sins … made alive in the spirit
note: pneumati parallel to "sarki" (flesh/spirit, two spheres) is better "in the spirit" than "by the Spirit", which the KJV capitalisation implies.

kjv: the answer of a good conscience toward God
mine: an appeal to God for a good conscience
note: eperotema is a request or pledge (perhaps the baptismal vow), not an "answer".

kjv: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified
mine: (absent)
note: TR adds a sentence absent from P72, Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: let him glorify God on this behalf
mine: let him glorify God in that name
note: TR "en to merei touto" (in this respect) against "en to onomati touto" (in this name; P72, Sinaiticus, A, B), which points back to "Christian".

kjv: Neither as being lords over God's heritage
mine: not domineering over those in your charge
note: ton kleron are the portions (congregations) allotted to each elder; "God's heritage" (KJV) is an interpretation. The source of the word "clergy", ironically here applied to the laity.

kjv: Peace [be] with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
mine: Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
note: TR adds "Iesou" and "Amen".

kjv: the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
mine: the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ
note: One article governs "God and Savior" (as at Titus 2:13), most naturally naming Jesus Christ as "our God and Savior"; the KJV's "God and our Saviour" allows two persons, unlike the identical construction in 1:11 ("Lord and Saviour") which it renders as one.

kjv: no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation
mine: no prophecy of Scripture comes from someone's own interpretation
note: In context (1:21) "idias epilyseos" is about the origin of prophecy (not the prophet's own explanation), not a ban on private Bible reading, which is how the KJV phrase has often been used.

kjv: holy men of God spake
mine: men spoke from God
note: TR "hagioi theou anthropoi" against "apo theou anthropoi" (P72, B).

kjv: cast [them (the angels)] down to hell
mine: cast them (the angels) into Tartarus
note: tartaroo (only here) is to cast into Tartarus, the Greek underworld prison of the Titans, distinct from Hades and Gehenna; the KJV's "hell" merges all three.

kjv: longsuffering to us-ward
mine: patient toward you
note: TR "eis hemas" against "eis hymas" (P72, B, C).

kjv: the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up
mine: the earth and the works that are done on it will be exposed
note: TR "katakaesetai" (will be burned up) against "heurethesetai" (will be found / laid bare; Sinaiticus, B, P72 vid). The early text speaks of the earth exposed to judgment, not annihilated; the reading is so difficult that many editors suspect corruption.

kjv: hasting unto the coming of the day of God
mine: waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God
note: speudontas is "hastening" (bringing it nearer by holy living), not "hasting unto"; the KJV makes believers hurry towards the day rather than speed its coming.

kjv: that your joy may be full
mine: so that our joy may be complete
note: TR "hymon" against "hemon" (Sinaiticus, A*, B); the author's joy is completed by the readers' fellowship.

kjv: the blood of Jesus Christ his Son
mine: the blood of Jesus His Son
note: TR adds "Christou"; absent from Sinaiticus, B, C.

kjv: ye know all things
mine: you all have knowledge
note: TR "panta" (all things) against "pantes" (all of you; Sinaiticus, B, P). The early text rejects an elite with special knowledge, rather than claiming omniscience.

kjv: [[but] he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also]
mine: Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also
note: The KJV prints the second half in italics, as doubtful, because it was missing from the Byzantine manuscripts behind the TR; it is in fact well attested (Sinaiticus, A, B, C). A rare case where the KJV marks as uncertain what the critical text includes.

kjv: that we should be called the sons of God
mine: that we should be called children of God; and so we are
note: TR omits "kai esmen" (and so we are; P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C).

kjv: Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin … he cannot sin
mine: No one born of God makes a practice of sinning … he cannot keep on sinning
note: Present tenses describe habitual action; the KJV's "cannot sin" seems to contradict 1:8–10 and has fed perfectionist readings.

kjv: Hereby perceive we the love [of God]
mine: By this we know love
note: The KJV supplies "of God" (in italics); John defines love itself by Christ's self-giving.

kjv: every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh
mine: every spirit that does not confess Jesus
note: TR expands "ton Iesoun" from 4:2; absent from Sinaiticus, A, B.

kjv: We love him, because he (God) first loved us
mine: We love because He (God) first loved us
note: TR adds "auton" (him); absent from A, B. The early text makes love in general the response to God's love.

kjv: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth
mine: For there are three that testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood
note: The "Johannine Comma" (5:7b–8a) appears in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century (and then only in a few late ones, some with the words added in the margin), in no early version, and in no Greek Father during the Trinitarian controversies; it arose in Latin commentary and entered the Vulgate tradition. Erasmus added it to his third edition (1522) after a recently copied Greek manuscript containing it (minuscule 61) was produced. It is the only explicit Trinitarian formula in the KJV NT and has no claim to be original. Spans 5:7–8. Context: three that testify: the Spirit, the water and the blood (no Comma) (high confidence). The heavenly witnesses appear in no Greek manuscript before about the 14th century (629, 61, 918, 2318 and a few margins), in no early version, and in no Greek Father during the Trinitarian debates; they arose in Latin sources (Priscillian, c. 380) and entered later Vulgate copies. 5:6 and 5:8 carry the Spirit-water-blood argument. Other possible meanings: (1) 'three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one' — TR (Erasmus 1522 onward), KJV, later Vulgate manuscripts, perhaps Cyprian (De unitate 6); the Byzantine Majority Text lacks it; (2) the Spirit, water and blood read as baptism, the cross and the eucharist — an interpretation of the shorter text.

kjv: and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God
mine: (absent)
note: TR repeats the clause; absent from Sinaiticus*, A, B.

kjv: he that is begotten of God keepeth himself
mine: He Who was born of God protects him
note: SBLGNT reads "auton" (him, i.e. Christ the one born of God keeps the believer) with A*, B; TR "heauton" (himself) makes the believer self-protecting.

kjv: Grace be with you … from the Lord Jesus Christ
mine: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us … from Jesus Christ
note: TR "hymon" (you) against "hemon" (us), and adds "kyriou" (Lord); absent from A, B.

kjv: that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive
mine: so that you may not lose what we have worked for, but may win
note: TR first-person "apolesomen … apolabomen" against second-person "apolesete … apolabete" (Sinaiticus, A, B).

kjv: Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ
mine: Everyone who goes on ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ
note: TR "parabainon" (transgressing) against "proagon" (going ahead; Sinaiticus, A, B); the early text targets those who claim advanced teaching beyond the gospel.

kjv: I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health
mine: I pray that all may go well with you and that you may be in good health
note: peri panton is "in all respects", not "above all things"; the KJV phrase has been used as a proof-text for a gospel of prosperity, which a conventional letter-greeting does not support.

kjv: for his name's sake
mine: for the sake of the name
note: TR adds "autou" (his); absent from Sinaiticus, A, B, C.

kjv: to them that are sanctified by God the Father
mine: to those who are … beloved in God the Father
note: TR "hegiasmenois" (sanctified) against "egapemenois" (beloved; P72, Sinaiticus, A, B).

kjv: denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ
mine: deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ
note: TR adds "theon" (God), making two persons; the early text calls Jesus Christ "our only Master and Lord".

kjv: how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt
mine: that Jesus, Who saved a people out of the land of Egypt
note: SBLGNT reads "Iesous" with A, B, 33, 1739 and early versions (TR "kyrios"); the early text names Jesus as Israel's deliverer at the exodus, a strikingly high Christology (cf. 1 Cor 10:4).

kjv: These (the ungodly people) are spots in your feasts of charity
mine: These (the ungodly people) are hidden reefs at your love feasts
note: spilades are submerged rocks that wreck ships; "spots" reads it as "spiloi" (stains, as at 2 Pet 2:13).

kjv: And of some have compassion, making a difference
mine: And have mercy on those who doubt
note: diakrinomenous here means "those who doubt" (as at Jas 1:6), not "making a difference"; the TR also has a two-clause form of 1:22–23 against the three-clause early text.

kjv: To the only wise God our Saviour … both now and ever
mine: to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord … before all time and now and forever
note: TR adds "sopho" (wise) and omits "dia Iesou Christou tou kyriou hemon" and "pro pantos tou aionos".

kjv: Unto him (Jesus Christ) that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood
mine: To Him (Jesus Christ) Who loves us and has freed us from our sins by His blood
note: TR "lousanti" (washed) against "lysanti" (freed; P18, Sinaiticus, A, C), one letter's difference; TR also has past "loved" for present "loves".

kjv: hath made us kings and priests
mine: made us a kingdom, priests
note: TR "basileis" (kings) against "basileian" (kingdom; Sinaiticus, A, C), from Exod 19:6. Also 5:10.

kjv: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord
mine: I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God
note: TR adds "arche kai telos" (from 21:6) and omits "ho theos".

kjv: Saying, I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: and, What thou (John) seest
mine: saying, "Write what you (John) see
note: TR adds "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last" and "which are in Asia"; absent from all early manuscripts.

kjv: the keys of hell and of death
mine: the keys of Death and Hades
note: hades is the realm of the dead, paired with Death (as in 6:8, 20:13–14); "hell" turns it into the place of punishment. TR also reverses the order and adds "Amen".

kjv: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty
mine: I know your tribulation and your poverty
note: TR adds "ta erga kai" (from 2:2, 19); absent from Sinaiticus, A, C. Also 2:13.

kjv: as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers
mine: as when earthen pots are broken in pieces
note: Shivers (fragments) is archaic.

kjv: four beasts full of eyes
mine: four living creatures, full of eyes
note: zoa are living beings (Ezek 1:5); "beasts" invites confusion with the "therion" (beast) of chapter 13. Systematic in Revelation; flagged once here.

kjv: for thy (God's) pleasure they (all things) are and were created
mine: by Your (God's) will they (all things) existed and were created
note: dia to thelema sou is "because of your will"; "for thy pleasure" suggests creation exists to please God, a different idea.

kjv: hast redeemed us to God by thy (the Lamb's) blood
mine: by Your (the Lamb's) blood You ransomed people for God
note: TR adds "hemas" (us); absent from A. With it the elders sing of their own redemption, which conflicts with "them" in 5:10 of the early text.

kjv: And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign
mine: and You have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign
note: TR "hemas … basileis … basileusomen" against "autous … basileian … basileusousin" (Sinaiticus, A).

kjv: the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him that liveth for ever and ever
mine: the elders fell down and worshiped
note: TR adds "twenty-four" and "him that liveth for ever and ever"; absent from all Greek manuscripts except a few late ones.

kjv: Come and see
mine: Come!
note: TR adds "kai ide" (and see), making the call an invitation to John rather than a summons to the horseman; also 6:3, 6:5, 6:7.

kjv: his name that sat on him (the pale horse) was Death, and Hell followed with him (Death)
mine: its rider's name was Death, and Hades followed him (Death)
note: Hades is the realm of the dead, personified alongside Death; "Hell" here is misleading. As at 1:18.

kjv: These (those clothed in white robes) are they which came out of great tribulation
mine: These (those clothed in white robes) are the ones coming out of the great tribulation
note: tes thlipseos tes megales has the article: "the great tribulation", a specific end-time ordeal; the KJV's "great tribulation" (no article) makes it general suffering. The present participle "coming" is also lost.

kjv: the third part of trees was burnt up
mine: a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees
note: TR omits "kai to triton tes ges katekae" (and a third of the earth was burned up; Sinaiticus, A, P), by homoeoteleuton.

kjv: I heard an angel flying through the midst of heaven
mine: I heard an eagle crying … as it flew directly overhead
note: TR "angelou" against "aetou" (eagle; Sinaiticus, A); the angel replaces John's eagle, perhaps under influence of 14:6.

kjv: the key of the bottomless pit
mine: the key to the shaft of the abyss
note: phrear tes abyssou is the shaft or well of the abyss; "bottomless pit" (systematic in Revelation) loses the image of a shaft leading down to the deep.

kjv: that there should be time no longer
mine: that there would be no more delay
note: chronos ouketi estai means "there will be no more delay" (cf. 6:11 "a little while longer"); the KJV phrase has been read as the end of time itself, a famous hymn line ("When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound, and time shall be no more").

kjv: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord
mine: The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord
note: TR plural "basileiai" against singular "basileia" (Sinaiticus, A, C, P); John sees one world-empire handed over.

kjv: which art, and wast, and art to come
mine: Who is and Who was
note: TR adds "kai ho erchomenos" (from 1:4, 8; 4:8); absent from all early manuscripts. Its absence is deliberate: at the seventh trumpet God has come.

kjv: the testimony of Jesus Christ
mine: the testimony of Jesus
note: TR adds "Christou"; absent from Sinaiticus, A, C.

kjv: And I (John) stood upon the sand of the sea (KJV 13:1a)
mine: And he (the dragon) stood on the sand of the sea
note: TR "estathen" (I stood, beginning 13:1) against "estathe" (he, the dragon, stood; P47, Sinaiticus, A, C). The early text puts the dragon on the shore summoning the beast from the sea; the KJV numbers the clause 13:1.

kjv: the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world
mine: whose name has not been written before the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb Who was slain
note: from the foundation of the world most likely modifies "written" (as in the parallel 17:8, where there is no Lamb); the KJV's word order makes the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, a phrase that has become a theological slogan.

kjv: He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity
mine: If anyone is to be taken captive, to captivity he goes
note: TR "ei tis aichmalosian synagei" (leads into captivity), a scribal attempt to make the line about retribution; the early text (A) is a call to endurance (Jer 15:2).

kjv: having his (the Lamb's) Father's name written in their foreheads
mine: who had His (the Lamb's) name and His Father's name written on their foreheads
note: TR omits "to onoma autou kai" (his name and; P47, Sinaiticus, A, C), by homoeoteleuton.

kjv: for they (the 144,000) are without fault before the throne of God
mine: for they (the 144,000) are blameless
note: TR adds "enopion tou thronou tou theou"; absent from all early manuscripts.

kjv: had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, [and] over the number of his name
mine: those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name
note: TR adds "ek tou charagmatos autou" (over his mark); absent from all early Greek manuscripts.

kjv: thou King of saints
mine: O King of the nations
note: TR "hagion" (saints) has almost no Greek support (Erasmus' text); Sinaiticus*, C read "aionon" (of the ages), A, P "ethnon" (of the nations). SBLGNT reads "ethnon", which fits 15:4 "all nations will come".

kjv: which art, and wast, and shalt be
mine: who is and who was, O Holy One
note: The TR's "kai ho esomenos" (and shalt be) is Theodore Beza's conjecture (1582), with no support in any Greek manuscript; all manuscripts read "ho hosios" (the Holy One). The KJV follows Beza and loses the title "Holy One".

kjv: a great voice out of the temple of heaven
mine: a loud voice came out of the temple
note: TR adds "tou ouranou"; absent from A and others.

kjv: the beast that was, and is not, and yet is
mine: because it was and is not and is to come
note: TR "kaiper estin" (and yet is) against "kai parestai" (and will be present / is to come; Sinaiticus, A, P), a parody of God's title "who was and is and is to come".

kjv: the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast
mine: the ten horns that you saw, they and the beast
note: TR "epi to therion" (upon the beast) against "kai to therion" (and the beast; Sinaiticus, A, P); the early text makes the beast join the horns in destroying the prostitute.

kjv: a cage of every unclean and hateful bird
mine: a haunt of every unclean bird, and a haunt of every unclean and hated beast
note: SBLGNT adds "kai phylakē pantos thēriou akathartou" (haunt of every unclean beast), which the TR lacks, so "hateful" attaches to the beasts rather than the birds.

kjv: have drunk of the wine
mine: have fallen from the wine
note: SBLGNT reads peptōkan "have fallen"; the TR reads pepōken "has drunk". The two Greek words differ by one letter and the manuscripts are divided.

kjv: the wine of the wrath of her (Babylon's) fornication
mine: the wine of the passion of her (Babylon's) sexual immorality
note: Thymos can mean wrath or hot passion; here it most likely means the intoxicating passion of her immorality, though it may also hint at God's wrath (14:10).

kjv: as she (Babylon) rewarded you
mine: as she (Babylon) herself has paid out
note: The TR adds hymin "you" after apedōken; SBLGNT has no object, so the payback is not described as aimed at the hearers.

kjv: who judgeth her (Babylon)
mine: Who has judged her (Babylon)
note: SBLGNT has the aorist ho krinas "who judged"; the TR has the present ho krinōn "who judges".

kjv: And cinnamon, and odours
mine: cinnamon and spice
note: SBLGNT includes kai amōmon (amomum, an aromatic spice) after cinnamon; the TR omits it.

kjv: thou shalt find them (the luxuries and splendor) no more
mine: people will never find them (the luxuries and splendor) again
note: SBLGNT reads the third plural heurēsousin "they will find"; the TR has the second singular heurēsēs "you will find".

kjv: all the company in ships
mine: everyone who sails anywhere
note: SBLGNT reads pas ho epi topon pleōn "everyone who sails to a place"; the TR reads pas epi tōn ploiōn ho homilos "all the company on the ships".

kjv: ye holy apostles and prophets
mine: you saints and apostles and prophets
note: SBLGNT reads hoi hagioi kai hoi apostoloi "the saints and the apostles", three groups called to rejoice; the TR reads hoi hagioi apostoloi "the holy apostles", making "holy" an adjective.

kjv: the light of a candle
mine: the light of a lamp
note: Lychnos is an oil lamp. "Candle" in 1611 meant any small light, but a modern reader pictures a wax candle.

kjv: Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God
mine: Salvation and glory and power belong to our God
note: The TR adds hē timē "honour" and has the dative kyriō tō theō hēmōn "to the Lord our God"; SBLGNT has no "honour" and reads the genitive tou theou hēmōn "of our God".

kjv: her (the great prostitute's) smoke rose up for ever and ever
mine: her (the great prostitute's) smoke goes up forever and ever
note: Both Greek texts have the present anabainei "goes up". The KJV's past tense loses the point that the smoke keeps rising forever.

kjv: the four beasts
mine: the four living creatures
note: Zōa means living creatures, the throne attendants of ch. 4. In this book "beast" now suggests thērion, the hostile Beast of ch. 13 and 19:19-20, which is a different word.

kjv: the fine linen is the righteousness of saints
mine: the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints
note: Dikaiōmata (plural) means righteous acts or just deeds, not righteousness as a quality or status. The KJV's abstract noun hides that the robe stands for what the saints have done.

kjv: he (the Word of God) shall rule them (the nations) with a rod of iron
mine: he (the Word of God) will shepherd them (the nations) with a rod of iron
note: Poimanei means "will shepherd". Following Ps 2:9 LXX, it is often taken as "rule" or even "break", so the KJV's sense is defensible, but the shepherd image is lost.

kjv: the supper of the great God
mine: the great supper of God
note: SBLGNT reads to deipnon to mega tou theou "the great supper of God"; the TR reads to deipnon tou megalou theou "the supper of the great God".

kjv: judgment was given unto them
mine: authority to judge was given to them
note: Krima edothē autois can mean that the enthroned were given power to judge, or that a verdict was given in their favor (cf. Dan 7:22). The KJV's "judgment" keeps the ambiguity; I take it as power to judge.

kjv: fire came down from God out of heaven
mine: fire came down from heaven
note: The TR adds apo tou theou "from God"; SBLGNT reads only ek tou ouranou "from heaven".

kjv: stand before God
mine: standing before the throne
note: SBLGNT reads enōpion tou thronou "before the throne"; the TR reads enōpion tou theou "before God".

kjv: death and hell delivered up the dead
mine: Death and Hades gave up the dead
note: Hadēs is the realm of the dead, not the place of final punishment. The KJV's "hell" here gives that impression, though the lake of fire is where final punishment happens.

kjv: death and hell were cast into the lake of fire
mine: Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire
note: With "hell" for hadēs, the KJV seems to throw hell into hell. The text means the realm of the dead is itself destroyed in the lake of fire.

kjv: This is the second death.
mine: This is the second death, the lake of fire.
note: SBLGNT adds hē limnē tou pyros "the lake of fire" as an explanation; the TR lacks it.

kjv: And I John saw the holy city
mine: And I saw the holy city
note: The TR adds egō Iōannēs "I John"; SBLGNT has only eidon "I saw".

kjv: a great voice out of heaven
mine: a loud voice from the throne
note: SBLGNT reads ek tou thronou "from the throne"; the TR reads ek tou ouranou "from heaven".

kjv: God himself shall be with them (human beings), and be their God
mine: God Himself will be with them (human beings)
note: The TR adds theos autōn "their God" at the end; SBLGNT lacks it.

kjv: they (human beings) shall be his (God's) people
mine: they (human beings) will be His (God's) peoples
note: Both Greek texts have the plural laoi "peoples". It recasts the covenant formula of Lev 26:12 to include many nations, and the KJV's singular loses that.

kjv: shall inherit all things
mine: will inherit these things
note: SBLGNT reads tauta "these things", the blessings just described; the TR reads panta "all things".

kjv: that great city, the holy Jerusalem
mine: the holy city Jerusalem
note: The TR reads tēn polin tēn megalēn tēn hagian "the great city, the holy", while SBLGNT has only tēn polin tēn hagian "the holy city". Without "great" the city is not echoing "the great city" Babylon.

kjv: the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it (the city)
mine: The nations will walk by its (the city's) light
note: The TR adds tōn sōzomenōn "of those being saved", which narrows "the nations". SBLGNT says simply that the nations will walk by its light. The TR also adds kai tēn timēn "and honour" later in the verse.

kjv: any thing that defileth
mine: nothing unclean
note: SBLGNT reads pan koinon "anything unclean"; the TR reads pan koinoun "anything that defiles", an active participle.

kjv: a pure river of water of life
mine: the river of the water of life
note: The TR adds katharon "pure" before potamon; SBLGNT lacks it.

kjv: the Lord God of the holy prophets
mine: The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets
note: SBLGNT reads ho theos tōn pneumatōn tōn prophētōn "the God of the spirits of the prophets", that is, the God who inspires them (cf. 1 Cor 14:32). The TR reads tōn hagiōn prophētōn "of the holy prophets".

kjv: I (Jesus) come quickly
mine: I (Jesus) am coming soon
note: Tachy here means "soon", not "fast". "Quickly" could mean either in 1611, but today it suggests speed of movement rather than nearness in time. The same phrase recurs in 22:12 and 22:20.

kjv: he that is righteous, let him be righteous still
mine: the righteous still do what is right
note: SBLGNT reads dikaiosynēn poiēsatō "let him do righteousness"; the TR reads dikaiōthētō "let him be made righteous".

kjv: Blessed are they that do his commandments
mine: Blessed are those who wash their robes
note: SBLGNT reads hoi plynontes tas stolas autōn "those who wash their robes", recalling 7:14 and the Lamb's blood. The TR reads hoi poiountes tas entolas autou "those who do his commandments". The two readings look alike in uncial script, and the choice has doctrinal weight. Context: those who wash their robes (high confidence). Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Vulgate read 'wash their robes', echoing 7:14. The Byzantine 'do his commandments' looks similar in uncial script (PLYNONTESTASSTOLAS / POIOUNTESTASENTOLAS) and may have been drawn to 12:17 and 14:12. The earlier witnesses and the book's own imagery favour 'wash'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'those who do his commandments' — TR, most Byzantine manuscripts (046), Tertullian, Cyprian, KJV, NKJV, cf. Rev 12:17; 14:12; (2) the washing understood specifically of baptism or of martyrdom (cf. 7:14) — various commentators.

kjv: God shall take away his part out of the book of life
mine: God will take away his share in the tree of life
note: All Greek manuscripts read tou xylou tēs zōēs "the tree of life". "Book of life" entered the TR through Erasmus, who supplied the end of Revelation by translating Latin back into Greek, using a Vulgate reading (libro for ligno). Context: tree of life (high confidence). Every Greek manuscript reads xylou 'tree' of life, as does the Vulgate (ligno); 'book' (libro) is a Latin copying slip. Erasmus, whose Greek manuscript lacked the end of Revelation, back-translated from Latin and so brought 'book of life' into the TR. 22:2 and 22:14 confirm 'tree'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'God shall take away his part out of the book of life' — TR, KJV, NKJV, some Latin manuscripts and Latin writers, echoing 3:5 and 20:15 where the book of life appears; the Majority Text reads 'tree'.

kjv: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
mine: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.
note: SBLGNT reads tou kyriou Iēsou meta pantōn "of the Lord Jesus with all". The TR adds hēmōn, Christou, hymōn and a final amēn.
